~: Expand to a directory. More information: <https://gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Tilde-Expansion>.
}: This shell keyword is used to close out `{`.
zstyle: Define and look up configuration styles in Zsh. This builtin is part of the `zsh/zutil` module. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Zsh-Modules.html>.
zsteg: Steganography detection tool for PNG and BMP file formats. It detects LSB steganography, ZLIB-compressed data, OpenStego, Camouflage, and LSB with the Eratosthenes set. More information: <https://github.com/zed-0xff/zsteg>.
zstdmt: This command is an alias of `zstd --threads 0`.
zstdless: Open a `zstd` compressed file for interactive reading, allowing scrolling and search. See also: `zstd`, `less`. More information: <https://manned.org/zstdless>.
zstdcat: This command is an alias of `zstd --decompress --stdout --force`.
zstd: Compress or decompress files with Zstandard compression. More information: <https://manned.org/zstd>.
zsh: Z SHell, a Bash-compatible command-line interpreter. See also: `bash`, `!`, `^`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Invocation.html#Invocation>.
zrun: Transparently uncompress argument files to a command. More information: <https://manned.org/zrun>.
zrok: Expose local services and files to the internet. Part of the OpenZiti project, offering secure, zero-trust sharing. More information: <https://docs.zrok.io/>.
zpaq: Incremental journaling backup utility and archiver. More information: <https://mattmahoney.net/dc/zpaqdoc.html>.
zoxide: Keep track of the most frequently used directories. Uses a ranking algorithm to navigate to the best match. More information: <https://manned.org/zoxide>.
zola: A static site generator in a single binary with everything built-in. More information: <https://www.getzola.org/documentation/getting-started/cli-usage/>.
znew: Recompress files from `.Z` to `gzip` format. More information: <https://manned.org/znew>.
zmv: Move or rename files matching a specified extended `glob` pattern. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/User-Contributions.html>.
zmore: View `gzip` compressed files with `more`. More information: <https://manned.org/zmore>.
zmap: Fast, open-source network scanner for Internet-wide surveys. See also: `hping3`, `masscan`, `naabu`, `nmap`, `rustscan`. More information: <https://manned.org/zmap>.
zm: A tool for managing articles of newspapers and blogs. More information: <https://github.com/ZERMZeitung/zm2>.
zlib-flate: Raw zlib compression and decompression program. Part of `qpdf`. More information: <https://manned.org/zlib-flate>.
zless: View `gzip` and `xz` compressed files. More information: <https://manned.org/zless>.
zle: Manage Zsh Line Editor widgets. Note: Some operations require ZLE to be active (typically inside a user-defined widget). See also: `bindkey`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Zsh-Line-Editor.html#Zle-Builtins>.
zizmor: Find security issues in GitHub Actions workflows and action definitions. More information: <https://docs.zizmor.sh/quickstart/>.
zipnote: View, add, or edit a Zip archive's comments. Files can also be renamed in the Zip archive. More information: <https://manned.org/zipnote>.
zipinfo: List detailed information about the contents of a Zip file. More information: <https://manned.org/zipinfo>.
zipgrep: Find patterns in files in a Zip archive using extended `regex` (supports `?`, `+`, `{}`, `()`, and `|`). More information: <https://manned.org/zipgrep>.
zipcloak: Encrypt the contents within a Zip archive. More information: <https://manned.org/zipcloak>.
zipalign: Zip archive alignment tool. Part of the Android SDK build tools. More information: <https://developer.android.com/tools/zipalign>.
zip2john: Extract password hashes from Zip archives for use with John the Ripper password cracker. This is a utility tool usually installed as part of the John the Ripper installation. More information: <https://www.openwall.com/john/>.
zip: Package and compress (archive) files into a Zip archive. See also: `unzip`. More information: <https://manned.org/zip>.
zint: Generate barcodes and QR codes. More information: <https://www.zint.org.uk/manual/chapter/4>.
zinit: Flexible and blazing fast Zsh plugin manager. More information: <https://github.com/zdharma-continuum/zinit>.
zig: The Zig compiler and toolchain. More information: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/>.
zgrep: Grep text patterns from files within compressed files. More information: <https://manned.org/zgrep>.
zformat: Format strings in Zsh. This builtin is part of the `zsh/zutil` module. See also: `zstyle`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Zsh-Modules.html>.
zfgrep: This command is an alias of `zgrep --fixed-strings`.
zerotier-one: Start the ZeroTier One daemon. See also: `zerotier-cli`, `zerotier-idtool`. More information: <https://github.com/zerotier/ZeroTierOne/blob/main/doc/zerotier-one.8.md>.
zerotier-idtool: Create and manipulate ZeroTier identities. See also: `zerotier-cli`, `zerotier-one`. More information: <https://github.com/zerotier/ZeroTierOne/blob/dev/doc/zerotier-idtool.1.md>.
zerotier-cli: Control the local ZeroTier virtual network service. See also: `zerotier-idtool`, `zerotier-one`. More information: <https://github.com/zerotier/ZeroTierOne/blob/main/doc/zerotier-cli.1.md>.
zeroclaw: Fast, small, and fully autonomous AI assistant infrastructure. Some subcommands such as `onboard`, `models`, `service`, etc. have their own usage documentation. See also: `openclaw`. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-status: Show the full system status for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-skills: Manage user-defined skills for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-service: Manage the ZeroClaw background service (launchd/systemd user service). More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-onboard: Initialize workspace and configuration for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-models: Manage provider model catalogs for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-migrate: Migrate data from other agent runtimes to ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-integrations: Browse and manage 50+ integrations for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-hardware: Discover and introspect USB hardware for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-gateway: Start the gateway server for ZeroClaw (webhooks and API). More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-doctor: Run diagnostics for ZeroClaw daemon, scheduler, and channel freshness. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-daemon: Start the full autonomous runtime for ZeroClaw (gateway + channels + heartbeat). More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-cron: Manage scheduled tasks for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-channel: Manage channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.) for ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zeroclaw-agent: Start the AI agent loop for interacting with ZeroClaw. More information: <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#quick-start>.
zellij: Terminal multiplexer with batteries included. See also: `tmux`, `screen`, `herdr`. More information: <https://zellij.dev/documentation/>.
zek: Generate a Go struct from XML. More information: <https://github.com/miku/zek#usage>.
zeisstopnm: Convert a Zeiss confocal file to Netbpm format. More information: <https://manned.org/zeisstopnm>.
zegrep: This command is an alias of `zgrep --extended-regexp`.
zeek: Passive network traffic analyzer. Any output and log files will be saved to the current working directory. More information: <https://docs.zeek.org/en/lts/quickstart.html#zeek-as-a-command-line-utility>.
zeditor: This command is an alias of `zed`.
zed: Text editor designed to be fast, efficient, and convenient. More information: <https://zed.dev/docs/reference/cli>.
zcat: This command is an alias of `gzip --stdout --decompress`.
zbarimg: Scan and decode bar codes from image file(s). More information: <https://manned.org/zbarimg>.
zapier: Create, automate, and manage zapier integrations. Some subcommands such as `build`, `init`, `scaffold`, `push`, `test`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/cli.md>.
zapier-versions: List the versions for a Zapier integration. More information: <https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/cli.md#validate>.
zapier-validate: Validate a Zapier integration. More information: <https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/cli.md#validate>.
zapier-test: Test a Zapier integration via the `test` script in your `package.json`. More information: <https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/cli.md#test>.
zapier-scaffold: Add a starting trigger, create, search, or resource to an integration. More information: <https://platform.zapier.com/reference/cli#scaffold>.
zapier-push: Build and upload a Zapier integration. More information: <https://platform.zapier.com/reference/cli#push>.
zapier-login: Log in to a Zapier account. More information: <https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/cli.md#login>.
zapier-init: Initialize a new Zapier integration. More information: <https://platform.zapier.com/reference/cli#init>.
zapier-history: List the history for a Zapier integration. More information: <https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/cli.md#history>.
zapier-convert: Convert a Visual Builder integration to a CLI integration. More information: <https://platform.zapier.com/reference/cli#convert>.
zapier-build: Build a pushable `zip` of a Zapier integration. More information: <https://platform.zapier.com/reference/cli#build>.
zapier-analytics: Show the status of the analytics that are collected. It is also used to change what is collected. More information: <https://platform.zapier.com/reference/cli#analytics>.
zabbix_server: Core daemon of Zabbix software. More information: <https://manned.org/zabbix_server>.
zabbix_agentd: Daemon for monitoring server parameters. More information: <https://manned.org/zabbix_agentd>.
zabbix_agent2: Daemon for monitoring server parameters. More information: <https://manned.org/zabbix_agent2>.
z: Track the most used (by frequency) directories and enable quickly navigating to them using string patterns or `regex`. More information: <https://github.com/rupa/z>.
yuy2topam: Convert YUY2 bytes to PAM. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/yuy2topam.html>.
yuvtoppm: Convert Abekas YUV bytes to PPM. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/yuvtoppm.html>.
yuvsplittoppm: Convert three subsampled Abekas YUV files to one PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/yuvsplittoppm.html>.
ytmdl: Download songs from YouTube and automatically add metadata. Fetch song information (artist, album, cover art) from iTunes, Spotify, and other sources. More information: <https://github.com/deepjyoti30/ytmdl#usage>.
yt-dlp: A youtube-dl fork with additional features and fixes. Download videos from YouTube and other websites. See also: `ytfzf`. More information: <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#usage-and-options>.
yq: A lightweight and portable YAML processor. More information: <https://mikefarah.gitbook.io/yq/>.
youtube-viewer: Search and play videos from YouTube. See also: `you-get`, `ytfzf`, `yt-dlp`. More information: <https://github.com/trizen/youtube-viewer>.
youtube-dl: Download videos from YouTube and other websites. See also: `yt-dlp`, `ytfzf`, `you-get`. More information: <https://rg3.github.io/youtube-dl/>.
you-get: Download media contents (videos, audios, images) from the Web. See also: `yt-dlp`, `youtube-viewer`, `instaloader`. More information: <https://you-get.org/#getting-started>.
yolo: Train, validate, or infer models on various tasks and versions. More information: <https://docs.ultralytics.com/usage/cli/>.
ykman: YubiKey Manager - configure YubiKeys. If there are multiple YubiKeys connected, you have to add `--device serial_number` before a subcommand. More information: <https://docs.yubico.com/software/yubikey/tools/ykman/index.html>.
ykman-openpgp: Manage the OpenPGP YubiKey application. Note: You need to use `gpg --card-edit` for some settings. More information: <https://docs.yubico.com/software/yubikey/tools/ykman/OpenPGP_Commands.html>.
ykman-oath: Manage the OATH YubiKey application. A `keyword` can be a part of the name or the issuer. More information: <https://docs.yubico.com/software/yubikey/tools/ykman/OATH_Commands.html>.
ykman-fido: Manage YubiKey FIDO applications. More information: <https://docs.yubico.com/software/yubikey/tools/ykman/FIDO_Commands.html>.
ykman-config: Enable or disable YubiKey applications. Note: You can use `ykman info` to see currently enabled applications. More information: <https://docs.yubico.com/software/yubikey/tools/ykman/Base_Commands.html#ykman-config-options-command-args>.
ykinfo: Get basic information from a YubiKey. More information: <https://developers.yubico.com/yubikey-personalization/Manuals/ykinfo.1.html>.
yj: Convert between YAML, TOML, JSON, and HCL, preserving map order. More information: <https://github.com/sclevine/yj>.
yesod: Helper tool for Yesod, a Haskell-based web framework. All Yesod commands are invoked through the `stack` project manager. More information: <https://github.com/yesodweb/yesod>.
yes: Output something repeatedly. This command is commonly used to answer yes to every prompt by install commands (such as `apt-get`). More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/yes-invocation.html>.
yek: Serialize a repository or directory into an LLM-friendly single file (fast Rust-based repomapper). More information: <https://github.com/bodo-run/yek#usage>.
ybmtopbm: Convert a Bennet Yee "face" file to PBM. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/ybmtopbm.html>.
ybacklight: Manage screen backlight brightness. See also: `xbacklight`. More information: <https://github.com/pixelcmtd/ybacklight>.
yazi: Blazing fast terminal file manager written in Rust. Efficient, user-friendly, and customizable file management experience. More information: <https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi>.
yarn: JavaScript and Node.js package manager alternative. More information: <https://yarnpkg.com/cli>.
yarn-why: Identify why a Yarn package has been installed. More information: <https://github.com/amio/yarn-why>.
yard: Documentation tool for Ruby. More information: <https://rubydoc.info/gems/yard/file/docs/GettingStarted.md#using-yard-to-generate-documentation>.
yarac: Compile YARA rule source files into a binary format for faster loading. See also: `yara`. More information: <https://manned.org/yarac>.
yara: Pattern matching tool for identifying and classifying malware. See also: `yarac`. More information: <https://yara.readthedocs.io/en/stable/commandline.html>.
yapf: Python style guide checker. More information: <https://github.com/google/yapf#usage>.
yank: Read input from `stdin` and display a selection interface that allows a field to be selected and copied to the clipboard. More information: <https://manned.org/yank>.
yamllint: A linter for YAML files. More information: <https://yamllint.readthedocs.io>.
yadm: A dotfiles manager that works by using `git`. Some subcommands such as `init`, `clone`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/overview>.
yadm-upgrade: Upgrade yadm to the latest version. Upgrading will attempt to de-initialize and re-initialize your submodules. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#commands>.
yadm-transcrypt: If `transcrypt` is installed, allows you to pass options directly to `transcrypt`. With the environment configured to use the yadm repository. Transcrypt enables transparent encryption and decryption of files in a Git repository. More information: <https://github.com/elasticdog/transcrypt#command-line-options>.
yadm-perms: Update permissions. It is usually unnecessary to run this command, as yadm automatically processes permissions by default. This automatic behavior can be disabled by setting the configuration `yadm.auto-perms` to `"false"`. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#permissions>.
yadm-list: Print a list of files managed by yadm. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#commands>.
yadm-introspect: Look at data that is managed by yadm. The purpose of introspection is to support command line completion. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#commands>.
yadm-init: Initialize a new, empty repository for tracking dotfiles. The repository is stored in `$HOME/.local/share/yadm/repo.git`. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/getting_started>.
yadm-gitconfig: Pass options to `git config`. Change the `.gitconfig` of the repository managed by yadm. See also: `git config`. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#commands>.
yadm-git-crypt: Git Crypt enables transparent encryption and decryption of files in a Git repository. More information: <https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt>.
yadm-enter: Run a sub-shell with all Git variables set. This sub-shell can be used to easily interact with the local yadm repository using Git commands. This could be useful if you are using a tool which uses Git directly. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#commands>.
yadm-encrypt: Encrypt files listed in the designated encrypt file. After the files are encrypted they will be save in the designated archive folder. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/encryption>.
yadm-decrypt: Decrypt files that were encrypted by yadm. When activating this command you will be prompted for a password. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/encryption>.
yadm-config: Pass options to yadm's config file. Change the `.config` of the repository managed by yadm. More information: <https://github.com/TheLocehiliosan/yadm/blob/master/yadm.md#configuration>.
yadm-clone: Works just like `git clone`. In addition you can pass extra flags to configure your repository. If there is a bootstrap file in the repository, you will be prompted to execute it. See also: `git clone`. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/common_commands>.
yadm-bootstrap: Execute Yadm's bootstrap file. This file should be created in `$HOME/.config/yadm/bootstrap`. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/bootstrap>.
yadm-alt: Create symbolic links and process templates for any managed files. Learn more about templates: <https://yadm.io/docs/templates>. More information: <https://yadm.io/docs/alternates>.
yacc: Generate an LALR parser (in C) with a formal grammar specification file. See also: `bison`. More information: <https://manned.org/yacc.1p>.
yacas: Yet Another Computer Algebra System. More information: <https://www.yacas.org/>.
ya: Manage Yazi plugins and flavors, publish or subscribe to DDS messages. More information: <https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/cli/>.
xzmore: Display text from `xz` or `lzma` compressed files. Almost equivalent to `xzless`, except it respects the `$PAGER` environment variable, uses `more` by default, and you cannot pass options to the pager. More information: <https://manned.org/xzmore>.
xzless: Display text from `xz` and `lzma` compressed files. See also: `less`. More information: <https://manned.org/xzless>.
xzgrep: Search files possibly compressed with `xz`, `lzma`, `gzip`, `bzip2`, `lzop`, or `zstd` using `regex`. See also: `grep`. More information: <https://manned.org/xzgrep>.
xzfgrep: This command is an alias of `xzgrep --fixed-strings`.
xzegrep: This command is an alias of `xzgrep --extended-regexp`.
xzdiff: Invoke `diff` on files compressed with `xz`, `lzma`, `gzip`, `bzip2`, `lzop`, or `zstd`. All options specified are passed directly to `diff`. More information: <https://manned.org/xzdiff>.
xzcmp: Invoke `cmp` on files compressed with `xz`, `lzma`, `gzip`, `bzip2`, `lzop`, or `zstd`. All options specified are passed directly to `cmp`. More information: <https://manned.org/xzcmp>.
xzcat: This command is an alias of `xz --decompress --stdout`.
xz: Compress or decompress XZ and LZMA files. More information: <https://manned.org/xz>.
xxh: Bring your shell with all of your customizations through SSH sessions. Note: `xxh` does not install anything into system directories on the target machine; removing `~/.xxh` will clear all traces of xxh on the target machine. More information: <https://github.com/xxh/xxh#usage>.
xxd: Create a hexadecimal representation (hexdump) from a binary file, or vice-versa. See also: `hexyl`, `od`, `hexdump`. More information: <https://manned.org/xxd>.
xwininfo: Display information about windows. See also: `xprop`, `xkill`. More information: <https://www.x.org/releases/current/doc/man/man1/xwininfo.1.xhtml>.
xwdtopnm: Convert an X11 or X10 window dump file to PNM. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/xwdtopnm.html>.
xvminitoppm: Convert an XV thumbnail picture to PPM. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/xvminitoppm.html>.
xteddy: A cuddly teddy bear for your X Windows desktop. More information: <https://manned.org/xteddy>.
xsv: A CSV toolkit written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/BurntSushi/xsv>.
xsp: Mono ASP.NET Web Server. More information: <https://www.mono-project.com/docs/web/aspnet/>.
xprop: Display window and font properties in an X server. More information: <https://manned.org/xprop>.
xpmtoppm: Convert an X11 pixmap to a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/xpmtoppm.html>.
xpdf: Portable Document Format (PDF) file viewer. More information: <https://www.xpdfreader.com/xpdf-man.html>.
xonsh: Python-powered, cross-platform, Unix-gazing shell. Write and mix sh/Python code in Xonsh (pronounced conch). More information: <https://xon.sh/contents.html>.
xo: A pluggable, zero-configuration linting utility for JavaScript. More information: <https://github.com/xojs/xo#usage>.
xmlto: Apply an XSL stylesheet to an XML document. More information: <https://manned.org/xmlto>.
xmlstarlet: An XML/XSLT toolkit. Note: You will likely need to know XPath: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/XPath>. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/docs.php>.
xmllint: XML parser and linter that supports XPath, a syntax for navigating XML trees. More information: <https://manned.org/xmllint>.
xml: XMLStarlet Toolkit: query, edit, check, convert, and transform XML documents. Some subcommands such as `validate` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139670224>.
xml-xmln: This command is an alias of `xml pyx`.
xml-unescape: Unescape special XML characters, e.g. `<a1>` → `<a1>`. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139540960>.
xml-transform: Transform XML documents using XSLT. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139602800>.
xml-select: Select from XML documents using XPATHs. Tip: use `xml elements` to display the XPATHs of an XML document. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139652416>.
xml-pyx: Convert an XML document to PYX (ESIS - ISO 8879) format. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139550832>.
xml-p2x: This command is an alias of `xml depyx`.
xml-list: List a directory's contents (like `ls`) in XML format. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139535968>.
xml-format: Format an XML document. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139569312>.
xml-escape: Escape special XML characters, e.g. `<a1>` → `<a1>`. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139540960>.
xml-elements: Extract elements and display the structure of an XML document. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139665568>.
xml-edit: Edit an XML document. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139594320>.
xml-depyx: Convert a PYX (ESIS - ISO 8879) document to XML format. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139550832>.
xml-canonic: Make XML documents canonical. More information: <https://xmlstar.sourceforge.net/doc/UG/xmlstarlet-ug.html#idm47077139560880>.
xml-c14n: This command is an alias of `xml canonic`.
xmake: A cross-platform C & C++ build utility based on Lua. More information: <https://github.com/xmake-io/xmake#command-line-interface-reference>.
xlsclients: List client applications running on an X11 display. More information: <https://manned.org/xlsclients>.
xkill: Kill a window interactively in a graphical session. See also: `kill`, `killall`. More information: <https://www.x.org/releases/current/doc/man/man1/xkill.1.xhtml>.
xkcdpass: A flexible and scriptable password generator which generates strong passphrases. Inspired by XKCD 936. More information: <https://github.com/redacted/XKCD-password-generator>.
xkbcli: Interact with X Keyboard keymaps. More information: <https://manned.org/xkbcli>.
ximtoppm: Convert a XIM file to a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/ximtoppm.html>.
xidel: Download and extract data from HTML/XML pages as well as JSON APIs. More information: <https://www.videlibri.de/xidel.html#examples>.
xh: Friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests. Note: `xh`, written in rust, serves as an effective drop-in replacement for `http`. See also: `http`, `curl`. More information: <https://github.com/ducaale/xh#usage>.
xgettext: Extract gettext strings from code files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#xgettext-Invocation>.
xev: Print contents of X events. More information: <https://manned.org/xev>.
xetex: Compile a PDF document from XeTeX source files. More information: <https://www.tug.org/xetex/>.
xephyr: A nested X server that runs as an X application. More information: <https://manned.org/xserver-xephyr>.
xe: Execute a command once for each line piped from another command or file. More information: <https://github.com/leahneukirchen/xe/blob/master/README>.
xdelta3: A delta compression tool for binary files. More information: <https://github.com/jmacd/xdelta/blob/wiki/CommandLineSyntax.md>.
xdelta: A delta encoding utility to generate and apply patches to binary files. For the modern version (v3), see `xdelta3`. More information: <https://manned.org/xdelta>.
xcv: Cut, copy, and paste in the command-line. More information: <https://github.com/busterc/xcv#xcv>.
xcaddy: The custom build tool for the Caddy Web Server. More information: <https://github.com/caddyserver/xcaddy#command-usage>.
xbmtopbm: Convert an X11 or X10 bitmap to a PBM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/xbmtopbm.html>.
xargs: Execute a command with piped arguments coming from another command, a file, etc. The input is treated as a single block of text and split into separate pieces on spaces, tabs, newlines, and end-of-file. See also: `parallel`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/findutils/manual/find.html#xargs-options>.
x_x: View Excel and CSV files. More information: <https://github.com/kristianperkins/x_x>.
x8: A hidden parameters discovery suite for identifying vulnerable or interesting web parameters. More information: <https://github.com/Sh1Yo/x8/blob/main/docs.md>.
x11docker: Securely run GUI applications and desktop UIs in Docker containers. See also: `xephyr`. More information: <https://github.com/mviereck/x11docker#terminal-syntax>.
x: Manage modules and packages. More information: <https://x-cmd.com>.
x-tping: Ping a host via TCP to check reachability. More information: <https://x-cmd.com/mod/tping>.
x-ping: Enhanced modules for ping. More information: <https://x-cmd.com/mod/ping>.
wuzz: Interactively inspect HTTP requests and responses. More information: <https://github.com/asciimoo/wuzz#commands>.
write: Write a message on the terminal of a specified logged in user (`<Ctrl c>` to stop writing messages). Use the `who` command to find out all terminal_ids of all active users active on the system. See also: `mesg`. More information: <https://manned.org/write>.
wpm: Typeracer-like console app for measuring your WPM. More information: <https://github.com/cslarsen/wpm>.
wpaclean: Clean capture files to get only the 4-way handshake and a beacon. Part of Aircrack-ng network software suite. More information: <https://manned.org/wpaclean>.
wpa_supplicant: Manage protected wireless networks. More information: <https://manned.org/wpa_supplicant.1>.
wp: The official interface to manage WordPress instances. More information: <https://developer.wordpress.org/cli/commands/>.
wormhole: Get things from one computer to another, safely. More information: <https://magic-wormhole.readthedocs.io/en/latest/welcome.html#cli-tool>.
woodpecker-cli: Manage, configure, and inspect Woodpecker CI servers, and run workflows locally. More information: <https://woodpecker-ci.org/docs/cli>.
wondershaper: Allow the user to limit the bandwidth of network adapters. More information: <https://github.com/magnific0/wondershaper#usage>.
wn: Look up related words in a WordNet database. More information: <https://wordnet.princeton.edu/documentation/wn1wn>.
wlsunset: Adjust the color temperature in Wayland compositors depending on the sunset/sunrise times. More information: <https://manned.org/wlsunset>.
wlc: Manage localization projects on a Weblate instance. More information: <https://docs.weblate.org/en/latest/wlc.html#commands>.
wkhtmltopdf: Convert HTML documents or web pages into PDF files. More information: <https://wkhtmltopdf.org/usage/wkhtmltopdf.txt>.
witr: Inspect processes, services, and ports by tracing their origin. More information: <https://github.com/pranshuparmar/witr>.
wishlist: SSH directory and multiplexer. Acts as a single entry point for connecting to SSH servers or Wish applications. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/wishlist>.
wipeclean: Clear the terminal screen using an animated wiper. More information: <https://github.com/JeanJouliaCode/wipeClean#usage>.
winicontoppm: This command has been superseded by `winicontopam`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/winicontoppm.html>.
winicontopam: Convert a Windows ICO file to a PAM file. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/winicontopam.html>.
wikit: Easily get Wikipedia summaries. More information: <https://github.com/KorySchneider/wikit#usage>.
wikiman: Offline search engine for documentation. Supports manual pages, Arch Wiki, Gentoo Wiki, FreeBSD documentation, and tldr-pages. More information: <https://github.com/filiparag/wikiman#usage>.
wiggle: A patch application tool resolving conflicts in patches that `patch` cannot handle. Note: Wiggle forcefully applies all changes, merging when conflicts arise, and reporting unresolvable issues. More information: <https://manned.org/wiggle>.
whois: Client for the WHOIS (RFC 3912) protocol. More information: <https://manned.org/whois>.
whoami: This command is an alias of `id --user --name`.
who: Display who is logged in and related data (processes, boot time). See also: `users`, `w`, `whoami`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/who-invocation.html>.
whisper: Convert audio files to `txt`, `vtt`, `srt`, `tsv`, and `json`. More information: <https://github.com/openai/whisper>.
while: Simple shell loop that repeats while the return value remains zero. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-while>.
which: Locate a program in the user's `$PATH`. See also: `whereis`, `type`. More information: <https://manned.org/which>.
where: Report all known instances of a command. It could be an executable in the `$PATH` environment variable, an alias, or a shell builtin. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Shell-Builtin-Commands.html>.
whence: A Zsh builtin to indicate how a command would be interpreted. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Shell-Builtin-Commands.html#index-whence>.
whatwaf: Detect and bypass web application firewalls and protection systems. More information: <https://github.com/Ekultek/WhatWaf#basic-help-menu>.
wget2: An improved version of `wget` for downloading files from the web. Supports HTTP, HTTPS, and HTTP/2 protocols with enhanced performance. By default, `wget2` uses multiple threads for faster downloads. More information: <https://manned.org/wget2>.
wget: Download files from the Web. Supports HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP. See also: `wcurl`, `curl`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/wget/manual/wget.html>.
wg: Manage the configuration of WireGuard interfaces. More information: <https://www.wireguard.com/quickstart/>.
wg-quick: Quickly set up WireGuard tunnels based on config files. More information: <https://manned.org/wg-quick>.
wfuzz: A web application bruteforcer. More information: <https://wfuzz.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/basicusage.html>.
wezterm: Wez's Terminal Emulator - a powerful cross-platform terminal emulator and multiplexer. Some subcommands such as `cli` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://wezterm.org/cli/general>.
wezterm-cli: Interact with a running Wezterm GUI or multiplexer. More information: <https://wezterm.org/cli/cli/index.html>.
weechat: Internet relay chat client with various features. More information: <https://weechat.org/doc/>.
webtorrent: The interface for WebTorrent. Supports magnets, URLs, info hashes, and `.torrent` files. More information: <https://github.com/webtorrent/webtorrent-cli>.
webstorm: The JetBrains JavaScript IDE. More information: <https://www.jetbrains.com/help/webstorm/working-with-the-ide-features-from-command-line.html>.
webpack: Bundle a web project's js files and other assets into a single output file. More information: <https://webpack.js.org/api/cli/>.
web-ext: Manage web extension development. More information: <https://github.com/mozilla/web-ext>.
weasyprint: Render HTML to PDF or PNG. More information: <https://doc.courtbouillon.org/weasyprint/stable/api_reference.html#command-line-api>.
wdiff: Display word differences between text files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/wdiff/manual/wdiff.html#wdiff-invocation>.
wcurl: A simple wrapper around `curl` to easily download files. See also: `wget`, `curl`. More information: <https://curl.se/wcurl/manual.html>.
wc: Count lines, words, and bytes. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/wc-invocation.html>.
wbmptopbm: Convert a wireless bitmap file to a PBM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/wbmptopbm.html>.
waymore: Fetch URLs of a domain from Wayback Machine, Common Crawl, Alien Vault OTX, URLScan, and VirusTotal. Note: Unless specified, output is dumped into the `results/` directory where waymore's `config.yml` resides (by default in `~/.config/waymore/`). More information: <https://github.com/xnl-h4ck3r/waymore>.
wayland-info: Display information about a Wayland compositor and available protocols. More information: <https://manned.org/wayland-info>.
waybar: Highly customizable Wayland bar for Sway and Wlroots based compositors. More information: <https://github.com/Alexays/Waybar>.
watson: A wonderful CLI to track your time. More information: <https://github.com/jazzband/Watson/blob/master/docs/user-guide/commands.md>.
watchman: A service that watches files, and triggers actions when changes occur. More information: <https://facebook.github.io/watchman/docs/cli-options>.
watchexec: Run arbitrary commands when files change. See also: `entr`. More information: <https://manned.org/watchexec>.
watch: Execute a program periodically and monitor the output in full-screen mode. More information: <https://manned.org/watch>.
wat2wasm: Convert a file from the WebAssembly text format to the binary format. More information: <https://webassembly.github.io/wabt/doc/wat2wasm.1.html>.
wasm2wat: Convert a file from the WebAssembly binary format to the text format. More information: <https://webassembly.github.io/wabt/doc/wasm2wat.1.html>.
wasm2c: Convert a file from the WebAssembly binary format to a C source file and header. More information: <https://webassembly.github.io/wabt/doc/wasm2c.1.html>.
wasm-opt: Optimize WebAssembly binary files. More information: <https://manned.org/wasm-opt>.
wasm-objdump: Display information from WebAssembly binaries. More information: <https://webassembly.github.io/wabt/doc/wasm-objdump.1.html>.
warp-diag: Diagnostic and feedback tool for Cloudflare's WARP service. See also: `warp-cli`. More information: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/>.
warp-cli: Connect, disconnect, and switch modes of a connection to Cloudflare's WARP service. WARP is a VPN that encrypts traffic for privacy, security, and speed. See also: `fastd`, `ivpn`, `mozillavpn`, `mullvad`. More information: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/>.
wapm: The WebAssembly package manager. More information: <https://wasmer.io/help/reference>.
wal: Create color schemes based on the dominant colors of a wallpaper. More information: <https://github.com/dylanaraps/pywal/wiki/Getting-Started>.
wakeonlan: Send packets to wake-on-LAN (WOL) enabled PCs. More information: <https://manned.org/wakeonlan>.
waitress-serve: Pure Python WSGI HTTP Server. More information: <https://docs.pylonsproject.org/projects/waitress/en/latest/runner.html>.
wait4x: Wait for a port or service to enter a requested state, with support for TCP, HTTP, DNS, databases, and message queues. Some subcommands such as `tcp` and `http` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/wait4x/wait4x>.
wait4x-tcp: Wait for TCP port(s) to become available. More information: <https://github.com/wait4x/wait4x>.
wait4x-http: Wait for an HTTP(S) endpoint to become available with flexible validation options. More information: <https://github.com/wait4x/wait4x>.
wait: Wait for a process to complete before proceeding. See also: `ps`, `waitpid`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-wait>.
waifu2x-ncnn-vulkan: Image upscaler for manga/anime-style images using NCNN neural network framework. More information: <https://github.com/nihui/waifu2x-ncnn-vulkan>.
wafw00f: Identify and fingerprint Web Application Firewall (WAF) products protecting a website. More information: <https://github.com/EnableSecurity/wafw00f/wiki/Usage#arguments-list>.
wacli: WhatsApp command-line client for sending messages, managing chats, and contacts. Some subcommands such as `auth`, `sync`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://wacli.sh/>.
wacli-sync: Synchronize WhatsApp messages to the local store. See also: `wacli auth`, `wacli messages list`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/sync.html>.
wacli-send-text: Send a text message via WhatsApp. See also: `wacli send file`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/send.html>.
wacli-send-file: Send a file (image, video, audio, or document) via WhatsApp. See also: `wacli send text`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/send.html>.
wacli-messages-show: Display a specific WhatsApp message by its ID. See also: `wacli messages list`, `wacli messages context`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/messages.html>.
wacli-messages-search: Search WhatsApp messages using full-text search. See also: `wacli messages list`, `wacli messages show`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/messages.html>.
wacli-messages-list: List messages from a WhatsApp chat. See also: `wacli messages search`, `wacli messages show`, `wacli messages context`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/messages.html>.
wacli-messages-context: Display messages surrounding a specific WhatsApp message. See also: `wacli messages show`, `wacli messages list`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/messages.html>.
wacli-contacts-tags-add: Add a tag to a WhatsApp contact. See also: `wacli contacts show`, `wacli contacts search`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/contacts.html>.
wacli-contacts-show: Display details of a specific WhatsApp contact. See also: `wacli contacts search`, `wacli contacts refresh`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/contacts.html>.
wacli-contacts-search: Search WhatsApp contacts by name. See also: `wacli contacts show`, `wacli contacts refresh`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/contacts.html>.
wacli-contacts-refresh: Synchronize contacts from the WhatsApp store. See also: `wacli contacts search`, `wacli contacts show`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/contacts.html>.
wacli-contacts-alias-set: Set a custom alias for a WhatsApp contact. See also: `wacli contacts show`, `wacli contacts search`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/contacts.html>.
wacli-auth: Authenticate wacli with WhatsApp via QR code. See also: `wacli sync`. More information: <https://wacli.sh/auth.html>.
w3m: A text-based web browser. Supports SSL and mouse input, even over SSH. More information: <https://w3m.sourceforge.net/MANUAL>.
w: Display who is logged in and their processes. See also: `who`, `users`. More information: <https://manned.org/w>.
vulkaninfo: Print system Vulkan information. More information: <https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/latest/linux/vulkaninfo.html>.
vue: Multi-purpose CLI for Vue.js. Some subcommands such as `build` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://cli.vuejs.org/guide/>.
vue-serve: A subcommand provided by `@vue/cli` and `@vue/cli-service-global` that enables quick prototyping. More information: <https://cli.vuejs.org/guide/cli-service.html#vue-cli-service-serve>.
vue-init: Legacy project initialization subcommand of the Vue.js framework. More information: <https://cli.vuejs.org/guide/creating-a-project.html#pulling-2-x-templates-legacy>.
vue-build: A subcommand provided by `@vue/cli` and `@vue/cli-service-global` that enables quick prototyping. More information: <https://cli.vuejs.org/guide/cli-service.html#vue-cli-service-serve>.
vt: Interface for VirusTotal. API key from a VirusTotal account is required for this command. More information: <https://github.com/VirusTotal/vt-cli>.
vsce: Extension manager for Visual Studio Code. More information: <https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-vsce>.
vp: Unified toolchain for web development. Some subcommands such as `env` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://viteplus.dev/guide/#quick-start>.
vp-env: Manage Node.js and package manager runtime environments for Vite+. More information: <https://viteplus.dev/guide/env>.
volta: A JavaScript Tool Manager that installs Node.js runtimes, npm and Yarn package managers, or any binaries from npm. More information: <https://docs.volta.sh/reference/>.
vmtouch: Manage the filesystem cache. More information: <https://manned.org/vmtouch>.
vllm: Serve large language models efficiently and interact with them through an OpenAI-compatible API. More information: <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/quickstart.html>.
vllm-chat: Generate chat completions via the running API server using the OpenAI-compatible REST API. More information: <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/serving/openai_compatible_server.html>.
vlc: Cross-platform multimedia player. See also: `mpv`, `mplayer`, `ytfzf`. More information: <https://wiki.videolan.org/Documentation:Command_line/>.
vladimyr: Dario Vladović's personal CLI. More information: <https://github.com/vladimyr/vladimyr-cli>.
vkcube: Test Vulkan rendering. See also: `glxgears`. More information: <https://github.com/krh/vkcube>.
vivaldi: This command is an alias of `chromium`. More information: <https://vivaldi.com/>.
viu: View images on the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/atanunq/viu#command-line-options>.
vitest: Fast, modern testing framework built for Vite, offering seamless integration, TypeScript support, and a Jest-compatible API for unit, integration, and snapshot testing. More information: <https://vitest.dev/guide/cli.html>.
vite: Create a Vite project. Used to build JavaScript projects. Available templates: vanilla, vanilla-ts, vue, vue-ts, react, react-ts, react-swc, react-swc-ts, preact, preact-ts, lit, lit-ts, svelte, svelte-ts. More information: <https://vite.dev/guide/>.
visudo: Safely edit the sudoers file. More information: <https://www.sudo.ws/docs/man/visudo.man/>.
virtualenvwrapper: Group of simple wrapper commands for Python's `virtualenv` tool. More information: <https://virtualenvwrapper.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_ref.html>.
virtualenv: Create virtual isolated Python environments. More information: <https://virtualenv.pypa.io/en/latest/reference/cli.html>.
virt-viewer: Minimal graphical interface for a virtual machine (VM). Note: `domain` refers to the name, UUID, or ID for the existing VMs. See also: `virsh`. More information: <https://manned.org/virt-viewer>.
virsh: Manage `virsh` guest domains. Note: Some of the commands below may require specifying `virsh --connect URI` explicitly. Some subcommands such as `list` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://libvirt.org/manpages/virsh.html>.
virsh-undefine: Delete a virtual machine. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-undefine: Delete the configuration file in `/etc/libvirt/storage` for a stopped virtual machine storage pool. See also: `virsh pool-destroy`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-start: Start a previously configured but inactive virtual machine storage pool. See also: `virsh pool-define-as`, `virsh pool-destroy`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-list: List information about virtual machine storage pools. See also: `virsh pool-autostart`, `virsh pool-define-as`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-info: List information about a virtual machine storage pool. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-destroy: Stop an active virtual machine storage pool. See also: `virsh pool-delete`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-delete: Delete the underlying storage system of an inactive virtual machine storage pool. See also: `virsh pool-destroy`, `virsh pool-undefine`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-define-as: Create a configuration file in `/etc/libvirt/storage` for a persistent virtual machine storage pool from the provided arguments. See also: `virsh pool-build`, `virsh pool-start`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-build: Build the underlying storage system for a virtual machine storage pool as defined in its configuration file in `/etc/libvirt/storage`. See also: `virsh pool-define-as`, `virsh pool-start`. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-pool-autostart: Enable or disable autostart for a virtual machine storage pool. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-list: List the ID, name, and state of virtual machines. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-help: Display information about `virsh` commands or command groups. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-dumpxml: Print virtual machine XML. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-domblklist: List information about block devices associated with a virtual machine. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-domblkinfo: Print block device size info. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
virsh-connect: Connect to a virtual machine hypervisor. More information: <https://manned.org/virsh>.
vipe: Run a text editor in the middle of a UNIX pipeline. More information: <https://manned.org/vipe>.
vinmap: A multithreaded Nmap scanner that splits IP ranges into chunks, performs parallel scans, and merges XML or JSON results. More information: <https://pypi.org/project/vinmap>.
vimtutor: Vim tutor, teaching the basic vim commands. See also: `vim`, `vimdiff`, `nvim`. More information: <https://manned.org/vimtutor>.
vimdiff: Open up two or more files in vim and show the differences between them. See also: `vim`, `vimtutor`, `nvim`. More information: <https://www.vim.org/>.
vim: Vim (Vi IMproved), a command-line text editor, provides several modes for different kinds of text manipulation. Pressing `<i>` in normal mode enters insert mode. Pressing `<Esc>` goes back to normal mode, which enables the use of Vim commands. See also: `vimdiff`, `vimtutor`, `nvim`, `gvim`. More information: <https://www.vim.org/>.
vifm: VI File Manager is a TUI file manager. See also: `clifm`, `mc`, `caja`. More information: <https://github.com/vifm/vifm>.
view: A read-only version of `vim`. This command is an alias of `vim -R`. More information: <https://www.vim.org/>.
vidir: Edit directories in a text editor. More information: <https://manned.org/vidir>.
vibe: Natural language code assistant for the terminal, powered by MistralAI. Reads and edits files in your current directory to fulfill requests. More information: <https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe#usage>.
vi: This command is an alias of `vim`.
vhs: Generate terminal GIFs from a tape file. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs>.
vgrep: A user friendly pager for grep. See also: `ugrep`, `rg`. More information: <https://github.com/vrothberg/vgrep/blob/main/docs/vgrep.1.md>.
vgmstream_cli: Play a wide variety of audio formats used in video games and convert them into `wav`. More information: <https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream/blob/master/doc/USAGE.md>.
vf: VirtualFish is a fish shell tool for managing Python virtual environments. More information: <https://virtualfish.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>.
vet: Scan package manifests, directories, container images, or GitHub repositories to identify vulnerabilities, malicious packages, and enforce security policies using CEL expressions. More information: <https://safedep.github.io/vet/vet.html>.
vertical-bar: Pipe data between programs. More information: <https://gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Pipelines>.
verilator: Convert Verilog and SystemVerilog hardware description language (HDL) design into a C++ or SystemC model to be executed after compiling. More information: <https://veripool.org/guide/latest/>.
vercel: Deploy and manage your Vercel deployments. More information: <https://vercel.com/docs/cli>.
venv: Create lightweight virtual environments in Python. More information: <https://docs.python.org/library/venv.html>.
velero: Back up and migrate Kubernetes applications and their persistent volumes. More information: <https://velero.io/docs/main/>.
vela: Tools for the Vela pipeline. More information: <https://go-vela.github.io/docs/reference/cli>.
vegeta: A utility and a library for HTTP load testing. See also: `ab`. More information: <https://github.com/tsenart/vegeta#usage-manual>.
vectorize-pixelart: Convert PNG pixel art graphics to SVG/EPS vector images. More information: <https://github.com/und3f/vectorize-pixelart>.
vdir: This command is an alias of `ls -l --escape`.
vcsh: Version Control System for the home directory using Git repositories. See also: `chezmoi`, `stow`, `tuckr`, `homeshick`. More information: <https://manned.org/vcsh>.
vcpkg: Package manager for C/C++ libraries. Note: Packages are not installed in the system. To use them, you need to tell your build system (e.g. CMake) to use `vckg`. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/vcpkg/>.
vcluster: Create and manage lightweight virtual Kubernetes clusters in namespaces. More information: <https://www.vcluster.com/docs/vcluster>.
vc: This command is an alias of `vercel`.
vboxmanage: Interface with VirtualBox. Includes all the functionality of the GUI and more. Some subcommands such as `startvm` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-intro>.
vboxmanage-unregistervm: Unregister a virtual machine (VM). More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-unregistervm>.
vboxmanage-startvm: Start a virtual machine. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-startvm>.
vboxmanage-showvminfo: Show information about registered virtual machine. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-showvminfo>.
vboxmanage-registervm: Register a virtual machine (VM). More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-registervm>.
vboxmanage-movevm: Move a virtual machine (VM) to a new location on the host system. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-movevm>.
vboxmanage-modifyvm: Change settings for a virtual machine that is stopped. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-modifyvm>.
vboxmanage-list: List information about the Oracle VM VirtualBox software and associated service. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-list>.
vboxmanage-import: Import a previously exported virtual machine (VM). More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-import>.
vboxmanage-extpack: Manage extension packs for Oracle VirtualBox. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-extpack>.
vboxmanage-export: Export virtual machines to a virtual appliance (ISO) or a cloud service. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-export>.
vboxmanage-createvm: Create a new virtual machine. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-createvm>.
vboxmanage-controlvm: Change the state and the settings of a currently running virtual machine. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-controlvm>.
vboxmanage-cloud: VirtualBox command-line interface for managing cloud instances and images. More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-cloud>.
vboxmanage-clonevm: Create a clone of an existing virtual machine (VM). More information: <https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch08.html#vboxmanage-clonevm>.
vault: Interact with HashiCorp Vault. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands>.
var-dump-server: Symfony dump server. Collects data dumped by the Symfony VarDumper component. More information: <https://symfony.com/doc/current/components/var_dumper.html#the-dump-server>.
valkey-cli: Open a connection to a Valkey server. More information: <https://valkey.io/topics/cli/>.
valgrind: Wrapper for a set of expert tools for profiling, optimizing, and debugging programs. Commonly used tools include `memcheck`, `cachegrind`, `callgrind`, `massif`, `helgrind`, and `drd`. More information: <https://valgrind.org/docs/manual/manual-core.html#manual-core.options>.
vale: Extensible style checker that supports multiple markup formats, such as Markdown and AsciiDoc. More information: <https://vale.sh/docs/cli>.
valac: Vala code compiler. Tutorial: <https://wiki.gnome.org/Projects/Vala/Tutorial>. More information: <https://docs.vala.dev/tutorials/programming-language/main/07-00-tools/07-01-valac.html>.
vala: Vala code runner. Tutorial: <https://wiki.gnome.org/Projects/Vala/Tutorial>. More information: <https://docs.vala.dev/index.html>.
vainfo: Display information from VA API driver. More information: <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Hardware_video_acceleration#Verifying_VA-API>.
vagrant: Manage lightweight, reproducible, and portable development environments. Some subcommands such as `box`, `snapshot`, `halt`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli>.
vagrant-version: Display Vagrant version information. Note: Internet access is required for vagrant version to check the latest available version. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/version>.
vagrant-validate: Check the validity of a Vagrantfile. See also: `vagrant box`, `vagrant plugin`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/validate>.
vagrant-upload: Upload files and directories from the host to the guest machine. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/upload>.
vagrant-suspend: Save the state of the guest machine rather than fully shutting it down. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/suspend>.
vagrant-status: Display the state of machines in the current Vagrant environment. See also: `vagrant global-status`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/status>.
vagrant-ssh: SSH into a running Vagrant machine. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/ssh>.
vagrant-ssh-config: Display configuration to SSH into a Vagrant machine manually (instead of using `vagrant ssh`). More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/ssh_config>.
vagrant-snapshot: Manage snapshots of Vagrant machines. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/snapshot>.
vagrant-resume: Resume a Vagrant managed machine that was previously suspended. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/resume>.
vagrant-reload: Equivalent of running `halt` followed by `up`. A reload is usually required for changes in a Vagrantfile to take effect. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/reload>.
vagrant-port: List mappings between guest and host ports. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/port>.
vagrant-init: Initialize a Vagrant environment in the current directory by creating a `Vagrantfile`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/init>.
vagrant-halt: Shut down the running machine Vagrant is managing. See also: `vagrant box`, `vagrant plugin`, `vagrant validate`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/halt>.
vagrant-global-status: Display the state of all Vagrant machines on the system. The info is based on a cache, which may become stale and require pruning. See also: `vagrant status`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/global-status>.
vagrant-destroy: Stop a guest machine and destroy all its resources. Any boxes installed are kept intact. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/destroy>.
vagrant-box: Manage Vagrant boxes (virtual machine images). More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vagrant/docs/cli/box>.
vacuumdb: Garbage-collect and analyze a PostgreSQL database. More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-vacuumdb.html>.
v: A tool for managing V source code. More information: <https://docs.vlang.io/getting-started.html>.
uvx: This command is an alias of `uv tool run`.
uvicorn: Python ASGI HTTP Server, for asynchronous projects. More information: <https://www.uvicorn.org/settings/>.
uv: A fast Python package and project manager. Some subcommands such as `tool`, `python`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/>.
uv-version: Read or update a project's version. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-version>.
uv-venv: Create an isolated Python environment for installing packages. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-venv>.
uv-tree: Display project dependencies in a tree format. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-tree>.
uv-tool: Install and run commands provided by Python packages. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-tool>.
uv-sync: Update the project's environment to match the lockfile. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-sync>.
uv-self: Manage the `uv` executable itself. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-self>.
uv-run: Run a command or script in the project environment. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-run>.
uv-remove: Remove dependencies from the project's `pyproject.toml` file. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-remove>.
uv-python: Manage Python versions and installations. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-python>.
uv-publish: Upload distributions to an index. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-publish>.
uv-pip: Provide pip-like commands for installing, uninstalling, and managing packages. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-pip>.
uv-lock: Update the project's lockfile. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-lock>.
uv-init: Create a new Python project. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-init>.
uv-help: Display detailed documentation for `uv` commands. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-help>.
uv-export: Export the project's lockfile to an alternate format. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-export>.
uv-cache: Manage `uv`'s global cache directory. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-cache>.
uv-build: Build Python packages into source distributions and wheels. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-build>.
uv-add: Add package dependencies to the `pyproject.toml` file. Packages are specified according to <https://peps.python.org/pep-0508/>. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-add>.
uuencode: Encode binary files into ASCII for transport via mediums that only support simple ASCII encoding. More information: <https://manned.org/uuencode>.
uudecode: Decode files encoded by `uuencode`. More information: <https://manned.org/uudecode>.
usql: Universal CLI interface for SQL databases. More information: <https://github.com/xo/usql#using>.
usleep: Delay execution for a specific interval in microseconds. Note: This command is deprecated, use `nanosleep` instead. See also: `sleep`. More information: <https://manned.org/usleep.1>.
users: Display a list of logged in users. See also: `who`, `w`, `useradd`, `userdel`, `usermod`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/users-invocation.html>.
upx: Compress or decompress executables. More information: <https://github.com/upx/upx/blob/devel/doc/upx.pod>.
uptime: Tell how long the system has been running and other information. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/uptime-invocation.html>.
upt: Unified interface for managing packages across various operating systems, like Windows, many Linux distributions, macOS, FreeBSD, and even Haiku. It requires the native OS package manager to be installed. See also: `flatpak`, `brew`, `scoop`, `apt`, `dnf`. More information: <https://github.com/sigoden/upt>.
updog: A replacement for Python's SimpleHTTPServer. It allows uploading and downloading via HTTP/S, can set ad hoc SSL certificates, and use HTTP basic auth. More information: <https://github.com/sc0tfree/updog>.
unzstd: This command is an alias of `zstd --decompress`.
unzip: Extract files/directories from Zip archives. See also: `zip`. More information: <https://manned.org/unzip>.
unxz: This command is an alias of `xz --decompress`.
until: Simple shell loop that repeats until it receives zero as return value. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-until>.
unsetopt: Unset options for the Z shell (`zsh`). Note: Zsh options are case-insensitive and underscores are ignored. See also: `setopt`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Options.html>.
unset: Remove shell variables or functions. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-unset>.
unp: Extract any archive. Relevant extractors need to be installed, e.g. `unrar` for RAR. More information: <https://manned.org/unp>.
unlzma: This command is an alias of `xz --format lzma --decompress`.
unlink: Remove a link to a file from the filesystem. The file contents is lost if the link is the last one to the file. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/unlink-invocation.html>.
unity: A tool for installing and managing Unity Editors, projects, and modules. More information: <https://docs.unity.com/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference>.
units: Convert between two units of measure. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/units/manual/units.html>.
unison: Bidirectional file synchronization tool. More information: <https://github.com/bcpierce00/unison>.
uniq: Output the unique lines from an input or file. Since it does not detect repeated lines unless they are adjacent, we need to sort them first. See also: `sort`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/uniq-invocation.html>.
unimatrix: Simulate the Matrix look with Unicode characters. See also: `cmatrix`. More information: <https://github.com/will8211/unimatrix>.
unhash: Remove hashed executable locations. See also: `hash`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Shell-Builtin-Commands.html>.
unfunction: This command is an alias of `unhash -f`.
unflatten: Adjust directed graphs to improve the layout aspect ratio. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://www.graphviz.org/pdf/unflatten.1.pdf>.
unexpand: Convert spaces to tabs. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/unexpand-invocation.html>.
uncrustify: C, C++, C#, D, Java, and Pawn source code formatter. More information: <https://manned.org/uncrustify>.
unclutter: Hide the mouse cursor. More information: <https://manned.org/unclutter.1x>.
unar: Extract contents from archive files. More information: <https://manned.org/unar>.
uname: Print details about the current machine and the operating system running on it. See also: `lsb_release`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/uname-invocation.html>.
unalias: Remove aliases. See also: `alias`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-unalias>.
umount: Unlink a filesystem from its mount point, making it no longer accessible. A filesystem cannot be unmounted when it is busy. More information: <https://manned.org/umount.8>.
umask: Manage the read/write/execute permissions that are masked out (i.e. restricted) for newly created files by the user. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-umask>.
ulimit: Get and set resource limits for user processes. This is a shell builtin hence not shell-agnostic. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-ulimit>.
ugrep: Ultra fast search tool with query TUI. More information: <https://github.com/Genivia/ugrep#man-page>.
ug: This command is an alias of `ugrep --config --pretty --sort`.
ufraw-batch: Convert RAW files from cameras into standard image files. More information: <https://manned.org/ufraw-batch>.
u3d: A set of tools to interact with Unity. More information: <https://github.com/DragonBox/u3d>.
tzconfig: Manage and set your local timezone. It accepts no parameters. More information: <https://manned.org/tzconfig>.
typst: Compile a Typst file to PDF. Note: Specifying the output location is optional. More information: <https://manned.org/typst>.
typos: Find and correct spelling mistakes in source code. More information: <https://github.com/crate-ci/typos/blob/master/docs/reference.md>.
typeset: This command is an alias of `declare`.
typeorm: A JavaScript ORM that can run on Node.js, browser, Cordova, Ionic, React Native, NativeScript, and Electron platforms. More information: <https://typeorm.io/docs/advanced-topics/using-cli/#initialize-a-new-typeorm-project>.
typeinc: An `ncurses` based terminal typing speed test program, written in Python. Try out different difficulty levels and improve your typing speed. More information: <https://github.com/AnirudhG07/Typeinc>.
type: Display the type of command the shell will execute. Note: All examples are not POSIX compliant. See also: `whereis`, `which`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-type>.
tye: Develop, test, and deploy microservices and distributed applications easily. More information: <https://github.com/dotnet/tye>.
twurl: Curl-like command but tailored specifically for the Twitter API. More information: <https://github.com/twitter/twurl#getting-started>.
twurl-authorize: Authorize twurl with Twitter API credentials. More information: <https://github.com/twitter/twurl>.
twurl-accounts: Manage and list Twitter accounts authorized with twurl. More information: <https://github.com/twitter/twurl#changing-your-default-profile>.
twopi: Render an image of a `radial` network graph from a `graphviz` file. Layouts: `dot`, `neato`, `twopi`, `circo`, `fdp`, `sfdp`, `osage` & `patchwork`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/doc/info/command.html>.
twm: A window manager for the X Window system. More information: <https://manned.org/twm>.
twine: Utility for publishing Python packages on PyPI. More information: <https://twine.readthedocs.io/en/stable/#commands>.
tw: View and query tabular data files using Tabiew. More information: <https://github.com/shshemi/tabiew#usage>.
tv: `tv` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
tv.fzf: Cross-platform, fast, extensible fuzzy-finder tool. Works with "channels" (e.g., files, env, git repos) or from `stdin`. More information: <https://alexpasmantier.github.io/television/>.
turbo: High-performance build system for JavaScript and TypeScript codebases. See also: `nx`. More information: <https://turborepo.com/docs/reference>.
tuptime: Report historical and statistical real time of the system, preserving it between restarts. Like `uptime`, but extended with startups count, graceful and bad shutdowns, uptime/downtime percentages, and averages since first boot. More information: <https://github.com/rfmoz/tuptime>.
tuitube: A terminal-based video downloader. More information: <https://github.com/remorses/tuitube>.
tuir: A text user-interface (TUI) to view and interact with Reddit from your terminal. Navigate with the Vim keys. More information: <https://gitlab.com/ajak/tuir>.
tuckr: Dotfile manager written in Rust. See also: `chezmoi`, `vcsh`, `homeshick`, `stow`. More information: <https://github.com/RaphGL/Tuckr#usage>.
tuc: Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts. A more user-friendly and powerful version of `cut` with sensible defaults. More information: <https://github.com/riquito/tuc#help>.
ttyd: Share a terminal or any command over the web. More information: <https://github.com/tsl0922/ttyd#command-line-options>.
tty: Return the terminal name. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/tty-invocation.html>.
tty-clock: A customizable terminal-based digital clock. More information: <https://github.com/xorg62/tty-clock>.
tte: A terminal visual effects engine, application, and library. More information: <https://github.com/ChrisBuilds/terminaltexteffects>.
tt: A terminal based typing test. More information: <https://github.com/lemnos/tt>.
tsv-filter: Filter lines of a TSV file by running tests against individual fields. More information: <https://github.com/eBay/tsv-utils#tsv-filter>.
tspin: A log file highlighter based on the `less` pager and basically behaves like any pager. More information: <https://github.com/bensadeh/tailspin#usage>.
tsort: Perform a topological sort. A common use is to show the dependency order of nodes in a directed acyclic graph. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/tsort-invocation.html>.
tslint: A pluggable linting utility for TypeScript. More information: <https://palantir.github.io/tslint/>.
tset: Initialize or reset terminal state. More information: <https://manned.org/tset>.
ts: Add timestamps to every line from `stdin`. More information: <https://manned.org/ts>.
ts-node: Run TypeScript code directly, without any compiling. More information: <https://typestrong.org/ts-node/docs/options/>.
try-rs: Manage temporary project workspaces with an interactive TUI. More information: <https://try-rs.org/#usage>.
trunk.rs: Bundle and serve Rust WASM web applications. More information: <https://trunkrs.dev/commands/>.
trunk: `trunk` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
trunk.io: Run linters, formatters, and security analyzers on code. More information: <https://docs.trunk.io/code-quality/overview/getting-started/commands-reference>.
truncate: Shrink or extend the size of a file to the specified size. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/truncate-invocation.html>.
trufflehog: Find and verify credentials in files, Git repositories, S3 buckets, and Docker images. More information: <https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog#memo-usage>.
truffle: Develop smart contracts for running services on the Ethereum blockchain. More information: <https://archive.trufflesuite.com/docs/truffle/reference/truffle-commands/>.
true: Return a successful exit status code of 0. See also: `false`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-true>.
troff: Typesetting processor for the groff (GNU Troff) document formatting system. See also: `groff`. More information: <https://manned.org/troff>.
trivy: Scanner for vulnerabilities in container images, filesystems, and Git repositories, as well as for configuration issues. More information: <https://trivy.dev/docs/latest/guide/references/configuration/cli/trivy/>.
trip: A network diagnostic tool. Combines the functionality of `traceroute` and `ping`. Designed to assist with the analysis of networking issues. More information: <https://trippy.rs/reference/cli/>.
treemd: View markdown files with tree-based navigation and an interactive TUI. More information: <https://github.com/Epistates/treemd#usage>.
tree: Show the contents of the current directory as a tree. More information: <https://manned.org/tree>.
tred: Compute the transitive reduction of directed graphs. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://www.graphviz.org/pdf/tred.1.pdf>.
tre: Show the contents of the current directory as a tree. Respects the `.gitignore` settings by default. More information: <https://github.com/dduan/tre#everything-else>.
trdsql: Execute SQL on CSV, LTSV, JSON, YAML, and TBLN files. More information: <https://noborus.github.io/trdsql/>.
trawl: Print out network interface information to the console, much like `ifconfig`/`ipconfig`/`ip`/`ifdata`. More information: <https://github.com/robphoenix/trawl>.
travis: Interface with Travis CI. More information: <https://github.com/travis-ci/travis.rb#command-line-client>.
trash-cli: This command is an alias of `trash`.
trap: Execute a command upon an event. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-trap>.
transmission: A simple torrent client. Note: Transmission isn't a command, but a set of commands. More information: <https://transmissionbt.com/>.
transmission-show: Get information about a torrent file. See also: `transmission`. More information: <https://manned.org/transmission-show>.
transmission-remote: Remote control utility for `transmission-daemon` and `transmission`. More information: <https://manned.org/transmission-remote>.
transmission-edit: Modify announce URLs from torrent files. See also: `transmission`. More information: <https://manned.org/transmission-edit>.
transmission-daemon: Daemon controlled with `transmission-remote` or its web interface. See also: `transmission`. More information: <https://manned.org/transmission-daemon>.
transmission-create: Create BitTorrent `.torrent` files. See also: `transmission`. More information: <https://manned.org/transmission-create>.
transmission-cli: A lightweight, command-line BitTorrent client. Note: This command is deprecated, use `transmission-remote` instead. More information: <https://manned.org/transmission-cli>.
transfersh: An unofficial client for transfer.sh. More information: <https://github.com/AlpixTM/transfersh>.
transcrypt: Transparently encrypt files within a Git repository. More information: <https://github.com/elasticdog/transcrypt#command-line-options>.
transcode: Transcode video and audio codecs, and convert between media formats. More information: <https://manned.org/transcode>.
trans: Translate Shell, a command-line translator. More information: <https://github.com/soimort/translate-shell>.
trafilatura: A Python tool for web scraping and crawling that extracts main text, metadata, and comments from web pages. Designed for creating text corpora and extracting structured content. More information: <https://trafilatura.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage-cli.html#further-information>.
traefik: An HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer. More information: <https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/v3.4/operations/cli/>.
trackfetch: Download songs listed in a text file as tagged MP3, M4A, or Opus files, using Spotify metadata and YouTube audio. Requires `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg`, and the `$SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `$SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variables. More information: <https://github.com/ByteMe6/trackfetch#usage>.
traceroute: Print the route packets trace to network host. See also: `mtr`. More information: <https://manned.org/traceroute>.
tr: Translate characters: run replacements based on single characters and character sets. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/tr-invocation.html>.
tqdm: Show progress over time of a command. More information: <https://tqdm.github.io/docs/cli/>.
tput: View and modify terminal settings and capabilities. See also: `stty`. More information: <https://manned.org/tput>.
tpp: Command-Line based presentation tool. More information: <https://manned.org/tpp>.
tpm2: Run various tpm2-tools via a single unified executable. Some subcommands such as `pcrread`, `pcrreset`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/tpm2>.
tpm2-pcrreset: Reset one or more PCR banks. Note: On operating system's locality, only PCR 16 and 23 can be reset. More information: <https://manned.org/tpm2_pcrreset>.
tpm2-pcrread: Read the PCR values from a TPM. More information: <https://manned.org/tpm2_pcrread>.
tox: Automate Python testing across multiple Python versions. Use `tox.ini` to configure environments and test command. More information: <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox>.
touch: Create files and set access/modification times. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/touch-invocation.html>.
