topydo: A to-do list application that uses the todo.txt format. More information: <https://github.com/topydo/topydo>.
topgrade: Update all applications on the system. More information: <https://github.com/r-darwish/topgrade>.
tokei: Display statistics about code. More information: <https://github.com/XAMPPRocky/tokei#options>.
toipe: Yet another typing test, but crab flavored. A trusty terminal typing tester. More information: <https://github.com/Samyak2/toipe>.
tofu: Create and deploy infrastructure as code to cloud providers. Open-source fork of Terraform. More information: <https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/>.
tofu-plan: Generate and show OpenTofu execution plans. More information: <https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/plan/>.
tofu-output: Export structured data about your OpenTofu resources. More information: <https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/output/>.
tofu-fmt: Format configuration according to OpenTofu language style conventions. More information: <https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/fmt/>.
todoman: This command is an alias of `todo`.
todoist: Access <https://todoist.com> from the command-line. More information: <https://github.com/sachaos/todoist#usage>.
todo.sh: Simple and extensible shell script for managing your `todo.txt` file. More information: <https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli>.
todo: A simple, standards-based, cli todo manager. More information: <https://todoman.readthedocs.io/en/stable/man.html>.
tmuxinator: Create and manage tmux sessions easily. More information: <https://manned.org/tmuxinator>.
tmux: Terminal multiplexer. It allows multiple sessions with windows, panes, and more. See also: `zellij`, `screen`, `herdr`. More information: <https://github.com/tmux/tmux>.
tmsu: Simple tool for tagging files. More information: <https://tmsu.org/>.
tmpmail: A temporary email right from your terminal written in POSIX sh. More information: <https://github.com/sdushantha/tmpmail#usage>.
tlsx: Fast and configurable TLS grabber focused on TLS based data collection and analysis. More information: <https://github.com/projectdiscovery/tlsx#usage>.
tlmgr: Manage packages and configuration options of an existing TeX Live installation. Some subcommands such as `paper` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#NAME>.
tlmgr-update: Update TeX Live packages. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#update-option...-pkg>.
tlmgr-shell: Start an interactive shell of the native TeX Live manager. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#shell>.
tlmgr-search: Search for TeX Live packages using (Perl) `regex`. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#search>.
tlmgr-restore: Restore package backups created with `tlmgr backup`. The default backup directory is specified by the `backupdir` option, and can be obtained with `tlmgr option`. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#restore>.
tlmgr-repository: Manage repositories of a TeX Live installation. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#repository>.
tlmgr-remove: Uninstall TeX Live packages. By default, removed packages will be backed up to `./tlpkg/backups` under the TL installation directory. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#remove-option...-pkg>.
tlmgr-recreate-tlpdb: Recreate the TeX Live package database. This command has a lack of documentation and should be used with caution. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/tlmgr.html>.
tlmgr-platform: Manage TeX Live platforms. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#platform>.
tlmgr-pinning: The pinning action manages the pinning file. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#pinning>.
tlmgr-path: Add or remove symlinks for TeX Live executables, man pages, and info pages. This command has to be re-run for files added in the future. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#path>.
tlmgr-paper: Manage paper size options of a TeX Live installation. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#paper>.
tlmgr-option: TeX Live settings manager. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#option>.
tlmgr-key: Manage GPG keys used to verify TeX Live databases. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#key>.
tlmgr-install: Install TeX Live packages. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#install-option...-pkg>.
tlmgr-info: Show information about TeX Live packages. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#info>.
tlmgr-gui: Start a graphical user interface for `tlmgr`. `tlmgr gui` depends on the package `perl-tk`, which has to be installed manually. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#gui>.
tlmgr-generate: Remake configuration files from information stored locally. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#generate>.
tlmgr-dump-tlpdb: Dump the TeX Live package database. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#dump-tlpdb-option...---json>.
tlmgr-conf: Manage the TeX Live configuration. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#conf>.
tlmgr-check: Check the consistency of a TeX Live installation. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#check-option...-depends-executes-files-runfiles-texmfdbs-all>.
tlmgr-candidates: Get available candidate repositories from which a TeX Live package can be installed. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#candidates-pkg>.
tlmgr-backup: Manage backups of TeX Live packages. The default backup directory is specified by the `backupdir` option, and can be obtained with `tlmgr option`. More information: <https://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/tlmgr.html#backup>.
tlmgr-arch: This command is an alias of `tlmgr platform`.
tldrl: This command is an alias of `tldr-lint`.
tldr: Display simple help pages for command-line tools from the tldr-pages project. Note: The `--language` and `--list` options are not required by the client specification, but most clients implement them. See also: `cheatshh`, `cheat`, `navi`. More information: <https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/CLIENT-SPECIFICATION.md#command-line-interface>.
tldr-lint: Lint and format `tldr` pages. Note: `tldrl` can be used as an alias for `tldr-lint`. More information: <https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr-lint#usage>.
tip: Connect to a remote system or serial console. More information: <https://manned.org/tip>.
tio: Monitor and interact with serial ports. See also: `picocom`, `cu`, `minicom`. More information: <https://github.com/tio/tio#3-usage>.
timidity: Play and convert MIDI files. More information: <https://manned.org/timidity>.
timg: A terminal image and video viewer. More information: <https://github.com/hzeller/timg#synopsis>.
timew: A time tracking tool used to measure the duration of activities. More information: <https://timewarrior.net/docs/>.
timetrap: Simple time tracker written in Ruby. More information: <https://github.com/samg/timetrap>.
times: Print the cumulative CPU usage time of the current shell. First line is current shell CPU usage for User and System. Second is all child processes. See also: `time`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-times>.
timeout: Run a command with a time limit. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/timeout-invocation.html>.
time: Measure how long a command took to run. Note: `time` can either exist as a shell builtin, a standalone program, or both. See also: `times`. More information: <https://manned.org/time>.
tig: A configurable `ncurses`-based TUI for Git. See also: `gitui`, `git-gui`. More information: <https://jonas.github.io/tig/doc/manual.html>.
tifftopnm: Convert a TIFF image to a PNM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/tifftopnm.html>.
tidy: Clean up and pretty print HTML, XHTML, and XML files. Note: `tidy` cannot preserve original indentation. More information: <https://api.html-tidy.org/tidy/tidylib_api_next/group__options__cli.html#gad7a9fcaf7b2a712a82e625e84c042b28>.
tidy-viewer: A data pretty-printer with column styling for CSV, TSV, PSV, Parquet, and Arrow IPC files. Commonly aliased as `tv`. More information: <https://github.com/alexhallam/tv#help>.
ticketconverter.py: Convert Kerberos tickets between kirbi and ccache formats. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
thunderbird: Email client and RSS reader. More information: <https://manned.org/thunderbird>.
thinkjettopbm: Convert an HP ThinkJet printer commands file to a PBM file. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/thinkjettopbm.html>.
then: This shell keyword is used in combination with `if` and `elif` to separate branches and branch conditions.
theharvester: A tool designed to be used in the early stages of a penetration test. More information: <https://github.com/laramies/theHarvester>.
tgutil: Manage a Telegram account. See also: `tgcloud`, `tgsend`, `tginfo`. More information: <https://pypi.org/project/telegram-cloud/>.
tgsend: Manage a Telegram account. See also: `tgcloud`, `tginfo`, `tgutil`. More information: <https://pypi.org/project/telegram-cloud/>.
tgpt: Talk to an AI chatbot without the need for API keys. Available providers: `openai`, `opengpts`, `koboldai`, `phind`, `llama2`, `blackboxai`. More information: <https://github.com/aandrew-me/tgpt>.
tginfo: Manage a Telegram account. See also: `tgcloud`, `tgsend`, `tgutil`. More information: <https://pypi.org/project/telegram-cloud/>.
tgcloud: Manage a Telegram account. See also: `tgsend`, `tginfo`, `tgutil`. More information: <https://pypi.org/project/telegram-cloud/>.
tgatoppm: Convert a TrueVision Targa file to a Netpbm image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/tgatoppm.html>.
textql: Execute SQL against structured text like CSV or TSV files. More information: <https://github.com/dinedal/textql#usage>.
textmaker: SoftMaker Office's word processor application. More information: <https://help.softmaker.com/textmaker2026/en/index.html>.
texliveonfly: Download missing TeX Live packages while compiling `.tex` files. More information: <https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/texliveonfly>.
texdoc: Search for appropriate documentation for (La)TeX commands or packages. More information: <https://manned.org/texdoc>.
texcount: Count words in TeX documents omitting macros. Note: If the TeX document uses `\include` or `\input` and you want to count the included files, `texcount` must be run in the directory of the root TeX file. More information: <https://app.uio.no/ifi/texcount/howto.html>.
texconfig: Configure TeX Live or teTeX. Superseded in many cases by `tlmgr`. More information: <https://manned.org/texconfig>.
tex: Compile a DVI document from TeX source files. More information: <https://www.tug.org/begin.html>.
tex-fmt: Format LaTeX source code. More information: <https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt>.
testssl: Check SSL/TLS protocols and ciphers supported by a server. More information: <https://testssl.sh/doc/testssl.1.html>.
testparm: Check a Samba configuration file for internal correctness. More information: <https://manned.org/testparm>.
testdisk: Scan and repair disk partitions. See also: `photorec`, `fdisk`. More information: <https://manned.org/testdisk>.
test: Check file types and compare values. Returns 0 if the condition evaluates to true, 1 if it evaluates to false. See also: `[`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/test-invocation.html>.
tesseract: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) engine. More information: <https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract/blob/main/doc/tesseract.1.asc>.
terragrunt: Keep your Terraform CLI arguments DRY. More information: <https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/docs/reference/cli/>.
terraform: Create and deploy infrastructure as code to cloud providers. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands>.
terraform-workspace: Manage Terraform workspaces for multiple environments. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/workspace>.
terraform-validate: Validate the configuration files in a directory. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/validate>.
terraform-untaint: Remove the tainted status from a resource instance. See also: `terraform taint`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/untaint>.
terraform-taint: Mark a resource instance as not fully functional to force replacement on next apply. Note: This command is deprecated, use `terraform apply -replace` instead. See also: `terraform apply`, `terraform untaint`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/taint>.
terraform-show: Read and output a Terraform state or plan file in human-readable form. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show>.
terraform-query: Query remote infrastructure for resources matching criteria in `.tfquery.hcl` files. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/query>.
terraform-providers: Manage provider dependencies for Terraform configurations. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/providers>.
terraform-plan: Generate and show Terraform execution plans. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/plan>.
terraform-output: Export structured data about your Terraform resources. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/output>.
terraform-logout: Log out from a remote host. See also: `terraform login`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/logout>.
terraform-login: Log in to a remote host. See also: `terraform logout`. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/login>.
terraform-init: Initialize a new or existing Terraform working directory. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/init>.
terraform-import: Import existing infrastructure into Terraform state. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import>.
terraform-graph: Generate a visual representation of configuration or execution plan. The output is in DOT format and can be rendered using GraphViz. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/graph>.
terraform-get: Download and update modules referenced in the root module. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/get>.
terraform-fmt: Format configuration according to Terraform language style conventions. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/fmt>.
terraform-destroy: Destroy all objects managed by a Terraform configuration. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/destroy>.
terraform-console: Start an interactive console for evaluating Terraform expressions. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/console>.
terraform-apply: Create or update infrastructure according to Terraform configuration files. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/apply>.
terminalizer: Record the terminal, generate animated GIFs and a web player, and optionally upload to <https://terminalizer.com>. See also: `asciinema`. More information: <https://www.terminalizer.com/docs#getting-started>.
termdown: Countdown timer and stopwatch. More information: <https://github.com/trehn/termdown>.
telnet: Connect to a specified port of a host using the telnet protocol. More information: <https://manned.org/telnet>.
telegram-desktop: Instant messenger with open source clients, chats, and stickers. More information: <https://manned.org/telegram-desktop>.
tee: Read from `stdin` and write to `stdout` and files (or commands). More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/tee-invocation.html>.
tectonic: A modern, self-contained TeX/LaTeX engine. More information: <https://tectonic-typesetting.github.io/book/latest/>.
tea: Interact with Gitea servers. More information: <https://gitea.com/gitea/tea>.
tdf: A tui PDF viewer. More information: <https://github.com/itsjunetime/tdf>.
tcsh: C shell with file name completion and command-line editing. See also: `csh`. More information: <https://manned.org/tcsh>.
tcpreplay: Replay network traffic stored in a `pcap` file. More information: <https://tcpreplay.appneta.com/wiki/tcpreplay-man.html>.
tcpdump: Dump traffic on a network. More information: <https://www.tcpdump.org/manpages/tcpdump.1.html>.
tcc: A tiny C compiler that can run C source files as scripts and otherwise has command-line options similar to `gcc`. More information: <https://bellard.org/tcc/tcc-doc.html>.
tbl: Table preprocessor for the groff (GNU Troff) document formatting system. See also: `groff`, `troff`. More information: <https://manned.org/tbl>.
tb: Manage tasks and notes across multiple boards. More information: <https://github.com/klaudiosinani/taskbook#usage>.
tarsnap: Manipulate remote Tarsnap encrypted backups. Note: You don't need to specify the key file and the cache directory if you configure them in `/usr/local/etc/tarsnap.conf` or `~/.tarsnaprc`. See also: `tarsnap-keygen`. More information: <https://www.tarsnap.com/man-tarsnap.1.html>.
tarsnap-keygen: Generate a key file for use with Tarsnap, an online backup service. More information: <https://www.tarsnap.com/man-tarsnap-keygen.1.html>.
tar: Archiving utility. Often combined with a compression method, such as `gzip` or `bzip2`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/tar/manual/tar.html>.
talosctl: Interact with Talos Linux, a minimal and immutable Kubernetes distribution. See also: `kubectl`. More information: <https://docs.siderolabs.com/talos/latest/reference/cli>.
takeout: A Docker-based development-only dependency manager. More information: <https://github.com/tighten/takeout>.
tailscale: A private WireGuard network service. Some subcommands such as `up` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://tailscale.com/kb/1080/cli>.
tailscale-up: Connect the client to the Tailscale network. All options described here can be changed later using `tailscale set --option argument`. Use `--option=false` to disable options that don't require arguments. Note: Run `sudo tailscale set --operator $USER` to allow the current user to run these commands. More information: <https://tailscale.com/kb/1080/cli/#up>.
tailscale-ssh: SSH to a Tailscale machine (Linux Only). More information: <https://tailscale.com/kb/1193/tailscale-ssh>.
tailscale-set: Change the specified preferences. These options can also be changed during the initial setup. This command can set all options documented in the page for `tailscale up`. More information: <https://tailscale.com/kb/1080/cli#set>.
tailscale-serve: Share a local server, file, or directory with devices on your Tailscale network. See also: `tailscale funnel`. More information: <https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/tailscale-cli/serve>.
tailscale-funnel: Share a local server on the internet using Tailscale. More information: <https://tailscale.com/kb/1311/tailscale-funnel>.
tailscale-file: Send files across connected devices on a Tailscale network. It currently does not support sending files to devices owned by other users even on the same Tailscale network. More information: <https://tailscale.com/kb/1106/taildrop>.
tailcat: WireGuard-encrypted tunnels using Tailscale's data plane, like `netcat` but encrypted. In the examples below, an `addrblob` is the connection token (`tcom...`) printed by a running `tailcat` server, used by clients to reach it. More information: <https://github.com/tailscale/tailcat#usage>.
tail: Display the last part of a file. See also: `head`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/tail-invocation.html>.
tac: Display and concatenate files with lines in reversed order. See also: `cat`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/tac-invocation.html>.
tabula: Extract tables from PDF files. More information: <https://github.com/tabulapdf/tabula-java#commandline-usage-examples>.
sysbench: Benchmark a System's CPU, IO, and memory. More information: <https://github.com/akopytov/sysbench#usage>.
syncthing: Continuous bidirectional decentralized folder synchronization tool. More information: <https://docs.syncthing.net/users/syncthing.html>.
symfony: The console component for the Symfony framework. More information: <https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html>.
syft: Generate a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) from container images and filesystems. More information: <https://oss.anchore.com/docs/reference/syft/cli/>.
swipl: SWI-Prolog - A comprehensive free Prolog environment. More information: <https://www.swi-prolog.org/pldoc/man?section=cmdline>.
swig: Generate bindings between C/C++ code and various high level languages such as JavaScript, Python, C#, and more. It uses special `.i` or `.swg` files to generate the bindings (C/C++ with SWIG directives), then outputs a C/C++ file that contains all the wrapper code needed to build an extension module. More information: <https://www.swig.org/Doc4.4/SWIGDocumentation.html#SWIG_nn2>.
swift: Create, run, and build Swift projects. More information: <https://manned.org/swiftc>.
swc: JavaScript and TypeScript compiler written in Rust. More information: <https://swc.rs/docs/usage/cli>.
swaynag: Display a message in a bar on top of a screen. More information: <https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/swaynag/swaynag.1.scd>.
swaymsg: Send messages to a running instance of Sway using IPC. See <https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/sway/sway.5.scd> for available commands. More information: <https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/swaymsg/swaymsg.1.scd>.
swaylock: Screen locking utility for Wayland compositors. More information: <https://manned.org/swaylock>.
swayidle: Idle management daemon for Wayland. Note: The configuration options are documented in its man page. More information: <https://github.com/swaywm/swayidle/blob/master/swayidle.1.scd>.
swaybg: Wallpaper tool for Wayland compositors. Note: Sway starts `swaybg` automatically if a wallpaper is set in the config file. More information: <https://github.com/swaywm/swaybg/blob/master/swaybg.1.scd>.
sway: A tiling Wayland compositor. It uses the same config format as `i3`, with some Wayland-specific additions. More information: <https://github.com/swaywm/sway/wiki>.
swagger-codegen: Generate code and documentation for your REST api from an OpenAPI/swagger definition. More information: <https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-codegen>.
svn-changelist: Associate a changelist with a set of files. More information: <https://svnbook.red-bean.com/en/1.7/svn-book.html#svn.ref.svn.c.changelist>.
svgtopam: Convert an SVG file to Netpbm format. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/svgtopam.html>.
svgr: Transform SVGs into React components. More information: <https://react-svgr.com/docs/options/>.
svgo: SVG Optimizer: optimizing Scalable Vector Graphics files. Based in Node.js. It applies a series of transformation rules (plugins), which can be toggled individually. More information: <https://manned.org/svgo>.
svg2png: Render an SVG image to a PNG image using cairo. More information: <https://cairographics.org/>.
sv: Control a running runsv service. More information: <https://manned.org/sv>.
suspend: Suspend the execution of the current shell. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-suspend>.
surfraw: Query a variety of web search engines. Consists of a collection of elvi, each of which knows how to search a website. More information: <https://manned.org/surfraw>.
supervisord: Client/server system for controlling some processes on UNIX-like operating systems. Server part of supervisor; it is primarily managed via a configuration file. More information: <https://supervisord.org/running.html#running-supervisord>.
supervisorctl: Client/server system that allows its users to control a number of processes on UNIX-like operating systems. Command-line client piece of the supervisor which provides a shell-like interface. More information: <https://supervisord.org/running.html#running-supervisorctl>.
supabase: Develop, deploy, and manage Supabase projects locally and on the cloud. More information: <https://supabase.com/docs/reference/cli>.
sup: Manage an RSS feed in the current directory. See also: `lb`. More information: <https://github.com/LukeSmithxyz/lb>.
sunicontopnm: Convert a Sun icon into a Netpbm image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/sunicontopnm.html>.
sum: Compute checksums and the number of blocks for a file. A predecessor to the more modern `cksum`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/sum-invocation.html>.
sui: Interact with the Sui network. More information: <https://docs.sui.io/references/cli/cheatsheet>.
sui-move: Work with Move source code. More information: <https://docs.sui.io/references/cli/move>.
sui-client: Publish smart contracts, get object information, execute transactions, and more. More information: <https://docs.sui.io/references/cli/client>.
sui-client-ptb: Create, sign, and execute programmable transaction blocks. More information: <https://docs.sui.io/references/cli/ptb>.
sui-client-faucet: Interact with the Sui faucet. More information: <https://docs.sui.io/references/cli/client#request-a-sui-coin-from-faucet>.
sudoedit: This command is an alias of `sudo --edit`.
sudo: Execute a single command as the superuser or another user. See also: `pkexec`, `run0`, `doas`. More information: <https://www.sudo.ws/sudo.html>.
sublist3r: Fast subdomains enumeration tool for penetration testers. More information: <https://github.com/aboul3la/Sublist3r>.
subfinder: Discover valid subdomains for websites. Designed as a passive framework to be useful for bug bounties and safe for penetration testing. More information: <https://docs.projectdiscovery.io/opensource/subfinder/usage>.
stylua: An opinionated Lua code formatter. More information: <https://github.com/JohnnyMorganz/StyLua>.
stty: Set or get options for a terminal device interface. See also: `tput`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/stty-invocation.html>.
stripe: Interact with Stripe payment processor. Some subcommands such as `docs`, `listen`, and `logs` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.stripe.com/cli>.
stripe-logs: Tail and filter live Stripe API request logs. More information: <https://docs.stripe.com/cli/logs/tail>.
stripe-listen: Forward Stripe webhook events to a local server for testing. More information: <https://docs.stripe.com/cli/listen>.
stripe-docs: Browse <https://docs.stripe.com> from the terminal. More information: <https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs>.
strip-nondeterminism: Remove non-deterministic information (e.g. timestamps) from files. More information: <https://salsa.debian.org/reproducible-builds/strip-nondeterminism>.
strings: Find printable strings in an object file or binary. More information: <https://manned.org/strings>.
stressapptest: Userspace memory and IO test. More information: <https://manned.org/stressapptest>.
stress-ng: Load and stress a Linux system in various ways (CPU, memory, I/O, etc.). Useful for benchmarking, hardware validation, and stability testing. More information: <https://manned.org/stress-ng>.
streamlit: Framework for creating interactive, data-driven web apps in Python. More information: <https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/cli>.
streamlink: Extract streams from various services and pipes them into a video player of choice. More information: <https://streamlink.github.io/cli.html#command-line-usage>.
stow: Symlink manager. Often used to manage dotfiles. See also: `chezmoi`, `tuckr`, `vcsh`, `homeshick`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/stow/manual/stow.html#Invoking-Stow>.
stolonctl: CLI for Stolon, a cloud native PostgreSQL manager for PostgreSQL high availability. More information: <https://github.com/sorintlab/stolon/blob/master/doc/commands/stolonctl.md>.

secretsdump.py: Dump NTLM hashes, plaintext passwords, and domain credentials from remote Windows systems. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
secrethub: Keep secrets out of configuration files. More information: <https://github.com/secrethub/secrethub-cli>.
searchsploit: Search Exploit Database for exploits, shellcodes and/or papers. If known version numbers are used as search terms, exploits for both the exact version and others whose version range covers the one specified are shown. More information: <https://www.exploit-db.com/searchsploit>.
sdkmanager: Install packages for the Android SDK. More information: <https://developer.android.com/tools/sdkmanager>.
sdk: Manage parallel versions of multiple Software Development Kits. Supports Java, Groovy, Scala, Kotlin, Gradle, Maven, Vert.x, and many others. More information: <https://sdkman.io/usage/>.
sdiff: Compare the differences between and optionally merge 2 files. More information: <https://manned.org/sdiff>.
sdcv: StarDict, a dictionary client. Dictionaries are provided separately from the client. More information: <https://manned.org/sdcv>.
sd: Intuitive find and replace. More information: <https://manned.org/sd>.
screen: Hold a session open on a remote server. Manage multiple windows with a single SSH connection. See also: `tmux`, `zellij`, `herdr`. More information: <https://manned.org/screen>.
scrcpy: Display and control your Android device on a desktop. See also: `adb connect`. More information: <https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy>.
scp: Secure copy. Copy files between hosts using Secure Copy Protocol over SSH. More information: <https://man.openbsd.org/scp>.
scim: A curses based, vim-like spreadsheet calculator. Use `<h><j><k><l>` or `<ArrowKeys>` to navigate. More information: <https://github.com/andmarti1424/sc-im>.
scheme: MIT Scheme language interpreter and REPL (interactive shell). More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/mit-scheme/documentation/stable/mit-scheme-user.html#Command_002dLine-Options>.
scd: File manager focused on shell integration. More information: <https://github.com/cshuaimin/scd>.
sccmap: Extract strongly connected components of directed graphs. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://www.graphviz.org/pdf/sccmap.1.pdf>.
sccache: A fast C/C++/Rust compiler cache. Composed of a client and a server, both running on the machine. More information: <https://manned.org/sccache>.
scc: Count lines of code. Written in Go. More information: <https://github.com/boyter/scc#usage>.
scan-build: Run a static analyzer over a codebase as part of performing a regular build. More information: <https://clang-analyzer.llvm.org/scan-build.html>.
scamper: Actively probes the Internet in order to analyze topology and performance. Includes some tools that start with `sc_`, for example `sc_warts2text` or `sc_ttlexp`. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
scalafmt: Code formatter for Scala. Configurations are stored in the `.scalafmt.conf` file. More information: <https://scalameta.org/scalafmt/>.
scala: Scala application launcher and interactive interpreter. More information: <https://scala-cli.virtuslab.org/docs/reference/cli-options/>.
scala-cli: Interact with the Scala programming language. More information: <https://scala-cli.virtuslab.org/docs/overview/>.
sc_wartsfilter: Select specific records from a `.warts` file. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_wartsdump: Verbose dump of information contained in a `.warts` file. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_warts2text: Simple dump of information contained in a `.warts` file. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_warts2pcap: Write packets included in `.warts` files to a PCAP file. This is only possible for packets of type `tbit`, `sting`, or `sniff`. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_warts2json: JSON dump of information contained in a `.warts` file. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_warts2csv: Dump traceroutes collected by `scamper` in CSV format. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_ttlexp: Dump source addresses from ICMP TTL expired messages in `.warts` files. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_tracediff: Display traceroute paths where the path has changed. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sc_analysis_dump: Dump of traceroute data in an easily parsed format. More information: <https://www.caida.org/catalog/software/scamper/>.
sbx: Create and manage isolated microVM sandboxes for running AI coding agents. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/sbx/>.
sbuild: Build a Debian binary package in a clean `chroot` environment. More information: <https://wiki.debian.org/sbuild>.
sbt: Build tool for Scala and Java projects. More information: <https://www.scala-sbt.org/1.x/docs/>.
sbigtopgm: Convert an SBIG CCDOPS file to PGM. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/sbigtopgm.html>.
sbcl: High performance Common Lisp compiler. More information: <https://www.sbcl.org/manual/#Command-Line-Options>.
satis: The utility for the Satis static Composer repository. More information: <https://github.com/composer/satis>.
sass: Convert SCSS or Sass files to CSS. More information: <https://sass-lang.com/documentation/cli/dart-sass/>.
samtools: Tools for handling high-throughput sequencing (genomics) data. Used for reading/writing/editing/indexing/viewing of data in SAM/BAM/CRAM format. More information: <https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools.html>.
samply: Sample and record CPU profiles for analysis. More information: <https://github.com/mstange/samply>.
sambapipe.py: Exploit CVE-2017-7494 (SambaCry) to upload and load a shared object (SO) file on a vulnerable Samba server for remote code execution. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
sam2p: Raster (bitmap) image converter with smart PDF and PostScript (EPS) output. More information: <https://github.com/pts/sam2p>.
salt: Execute commands and assert state on remote salt minions. More information: <https://docs.saltproject.io/en/latest/ref/cli/index.html>.
salt-run: Frontend for executing salt-runners on minions. More information: <https://docs.saltproject.io/en/latest/ref/cli/salt-run.html>.
salt-key: Manage salt minion keys on the salt master. Needs to be run on the salt master, likely as root or with `sudo`. More information: <https://docs.saltproject.io/en/latest/ref/cli/salt-key.html>.
salt-call: Invoke salt locally on a salt minion. More information: <https://docs.saltproject.io/en/latest/ref/cli/salt-call.html>.
sails: A realtime enterprise level MVC framework built on top of Node.js. More information: <https://sailsjs.com/documentation/reference/command-line-interface>.
safe: Interact with HashiCorp Vault. More information: <https://github.com/egen/safe>.
s3cmd: Upload, retrieve, and manage data in S3 compatible object storage. More information: <https://s3tools.org/s3cmd>.
s: Web search from the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/zquestz/s#s>.
rvm: Easily installing, managing, and working with multiple ruby environments. More information: <https://rvm.io/rvm/cli>.
rustup: Install, manage, and update Rust toolchains. Some subcommands such as `toolchain`, `target`, `update`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-which: Display which binary will be run for a command managed by `rustup`. Like `which`, but searches a Rust toolchain instead of `$PATH`. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-update: Update Rust toolchains and `rustup` itself (if not installed using a package manager). More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-uninstall: This command is an alias of `rustup toolchain uninstall`.
rustup-toolchain: Manage Rust toolchains. See `rustup help toolchain` for more information about toolchains. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-target: Modify a toolchain's supported targets. Without the `--toolchain` option `rustup` will use the default toolchain. See `rustup help toolchain` for more information about toolchains. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-show: Show installed toolchains, targets, and the version of `rustc`. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-run: Run a command with an environment configured for a Rust toolchain. Note: All commands managed by `rustup` have a shorthand for this: for example, `cargo +nightly build` is equivalent to `rustup run nightly cargo build`. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-override: Modify directory toolchain overrides. See `rustup help toolchain` for more information about toolchains. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-man: View the man page for a command managed by `rustup`. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/examples.html>.
rustup-install: This command is an alias of `rustup toolchain install`.
rustup-init.sh: Script to install `rustup` and the Rust toolchain. More information: <https://forge.rust-lang.org/infra/other-installation-methods.html#rustup>.
rustup-help: Display help on `rustup` and its subcommands. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-doc: Open the offline Rust documentation for the current toolchain. There are a lot more documentation pages not mentioned here. See `rustup help doc` for more information. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-default: Set the default Rust toolchain. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-component: Modify a toolchain's installed components. Without the `--toolchain` option `rustup` will use the default toolchain. See `rustup help toolchain` for more information about toolchains. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-completions: Generate shell completions for `rustup` and `cargo`. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustup-check: Check for updates to Rust toolchains and `rustup`. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/>.
rustscan: Modern Port Scanner written in Rust. Note: `nmap` must be installed for some of the examples below to work. See also: `hping3`, `masscan`, `naabu`, `nmap`, `zmap`. More information: <https://github.com/bee-san/RustScan/wiki>.
rustic: Create fast, encrypted, deduplicated backups powered by Rust. More information: <https://github.com/rustic-rs/rustic>.
rustfmt: Format Rust source code. More information: <https://github.com/rust-lang/rustfmt>.
rustdoc: Generate documentation for a Rust crate. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustdoc/>.
rustc: The Rust compiler. Rust projects usually use `cargo` instead of invoking `rustc` directly. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/>.
runsvdir: Run an entire directory of services. More information: <https://manned.org/runsvdir>.
runsvchdir: Change the directory `runsvdir` uses by default. More information: <https://manned.org/runsvchdir>.
runsv: Start and manage a runit service. More information: <https://manned.org/runsv>.
run-help: Get instructions for Zsh commands. Note: This command is an alias of `man` by default. More information: <https://manned.org/zshcontrib>.
rumdl: A fast Markdown linter and formatter written in Rust. More information: <https://rumdl.dev/usage/cli>.
ruff: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust. See also: `black`. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/tutorial/>.
ruff-format: An extremely fast Python code formatter. If no files or directories are specified, the current working directory is used by default. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/>.
ruff-check: An extremely fast Python linter. `check` is the default command - it can be omitted everywhere. If no files or directories are specified, the current working directory is used by default. More information: <https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/>.
ruby: Ruby programming language interpreter. See also: `gem`, `bundler`, `rake`, `irb`, `ri`. More information: <https://manned.org/ruby>.
rtv: Reddit Terminal Viewer. Use `<ArrowKeys>` to navigate. `<ArrowRight>` and `<ArrowLeft>` to view and return from a submission, respectively. More information: <https://github.com/michael-lazar/rtv>.
rtmpdump: Dump media content streamed over the RTMP protocol. More information: <https://rtmpdump.mplayerhq.hu/rtmpdump.1.html>.
rtl_sdr: Raw data recorder for RTL-SDR receivers. Data is encoded using I/Q sampling (aka quadrature sampling). More information: <https://osmocom.org/projects/rtl-sdr/wiki/Rtl-sdr>.
rsync: Transfer files either to or from a remote host (but not between two remote hosts), by default using SSH. To specify a remote path, use `user@host:path/to/file_or_directory`. More information: <https://download.samba.org/pub/rsync/rsync.1>.
rsql: SQL client to interface with databases and other data sources inside the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/theseus-rs/rsql>.
rspec: Behavior-driven development testing framework written in Ruby to test Ruby code. More information: <https://rspec.info/features/3-13/rspec-core/command-line/>.
rscript: Run a script with the R programming language. More information: <https://manned.org/Rscript>.
rsactftool.py: RSA attack tool for CTF challenges - recover private keys from weak public keys and/or decrypt data. More information: <https://github.com/RsaCtfTool/RsaCtfTool#usage>.
rr: Debugging tool designed to record and replay program execution. More information: <https://github.com/rr-debugger/rr/wiki/Usage>.
rpk: Manage Redpanda topics, clusters, groups, security, and more via a single binary. More information: <https://docs.redpanda.com/current/reference/rpk/>.
rpi-imager: Flash images onto storage devices. More information: <https://github.com/raspberrypi/rpi-imager>.
rpcmap.py: Look up listening MSRPC interfaces using a string binding (e.g., `ncacn_ip_tcp:host[port]`). Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
rpcdump.py: Dump remote RPC endpoints information via the Endpoint Mapper. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
route: Show and manipulate the route table. More information: <https://manned.org/route>.
ropper: Find ROP gadgets in binary files. More information: <https://scoding.de/ropper/>.
ropgadget: Find ROP gadgets in binary files. More information: <https://github.com/JonathanSalwan/ROPgadget#usage>.
roll: Roll a user-defined dice sequence. More information: <https://manned.org/roll>.
roave-backward-compatibility-check: Verify backward compatibility breaks between two versions of a PHP library. More information: <https://github.com/Roave/BackwardCompatibilityCheck>.
rnano: This command is an alias of `nano --restricted`. More information: <https://manned.org/rnano>.
rmlint: Find space waste and other broken things on your filesystem. More information: <https://rmlint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rmlint.1.html>.
rmdir: Remove directories without files. See also: `rm`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/rmdir-invocation.html>.
rm: Remove files or directories. See also: `rmdir`, `trash`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/rm-invocation.html>.
rlwrap: Add line editing, persistent history, and prompt completion to a REPL command. More information: <https://manned.org/rlwrap>.
rlog: Print the revision log of RCS files. See also: `ci`, `co`, `rcs`, `rcsdiff`. More information: <https://manned.org/rlog>.
rletopnm: Convert a Utah Raster Tools RLE image file to a PNM file. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/rletopnm.html>.
rlatopam: Convert Alias/Wavefront RLA and RPF image files to Netpbm format. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/rlatopam.html>.
rkdeveloptool: Flash, dump, and manage boot firmware for Rockchip-based computer devices. You will need to turn on the device into Maskrom/Bootrom mode before connecting it through USB. Some subcommands may require to run as root. More information: <https://github.com/rockchip-linux/rkdeveloptool>.
rip: Remove files or directories by sending them to the graveyard, allowing for them to be recovered. More information: <https://github.com/nivekuil/rip#-usage>.
rich: A toolbox for fancy output in the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/Textualize/rich-cli>.
ri: Browse structured API documentation for Ruby. See also: `ruby`. More information: <https://ruby.github.io/rdoc/RI_md.html>.
rhash: Calculate or check common message digests. More information: <https://rhash.sourceforge.io/manpage.php>.
rgrep: This command is an alias of `grep --recursive`.
rgpt: An automated code review tool that uses GPT you can use straight from your terminal. More information: <https://github.com/vaibhav-venkat/review-gpt>.
rgb3toppm: Combine three PGM images into one PPM image. See also: `ppmtorgb3`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/rgb3toppm.html>.
rga: Ripgrep wrapper with rich file type searching capabilities. More information: <https://github.com/phiresky/ripgrep-all>.
rg: Ripgrep, a recursive line-oriented search tool. Aims to be a faster alternative to `grep`. More information: <https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/blob/master/GUIDE.md>.
rfetch: A configurable fetch program to output system information. More information: <https://github.com/kamui-fin/rfetch>.
reuse: Tool for compliance with the REUSE recommendations. More information: <https://reuse.readthedocs.io/en/stable/man/index.html>.
return: Exit a function. Can exit out of a script if run with `source`. See also: `exit`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-return>.
retry: Repeat command until it succeeds or a criterion is met. More information: <https://manned.org/retry>.
resume: Easily setup a new resume. More information: <https://github.com/jsonresume/resume-cli>.
resticprofile: Configuration profiles manager for restic backup. See also: `restic`. More information: <https://creativeprojects.github.io/resticprofile/configuration/getting_started/index.html#write-your-first-configuration-file>.
resticprofile-unschedule: The command removes jobs for schedules declared in the selected profile or group (or of all profiles and groups). See also: `restic`, `resticprofile schedule`. More information: <https://creativeprojects.github.io/resticprofile/schedules/configuration/index.html>.
resticprofile-schedule: Schedule backups and run them in the background. See also: `restic`, `resticprofile unschedule`. More information: <https://creativeprojects.github.io/resticprofile/schedules/configuration/index.html>.
restic: A fast and secure backup program. More information: <https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/manual_rest.html#usage-help>.
resolvconf: Manage nameserver information. Acts as an intermediary between programs that supply nameserver information and applications that use this information. This page documents Debian's implementation of `resolvconf`. More information: <https://manned.org/resolvconf>.
resend: Send and manage emails from the command-line. More information: <https://github.com/resend/resend-cli#commands>.
repren: Multi-pattern string replacement and file renaming tool. More information: <https://github.com/jlevy/repren>.
repomix: Pack a GitHub repository into an AI-friendly file. More information: <https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix>.
renice: Alter the scheduling priority/niceness of running processes. Niceness values range from -20 (most favorable to the process) to 19 (least favorable to the process). See also: `nice`. More information: <https://manned.org/renice>.
rename: `rename` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
remove-nodeversion: Uninstall Node.js runtime versions for `ps-nvm`. This command is part of `ps-nvm` and can only be run under PowerShell. More information: <https://github.com/aaronpowell/ps-nvm>.
rekor-cli: Immutable tamper resistant ledger of metadata generated within a software projects supply chain. More information: <https://github.com/sigstore/rekor>.
reindexdb: Rebuild indexes in a PostgreSQL database. More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-reindexdb.html>.
rehash: This command is an alias of `hash -r`.
regex: Regular expressions (`regex`) are patterns used to match, search, and manipulate text. Note: `regex` isn't a command, but syntax to be used with other commands. See also: `egrep`, `glob`. More information: <https://cheatography.com/davechild/cheat-sheets/regular-expressions/>.
regedit: Wine registry counterpart of the Microsoft Windows `regedit` service. More information: <https://manned.org/regedit>.
reg.py: Query, add, delete, save, or back up registry keys/values on a remote Windows machine over SMB/RPC. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
reflex: Watch a directory and rerun a command when certain files change. More information: <https://github.com/cespare/reflex#usage>.
reflac: Recompress FLAC files in-place while preserving metadata. More information: <https://github.com/chungy/reflac#running>.
redshift: Adjust the color temperature of a screen according to its surroundings. Note: Redshift does not support Wayland. See also: `gammastep`. More information: <https://manned.org/redshift>.
redis-cli: Open a connection to a Redis server. More information: <https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/>.
redis-benchmark: Benchmark a Redis server. More information: <https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/optimization/benchmarks/>.
rector: An automated tool for updating and refactoring PHP 5.3+ code. More information: <https://github.com/rectorphp/rector>.
recsel: Print records from a recfile: a human-editable, plain text database. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/recutils/manual/recutils.html#Invoking-recsel>.
recon-ng: Automated reconnaissance and information gathering tool. More information: <https://github.com/lanmaster53/recon-ng/wiki>.
realpath: Display the resolved absolute path for a file or directory. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/realpath-invocation.html>.
readonly: Set read-only shell variables. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-readonly>.
readlink: Follow symlinks and get symlink information. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/readlink-invocation.html>.
readarray: Read lines from `stdin` into an array. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-readarray>.
read: Shell builtin for retrieving data from `stdin`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-read>.
react-native: A framework for building native apps with React. More information: <https://github.com/react-native-community/cli/blob/main/docs/commands.md>.
react-native-start: Start the React Native server. More information: <https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/community-cli-plugin#start>.
rdp_check.py: Test whether an account is valid on the target host using the RDP protocol (no full login, just authentication check). Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
rdiff-backup: Local/remote mirror and incremental backup tool. More information: <https://rdiff-backup.net/rdiff-backup.1.html>.
rdfind: Find files with duplicate content and get rid of them. More information: <https://rdfind.pauldreik.se/rdfind.1.html>.
rcsmerge: Merge RCS revisions into the working file. See also: `ci`, `co`, `rcs`, `rcsdiff`, `rlog`. More information: <https://manned.org/rcsmerge>.
rcsdiff: Compare RCS revisions (show differences between revisions in RCS files). See also: `ci`, `co`, `rcs`, `rlog`. More information: <https://manned.org/rcsdiff>.
rcs: Revision Control System - manage RCS file attributes. See also: `ci`, `co`, `rcsdiff`, `rlog`. More information: <https://manned.org/rcs>.
rclone: Copy, synchronize, or move files and directories to and from many cloud services. More information: <https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/>.
rcat: This command is an alias of `rc`.
rc: A modern simplistic port listener & reverse shell. See also: `nc`. More information: <https://github.com/robiot/rustcat/wiki/Basic-Usage>.
rbw: Unofficial Bitwarden-compatible password manager. More information: <https://github.com/doy/rbw#configuration>.
rbt: RBTools, a set of tools for working with Review Board and RBCommons. More information: <https://www.reviewboard.org/docs/rbtools/dev/>.
rbenv: Easily install Ruby versions and manage application environments. See also: `asdf`. More information: <https://manned.org/rbenv>.
rbash: This command is an alias of `bash --restricted`.
rbac-lookup: Find roles and cluster roles attached to any user, service account, or group name in your Kubernetes cluster. More information: <https://github.com/FairwindsOps/rbac-lookup>.
rawtoppm: Convert a raw RGB stream to a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/rawtoppm.html>.
rawtopgm: Convert a raw greyscale image to a PGM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/rawtopgm.html>.
rasttopnm: Convert a Sun rasterfile to a PNM file. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/rasttopnm.html>.
rarcrack: Password cracker for RAR, Zip, and 7z archives. More information: <https://www.kali.org/tools/rarcrack/>.
rar: The RAR archiver. Supports multi-volume archives that can be optionally self-extracting. More information: <https://manned.org/rar>.
rapper: The Raptor RDF parsing utility. Part of the Raptor RDF Syntax Library. More information: <https://librdf.org/raptor/rapper.html>.
ranger: Console file manager with VI key bindings. See also: `clifm`, `vifm`, `mc`, `dolphin`. More information: <https://github.com/ranger/ranger/blob/master/doc/ranger.pod>.
raku: Rakudo Raku (formerly Perl 6) programming language interpreter. See also: `perl`. More information: <https://manned.org/raku>.
rake: A Make-like program for Ruby. Tasks for `rake` are specified in a Rakefile. More information: <https://ruby.github.io/rake/>.
rainbowstream: Interactive Twitter client supporting realtime tweetstream, trends, sending, search, favorites, and user management. Online help with `<h>`, `<ArrowUp>` and `<ArrowDown>` for history, `<Tab>` to auto-complete, and 2-`<Tab>` for suggestion. More information: <https://github.com/orakaro/rainbowstream>.
railway: Connect code to a Railway project. More information: <https://docs.railway.com/reference/cli-api>.
rails: A server-side MVC framework written in Ruby. Some subcommands such as `generate` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/command_line.html>.
rails-server: Serve the Rails app in the current directory using the Puma web server, which comes bundled with Rails. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/command_line.html#bin-rails-server>.
rails-routes: List routes in a Rails application. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/routing.html>.
rails-new: Create a new Rails application. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/command_line.html#rails-new>.
rails-generate: Generate new Rails templates in an existing project. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/command_line.html#bin-rails-generate>.
rails-db: Various database-related subcommands for Ruby on Rails. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_migrations.html>.
rails-console: Interact with a Rails application. More information: <https://guides.rubyonrails.org/command_line.html#bin-rails-console>.
rage: A simple, secure, and modern file encryption tool (and Rust library) with small explicit keys, no configuration options, and UNIX-style composability. Rust implementation of `age`. More information: <https://github.com/str4d/rage>.
radare2: A set of reverse engineering tools. More information: <https://book.rada.re/first_steps/commandline_flags.html>.
rabin2: Get information about binary files (ELF, PE, Java CLASS, Mach-O) - symbols, sections, linked libraries, etc. Comes bundled with `radare2`. More information: <https://manned.org/rabin2>.
rabbitmqctl: Manage, configure, and inspect RabbitMQ servers. More information: <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/man/rabbitmqctl.8>.
rabbitmqctl-vhosts: Manage virtual hosts (vhosts) in RabbitMQ. Vhosts are used to separate multiple logical brokers on the same RabbitMQ server. More information: <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/vhosts>.
rabbitmqctl-users: Manage RabbitMQ users, their permissions, and tags. More information: <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/management>.
rabbitmqctl-cluster: Manage RabbitMQ nodes in a cluster. More information: <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/man/rabbitmqctl.8>.
rabbitmq-upgrade: Manage the upgrade of a RabbitMQ node. More information: <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/man/rabbitmq-upgrade.8>.
rabbitmq-diagnostics: Diagnose, monitor, and run health checks on RabbitMQ nodes. Many subcommands are delegated to `rabbitmqctl`. More information: <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/man/rabbitmq-diagnostics.8>.
r2e: Forward RSS feeds to an email address. Requires a configured `sendmail` or SMTP setup. More information: <https://manned.org/r2e>.
r2: This command is an alias of `radare2`.
r.zsh: This command is an alias of `fc -e -`.
r: `r` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
qwen: Launch an interactive prompt with Qwen3-Coder. See also: `gemini`. More information: <https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code>.
qutebrowser: A keyboard-driven, vim-like browser based on PyQt5. More information: <https://qutebrowser.org/doc/qutebrowser.1.html>.
quota: Display users' disk space usage and allocated limits. More information: <https://manned.org/quota>.
quilt: Manage a series of patches. More information: <https://manned.org/quilt>.
quarto: An open-source scientific and technical publishing system built on Pandoc. More information: <https://quarto.org/docs/reference/projects/options.html>.
quarkus: Create Quarkus projects, manage extensions, and perform essential build and development tasks. More information: <https://quarkus.io/guides/cli-tooling>.
qtcreator: Cross-platform IDE for Qt applications. More information: <https://doc.qt.io/qtcreator/creator-cli.html>.
qsv: Blazing-fast toolkit for querying, slicing, sorting, analyzing, filtering, transforming, and validating tabular data. More information: <https://qsv.dathere.com/>.
qrttoppm: Convert a QRT ray tracer file to a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/qrttoppm.html>.
qrencode: QR Code generator. Supports PNG and EPS. See also: `qr`. More information: <https://manned.org/qrencode>.
qr: Generate QR codes in the terminal with ANSI VT-100 escape codes. See also: `qrencode`. More information: <https://manned.org/qr>.
qpdf: Versatile PDF transformation software. More information: <https://manned.org/qpdf>.
qownnotes: Markdown note-taking application. Optionally integrates with the note-taking applications of Nextcloud and ownCloud. See also: `qc`. More information: <https://www.qownnotes.org/getting-started/cli-parameters.html>.
qoitopam: Convert a QOI image (Quite OK Image format) to Netpbm. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/qoitopam.html>.
qmv: Move files and directories using the default text editor to define the filenames. More information: <https://manned.org/qmv>.
qmmp: An audio player with an interface similar to Winamp or XMMS. See also: `clementine`, `ncmpcpp`, `cmus`. More information: <https://manned.org/qmmp>.
qmake: Generate Makefiles from Qt project files. More information: <https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qmake-running.html>.
qgis_process: Run QGIS processing algorithms from the command line without opening the GUI. See also: `qgis`. More information: <https://docs.qgis.org/latest/en/docs/user_manual/processing/standalone.html>.
qgis: View, create, and analyze geographic data in a Geographic Information System. Supports rasters, vectors, and project files (`.qgs`, `.qgz`, `.qlr`). More information: <https://docs.qgis.org/latest/en/docs/user_manual/introduction/qgis_configuration.html#running-qgis-with-advanced-settings>.
qemu-img: Create and manipulate Quick Emulator Virtual HDD images. More information: <https://qemu.readthedocs.io/en/master/tools/qemu-img.html>.
qdbus: Inter-Process Communication (IPC) and Remote Procedure Calling (RPC) mechanism originally developed for Linux. More information: <https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtdbus-index.html>.
qcp: Copy files using the default text editor to define the filenames. More information: <https://manned.org/qcp>.
qc: Manage and execute command snippets stored in QOwnNotes notes. See also: `qownnotes`. More information: <https://www.qownnotes.org/getting-started/command-line-snippet-manager.html>.
qalc: Powerful and easy to use calculator. See also: `bc`. More information: <https://qalculate.github.io/manual/qalc.html>.
q: Execute SQL-like queries on CSV and TSV files. More information: <https://harelba.github.io/q/>.
python3: This command is an alias of `python`.
python-m-json.tool: Validate and pretty-print JSON data. Part of Python's standard library. More information: <https://docs.python.org/library/json.html#module-json.tool>.
pystun3: Classic STUN client written in Python. More information: <https://github.com/talkiq/pystun3>.
pypy: Fast and compliant alternative implementation of the Python language. More information: <https://manned.org/pypy>.
pylint: A Python code linter. More information: <https://pylint.pycqa.org/en/latest/>.
pyinstaller: Bundle a Python application and its dependencies into a single package. More information: <https://pyinstaller.org/en/stable/man/pyinstaller.html>.
pyinfra: Automates infrastructure at a large scale. More information: <https://docs.pyinfra.com/en/3.x/cli.html>.
pygbag: Package Pygame projects as WebAssembly to run in web browsers. More information: <https://github.com/pygame-web/pygbag#pygbag>.
pyflakes: Check Python source code files for errors. More information: <https://pypi.org/project/pyflakes>.
pyenv: Switch between multiple versions of Python easily. See also: `asdf`. More information: <https://manned.org/pyenv>.
pyenv-virtualenv: Create virtual environments based on one's installed Python distributions. More information: <https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv-virtualenv#usage>.
pydocstyle: Statically check Python scripts for compliance with Python docstring conventions. More information: <https://pydocstyle.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage.html>.
pydoc: Display offline Python documentation. More information: <https://docs.python.org/library/pydoc.html>.
pycodestyle: Check Python code against PEP 8 style conventions. More information: <https://pycodestyle.pycqa.org/en/latest/intro.html#example-usage-and-output>.
pyats: A vendor agnostic test automation framework by Cisco Systems, used for network and systems testing. More information: <https://developer.cisco.com/pyats/>.
pyats-version: View and upgrade the pyATS installation. More information: <https://developer.cisco.com/pyats/>.
pyats-shell: Start a pre-loaded pyATS interactive Python Shell to save time in prototyping. More information: <https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/genie-docs/docs/cli/genie_shell.html>.
py-spy: A sampling profiler for Python programs. More information: <https://github.com/benfred/py-spy>.
pwsh: Shell and scripting language designed especially for system administration. This command refers to PowerShell version 6 and above (also known as PowerShell Core and cross-platform PowerShell). To use the original Windows version (5.1 and below, also known as the legacy Windows PowerShell), use `powershell` instead of `pwsh`. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_pwsh>.
pwqgen: Generate a random passphrase. More information: <https://manned.org/pwqgen>.
pwd: Print the name of current/working directory. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/pwd-invocation.html>.
pv: Monitor the progress of data through a pipe. More information: <https://manned.org/pv>.
putty: SSH, Telnet, and Rlogin client for connecting to remote servers. Note: On Linux, the native `ssh` client is often more convenient. PuTTY is more commonly used on Windows. More information: <https://the.earth.li/~sgtatham/putty/latest/htmldoc/Chapter3.html#using-cmdline>.
pushln: This command is an alias of `print -nz`.
pushd: Place a directory on a stack so it can be accessed later. See also: `popd`, `dirs`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-pushd>.
puppet: Manage and automate the configuration of servers. Puppet uses a declarative language to define system configurations and apply them automatically. Some subcommands such as `agent`, `apply` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/puppetlabs/puppet/blob/main/references/man/overview.md>.
puppet-apply: Apply Puppet manifests locally. More information: <https://github.com/puppetlabs/puppet/blob/main/references/man/apply.md>.
puppet-agent: Retrieve the client configuration from a Puppet server and apply it to the local host. More information: <https://github.com/puppetlabs/puppet/blob/main/references/man/agent.md>.
pulumi: Define infrastructure on any cloud using familiar programming languages. Some subcommands such as `up` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/>.
pulumi-whoami: Print information about the currently logged in user. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_whoami/>.
pulumi-version: Display Pulumi's version number. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_version/>.
pulumi-update: This command is an alias of `pulumi up`.
pulumi-up: Create or update the resources in a stack. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_up/>.
pulumi-state: Edit the current stack's state. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_state/>.
pulumi-stack: Manage stacks and view stack state. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_stack/>.
pulumi-stack-history: Display history for a stack. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_stack_history/>.
pulumi-stack-hist: This command is an alias of `pulumi stack history`.
pulumi-schema: Check a Pulumi package schema for errors. Schema reference: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/extending-pulumi/schema/>. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_schema/>.
pulumi-refresh: Refresh the resources in a stack. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_refresh/>.
pulumi-preview: Show a preview of updates to a stack's resources. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_preview/>.
pulumi-policy: Manage resource policies on Pulumi Cloud (Business Critical) or locally (no organization sub-commands). More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_policy/>.
pulumi-plugin: Manage language and resource provider plugins manually. Other commands manage these automatically. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_plugin/>.
pulumi-org: Manage Pulumi Organization configuration. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_org/>.
pulumi-new: Create a new Pulumi project. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_new/>.
pulumi-logout: Log out of the Pulumi cloud. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_logout/>.
pulumi-login: Log in to the Pulumi cloud. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_login/>.
pulumi-install: Install packages and plugins for the current program or policy pack. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_install/>.
pulumi-import: Import resources into an existing stack. Read syntax for your cloud provider: <https://www.pulumi.com/registry/>. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_import/>.
pulumi-gen-completion: Generate completion scripts for the Pulumi CLI. Supported shells are Bash, Zsh, fish. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_gen-completion/>.
pulumi-down: This command is an alias of `pulumi destroy`.
pulumi-destroy: Destroy all existing resources in a stack. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_destroy/>.
pulumi-console: Open a stack in the Pulumi Console (cloud or self-hosted). It gives you instructions to migrate if not available for your backend. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_console/>.
pulumi-config: Manage configuration of a Pulumi stack. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_config/>.
pulumi-cancel: Cancel a stack's currently running update, if any. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_cancel/>.
pulumi-about: Print information about the Pulumi environment. More information: <https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_about/>.
pueue: A task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks. Some subcommands such as `add` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-switch: Switch the queue position of two enqueued or stashed commands. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-status: Display the current status of all tasks. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-stash: Stash tasks to prevent them starting automatically. See also: `pueue start`, `pueue enqueue`. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-start: Resume operation of tasks or groups of tasks. See also: `pueue pause`. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-shutdown: Remotely shut down the daemon. Only use this subcommand if the daemon isn't started by a service manager. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-send: Send input to a task. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-reset: Kill everything and reset. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-remove: Remove tasks from the list. Running or paused tasks need to be killed first. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-pause: Pause running tasks or groups. See also: `pueue start`. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-parallel: Set the amount of allowed parallel tasks. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-log: Display the log output of 1 or more tasks. See also: `pueue status`. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-kill: Kill running tasks or whole groups. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-help: Display help for subcommands. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-group: Display, add, or remove groups. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-follow: Follow the output of a currently running task. See also: `pueue log`. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-enqueue: Enqueue stashed tasks. See also: `pueue stash`. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-edit: Edit the command or path of a stashed or queued task. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-completions: Generate shell completion files for Bash, Elvish, fish, PowerShell, and Zsh. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-clean: Remove all finished tasks from the list and clear logs. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
pueue-add: Enqueue a task for execution. More information: <https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue#how-to-use-it>.
ptpython3: This command is an alias of `ptpython`.
ptpython: A better Python REPL. More information: <https://github.com/prompt-toolkit/ptpython>.
ptghci: Interactive Haskell REPL with syntax highlighting, multiline editing, and real-time type display. See also: `ghci`. More information: <https://github.com/litxio/ptghci>.
ptargrep: Find `regex` patterns in `.tar` archive files. More information: <https://manned.org/ptargrep>.
pt: Platinum Searcher. A code search tool similar to `ag`. More information: <https://github.com/monochromegane/the_platinum_searcher>.
psysh: A runtime developer console, interactive debugger, and REPL for PHP. More information: <https://github.com/bobthecow/psysh/wiki/CLI-options>.
pstopnm: Convert a PostScript file to a PNM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/pstopnm.html>.
psidtopgm: Convert PostScript image data to a PGM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/psidtopgm.html>.
psgrep: Search running processes with `grep`. More information: <https://jvz.github.io/psgrep/>.
psexec.py: Execute commands on a remote Windows machine using `RemComSvc`, providing PsExec-like functionality. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
psalm: A static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. More information: <https://psalm.dev/docs/running_psalm/command_line_usage/#command-line-options>.
ps: Information about running processes. More information: <https://manned.org/ps>.
ps-nvm: PowerShell-based utility to manage multiple Node.js versions, inspired by `nvm`. This tool provides multiple commands that all can only be run through PowerShell. More information: <https://github.com/aaronpowell/ps-nvm>.
prqlc: PRQL compiler. PRQL is a modern language for transforming data - a simple, powerful, pipelined SQL replacement. More information: <https://prql-lang.org/book/project/integrations/prqlc-cli.html>.
proxify: A versatile and portable proxy for capturing, manipulating, and replaying HTTP/HTTPS traffic on the go. See also: `mitmproxy`. More information: <https://github.com/projectdiscovery/proxify#usage>.
prowler: Perform security best practices assessments, audits, and compliance checks across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Kubernetes. Some subcommands such as  `azure`, `gcp`, `kubernetes`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
prowler-m365: Assess Microsoft 365 (M365) security configurations and best practices. See also: `prowler aws`, `prowler azure`, `prowler gcp`, `prowler kubernetes`, `prowler github`. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
prowler-kubernetes: Assess Kubernetes cluster security best practices and configurations. See also: `prowler aws`, `prowler azure`, `prowler gcp`, `prowler m365`, `prowler github`. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
prowler-github: Assess GitHub account, repository, and organization security best practices. See also: `prowler aws`, `prowler azure`, `prowler gcp`, `prowler kubernetes`, `prowler m365`. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
prowler-gcp: Assess Google Cloud Platform (GCP) security best practices, audits, and compliance checks. See also: `prowler aws`, `prowler azure`, `prowler kubernetes`, `prowler m365`, `prowler github`. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
prowler-azure: Assess Azure security best practices, perform audits, compliance checks, and generate reports. See also: `prowler aws`, `prowler gcp`, `prowler kubernetes`, `prowler m365`, `prowler github`. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
prowler-aws: Assess AWS security best practices, perform audits, compliance checks, and generate reports. See also: `prowler azure`, `prowler gcp`, `prowler kubernetes`, `prowler m365`, `prowler github`. More information: <https://docs.prowler.com/user-guide/cli/tutorials/misc>.
protoc: Parse Google Protobuf `.proto` files and generate output in the specified language. More information: <https://manned.org/protoc>.
protector: Protect or unprotect branches on GitHub repositories. More information: <https://github.com/jcgay/protector#usage>.
prosodyctl: The control tool for the Prosody XMPP server. Note: Process management through `prosodyctl` is discouraged. Instead, use the tools provided by your system (e.g. `systemctl`). More information: <https://prosody.im/doc/prosodyctl>.
propelauth: Set up PropelAuth authentication as quickly and easily as possible. More information: <https://docs.propelauth.com/reference/api/cli>.
promtool: Tooling for the Prometheus monitoring system. More information: <https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/getting_started/>.
projucer: A project manager for JUCE framework applications. More information: <https://docs.juce.com/master/projucer_manual.html#projucer_manual_tools_command_line_tools>.
progress: Display/Monitor the progress of running coreutils. More information: <https://github.com/Xfennec/progress>.
progpilot: A PHP static analysis tool for detecting security vulnerabilities. More information: <https://github.com/designsecurity/progpilot>.
procs: Display information about the active processes. More information: <https://github.com/dalance/procs/blob/master/man/procs.1.adoc>.
printf: Format and print text. See also: `echo`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/printf-invocation.html>.
printenv: Print values of environment variables. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/printenv-invocation.html>.
print.zsh: Z Shell (`zsh`) builtin. Print arguments, similar to `echo`. See also: `echo`, `printf`, `zsh`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Shell-Builtin-Commands.html>.
print: `print` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
pretty-bytes: Convert bytes to a human-readable string. More information: <https://github.com/sindresorhus/pretty-bytes-cli>.
prettier: An opinionated code formatter for JavaScript, JSON, CSS, YAML, and more. More information: <https://prettier.io/docs/cli>.
presenterm: A terminal-based slideshow tool that renders markdown presentations. More information: <https://mfontanini.github.io/presenterm/>.
prename: This command is an alias of `rename`.
prek: Create Git hooks that run before commits. More information: <https://prek.j178.dev/reference/cli/>.
