oc: The OpenShift Container Platform CLI. Allows for application and container management. More information: <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/cli_tools/index>.
obsidian: Command-line interface for the Obsidian Markdown note-taking app. Note: Requires the Obsidian app to be running. More information: <https://obsidian.md/help/cli>.
obs: Open Broadcaster Software. Video recording and livestreaming program. More information: <https://obsproject.com/kb/launch-parameters>.
objdump: View information about object files. More information: <https://manned.org/objdump>.
oauth2c: Interact with OAuth 2.0 authorization servers. More information: <https://github.com/cloudentity/oauth2c#usage>.
oathtool: OATH one-time password tool. More information: <https://www.nongnu.org/oath-toolkit/oathtool.1.html>.
o: Orbiton, a simple configuration-free text editor. More information: <https://github.com/xyproto/orbiton>.
nyxt: A keyboard-driven web browser for power users. More information: <https://nyxt-browser.com/documentation>.
nxcdb: Interact with the NetExec database. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/getting-started/database-general-usage>.
nxc: Network service enumeration and exploitation tool. Some subcommands such as `smb` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/getting-started/selecting-and-using-a-protocol>.
nxc-wmi: Pentest and exploit the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/wmi-protocol/password-spraying>.
nxc-winrm: Pentest and exploit Windows Remote Management (winrm). More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/winrm-protocol/password-spraying>.
nxc-vnc: Pentest and exploit VNC servers. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/getting-started/selecting-and-using-a-protocol>.
nxc-ssh: Pentest and exploit SSH servers. See also: `hydra`. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/ssh-protocol/password-spraying>.
nxc-smb: Pentest and exploit SMB servers. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/smb-protocol/generate-hosts-file>.
nxc-rdp: Pentest and exploit RDP servers. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/rdp-protocol/password-spraying>.
nxc-nfs: Pentest and exploit NFS servers. Currently supports anonymous mode only. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/nfs-protocol/enumeration>.
nxc-mssql: Pentest and exploit Microsoft SQL servers. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/mssql-protocol/mssql-passwordspray>.
nxc-ldap: Pentest and exploit Windows Active Directory Domains via LDAP. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/ldap-protocol/authentication>.
nxc-ftp: Pentest and exploit FTP servers. More information: <https://www.netexec.wiki/ftp-protocol/password-spraying>.
nwipe: Securely erase disks using a variety of recognized methods. More information: <https://manned.org/nwipe>.
nvme: NVMe storage user space utility. More information: <https://manned.org/nvme>.
nvm: Install, uninstall, or switch between Node.js versions. Supports version numbers like "12.8" or "v16.13.1", and labels like "node", "system", etc. See also: `asdf`. More information: <https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm#usage>.
nvm.fish: Install, uninstall, or switch between Node.js versions under the fish shell. Supports version numbers like "12.8" or "v16.13.1", and labels like "stable", "system", etc. More information: <https://github.com/jorgebucaran/nvm.fish>.
nvim: Neovim, a programmer's text editor based on Vim, provides several modes for different kinds of text manipulation. Pressing `<i>` in normal mode enters insert mode. `<Esc>` or `<Ctrl c>` goes back to normal mode, which doesn't allow regular text insertion. See also: `vim`, `vimtutor`, `vimdiff`. More information: <https://neovim.io/>.
nvidia-smi: Aid the management and monitoring of NVIDIA GPU devices. More information: <https://developer.nvidia.com/system-management-interface>.
nvidia-smi-mig: Manage Nvidia multi-instance GPUs. More information: <https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/mig-user-guide/index.html>.
nvcc: The NVIDIA CUDA Compiler Driver. More information: <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-compiler-driver-nvcc/>.
numfmt: Convert numbers to and from human-readable strings. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/numfmt-invocation.html>.
numbat: A statically-typed scientific calculator with first-class support for physical units. See also: `qalc`, `bc`. More information: <https://numbat.dev/docs/cli/usage>.
nudoku: Sudoku game in terminal. More information: <https://jubalh.github.io/nudoku/>.
nuclei: Fast and customizable vulnerability scanner using a simple YAML-based DSL. More information: <https://docs.projectdiscovery.io/opensource/nuclei/running>.
nu: Nushell ("a new type of shell") takes a modern, structured approach to your command-line. See also: `elvish`. More information: <https://www.nushell.sh/book/configuration.html#flag-behavior>.
ntpctl: Display information about the running instance of OpenNTPD. More information: <https://man.openbsd.org/ntpctl>.
ntp-ctl: Management client for the `ntpd-rs` daemon. More information: <https://docs.ntpd-rs.pendulum-project.org/man/ntp-ctl.8/>.
ntl: This command is an alias of `netlify`.
nth: Name That Hash - Instantly name the type of any hash. More information: <https://github.com/bee-san/Name-That-Hash>.
ntfyme: A notification tool to track and notify you about your long-running termination process. Send notifications with success/error messages with Gmail, Telegram, and more. More information: <https://github.com/AnirudhG07/ntfyme>.
ntfy: Send and receive HTTP POST notifications. More information: <https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy>.
ntfs-read.py: A read-only NTFS explorer for accessing and extracting files from NTFS volumes. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
nslookup: Query name servers for various domain records. See also: `dig`, `resolvectl`, `host`. More information: <https://manned.org/nslookup>.
nrm: `npm` registry manager. Helps to easily switch between different `npm` registries. More information: <https://github.com/Pana/nrm#usage>.
npx: This command is an alias of `npm exec`.
nproc: Print the number of processing units (normally CPUs) available. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/nproc-invocation.html>.
npm: JavaScript and Node.js package manager. Manage Node.js projects and their module dependencies. Some subcommands such as `install`, `run`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm/>.
npm-why: Identify why an npm package is installed. More information: <https://github.com/amio/npm-why>.
npm-view: View registry information about a package. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-view/>.
npm-version: Bump a node package version. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-version/>.
npm-update: Update packages in the current project. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-update/>.
npm-unstar: Remove the favorite/star mark from a package. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/npm-unstar>.
npm-unpublish: Remove a package from the npm registry. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-unpublish/>.
npm-token: Manage and generate authentication tokens for the npm registry. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-token/>.
npm-test: This command is an alias of `npm run test`.
npm-team: Manage teams in an organization on the `npm` registry. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-team/>.
npm-stop: This command is an alias of `npm run stop`.
npm-start: This command is an alias of `npm run start`.
npm-stars: View packages marked as favorites. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/npm-stars>.
npm-star: Mark a package as favorite. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/npm-star>.
npm-shrinkwrap: Lock down the dependencies of a package, creating an `npm-shrinkwrap.json` file. Similar to `package-lock.json` but intended for published packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/npm-shrinkwrap>.
npm-search: Search for packages in the `npm` registry. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-search/>.
npm-sbom: Generate a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for your Node.js project. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-sbom/>.
npm-run-script: This command is an alias of `npm run`.
npm-root: Display path to `node_modules` directory. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-root/>.
npm-restart: This command is an alias of `npm run restart`.
npm-repo: Open the repository page of a package in the browser. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-repo/>.
npm-rebuild: Rebuild native Node.js packages after Node or dependency changes. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-rebuild/>.
npm-rb: This command is an alias of `npm-rebuild`.
npm-query: Print an array of dependency objects using CSS-like selectors. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-query/>.
npm-publish: Publish a package to the npm registry. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/publish/>.
npm-prune: Remove extraneous packages from `node_modules`. Note: Extraneous packages are those present in the node_modules folder that are not listed as any package's dependency list. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-prune/>.
npm-profile: Manage the npm profile and related settings. Note: This command is unaware of workspaces. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-profile/>.
npm-prefix: Print the local or global prefix to `stdout`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-prefix/>.
npm-pkg: Show or modify `package.json` properties. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-pkg/>.
npm-pack: Create a tarball from a package. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/pack/>.
npm-owner: Manage ownership of published packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-owner/>.
npm-outdated: Check for outdated npm package dependencies. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-outdated/>.
npm-name: Check whether a package or organization name is available on npm. More information: <https://github.com/sindresorhus/npm-name-cli>.
npm-ls: Print installed packages to `stdout`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-ls/>.
npm-logout: Log out of the registry user account. See also: `npm login`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-logout/>.
npm-login: Log in to a registry user account. See also: `npm logout`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-login/>.
npm-list: This command is an alias of `npm ls`.
npm-link: Symlink a local package into the global `node_modules` or another project for development. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-link/>.
npm-it: This command is an alias of `npm install-test`.
npm-install-test: Equivalent to running `npm install` followed by `npm test`. Note: `it` can be used as shorthand for `install-test`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-install-test/>.
npm-install-ci-test: Install project dependencies and run tests in a single command, mainly used in continuous integration (CI) environments. Equivalent to running `npm ci && npm test`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/install-ci-test/>.
npm-hook: Manage `npm` registry hooks for packages. Note: This command is deprecated. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/hook/>.
npm-home: Open the `npm` page, Yarn page, or GitHub repository of a package in the web browser. More information: <https://github.com/sindresorhus/npm-home>.
npm-help: Display an overview of `npm` syntax, frequently used commands, and a short description of each command. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-help/>.
npm-help-search: Search npm help documentation using a keyword. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-help-search/>.
npm-fund: Retrieve funding information from packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-fund/>.
npm-find-dupes: Identify duplicate dependencies in `node_modules`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-find-dupes/>.
npm-explore: Browse an installed npm package. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-explore/>.
npm-explain: Explain how a package is installed, detailing its dependencies and reasons for inclusion. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/explain/>.
npm-exec: Execute binaries from `npm` packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-exec/>.
npm-edit: Select a dependency in the current project and open the package folder in the default editor (`$EDITOR`). After editing, the package is rebuilt to pick up any changes in compiled packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-edit/>.
npm-doctor: Check the health of the npm environment. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-doctor/>.
npm-docs: Open the documentation for one or more packages in the default web browser. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-docs/>.
npm-dist-tag: Manage distribution tags on packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-dist-tag/>.
npm-diff: Compare package versions from the `npm` registry and show differences. Similar to `git diff`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-diff/>.
npm-deprecate: Mark a version or range of versions of an `npm` package as deprecated. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-deprecate/>.
npm-dedupe: Reduce duplication in the `node_modules` directory. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-dedupe/>.
npm-config: Manage the `npm` configuration settings. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-config/>.
npm-completion: Enable or set up tab-completion for npm commands. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-completion/>.
npm-ci: Clean install of `npm` project dependencies for automated environments. Installs packages based on `package-lock.json` or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-ci/>.
npm-check: Check for outdated, incorrect, and unused npm package dependencies. More information: <https://github.com/dylang/npm-check>.
npm-cache: Manage the npm package cache. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-cache/>.
npm-bugs: Report bugs for a package in a web browser. Attempts to open the package's bug tracker URL or support email. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-bugs/>.
npm-author: This command is an alias of `npm owner`.
npm-audit: Scan project dependencies for known security vulnerabilities. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-audit/>.
npm-adduser: Add a registry user account. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/npm-adduser>.
npm-access: Set access level on published packages. More information: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/npm-access/>.
nping: Network packet generation tool/ping utility. More information: <https://nmap.org/nping/>.
now: Cloud platform for serverless deployment. Note: This command is deprecated, use `vercel` instead. More information: <https://vercel.com/home>.
notmuch: Index, search, read, and tag large collections of email messages. More information: <https://notmuchmail.org/manpages/>.
notify-send: Use the current desktop environment's notification system to create a notification. More information: <https://manned.org/notify-send>.
noti: Monitor a process and trigger a banner notification. More information: <https://github.com/variadico/noti/blob/main/docs/noti.md>.
noseyparker: Scan text and Git history for secrets and sensitive information. Note: Use a separate datastore directory (`--datastore`) for each scan. See also: `trufflehog`. More information: <https://github.com/praetorian-inc/noseyparker#usage-examples>.
nop: Check validity and pretty-print graphs in canonical format. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://www.graphviz.org/pdf/nop.1.pdf>.
nomad: Distributed, highly available, datacenter-aware scheduler. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/nomad/commands>.
nokogiri: An HTML, XML, SAX, and Reader parser. More information: <https://manned.org/nokogiri>.
nohup: Allow for a process to live when the terminal gets killed. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/nohup-invocation.html>.
noglob: Execute a command in Zsh without globbing (expanding wildcard patterns). More information: <https://manned.org/zshmisc>.
nodemon: Watch files and automatically restart a node application when changes are detected. More information: <https://github.com/remy/nodemon/tree/main/doc/cli>.
nnn: Interactive terminal file manager and disk usage analyzer. More information: <https://github.com/jarun/nnn/wiki/Usage#program-options>.
nms: Tool that recreates the famous data decryption effect seen in the 1992 movie Sneakers from `stdin`. More information: <https://github.com/bartobri/no-more-secrets>.
nmap: Network exploration tool and security/port scanner. Some features (e.g. SYN scan) activate only when `nmap` is run with root privileges. See also: `hping3`, `masscan`, `naabu`, `rustscan`, `zmap`. More information: <https://nmap.org/book/man.html>.
nm: List symbol names in object files. More information: <https://manned.org/nm>.
nm-classic: This command is an alias of `nm`.
nload: Visualize network usage in the terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/nload>.
nl: Number lines from a file or from `stdin`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/nl-invocation.html>.
nkf: Network kanji filter: convert kanji code from one encoding to another. More information: <https://manned.org/nkf>.
nixpkgs-review: Review pull requests in the NixOS packages repository (nixpkgs). After a successful build, a `nix-shell` with all built packages is started. More information: <https://github.com/Mic92/nixpkgs-review#usage>.
nix: A powerful package manager that makes package management reliable, reproducible, and declarative. Some features of `nix` (`nix command`, `flakes`, etc.) are experimental and require enabling experimental features. Some subcommands such as `build`, `develop`, `flake`, `registry`, `profile`, `search`, `repl`, `store`, `edit`, `why-depends`, etc. have their own usage documentation. See also: `nix classic`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix>.
nix-why-depends: Show why a package depends on another package. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-why-depends.html>.
nix-store: `nix-store` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
nix-store.3: Manipulate the Nix store. See also: `nix-store`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-store.html>.
nix-store.2: Manipulate or query the Nix store. See also: `nix store.3`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/nix-store.html>.
nix-shell: `nix-shell` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
nix-shell.3: Start a shell in which the specified packages are available. See also: `nix-shell`, `nix flake`. More information: <https://manned.org/nix3-shell>.
nix-shell.2: Start an interactive shell based on a Nix expression. See also: `nix shell.3`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/nix-shell.html>.
nix-search: Search for packages in a Nix flake. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-search.html>.
nix-run: Run an application from a Nix flake. See also: `nix flake`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-run.html>.
nix-repl: Start an interactive environment for evaluating Nix expressions. See <https://nixos.org/manual/nix/stable/language/index.html> for a description of the Nix expression language. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-repl.html>.
nix-registry: Manage a Nix flake registry. See also: `nix flake`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-registry.html>.
nix-profile: Install, update, and remove packages from Nix profiles. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/latest/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-profile.html>.
nix-instantiate: Create store derivations from nix expressions. See also: `nix eval`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/latest/command-ref/nix-instantiate.html>.
nix-flake: Manage Nix flakes. Some subcommands such as `init`, `show`, and `info` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-flake.html>.
nix-flake-show: Show outputs provided by a flake. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-flake-show.html>.
nix-flake-init: Create a flake in the current directory from a template. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-flake-init.html>.
nix-eval: Evaluate a Nix expression and print the result to `stdout`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-eval.html>.
nix-env: Manipulate or query Nix user environments. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/nix-env.html>.
nix-edit: Open the Nix expression of a Nix package in `$EDITOR`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-edit.html>.
nix-develop: Run a Bash shell that provides the build environment of a derivation. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-develop.html>.
nix-collect-garbage: Delete unused and unreachable nix store paths. Generations can be listed using `nix-env --list-generations`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/nix-collect-garbage.html>.
nix-classic: A classic, stable interface to a powerful package manager that makes package management reliable, reproducible, and declarative. Some Nix commands such as `nix-build`, `nix-shell`, `nix-env`, and `nix-store` have their own pages. More information: <https://nixos.org/>.
nix-build: `nix-build` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
nix-build.3: Build a Nix expression (downloading from the cache when possible). See also: `nix-build`, `nix flake`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-build.html>.
nix-build.2: Build a Nix expression. See also: `nix build.3`. More information: <https://nix.dev/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/nix-build.html>.
ninja: A Build system designed to be fast. More information: <https://ninja-build.org/manual.html>.
nimble: Package manager for the Nim programming language. Manage Nim projects and their dependencies. More information: <https://github.com/nim-lang/nimble>.
nim: The Nim compiler. Process, compile, and link Nim language source files. More information: <https://nim-lang.org/docs/nimc.html>.
nikto: Web server scanner which performs tests against web servers for multiple items. More information: <http://cirt.net/nikto/>.
nicotine: Graphical client for the Soulseek peer-to-peer network. More information: <https://manned.org/nicotine>.
nice: Execute a program with a custom scheduling priority (niceness). Niceness values range from -20 (the highest priority) to 19 (the lowest). Note: Some modern schedulers ignore niceness or limit its effects inside autogroups. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/nice-invocation.html>.
ni: Use the right package manager (npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, or deno) automatically. Detect the current project's lockfile to run the corresponding commands. Note: In PowerShell, `ni` is a built-in alias for `New-Item`. To use this tool, the alias must be removed. More information: <https://github.com/antfu-collective/ni>.
nhentai: Download doujinshis from nhentai. More information: <https://github.com/RicterZ/nhentai#usage>.
nh: Modern helper utility tool for the Nix/NixOS ecosystem. Some subcommands such as `os`, `home`, `clean`, and `search` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/nix-community/nh#usage>.
nh-search: Search for packages in Nixpkgs. More information: <https://github.com/nix-community/nh#usage>.
nh-os: Reconfigure or debug a NixOS machine. More information: <https://github.com/nix-community/nh#usage>.
nh-home: Manage and configure per-user environment using Nix. Reimplementation of `home-manager`. More information: <https://github.com/nix-community/nh#usage>.
nh-clean: Clean Nix profiles and delete unused and unreachable Nix store paths. Generations can be listed using `nix-env --list-generations` or `nh os info`. More information: <https://github.com/nix-community/nh#usage>.
ngs: Scripting language created specifically for Ops. More information: <https://github.com/ngs-lang/ngs>.
ngrok: Reverse proxy that creates a secure tunnel from a public endpoint to a locally running web service. More information: <https://ngrok.com/docs/agent/cli>.
ngrep: Filter network traffic packets using `regex`. More information: <https://github.com/jpr5/ngrep/blob/master/EXAMPLES.md>.
ng: Create and manage Angular applications. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli>.
ng-version: Display Angular CLI version. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/version>.
ng-update: Update an Angular workspace and its dependencies. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/update>.
ng-test: Run unit tests in a project. Note: Some commands might require additional packages such as Vitest. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/test>.
ng-serve: Build and serve the application, rebuilding on file changes. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/serve>.
ng-run: Run an Architect target with an optional custom builder configuration. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/run>.
ng-new: Create and initialize a new Angular application. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/new>.
ng-lint: Check Angular project code for style and errors using the configured linter. Note: Linting requires setup via `ng add`. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/lint>.
ng-generate: Generate and/or modify files based on a schematic. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/generate>.
ng-extract-i18n: Extract i18n messages from source code. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/extract-i18n>.
ng-e2e: Build and serve an Angular application, then run end-to-end tests. Note: Available `e2e` packages include Playwright, Cypress, Nightwatch, WebdriverIO, and Puppeteer. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/e2e>.
ng-deploy: Invoke the deploy builder for a project in the workspace. Note: Deployment requires setup via `ng add`. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/deploy>.
ng-config: Use JSON path notation (camelCase) to edit workspace or project configurations, such as build options. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/config>.
ng-completion: Generate shell autocompletion scripts for the Angular CLI. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/completion>.
ng-cache: Configure the persistent disk cache and retrieve cache statistics. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/cache>.
ng-build: Compile an Angular application or library into an output directory named `dist/`. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/build>.
ng-analytics: Manage Angular CLI analytics settings. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/analytics>.
ng-add: Add and configure packages for the current workspace project. More information: <https://angular.dev/cli/add>.
nf-core: The nf-core framework tools to create, check, and develop best-practice guidelines for Nextflow. More information: <https://nf-co.re/docs/nf-core-tools>.
nextflow: Run computational pipelines. Mostly used for bioinformatics workflows. More information: <https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/cli.html>.
nextclade: Bioinformatics tool for virus genome alignment, clade assignment, and qc checks. More information: <https://docs.nextstrain.org/projects/nextclade/en/stable/user/nextclade-cli/reference.html>.
next: React framework that uses server-side rendering for building optimized web applications. More information: <https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next>.
newsboat: An RSS/Atom feed reader for text terminals. More information: <https://newsboat.org/releases/2.40/docs/newsboat.html#_first_steps>.
newman: Collection runner for Postman. More information: <https://github.com/postmanlabs/newman#command-line-options>.
nettacker: Automate information gathering, vulnerability scanning, and eventually generate a report. More information: <https://nettacker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Home/>.
netstat: Display network-related information such as open connections, open socket ports, etc. See also: `ss`. More information: <https://manned.org/netstat>.
netserver: Server-side command for `netperf`, the benchmarking application that measures network throughput. See also: `netperf`. More information: <https://manned.org/netserver>.
netperf: Client-side command for `netperf`, the benchmarking application that measures network throughput. Similar to `iperf`. See also: `netserver`. More information: <https://hewlettpackard.github.io/netperf/doc/netperf.html#Global-Command_002dline-Options>.
netlify: Deploy sites and configure continuous deployment to the Netlify platform. More information: <https://cli.netlify.com/>.
netexec: This command is an alias of `nxc`.
netdiscover: Network scanner used to find live hosts on a network. More information: <https://github.com/netdiscover-scanner/netdiscover>.
netcat: This command is an alias of `nc`.
nest: Initialize, develop, and maintain Nest applications. More information: <https://docs.nestjs.com/cli/overview>.
neotoppm: Convert an Atari Neochrome NEO file into a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/neotoppm.html>.
neofetch: Display information about the operating system, software, and hardware. Note: `neofetch` is no longer maintained. See also: `fastfetch`. More information: <https://manned.org/neofetch>.
neo4j-admin: Manage and administer a Neo4j DBMS (Database Management System). See also: `cypher-shell`, `mysqld`. More information: <https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/neo4j-admin-neo4j-cli/>.
ned: Like `grep` but with powerful replace capabilities. Unlike `sed`, as it isn't restricted to line oriented editing. More information: <https://github.com/nevdelap/ned#ned-usage>.
neato: Render an image of a `linear undirected` network graph from a `graphviz` file. Layouts: `dot`, `neato`, `twopi`, `circo`, `fdp`, `sfdp`, `osage` & `patchwork`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/doc/info/command.html>.
ndc: Name daemon control service for name servers. If a command isn't provided, NDC will prompt for one until EOF. More information: <https://manned.org/ndc>.
ncu: Find newer versions of package dependencies and check outdated npm packages locally or globally. `ncu` only updates dependency versions in `package.json`. To install the new versions, run `npm install` afterwards. More information: <https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates>.
ncspot: Cross-platform TUI Spotify client. More information: <https://github.com/hrkfdn/ncspot/blob/main/doc/users.md>.
ncmpcpp: A music player client for the Music Player Daemon. See also: `mpd`, `mpc`, `qmmp`, `termusic`. More information: <https://rybczak.net:443/ncmpcpp/>.
ncdu: Disk usage analyzer with an ncurses interface. See also: `duf`, `df`. More information: <https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu/man>.
ncc: Compile a Node.js application into a single file. Supports TypeScript, binary addons, and dynamic requires. More information: <https://github.com/vercel/ncc#usage>.
nc: Redirect I/O into a network stream through this versatile tool. More information: <https://manned.org/nc>.
nbtscan: Scan networks for NetBIOS name information. More information: <https://github.com/resurrecting-open-source-projects/nbtscan>.
nb: Note-taking, bookmarking, and archiving tool. Supports encryption, tagging, wiki-style links, Git syncing, Pandoc conversion, and more. More information: <https://github.com/xwmx/nb#-help>.
nativefier: Create a desktop app for any web site with minimal configuration. More information: <https://github.com/nativefier/nativefier>.
nasm: The Netwide Assembler, a portable 80x86 assembler. More information: <https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm02.html>.
nano: Text editor. An enhanced `pico` clone. See also: `pico`, `rnano`. More information: <https://nano-editor.org/dist/latest/nano.html>.
nano-ffmpeg: A wrapper for `ffmpeg` with an interactive file browser and operations. More information: <https://github.com/dgr8akki/nano-ffmpeg#usage>.
nagios4: Legacy host/service/networking monitoring program. See also: `nagios`, `nagios2`, `nagios3`. More information: <https://manned.org/nagios>.
nagios3: Legacy host/service/networking monitoring program. Note: This command is deprecated, use `nagios4` instead. See also: `nagios`, `nagios2`, `nagios4`. More information: <https://manned.org/nagios>.
nagios2: Legacy host/service/networking monitoring program. Note: This command is deprecated, use `nagios4` instead. See also: `nagios`, `nagios3`, `nagios4`. More information: <https://manned.org/nagios>.
nagios: Legacy host/service/networking monitoring program. Note: This command is deprecated, use `nagios4` instead. See also: `nagios2`, `nagios3`, `nagios4`. More information: <https://manned.org/nagios>.
naabu: A fast port scanner written in Go with a focus on reliability and simplicity. Note: Some features are only activated when `naabu` is run with root privileges such as SYN scan. See also: `hping3`, `masscan`, `nmap`, `rustscan`, `zmap`. More information: <https://docs.projectdiscovery.io/opensource/naabu/running>.
n: Manage multiple node versions. More information: <https://github.com/tj/n>.
mytop: Display MySQL server performance info like `top`. More information: <https://jeremy.zawodny.com/mysql/mytop/mytop.html>.
mysqlsh: Advanced client for MySQL, supporting SQL, JavaScript, and Python. It offers features for managing InnoDB clusters and document store collections. More information: <https://manned.org/mysqlsh>.
mysqldump: Back up MySQL databases. See also: `mysql`. More information: <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/en/mysqldump.html>.
mysqld: Start the MySQL database server. More information: <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/en/mysqld.html>.
mysqlcheck: Check and repair MySQL tables. More information: <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/en/mysqlcheck.html>.
mysqlbinlog: Utility for processing MySQL binary log files. More information: <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/en/mysqlbinlog.html>.
mysql_secure_installation: Set up MySQL to have better security. More information: <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/en/mysql-secure-installation.html>.
mypy: Type check Python code. More information: <https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html>.
mycli: A CLI for MySQL, MariaDB, and Percona that can do auto-completion and syntax highlighting. More information: <https://manned.org/mycli>.
mvn: Apache Maven: build and manage Java-based projects. More information: <https://manned.org/mvn>.
mvn-site: Generate a project website based on the information in the `pom.xml` file. More information: <https://maven.apache.org/plugins/maven-site-plugin/usage.html>.
mvn-package: Package the compiled code of a Maven project into its distributable format (such as a `.jar` or `.war`). More information: <https://manned.org/mvn>.
mvn-install: Install third-party Maven dependencies and build the project. More information: <https://manned.org/mvn>.
mvn-idea: Generate IntelliJ IDEA project files (`.ipr`, `.iml`, and `.iws`) for a Maven project. Note: This plugin is retired. It is no longer maintained. More information: <https://maven.apache.org/plugins/maven-idea-plugin/usage.html>.
mvn-generate-sources: Generate source code for a Maven project before the main compilation phase. This phase runs after `initialize` and before `process-sources`. More information: <https://manned.org/mvn>.
mvn-deploy: Add an artifact to a remote repository. More information: <https://manned.org/mvn>.
mvn-dependency: Manage and analyze Maven project dependencies. Provides goals for viewing, resolving, and copying project dependencies. More information: <https://maven.apache.org/plugins/maven-dependency-plugin/usage.html>.
mvn-compile: Compile a Maven project's source code. More information: <https://manned.org/mvn>.
mvn-archetype: Generate a new Maven project from a predefined template (archetype). More information: <https://maven.apache.org/archetype/maven-archetype-plugin/usage.html>.
mv: Move or rename files and directories. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/mv-invocation.html>.
mutool: Convert, query information, and extract data from PDF files. More information: <https://mupdf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/mutool.html>.
mutagen: Real-time file synchronization and network forwarding tool. More information: <https://mutagen.io/documentation/introduction/>.
musl-gcc: A wrapper around `gcc` that automatically sets options for linking against musl libc. All options specified are passed directly to `gcc`. More information: <https://manned.org/musl-gcc>.
musescore: MuseScore sheet music editor. See also: `lilypond`. More information: <https://handbook.musescore.org/appendix/command-line-usage>.
mupdf: A lightweight PDF, XPS, and E-book viewer. More information: <https://mupdf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/mupdf-gl.html>.
mumble: Low-latency, high quality voice chat software. More information: <https://manned.org/mumble>.
multipass: Manage Ubuntu virtual machines using native hypervisors. More information: <https://canonical.com/multipass/docs/latest/reference/command-line-interface/>.
multipass-transfer: Transfer files between the host and the virtual machine. Note: Relative paths on an instance start from the user's home directory. More information: <https://canonical.com/multipass/docs/latest/reference/command-line-interface/transfer/>.
mullvad: CLI client for Mullvad VPN. See also: `fastd`, `ivpn`, `mozillavpn`, `warp-cli`. More information: <https://mullvad.net/en/help/how-use-mullvad-cli>.
mu: Index and search emails from a local Maildir. More information: <https://man.cx/mu>.
mtvtoppm: Convert an MTV or PRT ray tracer file to a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/mtvtoppm.html>.
mtr: Matt's Traceroute: combined traceroute and ping tool. See also: `traceroute`, `ping`. More information: <https://manned.org/mtr>.
mtm: Minimal terminal multiplexer. See also: `tmux`, `screen`. More information: <https://manned.org/mtm>.
mssqlclient.py: Connect to Microsoft SQL Server instances and execute queries. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
msmtp: An SMTP client. It reads text from `stdin` and sends it to an SMTP server. More information: <https://marlam.de/msmtp/>.
msgunfmt: Decompile message catalog from the binary format. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#msgunfmt-Invocation>.
msgmerge: Update an existing translation file from a new template. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#msgmerge-Invocation>.
msginit: Generate language specific translation files based on Portable Object Templates. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#msginit-Invocation>.
msgfmt: Compile message catalog to binary format. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#msgfmt-Invocation>.
msgcat: Concatenate and merge multiple `.po` translation files. Useful in software localization pipelines to combine message catalogs with filtering options. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#msgcat-Invocation>.
msgattrib: Filter and manipulate message attributes in `.po` translation files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#msgattrib-Invocation>.
msfvenom: Manually generate payloads for metasploit. More information: <https://docs.metasploit.com/docs/using-metasploit/basics/how-to-use-msfvenom.html>.
msfconsole: Console for the Metasploit Framework. Note: Run `sudo msfdb init` to enable the Metasploit database backend prior to launching `msfconsole`. More information: <https://docs.rapid7.com/metasploit/msf-overview/>.
msedit: This command is an alias of `edit`.
msedge: The Microsoft Edge command-line utility is available as `msedge` on Windows and `microsoft-edge` for other platforms. More information: <https://microsoft.com/edge>.
mscore: This command is an alias of `musescore`.
msbuild: The Microsoft build tool for Visual Studio project solutions. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/visualstudio/msbuild>.
mr: Manage all of your version control repositories at once. More information: <https://manned.org/mr>.
mqtt_check.py: Simple utility for testing and validating MQTT login credentials. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
mpv: An audio/video player based on MPlayer. See also: `mplayer`, `vlc`. More information: <https://mpv.io/manual/stable/>.
mpremote: Remotely control MicroPython devices. More information: <https://docs.micropython.org/en/latest/reference/mpremote.html>.
mpirun: Execute serial and parallel jobs in Open MPI. See also: `mpic++`. More information: <https://docs.open-mpi.org/en/main/man-openmpi/man1/mpirun.1.html>.
mpijavac: Open MPI compiler wrapper for Java. See also: `mpirun`. More information: <https://docs.open-mpi.org/en/main/features/java.html#building-java-mpi-applications>.
mpiexec: This command is an alias of `mpirun`.
mpicxx: This command is an alias of `mpic++`.
mpicc: Open MPI C wrapper compiler. More information: <https://www.mpich.org/static/docs/latest/www1/mpicc.html>.
mpic++: Open MPI wrapper compiler for C++. See also: `mpirun`. More information: <https://manned.org/mpicxx>.
mpg321: High Performance MPEG 1.0/2.0/2.5 Audio Player for Layer 1, 2, and 3. Written (sometime in 1999) to be a drop-in replacement for the (previously) non-free mpg123 player. More information: <https://manned.org/mpg321>.
mpd: Music Player Daemon. See also: `mpc`, `ncmpcpp`. More information: <https://mpd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mpd.1.html>.
mpc: Music Player Client: control the Music Player Daemon (MPD). See also: `mpd`, `ncmpcpp`, `cmus`. More information: <https://www.musicpd.org/doc/mpc/html/>.
mp4decrypt: Decrypt an MP4 file. Part of the Bento4 tools. More information: <https://www.bento4.com/documentation/mp4decrypt/>.
mp4box: MPEG-4 Systems Toolbox: muxe streams into MP4 container. More information: <https://github.com/gpac/gpac/wiki/Fragmentation,-segmentation,-splitting-and-interleaving>.
mp3info: Viewer/editor for ID3v1 (but not ID3v2) tags of MP3 files. More information: <https://www.ibiblio.org/mp3info/mp3info.html>.
mozillavpn: A Virtual Private Network from the makers of Firefox. See also: `fastd`, `ivpn`, `mullvad`, `warp-cli`. More information: <https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/mozilla-vpn-client/wiki/Command-line-interface>.
most: Open one or several files for interactive reading, allowing scrolling and search. More information: <https://manned.org/most>.
mosquitto_sub: A simple MQTT version 3.1.1 client that will subscribe to topics and print the messages that it receives. More information: <https://mosquitto.org/man/mosquitto_sub-1.html>.
mosquitto_pub: A simple MQTT version 3.1.1 client that will publish a single message on a topic and exit. More information: <https://mosquitto.org/man/mosquitto_pub-1.html>.
mosquitto_passwd: Manage password files for mosquitto. See also: `mosquitto`. More information: <https://mosquitto.org/man/mosquitto_passwd-1.html>.
mosh: Mobile Shell (`mosh`) is a robust and responsive replacement for SSH. `mosh` persists connections to remote servers while roaming between networks. More information: <https://manned.org/mosh>.
more: Interactively display a file, allowing scrolling and searching. See also: `less`. More information: <https://manned.org/more>.
moon-buggy: Chrome dino-like game on the terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/moon-buggy>.
montage: This command is an alias of `magick montage`.
monop: Find and display signatures of Types and methods inside .NET assemblies. More information: <https://manned.org/monop>.
monolith: Save a web page as a single HTML file. More information: <https://github.com/Y2Z/monolith>.
monodis: The Mono Common Intermediate Language (CIL) disassembler. More information: <https://www.mono-project.com/docs/tools+libraries/tools/monodis/>.
monodevelop: Cross platform IDE for C#, F#, and more. More information: <https://www.monodevelop.com/documentation/>.
mongosh: A new shell for MongoDB, replacement for `mongo`. Note: All connection options can be replaced with one string: `mongodb://user@host:port/db_name?authSource=authdb_name`. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/>.
mongorestore: Utility to import a collection or database from a binary dump into a MongoDB instance. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/>.
mongoimport: Import content from a JSON, CSV, or TSV file into a MongoDB database. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoimport/>.
mongoexport: Produce exports of data stored in a MongoDB instance formatted as JSON or CSV. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoexport/>.
mongodump: Utility to export the contents of a MongoDB instance. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump/>.
mongod: The MongoDB database server. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod/>.
mongo: The legacy MongoDB shell. See `mongosh` for the new shell. Note: All connection options can be replaced with one string: `mongodb://user@host:port/db_name?authSource=authdb_name`. More information: <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/>.
molecule: Molecule helps testing Ansible roles. More information: <https://docs.ansible.com/projects/molecule/usage/>.
mold: A modern linker, and a faster drop-in replacement for GNU `ld`. See also: `ld`. More information: <https://github.com/rui314/mold/blob/main/docs/mold.md>.
mogrify: This command is an alias of `magick mogrify`.
moe: A WYSIWYG text editor for ISO-8859-15 encoded text. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/moe/moe.html>.
modutil: Manage PKCS #11 module information within the NSS security module database. More information: <https://manned.org/modutil>.
mods: AI for the command-line, built for pipelines. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/mods#usage>.
mocha: A feature-rich JavaScript test framework. More information: <https://mochajs.org/#command-line-usage>.
mmv: Move and rename files in bulk. More information: <https://manned.org/mmv.1>.
mmls: Display the partition layout of a volume system. More information: <https://wiki.sleuthkit.org/Mmls/>.
mmdc: CLI for mermaid, a diagram generation tool with a domain-specific language. A mermaid definition file is taken as input and an SVG, PNG, or PDF file is generated as output. More information: <http://mermaid.js.org/>.
mmdblookup: A utility to look up an IP address in a MaxMind DB file. More information: <https://maxmind.github.io/libmaxminddb/mmdblookup.html>.
mm2gv: Convert a graph from Matrix Market `mm` format to `gv` format. Converters: `gml2gv`, `gv2gml`, `gv2gxl`, `gxl2gv`, `graphml2gv` & `mm2gv`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/mm2gv.1.pdf>.
mlr: Miller is like `awk`, `sed`, `cut`, `join`, and `sort` for name-indexed data such as CSV, TSV, and tabular JSON. More information: <https://miller.readthedocs.io/en/latest/manpage/>.
mkvmerge: Merge and extract multimedia streams. More information: <https://mkvtoolnix.download/doc/mkvmerge.html>.
mktorrent: Create BitTorrent metainfo files. More information: <https://manned.org/mktorrent>.
mktexfmt: Create a TeX format or Metafont base. More information: <https://manned.org/fmtutil-sys>.
mktemp: Create a temporary file or directory. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/mktemp-invocation.html>.
mkfile: Create empty files of any size. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfile>.
mkfifo: Make named pipes, also known as First In First Out (FIFO). More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/mkfifo-invocation.html>.
mkdocs: Project documentation with Markdown. More information: <https://www.mkdocs.org/user-guide/cli/>.
mkdir: Create directories and set their permissions. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/mkdir-invocation.html>.
mkcert: Make locally-trusted development certificates. More information: <https://manned.org/mkcert>.
mk: Task runner for targets described in Mkfile. Mostly used to control the compilation of an executable from source code. More information: <https://doc.cat-v.org/plan_9/4th_edition/papers/mk>.
mixxx: Free and open source cross-platform DJ software. See also: `lmms`. More information: <https://mixxx.org/manual/latest/chapters/appendix.html#command-line-options>.
mix: Build tool that provides tasks for creating, compiling, and testing Elixir projects, managing its dependencies, and more. More information: <https://hexdocs.pm/mix/index.html>.
mitmweb: A web-based interactive man-in-the-middle HTTP proxy. See also: `mitmproxy`. More information: <https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/concepts-options/>.
mitmproxy: An interactive man-in-the-middle HTTP proxy. See also: `mitmweb`, `mitmdump`. More information: <https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/>.
mitmdump: View, record, and programmatically transform HTTP traffic. The command-line counterpart to mitmproxy. More information: <https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/#mitmdump>.
mispipe: Pipe two commands and return the exit status of the first command. More information: <https://manned.org/mispipe>.
mise: Manage language runtimes like Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, Java, etc. and various tools. More information: <https://mise.jdx.dev/cli/>.
mirrord: Run code locally as if it were a pod in a Kubernetes cluster. Skip the build-push-deploy cycle when shipping features or fixing bugs against real services. More information: <https://metalbear.com/mirrord/docs/getting-started/quick-start#cli>.
minisign: A dead simple tool to sign files and verify signatures. More information: <https://jedisct1.github.io/minisign/>.
miniserve: Simple HTTP file server. More information: <https://github.com/svenstaro/miniserve#usage>.
minipro: Control Xgecu chip programmers (TL866A/CS, TL866II+, T48, T56). Supports various chips including AVRs, PICs, microcontrollers, and memory chips. More information: <https://manned.org/minipro>.
minio-server: MinIO server command for starting the MinIO S3 compatible storage engine. More information: <https://docs.min.io/enterprise/aistor-object-store/reference/aistor-server/>.
minio-client: This command is an alias of `mc` (MinIO client).
minikube-start: Start `minikube` with different configurations. More information: <https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io/docs/commands/start/>.
minifab: Automate the setup and deployment of Hyperledger Fabric networks. More information: <https://github.com/hyperledger-labs/minifabric>.
minidlna: ReadyMedia (formerly MiniDLNA) is a lightweight media server compatible with DLNA/UPnP-AV clients. Used to stream media to smart TVs, consoles, and other DLNA-compatible devices. Configuration is typically done via the `minidlna.conf` file. More information: <https://manned.org/minidlna>.
mingle: Bundle the edges of a graph layout. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://www.graphviz.org/pdf/mingle.1.pdf>.
minetestserver: This command is an alias of `luanti --server`.
minetest: This command is an alias of `luanti`.
minecraft: Run a headless Minecraft server. More information: <https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial:Setting_up_a_Java_Edition_server>.
middleman: Static site generator written in Ruby. More information: <https://middlemanapp.com/basics/install/>.
mid3v2: Edit audio tags. See also: `id3v2`. More information: <https://mutagen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man/mid3v2.html>.
microsoft-edge: Modern web browser developed by Microsoft based on the Chromium web browser developed by Google. This command is available instead as `msedge` for Windows. Note: Additional command arguments from `chromium` may also be usable to control Microsoft Edge. More information: <https://microsoft.com/edge>.
micromamba: A fast, minimal, standalone package and environment manager for `conda` packages. Drop-in replacement for `conda`, ideal for CI, Docker, and lightweight setups. More information: <https://manned.org/micromamba>.
micro: A modern and intuitive terminal-based text editor. You can use your keyboard, but also your mouse to navigate and/or select text. More information: <https://github.com/zyedidia/micro#usage>.
mh_metric: Calculate and enforce code metrics for MATLAB or Octave code. More information: <https://florianschanda.github.io/miss_hit/metrics.html>.
mh_lint: Attempt to find bugs in MATLAB or Octave code. Please note that this tool is neither sound nor complete. More information: <https://florianschanda.github.io/miss_hit/cli.html>.
mh_copyright: Adjust copyright headers for MATLAB or Octave code. More information: <https://florianschanda.github.io/miss_hit/copyright.html>.
mgrtopbm: Convert an MGR bitmap into a PBM file. See also: `pbmtomgr`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/mgrtopbm.html>.
mg: A small, fast, and portable text editor based on `emacs`. More information: <https://manned.org/mg>.
meteor: Full-stack JavaScript platform for building web applications. More information: <https://docs.meteor.com/cli/>.
metaflac: View and edit metadata in FLAC audio files. See also: `flac`. More information: <https://xiph.org/flac/documentation_tools_metaflac.html>.
meson: SCons-like build system that uses Python as a front-end language and Ninja as a building backend. More information: <https://mesonbuild.com/Commands.html>.
meshnamed: Distributed naming system for IPv6 mesh networks. More information: <https://github.com/zhoreeq/meshname>.
meshlabserver: Interface for the MeshLab 3D mesh processing software. More information: <https://manned.org/meshlabserver>.
mesg: Check or set a terminal's ability to receive messages from other users, usually from the `write` command. See also: `write`, `talk`. More information: <https://manned.org/mesg>.
memray: Profile memory usage of a Python application. More information: <https://github.com/bloomberg/memray#usage>.
melt: Back up and restore Ed25519 SSH keys using memorizable seed phrases. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/melt#usage>.
meld: Graphical diffing and merging tool. More information: <https://manned.org/meld>.
medusa: A modular and parallel login brute-forcer for a variety of protocols. More information: <https://manned.org/medusa>.
mediainfo: Display metadata from video and audio files. More information: <https://mediaarea.net/MediaInfo>.
mdp: Make presentations from Markdown files. More information: <https://manned.org/mdp>.
mdk4: A proof-of-concept tool to exploit common IEEE 802.11 protocol weaknesses. Note: Exercise extreme caution as this tool can disrupt Wi-Fi networks and disconnect nearby users. See also: `airodump-ng`, `airmon-ng`. More information: <https://github.com/aircrack-ng/mdk4>.
mdatopbm: Convert a Microdesign MDA file to a PBM image. See also: `pbmtomda`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/mdatopbm.html>.
md5sum: Calculate MD5 cryptographic checksums. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/md5sum-invocation.html>.
md-to-clip: Convert tldr-pages to Command Line Interface Pages. See also: `clip-view`. More information: <https://github.com/command-line-interface-pages/v2-tooling/tree/main/md-to-clip>.
mcopy: Copy MSDOS files to/from Unix. Note: Use forward slash (`/`) instead of backlash (`\`) to refer to DOS subdirectories. Part of the `mtools` package. More information: <https://gnu.org/software/mtools/manual/mtools.html#mcopy>.
mcli: This command is an alias of `mc` (MinIO client).
mcfly: A smart command history search and management tool. Replaces your default shell history search (`<Ctrl r>`) with an intelligent search engine providing context and relevance to the commands. More information: <https://github.com/cantino/mcfly>.
mcat: Parse, convert, and preview files (including Markdown), directories, images, and videos. More information: <https://github.com/Skardyy/mcat#example-usage>.
mc: `mc` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
mc.fm: Midnight Commander, a TUI file manager. Navigate the directory structure using the `<ArrowKeys>`, the mouse, or by typing the commands into the terminal. See also: `ranger`, `clifm`, `vifm`, `nautilus`. More information: <https://source.midnight-commander.org/man/mc.html>.
mc.cli: MinIO Client for object storage and filesystems. May be named `mc` or `mcli` on some systems. More information: <https://minio.github.io/mc/>.
maza: Local ad blocker. Like Pi-hole but local and using the operating system. More information: <https://github.com/tanrax/maza-ad-blocking>.
matlab: Numerical computation environment by MathWorks. More information: <https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/matlab_env/startup-options/>.
mate-dictionary: Look up words on dictionaries. More information: <https://manned.org/mate-dictionary>.
mat2: Anonymize various file formats by removing metadata. More information: <https://0xacab.org/jvoisin/mat2>.
massdns: Resolve DNS records in bulk with high performance for reconnaissance. See also: `dig`, `dnsx`. More information: <https://github.com/blechschmidt/massdns#usage>.
masscan: A very fast network scanner. Works best with elevated privileges. For help with Nmap compatibility, run `masscan --nmap`. See also: `hping3`, `naabu`, `nmap`, `rustscan`, `zmap`. More information: <https://manned.org/masscan>.
markdown2pdf: Convert markdown to PDF. More information: <https://github.com/theiskaa/markdown2pdf>.
marimo: A reactive Python notebook environment. Combines features of Jupyter, Streamlit, and other notebook tools with reactive execution. More information: <https://docs.marimo.io/cli/>.
mariadb: The mariadb client tool. More information: <https://mariadb.com/docs/server/clients-and-utilities/mariadb-client/mariadb-command-line-client>.
mariadb-install-db: Initialize a MariaDB database. More information: <https://manned.org/mariadb-install-db>.
mariadb-binlog: Utility for processing MariaDB binary log files. More information: <https://manned.org/mariadb-binlog>.
mapfile: This command is an alias of `readarray`.
manim: Animation engine for explanatory math videos. More information: <https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/tutorials/quickstart.html>.
man: Format and display manual pages. See also: `whatis`, `apropos`. More information: <https://manned.org/man>.
mamba: Fast, cross-platform package manager, intended as a drop-in replacement for conda. Some subcommands such as `repoquery` have their own usage documentation. See also: `conda`. More information: <https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/mamba.html>.
mamba-repoquery: Efficiently query conda and mamba package repositories and package dependencies. More information: <https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/mamba.html#repoquery>.
makepasswd: Generate and encrypt passwords. More information: <https://manned.org/makepasswd>.
makensis: Cross-platform compiler for NSIS installers. It compiles an NSIS script into a Windows installer executable. More information: <https://nsis.sourceforge.io/Docs/Chapter3.html>.
makebuildserver: Create an F-Droid build server virtual machine. More information: <https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Build_Server_Setup/>.
make: Task runner for targets described in Makefile. Mostly used to control the compilation of an executable from source code. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/make/manual/make.html>.
mailx: Send and receive mail. More information: <https://manned.org/mailx>.
mailsy: Quickly generate a disposable email using `mail.tm` API. More information: <https://github.com/BalliAsghar/Mailsy#usage>.
mail: Operate on the user's mailbox. To send an email the message body is built from `stdin`. More information: <https://manned.org/mail>.
maigret: Collect OSINT information about usernames across thousands of websites. Note: The Maigret database is a local JSON file bundled with the tool. See also: `sherlock`. More information: <https://maigret.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage-examples.html>.
magick: Create, edit, compose, or convert between image formats. This tool replaces `convert` in ImageMagick 7+. See `magick convert` to use the old tool in versions 7+. Some subcommands such as `mogrify` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/magick.php>.
magick-montage: Tile images into a customizable grid. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/montage.php>.
magick-mogrify: Perform operations on multiple images, such as resizing, cropping, flipping, and adding effects. Changes are applied directly to the original file. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/mogrify.php>.
magick-import: Capture some or all of an X server screen and save the image to a file. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/import.php>.
magick-identify: Describe the format and characteristics of image files. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/identify.php>.
magick-convert: Convert between image formats, scale, join, and create images, and much more. Note: This tool (previously `convert`) has been replaced by `magick` in ImageMagick 7+. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/convert.php>.
magick-compare: Create a comparison image to visually annotate the difference between two images. More information: <https://imagemagick.org/script/compare.php>.
magento: Manage the Magento PHP framework. More information: <https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/tools/cli-reference/commerce-on-premises>.
maestral: A lightweight Dropbox client for macOS and Linux. More information: <https://maestral.app/cli>.
mado: A fast Markdown linter for CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown. More information: <https://github.com/akiomik/mado>.
macptopbm: Read a MacPaint file as input and produce a PBM image as output. See also: `pbmtomacp`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/macptopbm.html>.
machine_role.py: Determine the role of a remote Windows machine (e.g. domain controller, member server, or workstation). Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
macchina: Display information about your computer. More information: <https://github.com/Macchina-CLI/macchina>.
m4b-tool: Merge, split, and manipulate audiobook files with chapters. More information: <https://github.com/sandreas/m4b-tool>.
lzop: Compress or decompress files with LZO compression. More information: <https://www.lzop.org/lzop_man.php>.
lzmore: This command is an alias of `xzmore`.
lzma: This command is an alias of `xz --format lzma`.
lzless: This command is an alias of `xzless`.
lzip: A lossless data compressor with a user interface similar to `gzip` or `bzip2`. Lzip uses a simplified form of the "Lempel-Ziv-Markovchain-Algorithm" (LZMA) stream format and provides 3-factor integrity checking to maximize interoperability and optimize safety. More information: <https://www.nongnu.org/lzip/manual/lzip_manual.html#Invoking-lzip>.
lzgrep: This command is an alias of `xzgrep`.
lzfgrep: This command is an alias of `xzgrep --fixed-strings`.
lzegrep: This command is an alias of `xzgrep --extended-regexp`.
lzdiff: This command is an alias of `xzdiff`.
lzcmp: This command is an alias of `xzcmp`.
lzcat: This command is an alias of `xz --format lzma --decompress --stdout`.
lz4: Compress or decompress `.lz4` files. More information: <https://github.com/lz4/lz4>.
lwp-request: Simple HTTP client. Built with libwww-perl. More information: <https://metacpan.org/pod/lwp-request>.
lumen: An installer for the Lumen micro-framework. More information: <https://lumen.laravel.com>.
ludusavi: Back up video game save data. More information: <https://github.com/mtkennerly/ludusavi/blob/master/docs/cli.md>.
luantiserver: This command is an alias of `luanti --server`.
luanti: Infinite-world block sandbox game. More information: <https://manned.org/luanti>.
lualatex: An extended version of TeX using Lua to compile. More information: <https://texdoc.org/serve/tex.man1.pdf/0>.
luajit: A just-in-time compiler (JIT) for the Lua programming language. See also: `lua`. More information: <https://luajit.org/luajit.html>.
lua: A powerful, light-weight embeddable programming language. More information: <https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/lua.html>.
lt: Localtunnel exposes your localhost to the world for easy testing and sharing. More information: <https://github.com/localtunnel/localtunnel>.
lsyncd: Watch files and directories and run `rsync` when they change. It is often used to keep two directories on separate systems in sync, ensuring that changes made in one directory are immediately mirrored to the other. More information: <https://github.com/lsyncd/lsyncd/blob/master/docs/manpage/lsyncd.1.txt>.
lstopo: Show the hardware topology of the system. More information: <https://manned.org/lstopo>.
lspath: List the contents of the `$PATH` environment variable, with optional paging. More information: <https://github.com/clementi/lspath>.
lsof: List open files and the corresponding processes. Note: Root privileges are required to list files opened by others. More information: <https://manned.org/lsof>.
lsix: List and display images in sixel format on the terminal. See also: `img2sixel`. More information: <https://github.com/hackerb9/lsix>.
lsd: List directory contents. The next generation `ls` command, written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/lsd-rs/lsd/blob/main/doc/lsd.md>.
lsar: List an archive file's contents. See also: `unar`, `ar`. More information: <https://manned.org/lsar>.
lpstat: Show status information about printers. See also: `lp`, `lpoptions`. More information: <https://manned.org/lpstat>.
lprm: Cancel queued print jobs of a server. See also: `lpq`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lprm.html>.
lpr: Print files. See also: `lpstat`, `lpadmin`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lpr.html>.
lpq: Show printer queue status. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lpq.html>.
lpoptions: Display or set printer options and defaults. See also: `lpadmin`, `lp`, `lpstat`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lpoptions.html>.
lpmove: Move a job or all jobs to another printer. See also: `cancel`, `lp`, `lpr`, `lprm`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lpmove.html>.
lpinfo: List connected printers and installed drivers for the CUPS print server. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lpinfo.html>.
lpass: Interface for the LastPass password manager. More information: <https://lastpass.github.io/lastpass-cli/lpass.1.html>.
lpadmin: Configure CUPS printers and classes. See also: `lpoptions`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-lpadmin.html>.
lp: Print files. See also: `lpstat`, `lpoptions`. More information: <https://manned.org/lp>.
lorem: Create some random Latin looking placeholder text. More information: <https://manned.org/lorem>.
lore: Version control system by Epic Games. Optimized for projects combining code with large binary assets. More information: <https://github.com/EpicGames/lore/blob/main/docs/reference/lore-cli-commands.md>.
look: Display lines beginning with a prefix in a file. Note: The lines in the file must be sorted. See also: `grep`, `sort`. More information: <https://manned.org/look>.
longbridge: AI-native tool for Longbridge Securities - real-time market data, portfolio management, and trading. More information: <https://open.longbridge.com/docs/cli>.
lolcat: Put a rainbow in everything you `cat` to the console. More information: <https://manned.org/lolcat>.
logstash: An Elasticsearch ETL (extract, transform, and load) tool. Commonly used to load data from various sources (such as databases and log files) into Elasticsearch. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/logstash>.
logout: Exit a login shell. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-logout>.
logname: Show the user's login name. See also: `id`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/logname-invocation.html>.
logger: Add messages to the system log. More information: <https://manned.org/logger>.
loft: Install and manage multi-tenant Kubernetes environments using virtual clusters. More information: <https://loft.sh/docs/cli/loft/>.
locust: Load-testing tool to determine number of concurrent users a system can handle. More information: <https://docs.locust.io/en/stable/configuration.html#configuration>.
local: Declare local variables and give them attributes. See also: `declare`, `export`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-local>.
loc: Count lines of code. Written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/cgag/loc>.
loadtest: Run a load test on the selected HTTP or WebSockets URL. More information: <https://github.com/alexfernandez/loadtest#usage>.
ln: Create links to files and directories. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/ln-invocation.html>.
lmms: Free, open source, cross-platform digital audio workstation. Render a `.mmp` or `.mmpz` project file, dump a `.mmpz` as XML, or start the GUI. See also: `mixxx`. More information: <https://manned.org/lmms>.
llvm-strings: This command is an alias of `strings`.
llvm-objdump: This command is an alias of `objdump`.
llvm-nm: This command is an alias of `nm`.
llvm-mc: LLVM Machine Code Playground. It provides a set of tools for working with LLVM machine code. Part of LLVM. More information: <https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-mc.html>.
llvm-gcc: This command is an alias of `clang`.
llvm-g++: This command is an alias of `clang++`.
llvm-dis: Convert LLVM bitcode files into human-readable LLVM Intermediate Representation (IR). More information: <https://www.llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-dis.html>.
llvm-config: Get various configuration information needed to compile programs which use LLVM. Typically called from build systems, like in Makefiles or configure scripts. More information: <https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-config.html>.
llvm-cat: Concatenate LLVM Bitcode (`.bc`) files. More information: <https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/llvm/tools/llvm-cat/llvm-cat.cpp>.
llvm-as: LLVM Intermediate Representation (`.ll`) to Bitcode (`.bc`) assembler. More information: <https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-as.html>.
llvm-ar: This command is an alias of `ar`.
llvd: Linkedin Learning Video Downloader. More information: <https://github.com/knowbee/llvd>.
llm: Interact with Large Language Models (LLMs) via remote APIs and models that can be installed and run on your machine. More information: <https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/help.html>.
llm-models: Manage models available to the `llm` command. More information: <https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/help.html#llm-models-help>.
llm-logs: Explore prompts and responses logged to an SQLite database by the `llm` command. More information: <https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/help.html#llm-logs-help>.
llm-keys: Manage stored API keys for different models. More information: <https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/help.html#llm-keys-help>.
llm-install: Install Python packages in the same environment as LLM, typically to add plugins. More information: <https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/help.html#llm-install-help>.
lli: Directly execute programs from LLVM bitcode. More information: <https://www.llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/lli.html>.
lldb: The LLVM Low-Level Debugger. More information: <https://lldb.llvm.org/man/lldb.html>.
llc: Compile LLVM Intermediate Representation or bitcode to target-specific assembly language. More information: <https://www.llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llc.html>.
live-server: A simple development HTTP server with live reload capability. More information: <https://github.com/tapio/live-server>.
litert-lm: Run and manage LiteRT-LM models. More information: <https://developers.google.com/edge/litert-lm/cli/usage>.
lit: LLVM integrated tester for executing LLVM and Clang style test suites, summarizing results. Part of LLVM. More information: <https://www.llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/lit.html>.
lispmtopgm: Convert a Lisp Machine bitmap into a PGM image. See also: `pgmtolispm`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/lispmtopgm.html>.
linode-cli: Manage Linode cloud services. Some subcommands such as `events` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli>.
linode-cli-tickets: Manage Linode Support Tickets. More information: <https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/cli-commands-for-account-management>.
linode-cli-object-storage: Manage Linode Object Storage. More information: <https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/cli-commands-for-object-storage>.
linode-cli-lke: Manage Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE) clusters. More information: <https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/cli-commands-for-lke>.
linode-cli-domains: Manage Linode Domains and DNS configuration. More information: <https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/cli-commands-for-the-dns-manager>.
linkchecker: Client to check HTML documents and websites for broken links. More information: <https://linkchecker.github.io/linkchecker/man/linkchecker.html>.
link: Create a hard link to an existing file. For more options, see the `ln` command. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/link-invocation.html>.
limactl: Virtual machine manager for Linux guests, with multiple VM templates available. Can be used to run containers on macOS, but also for generic virtual machine use cases on macOS and Linux hosts. More information: <https://github.com/lima-vm/lima>.
lima: This command is an alias of `limactl shell` for the default VM instance. You can also set the `$LIMA_INSTANCE` environment variable to work on a different instance.
lilypond: Typeset music and/or produce MIDI from file. See also: `musescore`. More information: <https://lilypond.org/doc/latest/Documentation/usage/command_002dline-usage>.
lighthouse: Analyze web applications and web pages. Collects modern performance metrics and insights on developer best practices. More information: <https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse#cli-options>.
light-arionum-cli: The PHP light wallet for the Arionum cryptocurrency. More information: <https://github.com/arionum/lightWalletCLI#usage>.
license: Create license files for open-source projects. More information: <https://nishanths.github.io/license/>.
librewolf: This command is an alias of `firefox`. More information: <https://librewolf.net/>.
libreoffice: This command is an alias of `soffice`.
lex: This command is an alias of `flex`.
let: Evaluate arithmetic expressions in shell. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-let>.
lesskey: Customize keybindings for `less`. Note: This command is deprecated. More information: <https://manned.org/lesskey>.
less: Open a file for interactive reading, allowing scrolling and search. More information: <https://manned.org/less>.
less-than-more-than: Open a file descriptor for read and write. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Opening-File-Descriptors-for-Reading-and-Writing>.
lerna: Manage JavaScript projects with multiple packages. More information: <https://lerna.js.org/docs/api-reference/commands>.
lein: Manage Clojure projects with declarative configuration. More information: <https://manned.org/lein>.
ledger: A powerful, double-entry accounting system. More information: <https://ledger-cli.org/doc/ledger.1.html>.
lebab: A JavaScript modernizer for transpiling code to ES6/ES7. Transformations must be provided for all examples. More information: <https://github.com/lebab/lebab>.
leave: Set a reminder for when it's time to leave. To remove reminders use `kill $(pidof leave)`. More information: <https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=leave>.
leaftoppm: Convert an Interleaf image to a PPM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/leaftoppm.html>.
ldc: D compiler using LLVM as a backend. More information: <https://wiki.dlang.org/Using_LDC>.
ldapsearch: Query an LDAP directory. More information: <https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/tool-usages/ldapsearch.html>.
ld: Link object files together. More information: <https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/ld.html#Options>.
lckdo: Note: This command is deprecated, use `flock` instead. More information: <https://manned.org/lckdo>.
lb: Manage a blog contained in the current directory. Drafts and posts to operate on are selected interactively when running the commands. More information: <https://github.com/LukeSmithxyz/lb#usage>.
lazygit: A simple terminal UI for Git commands, providing an intuitive interface for managing repositories. More information: <https://manned.org/lazygit>.
lazydocker: A terminal UI for managing Docker containers, images, volumes, and more. More information: <https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazydocker>.
laydown: Prepare for Daily Standup. More information: <https://github.com/badjr13/laydown>.
lavat: Display an animated lava lamp effect in the terminal. Customize colors, speed, size, movement, and display style. More information: <https://github.com/AngelJumbo/lavat#usage>.
latexpand: Simplify LaTeX source files by removing comments and resolving `\include`s, `\input`s, etc. More information: <https://www.ctan.org/pkg/latexpand>.
latexmk: Compile LaTeX source files into finished documents. Automatically does multiple runs when needed. More information: <https://mg.readthedocs.io/latexmk.html>.
latexdiff: Determine differences between two LaTeX files. More information: <https://ctan.org/pkg/latexdiff>.
latex: Compile a DVI document from LaTeX source files. More information: <https://texdoc.org/serve/tex.man1.pdf/0>.
lastcomm: Show last commands executed. More information: <https://manned.org/lastcomm>.
laravel: Installer for the Laravel framework. More information: <https://laravel.com/docs/installation>.
laravel-zero: An installer for the Laravel Zero framework. More information: <https://laravel-zero.com/>.
lando: Local development environment and DevOps tool built on Docker. More information: <https://docs.lando.dev/cli/>.
lame: Encode WAV to MP3 files. More information: <https://svn.code.sf.net/p/lame/svn/trunk/lame/USAGE>.
lambo: A super-powered `laravel new` for Laravel and Valet. Some subcommands such as `new` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/tighten/lambo#usage>.
lambo-new: A super-powered `laravel new` for Laravel and Valet. More information: <https://github.com/tighten/lambo#lambo-commands>.
l2ping: Send an L2CAP echo request and receive an answer. More information: <https://manned.org/l2ping>.
