go-install: Compile and install packages named by the import paths. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Compile_and_install_packages_and_dependencies>.
go-get: Add a dependency package, or download packages in legacy GOPATH mode. Note: `./...` is a Go package pattern understood by Go tooling. It matches the current package and all packages recursively under the current directory. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Add_dependencies_to_current_module_and_install_them>.
go-generate: Generate Go files by running commands within source files. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Generate_Go_files_by_processing_source>.
go-fmt: Format Go source files, printing the changed filenames. Note: `./...` is a Go package pattern understood by Go tooling. It matches the current package and all packages recursively under the current directory. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Gofmt__reformat__package_sources>.
go-fix: Update packages to use new APIs. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Update_packages_to_use_new_APIs>.
go-env: Manage environment variables used by the Go toolchain. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Print_Go_environment_information>.
go-doc: View documentation for a package or symbol. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Show_documentation_for_package_or_symbol>.
go-clean: Remove object files and cached files. More information: <https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Remove_object_files_and_cached_files>.
gnuplot: A graph plotter that outputs in several formats. More information: <https://manned.org/gnuplot>.
gnugo: Play Go on the command-line. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gnugo/gnugo_3.html>.
gnuchess: Play chess against an engine. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/chess/manual/gnuchess.html#Running-GNU-Chess>.
gnucash: Personal and small-business financial-accounting software. More information: <https://manned.org/gnucash>.
gnucash-cli: A command-line version of GnuCash. More information: <https://gnucash.org/viewdoc.phtml?rev=5&lang=C&doc=help>.
gnomon: Utility to annotate console logging statements with timestamps and find slow processes. More information: <https://github.com/paypal/gnomon#options>.
gnmic: A gNMI client. Manage gNMI network device configuration and view operational data. More information: <https://gnmic.openconfig.net/user_guide/configuration_flags/>.
gnmic-subscribe: Subscribe to a gnmic network device state updates. More information: <https://gnmic.openconfig.net/cmd/subscribe/>.
gnmic-sub: This command is an alias of `gnmic subscribe`.
gnmic-set: Modify gnmi network device configuration. More information: <https://gnmic.openconfig.net/cmd/set/>.
gnmic-get: Get a snapshot of a gnmi network device operation data. More information: <https://gnmic.openconfig.net/cmd/get/>.
gnatprep: Preprocessor for Ada source code files (part of the GNAT toolchain). More information: <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gnat_ugn/Preprocessing-with-gnatprep.html>.
gnatmake: A low-level build tool for Ada programs (part of the GNAT toolchain). More information: <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gnat_ugn/Switches-for-gnatmake.html>.
gmssl: Crypto toolkit supporting SM1, SM2, SM3, SM4, SM9, and ZUC/ZUC256. More information: <http://gmssl.org/english.html>.
gml2gv: Convert a graph from `gml` to `gv` format. Converters: `gml2gv`, `gv2gml`, `gv2gxl`, `gxl2gv`, `graphml2gv` & `mm2gv`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/gml2gv.1.pdf>.
glxgears: Test OpenGL rendering. See also: `vkcube`. More information: <https://manned.org/glxgears>.
glow: Render Markdown in the terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/glow>.
glob: `glob` patterns are patterns used to match and search text. Note: `glob` isn't a command, but syntax to be used with other commands or the shell. See also: `regex`. More information: <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glob_(programming)>.
glib-compile-resources: Compile resource files (e.g. images) into a binary resource bundle. These may be linked into GTK applications using the GResource API. More information: <https://manned.org/glib-compile-resources>.
gleam: The compiler, build tool, package manager, and code formatter for Gleam, "a friendly language for building type-safe systems that scale!". More information: <https://gleam.run/writing-gleam/command-line-reference/>.
glances: A cross-platform system monitoring tool. See also: `htop`, `atop`, `top`, `btm`, `btop`. More information: <https://nicolargo.github.io/glances/>.
gladtex: A LaTeX formula preprocessor for HTML files. It converts LaTeX formulas to images. More information: <https://manned.org/gladtex>.
glab: Work seamlessly with GitLab. Some subcommands such as `repo` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/tree/main/docs/source>.
glab-repo: Work with GitLab repositories. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/repo/_index.md>.
glab-pipeline: List, view, and run GitLab CI/CD pipelines. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/_index.md>.
glab-mr: Manage GitLab merge requests. Some subcommands such as `create` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/mr/_index.md>.
glab-mr-merge: Merge GitLab merge requests. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/mr/merge.md>.
glab-mr-create: Manage GitLab merge requests. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/mr/create.md>.
glab-auth: Authenticate with a GitLab host. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/auth/_index.md>.
glab-alias: Manage GitLab CLI command aliases. More information: <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/alias/_index.md>.
gixy-next: Analyze NGINX configuration files for security and performance misconfigurations. More information: <https://gixy.io/usage/>.
gitwatch: Automatically commit file or directory changes to a Git repository. More information: <https://github.com/gitwatch/gitwatch>.
gitui: A lightweight keyboard-only TUI for Git. See also: `tig`, `git-gui`. More information: <https://github.com/gitui-org/gitui>.
gitstats: Git repository statistics generator. More information: <https://gitstats.readthedocs.io/en/stable/getting-started.html#command-line-usage>.
gitsome: A terminal-based interface for GitHub, accessed via the `gh` command. It also provides menu-style autocomplete suggestions for `git` commands. More information: <https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome#index>.
gitmoji: Interactively insert emojis on commits. More information: <https://github.com/carloscuesta/gitmoji-cli>.
gitman: Language-agnostic dependency manager using Git. Clones repositories listed in `gitman.yml` and pins each one to a branch, tag, or commit. More information: <https://gitman.readthedocs.io>.
gitlint: Git commit message linter checks your commit messages for style. More information: <https://jorisroovers.com/gitlint/>.
gitleaks: Detect secrets and API keys leaked in Git repositories. More information: <https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks#usage>.
gitlab: Ruby wrapper for the GitLab API. Some subcommands such as `ctl` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://narkoz.github.io/gitlab/>.
gitlab-ctl: Manage the GitLab omnibus. More information: <https://docs.gitlab.com/omnibus/maintenance/>.
gitlab-backup: Manage backups for a GitLab Omnibus installation. See also: `gitlab-ctl`, `gitlab-runner`. More information: <https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/backup_restore/backup_gitlab/>.
gitk: Browse Git repositories graphically. See also: `git gui`, `git cola`, `tig`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/gitk>.
gitea: Administer Gitea, a lightweight Git hosting server. Requires a configured `app.ini` file or environment variables. More information: <https://docs.gitea.com/administration/command-line>.
gita: Manage multiple Git repositories side by side. See also: `git`. More information: <https://github.com/nosarthur/gita>.
git: Distributed version control system. Some subcommands such as `commit`, `add`, `branch`, `switch`, `push`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git>.
git-write-tree: Low level utility to create a tree object from the current index. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-write-tree>.
git-worktree: Manage multiple working trees attached to the same repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree>.
git-whatchanged: This command is an alias of `git log --raw --no-merges` (log with raw diffs for each commit). Note: This command is deprecated and will be removed in the future. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-whatchanged>.
git-verify-tag: Check for GPG verification of tags. If a tag wasn't signed, an error will occur. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-verify-tag>.
git-verify-pack: Verify packed Git archive files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-verify-pack>.
git-verify-commit: Check for GPG verification of commits. If no commits are verified, nothing will be printed, regardless of options specified. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-verify-commit>.
git-var: Print a Git logical variable's value. See `git config`, which is preferred over `git var`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-var>.
git-utimes: Change files' modification times to their last commit dates. Does not touch files that are in the working tree or index. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-utimes>.
git-update-server-info: Update auxiliary repository information for dumb servers (a regular web server that only serves files). More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-server-info>.
git-update-ref: Git command for creating, updating, and deleting Git refs. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-ref>.
git-update-index: Git command for manipulating the index. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-index>.
git-unpack-objects: Git command for unpacking objects from a packed archive. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-unpack-objects>.
git-unpack-file: Create a temporary file with a blob's contents. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-unpack-file>.
git-unlock: Unlock a file in a Git repository so it can be modified by a commit. Part of `git-extras`. See also: `git lock`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-unlock>.
git-undo: Undo recent commits. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-undo>.
git-touch: Create new files and add them to the index. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-touch>.
git-tag: Create, list, delete, or verify tags. A tag is a static reference to a commit. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-tag>.
git-sync: Sync local branches with remote branches. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-sync>.
git-symbolic-ref: Read, change, or delete files that store references. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-symbolic-ref>.
git-switch: Switch between Git branches. Requires Git version 2.23+. See also: `git checkout`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-switch>.
git-svn: Bidirectional operation between a Subversion repository and Git. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-svn>.
git-summary: Display information about a Git repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-summary>.
git-subtree: Merge subtrees together or split repository into subtrees. More information: <https://manned.org/git-subtree>.
git-submodule: Inspect, update, and manage submodules. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-submodule>.
git-stripspace: Read text (e.g. commit messages, notes, tags, and branch descriptions) from `stdin` and clean it into the manner used by Git. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-stripspace>.
git-status: Show the changes to files in a Git repository. List changed, added, and deleted files compared to the currently checked-out commit. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-status>.
git-stash: Stash local Git changes in a temporary area. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-stash>.
git-standup: See commits from a specified user. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-standup>.
git-stamp: Stamp the last commit message, with the possibility to reference issue numbers from your bug tracker or link to its review page. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-stamp>.
git-stage: This command is an alias of `git add`.
git-squash: Squash multiple commits into a single commit. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-squash>.
git-sparse-checkout: Check out only part of a repository's files instead of cloning or checking out everything. More information: <https://manned.org/git-sparse-checkout>.
git-sizer: Compute various Git repository size metrics and alert you to any that might cause problems or inconvenience. More information: <https://github.com/github/git-sizer>.
git-show: Show various types of Git objects (commits, tags, etc.). More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-show>.
git-show-unmerged-branches: Print all branches which are not merged into the current `HEAD`. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-show-unmerged-branches>.
git-show-tree: Show a decorated tree graph with all branches of a Git repository, showing annotations. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-show-tree>.
git-show-ref: Git command for listing references. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-show-ref>.
git-show-merged-branches: Print all branches which are merged into the current head. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-show-merged-branches>.
git-show-index: Show the packed archive index of a Git repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-show-index>.
git-show-branch: Show branches and their commits. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-show-branch>.
git-shortlog: Summarize the `git log` output. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-shortlog>.
git-setup: Create a Git repository in a directory and commit all files. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-setup>.
git-send-email: Send a collection of patches as emails. Patches can be specified as files, directories, or a revision list. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-send-email>.
git-sed: Replace patterns in git-controlled files using sed. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-sed>.
git-secret: Store private data inside a Git repository. Written in Bash. More information: <https://github.com/sobolevn/git-secret>.
git-scp: Copy files from the current working tree to the working directory of a remote repository. Part of `git-extras`. Uses `rsync` to transfer files. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-scp>.
git-rscp: Reverse `git scp` - copy files from the working directory of a remote repository to the current working tree. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-scp>.
git-root: Print the root directory of the current Git repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-root>.
git-rm: Remove files from repository index and local filesystem. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rm>.
git-revert: Create new commits which reverse the effect of earlier ones. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-revert>.
git-rev-parse: Display metadata related to revisions. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse>.
git-rev-list: List revisions (commits) in reverse chronological order. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-list>.
git-restore: Restore working tree files. Requires Git version 2.23+. See also: `git checkout`, `git reset`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-restore>.
git-reset: Undo commits or unstage changes by resetting the current Git HEAD to the specified state. If a path is passed, it works as "unstage"; if a commit hash or branch is passed, it works as "uncommit". More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-reset>.
git-reset-file: Revert a file to `HEAD` or a commit. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-reset-file>.
git-rerere: Reuse fixes for merge conflicts. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rerere>.
git-request-pull: Generate a request asking the upstream project to pull changes into its tree. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-request-pull>.
git-replace: Create, list, and delete refs to replace objects. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-replace>.
git-repl: Git REPL (read-evaluate-print-loop) - an interactive Git shell. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-repl>.
git-repack: Pack unpacked objects in a Git repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-repack>.
git-rename-tag: Rename a Git tag. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-rename-tag>.
git-rename-remote: Change remote for pulling and pushing. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-rename-remote>.
git-rename-branch: Rename a Git branch. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-rename-branch>.
git-remote: Manage set of tracked repositories ("remotes"). More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-remote>.
git-release: Create a Git tag for a release. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-release>.
git-reflog: Show a log of changes to local references like HEAD, branches, or tags. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-reflog>.
git-rebase: Reapply commits from one branch on top of another branch. Commonly used to "move" an entire branch to another base, creating copies of the commits in the new location. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rebase>.
git-rebase-patch: Find the commit the patch applies to and do a rebase. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-rebase-patch>.
git-reauthor: Change details about an author identity. Since this command rewrites the Git history, `--force` will be needed when pushing next time. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-reauthor>.
git-range-diff: Compare two commit ranges (e.g. two versions of a branch). More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-range-diff>.
git-push: Push commits to a remote repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push>.
git-pull: Fetch branch from a remote repository and merge it to local repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pull>.
git-pull-request: Create a pull request for a project on GitHub. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-pull-request>.
git-psykorebase: Rebase a branch on top of another using a merge commit while requiring conflict resolution only once. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-psykorebase>.
git-prune: Git command for pruning all unreachable objects from the object database. This command is often not used directly but as an internal command that is used by Git gc. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-prune>.
git-pr: Check out GitHub pull requests locally. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-pr>.
git-paste: Send commits to a pastebin site using `pastebinit`. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-paste>.
git-p4: Import from and submit to Perforce repositories. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-p4>.
git-obliterate: Delete files and erase their history from a Git repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-obliterate>.
git-notes: Add or inspect object notes. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-notes>.
git-name-rev: Describe a commit using existing ref names. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-name-rev>.
git-mv: Move or rename files and update the Git index. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-mv>.
git-mr: Check out GitLab merge requests locally. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-mr>.
git-mktree: Build a tree object using `ls-tree` formatted text. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-mktree>.
git-missing: Show commits which aren't shared between two branches. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-missing>.
git-mergetool: Run merge conflict resolution tools to resolve merge conflicts. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-mergetool>.
git-merge-tree: Merge branches without changing files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-tree>.
git-merge-repo: Merge two repository histories. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-merge-repo>.
git-merge-one-file: Resolve a single file merge after a trivial merge. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-one-file>.
git-merge-into: Merge one branch into another branch. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-merge-into>.
git-merge-index: Run a merge program on files that need merging. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-index>.
git-merge-base: Find a common ancestor of two commits. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-base>.
git-maintenance: Run tasks to optimize Git repository data. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-maintenance>.
git-mailinfo: Extract patch and authorship information from a single email message. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-mailinfo>.
git-magic: Automate add, commit, and push routines. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-magic>.
git-ls-tree: List the contents of a tree object. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-tree>.
git-ls-remote: Git command for listing references in a remote repository based on name or URL. If no name or URL are given, then the configured upstream branch will be used, or remote origin if the former is not configured. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-remote>.
git-ls-files: Show information about files in the index and the working tree. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-files>.
git-log: Show a history of commits. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log>.
git-locked: List locked files in a Git repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-locked>.
git-lock: Lock a file in a Git repository from being modified by a commit. Part of `git-extras`. See also: `git unlock`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-lock>.
git-local-commits: Show local commits that haven't been pushed to origin. Any additional arguments will be passed directly to `git log`. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-local-commits>.
git-lfs: Work with large files in Git repositories. More information: <https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/tree/main/docs>.
git-lfs-transfer: Server-side implementation of the Git LFS pure SSH transfer protocol. Allows Git LFS to upload and download large files over SSH instead of HTTPS. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/git-lfs-transfer#usage>.
git-instaweb: Helper to launch a GitWeb server. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-instaweb>.
git-init: Initialize a new local Git repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init>.
git-info: Display Git repository information. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-info>.
git-imerge: Perform a merge or rebase between two Git branches incrementally. Conflicts between branches are tracked down to pairs of individual commits, to simplify conflict resolution. More information: <https://github.com/mhagger/git-imerge>.
git-ignore: Show/update `.gitignore` files. Part of `git-extras`. See also: `git ignore-io`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-ignore>.
git-ignore-io: Generate `.gitignore` files from predefined templates. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-ignore-io>.
git-help: Display help information about Git. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-help>.
git-hash-object: Compute the unique hash key of content and optionally create an object with specified type. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-hash-object>.
git-guilt: Show total blame count for files with unstaged changes or calculate the change in blame between two revisions. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-guilt>.
git-gui: A GUI for Git to manage branches, commits, and remotes, and perform local merges. See also: `git cola`, `gitk`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-gui>.
git-grep: Find strings inside tracked files in a repository. Accepts a lot of the same flags as regular `grep`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep>.
git-graft: Merge commits from a branch into another branch and delete the source branch. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-graft>.
git-gh-pages: Create a new branch inside the current repository called `gh-pages`. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-gh-pages>.
git-get-tar-commit-id: Extract commit ID from an archive created using `git archive`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-get-tar-commit-id>.
git-gc: Optimize the local repository by cleaning unnecessary files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-gc>.
git-fsck: Verify the validity and connectivity of nodes in a Git repository index. Note: Does not make any modifications. See also: `git gc`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fsck>.
git-fresh-branch: Create an empty local branch. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-fresh-branch>.
git-format-patch: Prepare `.patch` files. Useful when emailing commits elsewhere. See also: `git am`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-format-patch>.
git-fork: Fork a GitHub repo. Like `git clone` but forks first. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-fork>.
git-force-clone: Get the basic functionality of `git clone`, but if the destination Git repository already exists it will force-reset it to resemble a clone of the remote. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-force-clone>.
git-for-each-repo: Run a Git command on a list of repositories. Note: This command is experimental and may change. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-for-each-repo>.
git-for-each-ref: List and optionally format references (branches, tags) in a Git repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-for-each-ref>.
git-flow: A collection of Git extensions to provide high-level repository operations. More information: <https://github.com/nvie/gitflow>.
git-filter-repo: A versatile tool for rewriting Git history. See also: `bfg`. More information: <https://github.com/newren/git-filter-repo>.
git-filter-branch: Change branch history, like removing files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-filter-branch>.
git-fetch: Download objects and refs from a remote repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fetch>.
git-feature: Create or merge feature branches. Feature branches obey the format feature/name. More information: <https://manned.org/git-feature>.
git-fast-export: Export the contents and history of a Git repository in a streamable, plain-text format. More information: <https://manned.org/git-fast-export>.
git-fame: Pretty-print Git repository contributions. More information: <https://manned.org/git-fame>.
git-effort: Display how much activity a file has had, showing commits per file and "active days", i.e. the total number of days with contributions to the file. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-effort>.
git-difftool: Show file changes using external diff tools. Accepts the same options and arguments as `git diff`. See also: `git diff`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-difftool>.
git-diff: Show changes to tracked files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff>.
git-diff-tree: Compare the content and mode of blobs found via two tree objects. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff-tree>.
git-diff-index: Compare the working directory with a commit or tree object. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff-index>.
git-diff-files: Compare files using their sha1 hashes and modes. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff-files>.
git-describe: Give an object a human-readable name based on an available ref. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-describe>.
git-delta: List files that differ from another branch. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-delta>.
git-delete-tag: Delete existing local and remote tags. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-delete-tag>.
git-delete-submodule: Delete a submodule from a Git repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-delete-submodule>.
git-delete-squashed-branches: Delete branches that have been "squashed-merged" into a specified branch and checkout. If no branch is specified, default to the currently checked out branch. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-delete-squashed-branches>.
git-delete-merged-branches: Delete branches that are listed in `git branch --merged` excluding master. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-delete-merged-branches>.
git-delete-branch: Delete local and remote Git branches. Part of `git-extras`. If deleting the checked out branch, only the remote branch will be deleted. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-delete-branch>.
git-daemon: A really simple server for Git repositories. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-daemon>.
git-cvsexportcommit: Export a single `Git` commit to a CVS checkout. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cvsexportcommit>.
git-credential: Retrieve and store user credentials. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-credential>.
git-credential-store: Git helper to store passwords on disk. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-credential-store>.
git-credential-cache: Git helper to temporarily store passwords in memory. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-credential-cache>.
git-create-branch: Create a Git branch in a repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-create-branch>.
git-cp: Copy an existing file to a new location, preserving history. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-cp>.
git-count: Print the total number of commits. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-count>.
git-count-objects: Count the number of unpacked objects and their disk consumption. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-count-objects>.
git-contrib: Display commits from an author. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-contrib>.
git-continue: This command is an alias of `git abort`.
git-config: Manage custom configuration options for Git repositories. These configurations can be local (for the current repository) or global (for the current user). More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config>.
git-commits-since: Display commits since a time or date. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-commits-since>.
git-commit: Commit files to the repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit>.
git-commit-tree: Low level utility to create commit objects. See also: `git commit`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit-tree>.
git-commit-graph: Write and verify Git commit-graph files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit-graph>.
git-column: Display data in columns. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-column>.
git-cola: A powerful Git GUI with a slick and intuitive user interface. More information: <https://git-cola.readthedocs.io/en/latest/git-cola.html>.
git-coauthor: Add another author to the latest commit. Since this command rewrites the Git history, `--force` will be needed when pushing next time. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-coauthor>.
git-clone: Clone an existing repository. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone>.
git-cliff: A highly customizable changelog generator. More information: <https://git-cliff.org/docs/usage/args/>.
git-clear: Clear a Git working directory as if it was freshly cloned with the current branch including files in `.gitignore`. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-clear>.
git-clear-soft: Clear a Git working directory as if it was freshly cloned with the current branch excluding files in `.gitignore`. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-clear-soft>.
git-clean: Remove files not tracked by Git from the working tree. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clean>.
git-cherry: Find commits that have yet to be applied upstream. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cherry>.
git-cherry-pick: Apply the changes introduced by existing commits to the current branch. To apply changes to another branch, first use `git checkout` to switch to the desired branch. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cherry-pick>.
git-checkout: Check out a branch or paths to the working tree. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout>.
git-checkout-index: Copy files from the index to the working tree. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout-index>.
git-check-ref-format: Check if a reference name is acceptable, and exit with a non-zero status if it is not. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ref-format>.
git-check-mailmap: Show canonical names and email addresses of contacts. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-mailmap>.
git-check-ignore: Analyze and debug Git ignore/exclude (`.gitignore`) files. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ignore>.
git-check-attr: For every pathname, list if each attribute is unspecified, set, or unset as a gitattribute on that pathname. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-attr>.
git-changelog: Generate a changelog report from repository commits and tags. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-changelog>.
git-cat-file: Provide content or type and size information for Git repository objects. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cat-file>.
git-bundle: Package objects and references into an archive. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bundle>.
git-bulk: Execute operations on multiple Git repositories. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-bulk>.
git-bugreport: Capture debug information from the system and user, generating a text file to aid in the reporting of a bug in Git. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bugreport>.
git-bug: A distributed bug tracker that uses Git's internal storage, so no files are added to your project. You may submit your problems to the same Git remote you use to interact with others, much like commits and branches. More information: <https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/doc/md/git-bug.md>.
git-brv: Print a list of branches, sorted by last commit date. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-brv>.
git-browse: View an upstream repository in the default browser. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-browse>.
git-browse-ci: Open the current Git repository's CI website in the default web browser. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-browse-ci>.
git-branch: Main Git command for working with branches. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-branch>.
git-blame: Show what commit and author last modified each line of a file. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-blame>.
git-blame-someone-else: Blame someone else for your bad code. More information: <https://github.com/jayphelps/git-blame-someone-else>.
git-bisect: Use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug. Git automatically jumps back and forth in the commit graph to progressively narrow down the faulty commit. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bisect>.
git-authors: Generate a list of committers of a Git repository. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://manned.org/git-authors>.
git-archive: Create an archive of files from a tree. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-archive>.
git-archive-file: Export all the files of the current Git branch into a Zip archive. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-archive-file>.
git-apply: Apply a patch to files and/or to the index without creating a commit. See also: `git am`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-apply>.
git-annotate: Show commit hash and last author on each line of a file. See `git blame`, which is preferred over `git annotate`. `git annotate` is provided for those familiar with other version control systems. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-annotate>.
git-annex: Manage files with Git, without checking their contents in. When a file is annexed, its content is moved into a key-value store, and a symlink is made that points to the content. More information: <https://git-annex.branchable.com/git-annex/>.
git-am: Apply patch files and create a commit. Useful when receiving commits via email. See also: `git format-patch`. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-am>.
git-alias: Create shortcuts for Git commands. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-alias>.
git-add: Stage changed files for a commit. More information: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-add>.
git-abort: Abort an ongoing rebase, merge, or cherry-pick. Part of `git-extras`. More information: <https://github.com/tj/git-extras/blob/main/Commands.md#git-abort>.
gimp: GNU image manipulation program. See also: `krita`. More information: <https://docs.gimp.org/en/gimp-fire-up.html#gimp-concepts-running-command-line>.
giftopnm: Convert a GIF file into a PNM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/giftopnm.html>.
gifsicle: Create, edit, manipulate, and get information about GIF files. More information: <https://www.lcdf.org/gifsicle/>.
gifdiff: Compare two GIFs for identical visual appearance. See also: `gifsicle`. More information: <https://www.lcdf.org/gifsicle/>.
ghq: Manage remote repository clones organized by hostname and path. More information: <https://github.com/x-motemen/ghq>.
ghostty: A fast, feature-rich, and cross-platform terminal emulator that uses platform-native UI and GPU acceleration. Note: All options from the configuration file can also be used on the command-line (using `--option=argument`). More information: <https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference>.
ghost: A blogging platform and headless CMS. More information: <https://docs.ghost.org/ghost-cli>.
ghdl: Open-source simulator for the VHDL language. More information: <https://ghdl.github.io/ghdl/>.
ghcup: Haskell toolchain installer. Install, manage, and update Haskell toolchains. More information: <https://gitlab.haskell.org/haskell/ghcup-hs>.
ghcid: Simple and efficient CLI IDE for Haskell that reloads code on file changes. Continuously displays compile errors, warnings, and test results. More information: <https://github.com/ndmitchell/ghcid>.
ghci: The Glasgow Haskell Compiler's interactive environment. More information: <https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/latest/docs/users_guide/ghci.html>.
ghc: The Glasgow Haskell Compiler. Compiles and links Haskell source files. More information: <https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/latest/docs/users_guide/usage.html>.
gh: Work seamlessly with GitHub. Some subcommands such as `config` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh>.
gh-workflow: List, view, and run GitHub Actions workflows. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_workflow>.
gh-variable: Manage GitHub Actions and Dependabot variables. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_variable>.
gh-status: Check the status of subscribed repositories on GitHub. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_status>.
gh-stack: A GitHub CLI extension for managing stacked branches and pull requests. More information: <https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands>.
gh-ssh-key: Manage GitHub SSH keys. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_ssh-key>.
gh-skyline: Generate a 3D model of your GitHub contribution history. By default, it will create a `{username}-{year}-github-skyline.stl` file in the current directory. More information: <https://github.com/github/gh-skyline>.
gh-secret-set: Create or update GitHub secrets. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_secret_set>.
gh-search: Search across all of GitHub. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_search>.
gh-screensaver: Extension for GitHub CLI that runs animated terminal screensavers. See also: `gh extension`. More information: <https://github.com/vilmibm/gh-screensaver>.
gh-run: View, run, and watch recent GitHub Actions workflow runs. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run>.
gh-ruleset: Manage GitHub repository rulesets. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_ruleset>.
gh-rs: This command is an alias of `gh ruleset`.
gh-repo: Work with GitHub repositories. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo>.
gh-repo-create: Create a new GitHub repository. Note: `--public`, `--private`, or `--internal` is required when not running interactively. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_create>.
gh-reference: Display a reference about the GitHub CLI command. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_reference>.
gh-project: Work with GitHub Projects. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_project>.
gh-preview: Preview GitHub CLI programs for testing and development purposes. These commands are unstable and may change at any time. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_preview>.
gh-pr: Manage GitHub pull requests. Some subcommands such as `create` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr>.
gh-pr-view: View details of a GitHub pull request. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_view>.
gh-pr-merge: Merge a GitHub pull request. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_merge>.
gh-pr-create: Manage GitHub pull requests. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create>.
gh-pr-comment: Add a comment to a GitHub pull request. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_comment>.
gh-pr-checks: View CI checks for a GitHub pull request. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_checks>.
gh-org: Work with GitHub organizations. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_org>.
gh-mintty: Display help about MinTTY integration for the GitHub CLI command. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_mintty>.
gh-label: Work with GitHub labels. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_label>.
gh-issue-create: Create GitHub issues on a repository. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_create>.
gh-help: Display help about the GitHub CLI command. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help>.
gh-gpg-key: Manage GPG keys registered with the authorized GitHub account. See also: `gpg`. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_gpg-key>.
gh-gist: Work with GitHub Gists. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_gist>.
gh-formatting: Formatting options for JSON data exported from gh GitHub CLI command. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_formatting>.
gh-extension: Manage extensions for the GitHub CLI. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_extension>.
gh-environment: Display help about environment variables for the GitHub CLI command. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment>.
gh-cs: This command is an alias of `gh codespace`.
gh-copilot: Interact with GitHub Copilot. Note: This command is deprecated, use `copilot` instead. More information: <https://github.com/github/gh-copilot#usage>.
gh-config: Change configuration for GitHub CLI. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_config>.
gh-completion: Generate shell completion scripts for GitHub CLI commands. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_completion>.
gh-codespace: Connect and manage your codespaces in GitHub. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_codespace>.
gh-cache: Manage GitHub Actions caches. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_cache>.
gh-browse: Open a GitHub repository in the browser or print the URL. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_browse>.
gh-auth: Authenticate with a GitHub host. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth>.
gh-attestation: Download and verify artifact attestations to ensure their integrity and provenance. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation>.
gh-at: This command is an alias of `gh attestation`.
gh-api: Make authenticated HTTP requests to the GitHub API and print the response. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api>.
gh-alias: Manage GitHub CLI command aliases. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_alias>.
gh-agent: This command is an alias of `gh agent-task`.
gh-agent-task: Manage GitHub agent tasks. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_agent-task>.
gh-accessibility: Learn about GitHub CLI's accessibility experiences. More information: <https://cli.github.com/manual/>.
gh-a11y: This command is an alias of `gh accessibility`.
gfortran: Preprocess and compile Fortran source files, then assemble and link them together. More information: <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gfortran/Invoking-GNU-Fortran.html>.
getuserspns.py: Retrieve Service Principal Names (SPNs) associated with Active Directory user accounts. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
gettgt.py: Request a Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT). Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
gettext: Translate a string using stored translations in a compiled `.mo` file. Translations are stored in `/usr/share/locale/locale_name/LC_MESSAGES/` with `domain` being the filename without its extension. See also: `msgfmt`, `msgunfmt`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#gettext-Invocation>.
getst.py: Request a Kerberos Service Ticket (TGS). Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
getopts: Parse shell options from arguments. Note: This command does not support longform options and thus using `getopt` is recommended instead. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-getopts>.
getnpusers.py: Enumerate Active Directory accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled, which may be susceptible to AS-REP roasting attacks. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
getln: This command is an alias of `read -zr`.
geth: The go-ethereum command-line interface. More information: <https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/fundamentals/command-line-options>.
getarch.py: Determine the OS architecture (x86 or x64) of a remote Windows system. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
getadusers.py: Retrieve a list of users from Active Directory, including attributes like last logon timestamp and email. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
get_iplayer: Indexing tool and personal video recorder for BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds. More information: <https://github.com/get-iplayer/get_iplayer/wiki/manpage>.
get-nodeversions: List installed and available Node.js versions for `ps-nvm`. Part of `ps-nvm` and can only be run under PowerShell. More information: <https://github.com/aaronpowell/ps-nvm>.
get-nodeinstalllocation: Get the current Node.js installation directory for `ps-nvm`. Part of `ps-nvm` and can only be run under PowerShell. More information: <https://github.com/aaronpowell/ps-nvm>.
ges-launch-1.0: Create and render multimedia timelines. More information: <https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/documentation/tools/ges-launch.html>.
gendesk: Specify the command to generate a `.desktop` file and a download icon with minimal information. More information: <https://manned.org/gendesk>.
gemtopnm: Convert a GEM image file into a PNM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/gemtopnm.html>.
gemtopbm: This command has been superseded by `gemtopnm`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/gemtopbm.html>.
gemini: Launch an interactive prompt with Gemini AI. More information: <https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/cli-reference/>.
gem: A package manager for the Ruby programming language. More information: <https://guides.rubygems.org/command-reference/>.
gdu: Disk usage analyzer with console interface. More information: <https://github.com/dundee/gdu#usage>.
gdrive: Interact with Google Drive. Folder/file ID can be obtained from the Google Drive folder or ID URL. More information: <https://github.com/prasmussen/gdrive>.
gdown: Download files from Google Drive and other URLs. More information: <https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown#usage>.
gdmsetup: Launch a GUI for configuring the GNOME Display Manager (GDM). Results in edited files in either `/etc/X11/gdm/gdm.conf` or `/etc/gdm/gdm.conf` depending on distribution and environment. See also: `gdm`, `gdm-binary`, `gdm-stop`, `gdm-restart`, `gdm-safe-restart`. More information: <https://manned.org/gdm>.
gdm: The GNOME Display Manager (GDM) is a replacement for the X Display Manager (XDM). See also: `gdm-binary`, `gdmsetup`, `gdm-stop`, `gdm-restart`, `gdm-safe-restart`. More information: <https://manned.org/gdm>.
gdm-stop: Immediately stop running the GNOME Display Manager (GDM). See also: `gdm`, `gdm-binary`, `gdmsetup`, `gdm-restart`, `gdm-safe-restart`. More information: <https://manned.org/gdm>.
gdm-safe-restart: Restart the GNOME Display Manager (GDM) only when all users have logged out. See also: `gdm`, `gdm-binary`, `gdmsetup`, `gdm-stop`, `gdm-restart`. More information: <https://manned.org/gdm>.
gdm-restart: Restart the GNOME Display Manager (GDM) daemon. See also: `gdm`, `gdm-binary`, `gdmsetup`, `gdm-stop`, `gdm-safe-restart`. More information: <https://manned.org/gdm>.
gdm-binary: This command is an alias of `gdm`.
gdc: D compiler using GCC as a backend. More information: <https://wiki.dlang.org/Using_GDC>.
gdalwarp: Image reprojection and warping utility. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdalwarp.html>.
gdalinfo: List various information about a GDAL supported raster dataset. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdalinfo.html>.
gdaldem: Analyze and visualize digital elevation models (DEM). More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdaldem.html>.
gdalbuildvrt: Build Virtual Datasets from a list of existing datasets. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdalbuildvrt.html>.
gdaladdo: Build overview images of raster datasets. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdaladdo.html>.
gdal_translate: Convert raster data between different formats. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdal_translate.html>.
gdal_contour: Create contour lines and polygons from a digital elevation model. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdal_contour.html>.
gdal2tiles.py: Generate TMS or XYZ tiles for a raster dataset. More information: <https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdal2tiles.html>.
gcrane: Container images managing tool. This tool implements a superset of the `crane` commands, with additional commands that are specific to Google Container Registry (`gcr.io`). Some subcommands such as `copy`, `gc`, `help`, `ls`, etc. have their own usage documentation. See also: `crane`. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/gcrane/README.md>.
gcrane-ls: List the tags in a repository. More complex form than `crane ls`, which allows for listing tags, manifest, and sub-repositories. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/gcrane/README.md>.
gcrane-help: Help provides help for any command in the application. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/gcrane/README.md>.
gcrane-gc: List images that are not tagged. Will calculate images that can be garbage-collected. This can be composed with `gcrane delete` to actually garbage collect them. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/gcrane/README.md>.
gcrane-copy: Efficiently copy a remote image from source to target while retaining the digest value. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/gcrane/README.md>.
gcpdiag: Google Cloud Platform troubleshooting and diagnostics tool. Run in a Docker container or in GCP Cloudshell. More information: <https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcpdiag#usage>.
gcloud: The official CLI tool for Google Cloud Platform. Some subcommands such as `app`, `init`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud>.
gcloud-version: Print version information for Google Cloud CLI components. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/version>.
gcloud-topic: Display supplementary help for topics not directly associated with individual commands. See also: `gcloud help`. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/topic>.
gcloud-sql-export-sql: Export data from a Cloud SQL instance to an SQL file in Google Cloud Storage. Useful for creating backups or migrating data. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/sql/export/sql>.
gcloud-sql-backups-describe: Retrieve information about a backup. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/sql/backups/describe>.
gcloud-projects: Manage project access policies in Google Cloud. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/projects>.
gcloud-logging-logs-list: List logs in a Google Cloud project. Useful for identifying available logs for monitoring and analysis. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/logging/logs/list>.
gcloud-kms-decrypt: Decrypt a ciphertext file using a Cloud KMS key. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/kms/decrypt>.
gcloud-init: Launch an interactive workflow to set up `gcloud` or reinitialize configurations. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/init>.
gcloud-info: Display information about the current `gcloud` environment. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/info>.
gcloud-iam: Configure Identity and Access Management (IAM) preferences and service accounts. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/iam>.
gcloud-help: Display help and reference information for `gcloud`. See also: `gcloud topic`. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/help>.
gcloud-feedback: Provide feedback to the Google Cloud team. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/feedback>.
gcloud-container: Manage containerized applications on Kubernetes and clusters. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container>.
gcloud-config: Manage different configurations of `gcloud`. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/config>.
gcloud-config-set: Set a property in the Google Cloud CLI configuration. Properties control various aspects of Google Cloud CLI behavior. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/config/set>.
gcloud-compute: Create, run, and manage VMs on Google Cloud infrastructure. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/compute>.
gcloud-components: Manage Google Cloud CLI components. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/components>.
gcloud-auth: Grant and revoke authorization to `gcloud` and manage credentials. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/auth>.
gcloud-app: Build scalable applications on a managed serverless platform. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/app>.
gcc: Preprocess and compile C and C++ source files, then assemble and link them together. Part of GCC (GNU Compiler Collection). More information: <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/>.
gcalcli: Interact with Google Calendar. Requests Google API authorization upon first launch. More information: <https://github.com/insanum/gcalcli>.
gc: Count nodes, edges, connected components, or clusters in Graphviz `.dot` files. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/gc.1.pdf>.
gawk: GNU version of awk, a versatile programming language for working on files. See also: `awk`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gawk/manual/gawk.html>.
gau: Get All URLs: fetch known URLs from AlienVault's Open Threat Exchange, the Wayback Machine, and Common Crawl for any domains. More information: <https://github.com/lc/gau#usage>.
gatsby: Static site generator for React. More information: <https://www.gatsbyjs.com/docs/reference/gatsby-cli/>.
ganache-cli: Command-line version of Ganache, your personal blockchain for Ethereum development. More information: <https://archive.trufflesuite.com/ganache/>.
gammastep: Adjust the screen's color temperature according to the time of day. See also: `redshift`. More information: <https://manned.org/gammastep>.
gallery-dl: Download image galleries and collections from several image hosting sites. More information: <https://github.com/mikf/gallery-dl>.
gacutil: Global Assembly Cache (GAC) management utility. More information: <https://manned.org/gacutil>.
g++: Compile C++ source files. Part of GCC (GNU Compiler Collection). More information: <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/C_002b_002b-Dialect-Options.html>.
fzf: Fuzzy finder. See also: `sk`. More information: <https://github.com/junegunn/fzf#usage>.
fx: View and process JSON. More information: <https://fx.wtf/getting-started>.
fusermount: Mount and unmount FUSE filesystems. More information: <https://manned.org/fusermount>.
funzip: Print the content of the first (non-directory) member in an archive without extraction. More information: <https://manned.org/funzip>.
function: Define a function. See also: `declare`, `unset`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Shell-Functions>.
func: Azure Functions Core Tools: develop and test Azure Functions locally. Local functions can connect to live Azure services, and can deploy a function app to an Azure subscription. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-run-local>.
fuck: Correct your previous console command. More information: <https://github.com/nvbn/thefuck>.
ftp: Tools to interact with a server via File Transfer Protocol. More information: <https://manned.org/ftp>.
fswebcam: Small and simple webcam for *nix. More information: <https://www.sanslogic.co.uk/fswebcam/>.
fswatch: A cross-platform file change monitor. More information: <https://emcrisostomo.github.io/fswatch/>.
fstopgm: Convert a Usenix FaceSaver file into a PGM image. See also: `pgmtofs`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/fstopgm.html>.
fselect: Find files with SQL-like queries. More information: <https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/blob/master/docs/usage.md>.
frps: Quickly set up a reverse proxy service. Part of `frp`. More information: <https://github.com/fatedier/frp>.
frpc: Connect to a `frps` server to start proxying connections on the current host. Part of `frp`. More information: <https://github.com/fatedier/frp>.
frp: Fast Reverse Proxy: quickly set up network tunnels to expose certain services to the Internet or other external networks. Note: `frp` isn't a command, but a set of commands. More information: <https://github.com/fatedier/frp#example-usage>.
from: Print mail header lines from the current user's mailbox. More information: <https://mailutils.org/manual/html_chapter/Programs.html#frm-and-from>.
frida: A dynamic instrumentation toolkit for developers, reverse-engineers, and security researchers. More information: <https://frida.re/docs/frida-cli/>.
frida-trace: Dynamically trace function calls. More information: <https://frida.re/docs/frida-trace/>.
frida-ps: List processes on a local or remote device. More information: <https://frida.re/docs/frida-ps/>.
freshclam: Update virus definitions for ClamAV antivirus program. More information: <https://docs.clamav.net/manual/Usage/SignatureManagement.html#freshclam>.
fresh: A fully-featured terminal-based text editor. More information: <https://getfresh.dev/docs/>.
freeze: Generate images of code and terminal output. Supported formats are PNG, SVG, and WebP. See also: `silicon`. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/freeze#flags>.

fpsync: Execute several synchronization processes locally or on several remote workers through SSH. More information: <https://manned.org/fpsync>.
fping: A more powerful ping which can ping multiple hosts. More information: <https://fping.org/fping.8.html>.

fossil-new: This command is an alias of `fossil init`.
fossil-init: Initialize a new repository for a project. More information: <https://fossil-scm.org/home/help/init>.
fossil-forget: This command is an alias of `fossil rm`, with the exception that it never removes files from the disk. More information: <https://fossil-scm.org/home/help/forget>.
fossil-delete: Remove files or directories from Fossil version control. See also: `fossil forget`. More information: <https://fossil-scm.org/home/help/delete>.

fortune: Print a random quotation (fortune-cookie style). More information: <https://manned.org/fortune>.
forever: Server-side JavaScript application that makes sure Node.js applications run indefinitely (restarts after exit). More information: <https://github.com/foreversd/forever#usage>.
for: Perform a command several times. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Looping-Constructs>.
footclient: Start a new terminal window handled by the `foot` server. Note: `foot --server` must be started before using the client. More information: <https://manned.org/footclient>.
foot: A fast, lightweight, and minimalistic Wayland terminal emulator. More information: <https://manned.org/foot>.
fold: Folds long lines for fixed-width output devices. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/fold-invocation.html>.
fnm: Fast Node.js version manager. More information: <https://github.com/Schniz/fnm/blob/master/docs/commands.md>.
fmtutil: Manage TeX formats and Metafont bases. More information: <https://manned.org/fmtutil>.
fmtutil-user: This command is an alias of `fmtutil --user`.
fmtutil-sys: This command is an alias of `fmtutil --sys`.
fmt: Reformat a text file by joining its paragraphs and limiting the line width to a number of characters (75 by default). More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/fmt-invocation.html>.
fluxctl: Tool for Flux v1. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/migration/>.
flux: Continuous and progressive delivery solution for Kubernetes. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/cmd/>.
flux-uninstall: Uninstall Flux and its custom resource definitions. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/cmd/flux_uninstall/>.
flux-resume: Resume suspended Flux resources. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/cmd/flux_resume/>.
flux-reconcile: Trigger a reconciliation of Flux sources and resources. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/cmd/flux_reconcile/>.
flux-get: Display the status of Flux resources. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/cmd/flux_get/>.

flux-check: Check Flux prerequisites and cluster health. More information: <https://fluxcd.io/flux/cmd/flux_check/>.

flutter: Google's free, open source, and cross-platform mobile app SDK. Some subcommands such as `pub` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/docs/tool/README.md>.
flutter-pub: Flutter's package manager. Note: Packages are available on <https://pub.dev>. More information: <https://docs.flutter.dev/packages-and-plugins/using-packages>.

flox: Easy to use Nix package and environment manager. More information: <https://flox.dev/docs/reference/command-reference/flox/>.
flow: A static type checker for JavaScript. More information: <https://flow.org/en/docs/cli/>.
float: Declare floating point variable(s). Equivalent to `typeset -E` except that options irrelevant to floating point numbers are not permitted. See also: `typeset`, `declare`. More information: <https://manned.org/zshbuiltins>.
flips: Create and apply IPS and BPS patches. More information: <https://git.disroot.org/Sir_Walrus/Flips>.
flexget: A multipurpose automation tool for content like torrents, nzbs, podcasts, comics, series, movies, etc. More information: <https://flexget.com/en/CLI>.
flask: A general utility script for Flask applications. Loads the application defined in the `$FLASK_APP` environment variable. More information: <https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/cli/>.
flask-unsign: A tool to brute-force, decode, and craft `Flask` session cookies. More information: <https://github.com/Paradoxis/Flask-Unsign>.
flarectl: Official CLI for Cloudflare. More information: <https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-go/blob/v0/cmd/flarectl/README.md>.
flake8: Check the style and quality of Python code. More information: <https://flake8.pycqa.org/en/latest/user/options.html>.
flac: Encode, decode, and test FLAC files. More information: <https://xiph.org/flac/documentation_tools_flac.html>.
fkill: Fabulously kill processes. Cross-platform. More information: <https://manned.org/fkill>.
fj: Interact with Forgejo instances from the terminal. More information: <https://codeberg.org/forgejo-contrib/forgejo-cli>.
fitstopnm: Convert a Flexible Image Transport System (FITS) file to a PNM image. See also: `pamtofits`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/fitstopnm.html>.
fisher: Fisher, a fish-shell plugin manager. Install plugins by name or from a managed `fishfile` for bundled installs. More information: <https://github.com/jorgebucaran/fisher>.
fish: The Friendly Interactive SHell, a command-line interpreter designed to be user friendly. More information: <https://fishshell.com/docs/current/cmds/fish.html>.
firefox: A free and open source web browser. More information: <https://wiki.mozilla.org/Firefox/CommandLineOptions>.
firebase: Test, manage, and deploy Firebase projects. More information: <https://github.com/firebase/firebase-tools>.
fio: Flexible I/O tester: do an I/O action spawning multiple threads or processes. More information: <https://fio.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fio_doc.html>.
finger: User information lookup program. More information: <https://manned.org/finger>.
find: Find files or directories under a directory tree, recursively. See also: `fd`. More information: <https://manned.org/find>.
filen: Interface with Filen, an end-to-end encrypted cloud storage service. More information: <https://github.com/FilenCloudDienste/filen-cli>.
filecheck: Flexible pattern matching file verifier. It is typically used from LLVM regression tests and forms a part of a `lit` test. More information: <https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/FileCheck.html>.

file: Determine file type. See also: `stat`. More information: <https://manned.org/file>.
file-rename: This command is an alias of `rename`.
figlist: List the figlet fonts and control files. See also: `figlet`, `showfigfonts`, `chkfont`. More information: <https://manned.org/figlist>.
figlet: Generate ASCII banners from user input. See also: `showfigfonts`. More information: <https://www.figlet.org/figlet-man.html>.

fgrep: This command is an alias of `grep --fixed-strings`.
fg: Run jobs in foreground. See also: `jobs`, `bg`, `disown`, `%`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-fg>.

feh: Lightweight image viewing utility. More information: <https://man.finalrewind.org/1/feh/>.
fdupes: Find duplicate files in a set of directories. More information: <https://github.com/adrianlopezroche/fdupes#introduction>.
fdroidcl: Manage F-Droid apps of devices connected via ADB. More information: <https://github.com/Hoverth/fdroidcl#commands>.

fdfind: This command is an alias of `fd`.
fd: Find entries in the filesystem. See also: `find`, `regex`. More information: <https://github.com/sharkdp/fd#command-line-options>.
fd-type: Search for specific filetypes. More information: <https://manned.org/fd>.
fcrackzip: ZIP archive password cracking utility. More information: <https://manned.org/fcrackzip>.
fclones: Efficient duplicate file finder and remover. More information: <https://github.com/pkolaczk/fclones#usage>.
fc: Open the recent commands for editing and then run them. See also: `history`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-fc>.

fastlane: Build and release mobile applications. More information: <https://docs.fastlane.tools/actions/>.
fastfetch: Display information about your operating system, software, and hardware. More information: <https://manned.org/fastfetch>.

fastapi: Run FastAPI apps which uses Uvicorn under the hood. More information: <https://manned.org/fastapi>.
fast: Test your download and upload speed using fast.com. More information: <https://github.com/sindresorhus/fast-cli>.
far2l: Linux and macOS port of FAR Manager. More information: <https://github.com/elfmz/far2l>.
false: Return a non-zero exit code. See also: `true`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-false>.
faker: A Python library and a tool to generate fake data. More information: <https://faker.readthedocs.io/en/master/>.
fakedata: Generate fake data using a large variety of generators. More information: <https://github.com/lucapette/fakedata>.
factor: Print the prime factorization of a number. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/factor-invocation.html>.

expose: An open source tunnel application for sharing websites. More information: <http://expose.dev/docs/introduction>.
export: Export shell variables to child processes. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-export>.
expo: Build, develop, and deploy React Native apps. More information: <https://docs.expo.dev/eas/>.
expand: Convert tabs to spaces. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/expand-invocation.html>.

exenv: Easily install Elixir versions and manage application environments. More information: <https://github.com/mururu/exenv>.
exec: Execute a command without creating a child process. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-exec>.
exa: A modern replacement for `ls` (List directory contents). Note: `exa` is no longer maintained. Use `eza` instead. See also: `eza`. More information: <https://github.com/ogham/exa#command-line-options>.
ex: Text editor. This command is an alias of `vim -e`. More information: <https://www.vim.org/>.
evil-winrm: Windows Remote Management (WinRM) shell for pentesting. Once connected, we get a PowerShell prompt on the target host. More information: <https://github.com/Hackplayers/evil-winrm>.
eval: Execute arguments as a single command in the current shell and return its result. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-eval>.
eva: Simple calculator REPL, similar to `bc`, with syntax highlighting and persistent history. More information: <https://github.com/oppiliappan/eva#usage>.
etcdctl: Interact with `etcd`, a highly-available key-value pair store. More information: <https://etcd.io/docs/latest/dev-guide/interacting_v3/>.
etcd: A distributed, reliable key-value store for the most critical data of a distributed system. More information: <https://etcd.io/docs/latest/op-guide/configuration/#command-line-flags>.
esptool.py: Bootloader utility for Espressif chips (e.g. ESP8266). More information: <https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esptool/en/latest/esp32/>.
espeak: A multi-lingual software speech synthesizer. Note: `espeak` is considered discontinued, as development has shifted to `espeak-ng`. More information: <https://manned.org/espeak>.
espeak-ng: A multi-lingual software speech synthesizer. See also: `speak-ng`, `espeak`. More information: <https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng/blob/master/src/espeak-ng.1.ronn>.
espanso: Cross-platform Text Expander written in Rust. More information: <https://espanso.org/docs/command%20lIne/cli_list/>.
eslint: A pluggable linting utility for JavaScript and JSX. More information: <https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/command-line-interface>.
escp2topbm: Convert a PBM image to an ESC/P2 printer file. See also: `pbmtoescp2`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/escp2topbm.html>.
esbuild: JavaScript bundler and minifier built for speed. More information: <https://esbuild.github.io/api/#general-options>.
esac: This shell keyword is used to end a `case` statement.
errno: Look up errno names and descriptions. More information: <https://joeyh.name/code/moreutils/>.
ern: Electrode Native platform client. More information: <https://native.electrode.io/reference/index-6>.
erl: Run and manage programs in the Erlang programming language. More information: <https://erlang.org/documentation/doc-16.0/erts-16.0/doc/html/erl_cmd.html>.
eqn: Equation preprocessor for the groff (GNU Troff) document formatting system. See also: `troff`, `groff`. More information: <https://manned.org/eqn>.
eol: Show end-of-life dates (EoLs) for a number of products. More information: <https://github.com/hugovk/norwegianblue#example-command-line-use>.
envsubst: Substitute environment variables with their value in shell format strings. Variables to be replaced should be in either `${var}` or `$var` format. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#envsubst-Invocation>.
envoy: A PHP-based task manager for Laravel remote servers. More information: <https://laravel.com/docs/envoy>.
env: Show the environment or run a program in a modified environment. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/env-invocation.html>.
entr: Run arbitrary commands when files change. See also: `watchexec`. More information: <https://eradman.com/entrproject/>.
enscript: Convert text files to PostScript, HTML, RTF, ANSI, and overstrikes. More information: <https://manned.org/enscript>.
encfs: Mount or create encrypted virtual filesystems. See also: `fusermount`. More information: <https://manned.org/encfs>.
enca: Detect and convert the encoding of text files. More information: <https://manned.org/enca>.
enable: Enable and disable shell builtins. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-enable>.
emulate: Reset shell options to match a certain shell's behavior. Also used to ensure a shell function runs with the default configuration. More information: <https://github.com/antonio/zsh-config/blob/master/help/emulate>.
ember: Ember CLI: create and manage Ember.js applications. More information: <https://cli.emberjs.com/release/advanced-use/cli-commands-reference/>.
emacsclient: Open files in an existing Emacs server. See also: `emacs`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/emacsclient-Options.html>.
emacs: The extensible, customizable, self-documenting, real-time display editor. See also: `emacsclient`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs>.
elvish: Expressive programming language and a versatile interactive shell. See also: `nu`. More information: <https://elv.sh/ref/command.html>.
else: This shell keyword is used in combination with `if` and `elif` to define a code branch if no other branch was valid.
elm: Compile and run Elm source files. More information: <https://guide.elm-lang.org/install/elm.html>.
elixir: Elixir programming language interpreter. More information: <https://manned.org/elixir>.
elinks: A text based browser similar to `lynx`. More information: <https://github.com/rkd77/elinks>.
elif: This shell keyword is used in combination with `if` and `else` to define a code branch.
electrum: Ergonomic Bitcoin wallet and private key management. More information: <https://manned.org/electrum>.
electron-packager: Build Electron app executables for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Requires a valid `package.json` in the application directory. More information: <https://github.com/electron/packager>.
elasticsearch-users: Manage native realm users in Elasticsearch, including creating, updating, and deleting users. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/users-command>.
