elasticsearch-syskeygen: Create a system key file in the Elasticsearch configuration directory. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/syskeygen>.
elasticsearch-saml-metadata: Generate SAML Service Provider metadata for configuring a SAML Identity Provider. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/saml-metadata>.
elasticsearch-reset-password: Reset the passwords of users in the native realm and built-in users. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/reset-password>.
elasticsearch-node: Manage low-level Elasticsearch node operations such as shutdown, repurpose, or viewing info. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/node-tool>.
elasticsearch-keystore: Manage secure settings (e.g., passwords, tokens, and credentials) used by Elasticsearch. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/elasticsearch-keystore>.
elasticsearch-croneval: Validate and evaluate a `cron` expression. This command helps verify that `cron` expressions are valid for use with Elasticsearch and produce the expected results. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/elasticsearch-croneval>.
elasticsearch-create-enrollment-token: Create enrollment tokens for Elasticsearch nodes and Kibana instances. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/create-enrollment-token>.
elasticsearch-certutil: Generate and manage SSL certificates for Elasticsearch security. More information: <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/command-line-tools/certutil>.
eksctl: The official CLI for Amazon EKS. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/eksctl/what-is-eksctl.html>.
eim: Install and manage ESP-IDF. More information: <https://docs.espressif.com/projects/idf-im-ui/en/latest/cli_commands.html>.
egrep: Find patterns in files using extended `regex`es. Note: This command is an alias of `grep --extended-regexp`. See also: `regex`. More information: <https://manned.org/egrep>.
eget: Easily install prebuilt binaries from GitHub. More information: <https://github.com/zyedidia/eget#usage>.
edit: This command is an alias of `run-mailcap --action=edit`.
edgepaint: Colorize edges of a graph layout to clarify crossing edges. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/edgepaint.1.pdf>.
ed: The original Unix text editor. See also: `awk`, `sed`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/ed/manual/ed_manual.html>.
ect: Efficient Compression Tool. File optimizer written in C++. It supports PNG, JPEG, gzip, and Zip files. More information: <https://github.com/fhanau/Efficient-Compression-Tool>.
ecpg: Embedded SQL preprocessor for C programs. More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-ecpg.html>.
echo: Print given arguments. See also: `printf`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/echo-invocation.html>.
ebook-convert: Can be used to convert e-books between common formats, e.g. PDF, EPUB, and MOBI. Part of the Calibre e-book library tool. More information: <https://manual.calibre-ebook.com/generated/en/ebook-convert.html>.
dzdo: Execute privileged commands as root or another user via Active Directory roles. Similar to `sudo` but integrated with Delinea; supports Ansible become plugin. More information: <https://docs.delinea.com/online-help/server-suite/commandref/centrify-command-reference-2025.pdf#page=102>.
dwebp: `dwebp` decompresses WebP files into PNG, PAM, PPM, or PGM images. Animated WebP files are not supported. More information: <https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/dwebp/>.
dvc: Data Version Control system for machine learning projects. Some subcommands such as `commit` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference>.
dvc-unfreeze: Unfreeze stages in the DVC pipeline. This allows DVC to start tracking changes in stage dependencies again after they were frozen. See also: `dvc freeze`. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/unfreeze>.
dvc-init: Initialize a new local DVC repository. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/init>.
dvc-gc: Remove unused files and directories from the cache or remote storage. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/gc>.
dvc-freeze: Freeze stages in the DVC pipeline. This prevents DVC from tracking changes in stage dependencies and re-execution until unfreeze. See also: `dvc unfreeze`. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/freeze>.
dvc-fetch: Download DVC tracked files and directories from a remote repository. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/fetch>.
dvc-diff: Show changes in DVC tracked file and directories. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/diff>.
dvc-destroy: Remove all DVC files and directories from a DVC project. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/destroy>.
dvc-dag: Visualize the pipeline(s) defined in `dvc.yaml`. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/dag>.
dvc-config: Low level command to manage custom configuration options for dvc repositories. These configurations can be on project, local, global, or system level. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/config>.
dvc-commit: Record changes to DVC-tracked files in the project. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/commit>.
dvc-checkout: Check out data files and directories from cache. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/checkout>.
dvc-add: Add changed files to the index. More information: <https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/add>.
dust: Give an instant overview of which directories are using disk space. See also: `du`, `ncdu`. More information: <https://github.com/bootandy/dust#usage>.
duplicity: Create incremental, compressed, encrypted, and versioned backups. Can also upload the backups to a variety of backend services. Note: Depending on the version, some options may not be available (e.g. `--gio` in 2.0.0). More information: <https://duplicity.gitlab.io/stable/duplicity.1.html#name>.
duplicacy: A lock-free deduplication cloud backup tool. More information: <https://github.com/gilbertchen/duplicacy/wiki>.
dunstify: A notification tool that is an extension of `notify-send`, but has more features based around `dunst`. Accepts all options of `notify-send`. More information: <https://dunst-project.org/documentation/dunstify/>.
dunstctl: Control the `dunst` notification daemon. More information: <https://dunst-project.org/documentation/dunstctl/>.
dunst: A lightweight and customizable notification daemon for X11 and Wayland. If not started manually, D-Bus will automatically start `dunst` when a notification is sent. More information: <https://dunst-project.org/documentation/dunst/>.
dune: A build system for OCaml programs. More information: <https://dune.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/cli.html>.
dumpntlminfo.py: Perform NTLM authentication against a remote host without credentials and dump information leaked in the NTLMSSP message. Part of the Impacket suite. More information: <https://github.com/fortra/impacket>.
dumpkeys: Dump keyboard translation tables. More information: <https://manned.org/dumpkeys>.
dumpcap: A network traffic dump tool. More information: <https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/dumpcap.html>.
duf: Disk Usage/Free Utility. See also: `ncdu`, `df`. More information: <https://github.com/muesli/duf#usage>.
duckdb: Client for DuckDB, an in-process analytical SQL engine. More information: <https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/cli/arguments>.
duc: A collection of tools for indexing, inspecting, and visualizing disk usage. Duc maintains a database of accumulated sizes of directories of the filesystem, allowing queries in this database, or creating fancy graphs to show where data is. More information: <https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/zevv/duc/blob/master/doc/duc.1.html>.
dub: Package manager for D packages. More information: <https://dub.pm/commandline/>.
dua: Dua (Disk Usage Analyzer): get the disk space usage of a directory. More information: <https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli>.
du: Disk usage: estimate and summarize file and directory space usage. See also: `ncdu`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/du-invocation.html>.
dtrx: "Do The Right eXtraction" - extract any archive into new directory by guessing the tool from extension. More information: <https://github.com/dtrx-py/dtrx>.
dtc: The Device Tree Compiler, a tool for recompiling device trees between formats. More information: <https://manned.org/dtc>.
dtach: Run a program in a session you can detach from and reattach to. See also: `screen`, `tmux`, `abduco`. More information: <https://manned.org/dtach>.
drush: Shell and scripting interface for Drupal. More information: <https://www.drush.org/latest/usage/>.
drupal: Generate boilerplate code, interact with and debug Drupal projects. Note: This command is deprecated, use `drush` instead. Some subcommands such as `check` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://drupalize.me/topic/drupal-console>.
drupal-check: Check Drupal PHP code for deprecations. More information: <https://github.com/mglaman/drupal-check#usage>.
dropuser: Remove an existing PostgreSQL user (role). More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-dropuser.html>.
dropdb: Remove a PostgreSQL database. A simple wrapper around the SQL command `DROP DATABASE`. More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-dropdb.html>.
drill: Perform various DNS queries. More information: <https://manned.org/drill>.
doxygen: A documentation system for various programming languages. More information: <https://manned.org/doxygen>.
doxx: View `.docx` files in the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx#-command-line-options>.
dotty: A customizable interactive graph editor for the X Window System. Note: This command is deprecated. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/dotty.1.pdf>.
dotnet: Cross platform .NET tools for .NET Core. Some subcommands such as `build` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools>.
dotnet-tool: Manage .NET tools and search published tools in NuGet. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/global-tools>.
dotnet-test: Execute tests for a .NET application. Note: View <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/testing/selective-unit-tests> for supported filter expressions. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-test>.
dotnet-run: Run a .NET application without explicit compile or launch commands. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-run>.
dotnet-restore: Restore the dependencies and tools of a .NET project. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-restore>.
dotnet-publish: Publish a .NET application and its dependencies to a directory for deployment to a hosting system. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-publish>.
dotnet-ef: Perform design-time development tasks for Entity Framework Core. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/ef/core/cli/dotnet>.
dotnet-build: Build a .NET application and its dependencies. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-build>.
dotnet-add-package: Add or update a .NET package reference in a project file. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-add-package>.
dotenvx: A better `dotenv`, from the creator of `dotenv`. More information: <https://dotenvx.com/docs/>.
dot2gxl: Convert between graphs represented in GXL and in the DOT language. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/gxl2gv.1.pdf>.
dot: Render an image of a `linear directed` network graph from a `graphviz` file. Layouts: `dot`, `neato`, `twopi`, `circo`, `fdp`, `sfdp`, `osage` & `patchwork`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/doc/info/command.html>.
dosbox: MS-DOS emulator to run legacy DOS applications and games. More information: <https://www.dosbox.com/wiki/Usage>.
doppler: Manage environment variables across different environments. Some subcommands such as `run`, `secrets`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.doppler.com/docs/cli>.
doppler-secrets: Manage your Doppler project's secrets. More information: <https://docs.doppler.com/docs/accessing-secrets>.
doppler-run: Run a command with Doppler secrets injected into the environment. More information: <https://docs.doppler.com/docs/cli#run-a-command-with-secrets-populated-in-environment>.
doom: Classic open-source boomer shooter featuring modding and multiplayer. `zandronum-server` can be replaced with almost any sourceport. More information: <https://doomwiki.org/wiki/Source_port_parameters>.
done: This shell keyword is used with `for`, `while`, `select`, and `until` to mark the end of a loop.
dolt: An SQL database that you can fork, clone, branch, merge, push, and pull just like a Git repository. Some subcommands such as `commit` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli>.
dolt-version: Display the current dolt CLI version. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-version>.
dolt-status: Display the status of the database session. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-status>.
dolt-sql: Run an SQL query. Multiple SQL statements must be separated by semicolons. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-sql>.
dolt-merge: Join two or more development histories together. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-merge>.
dolt-init: Create an empty Dolt data repository. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-init>.
dolt-gc: Search the repository for data that are no longer referenced and no longer needed. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-gc>.
dolt-fetch: Download objects and refs from another repository. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-fetch>.
dolt-config: Read and write local (per repository) and global (per user) Dolt configuration variables. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-config>.
dolt-commit: Commit staged changes to tables. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-commit>.
dolt-clone: Clone a repository into a new directory. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-clone>.
dolt-checkout: Check out the work tree or tables to a branch or commit. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-checkout>.
dolt-blame: Display commit information for each row of a Dolt table. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-blame>.
dolt-add: Add the contents of a table to the list of Dolt staged tables. More information: <https://docs.dolthub.com/cli-reference/cli#dolt-add>.
dolos: Plagiarism detection for programming exercises. More information: <https://dolos.ugent.be/docs/running.html>.
dokku: Docker powered mini-Heroku (PaaS). Easily deploy multiple apps to your server in different languages using a single `git-push` command. More information: <https://dokku.com/docs/deployment/application-deployment/>.
doggo: DNS client for Humans. Written in Golang. More information: <https://github.com/mr-karan/doggo/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/guide/reference.md>.
dog: DNS lookup utility. It has colorful output, supports DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON. More information: <https://github.com/ogham/dog#examples>.
doctum: Generate documentation for a PHP API. More information: <https://github.com/code-lts/doctum>.
doctl-vpcs: Manage DigitalOcean VPC networks. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/vpcs/>.
doctl-kubernetes-options: Get values available for use with `doctl`'s Kubernetes commands. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/kubernetes/options/>.
doctl-kubernetes-cluster: Manage Kubernetes clusters and view configuration options relating to clusters. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/kubernetes/cluster/>.
doctl-invoice: Retrieve details about invoices for a DigitalOcean account. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/invoice/>.
doctl-databases: Manage your MySQL, Redis, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB database services. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/>.
doctl-databases-user: View details for, and create, database users. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/user/>.
doctl-databases-sql-mode: View and configure a MySQL database cluster's global SQL modes. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/sql-mode/>.
doctl-databases-replica: Manage read-only replicas associated with a database cluster. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/replica/>.
doctl-databases-pool: Manage connection pools for your database cluster. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/pool/>.
doctl-databases-options: Enable the navigation of available options under each database engine. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/options/>.
doctl-databases-maintenance-window: Schedule, and check the schedule of, maintenance windows for your databases. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/maintenance-window/>.
doctl-databases-firewalls: Manage firewalls for database clusters. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/firewalls/>.
doctl-databases-db: Manage databases that are served by a database cluster. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/db/>.
doctl-compute-droplet: List, create, and delete virtual machines which are called droplets. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/compute/droplet/>.
doctl-completion: Generate the autocompletion script for `doctl` for the specified shell. Note: This subcommand does not have a documentation page and is likely deprecated. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/>.
doctl-billing-history: Retrieve the billing history for a DigitalOcean account. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/billing-history/>.
doctl-balance: Show the balance of a Digital Ocean account. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/balance/>.
doctl-auth: Authenticate `doctl` with API tokens. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/auth/>.
doctl-account: Retrieve information about Digital Ocean accounts. More information: <https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/account/>.
docsify: Initialize and serve markdown documentation. More information: <https://cli.docsifyjs.org/#/?id=usage>.
docker: Manage Docker containers and images. Some subcommands such as `container`, `image`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/>.
docker-update: This command is an alias of `docker container update`.
docker-top: This command is an alias of `docker container top`.
docker-tag: This command is an alias of `docker image tag`.
docker-system: Manage Docker data and display system-wide information. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/system/>.
docker-swarm: A container orchestration tool. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/>.
docker-stop: This command is an alias of `docker container stop`.
docker-stats: This command is an alias of `docker container stats`.
docker-start: This command is an alias of `docker container start`.
docker-slim: This command is an alias of `slim`.
docker-service: Manage the services on a Docker daemon. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/>.
docker-secret: Manage Docker swarm secrets. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/secret/>.
docker-search: Search for Docker images on Docker Hub. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/search/>.
docker-save: This command is an alias of `docker image save`.
docker-run: This command is an alias of `docker container run`.
docker-rmi: This command is an alias of `docker image rm`.
docker-rm: This command is an alias of `docker container rm`.
docker-rename: This command is an alias of `docker container rename`.
docker-pull: This command is an alias of `docker image pull`.
docker-ps: This command is an alias of `docker container ls`.
docker-node: Manage Docker Swarm nodes. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/node/>.
docker-network: Create and manage Docker networks. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/>.
docker-machine: Create and manage machines running Docker. More information: <https://github.com/docker-archive-public/docker.machine>.
docker-logs: This command is an alias of `docker container logs`.
docker-login: Log into a Docker registry. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/login/>.
docker-load: This command is an alias of `docker image load`.
docker-inspect: Return low-level information on Docker objects. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/inspect/>.
docker-images: This command is an alias of `docker image ls`.
docker-image: Manage Docker images. See also: `docker build`. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/>.
docker-image-tag: Assign tags to existing Docker images. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/tag/>.
docker-image-save: Export Docker images to archive. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/save/>.
docker-image-pull: Download Docker images from a registry. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/pull/>.
docker-image-load: Load Docker images from files or `stdin`. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/load/>.
docker-exec: This command is an alias of `docker container exec`.
docker-diff: This command is an alias of `docker container diff`.
docker-cp: This command is an alias of `docker container cp`.
docker-context: Switch between contexts to manage multiple Docker environments. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/context/>.
docker-container-update: Update configuration of Docker containers. Note: This command is not supported for Windows containers. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/update/>.
docker-container-top: Display the running processes of a container. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/top/>.
docker-container-stop: Stop one or more running containers. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/stop/>.
docker-container-stats: Display a live stream of resource usage statistics for containers. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/stats/>.
docker-container-run: Run a command in a new Docker container. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/>.
docker-container-remove: This command is an alias of `docker container rm`.
docker-container-exec: Execute a command on an already running Docker container. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/exec/>.
docker-container-diff: Inspect changes to files or directories on a container's filesystem. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/diff/>.
docker-container-cp: Copy files or directories between host and container filesystems. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/cp/>.
docker-container-commit: Create a new image from a container's changes. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/commit/>.
docker-compose: Run and manage multi container Docker applications. Some subcommands such as `up`, `down`, `logs`, `stop`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/>.
docker-compose-up: Start and run Docker services defined in a Compose file. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/up/>.
docker-compose-stop: Stop running containers without removing them. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/stop>.
docker-compose-start: Start existing containers for services. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/start/>.
docker-compose-logs: View output from containers in a Docker Compose application. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/logs/>.
docker-compose-down: Stop and remove containers, networks, images, and volumes created by `docker compose up`. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/down/>.
docker-commit: This command is an alias of `docker container commit`.
docker-buildx-use: Set the current builder instance. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/use>.
docker-buildx-stop: Stop a builder instance. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/stop>.
docker-buildx-rm: Remove one or more builder instances. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/rm/>.
docker-buildx-prune: Remove the build cache. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/prune/>.
docker-buildx-ls: List builder instances and associated nodes. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/ls/>.
docker-buildx-inspect: Inspect the current or a specified builder instance. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/inspect>.
docker-buildx-du: See disk usage for a builder. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/du/>.
docker-buildx-create: Create a new builder instance. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/create/>.
docker-buildx-build: Build an image from a Dockerfile using the BuildKit engine. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/build>.
docker-build: This command is an alias of `docker buildx build`.
dockdiver: A tool for interacting with Docker registries, including listing and dumping repositories. More information: <https://github.com/MachiavelliII/dockdiver#instructions>.
doas: Execute a command as another user. See also: `sudo`, `pkexec`, `run0`. More information: <https://man.openbsd.org/doas>.
do: This shell keyword is used with `for`, `while`, `select`, and `until` to mark the start of a loop.
dnsx: A fast and multi-purpose DNS toolkit to run multiple DNS queries. Note: Input to `dnsx` needs to be passed through `stdin` (pipe `|`) in some cases. See also: `dig`, `dog`, `dnstracer`. More information: <https://docs.projectdiscovery.io/opensource/dnsx/usage>.
dnswalk: DNS debugger. "Walk" across zones and validate database consistency and best practices. More information: <https://manned.org/dnswalk>.
dnsmasq: Lightweight DNS, DHCP, TFTP, and PXE server. More information: <https://manned.org/dnsmasq>.
dnote: A multi-device notebook for capturing commands, snippets, and notes. More information: <https://www.getdnote.com/docs/cli/commands/>.
dmypy: Type check Python code, running `mypy` as a daemon for better speed. See also: `mypy`. More information: <https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mypy_daemon.html>.
dlv: Debugger for the Go programming language. More information: <https://github.com/go-delve/delve/blob/master/Documentation/usage/dlv.md>.
dlt: Create, inspect, and maintain data load tool (dlt) pipelines. More information: <https://dlthub.com/docs/reference/command-line-interface>.
djxl: Decompress JPEG XL images. Accepted output extensions are PNG, APNG, JPEG, EXR, PGM, PPM, PNM, PFM, PAM, EXIF, XMP, and JUMBF. More information: <https://github.com/libjxl/libjxl/blob/main/doc/man/djxl.txt>.
djpeg: Decompress a JPEG file. More information: <https://manned.org/djpeg>.
django-admin: Django's utility for administrative tasks. More information: <https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/ref/django-admin/>.
dive: Explore a Docker image, layer contents, and discover ways to shrink it. More information: <https://github.com/wagoodman/dive>.
distccd: Server daemon for the distcc distributed compiler. More information: <https://manned.org/distccd>.
distcc: Distributed C/C++/ObjC compilation client that works with `distccd`. More information: <https://manned.org/distcc>.
disown: Allow sub-processes to live beyond the shell that they are attached to. See also: `jobs`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-disown>.
diskonaut: Terminal disk space navigator, written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/imsnif/diskonaut>.
disable: Disable built-in shell commands in Zsh. See also: `enable`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Shell-Builtin-Commands.html>.
dirs: Display or manipulate the directory stack. The directory stack is a list of recently visited directories that can be manipulated with the `pushd` and `popd` commands. See also: `pushd`, `popd`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Directory-Stack-Builtins>.
dirname: Remove trailing filename portion from a path. See also: `basename`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/dirname-invocation.html>.
direnv: Shell extension to load and unload environment variables depending on the current directory. More information: <https://github.com/direnv/direnv/blob/master/man/direnv.1.md>.
dircolors: Output commands to set the `$LS_COLOR` environment variable and style `ls`, `dir`, etc. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/dircolors-invocation.html>.
dillo: A lightweight web browser intended for slow computers. More information: <https://manned.org/dillo>.
dijkstra: Compute shortest-path distances from a single source node in a graph. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/dijkstra.1.pdf>.
dig: DNS lookup utility. See also: `resolvectl`, `nslookup`, `host`. More information: <https://manned.org/dig>.
difft: Compare files or directories based on the syntax of the programming language. See also: `delta`, `diff`. More information: <https://difftastic.wilfred.me.uk/introduction.html>.
diffstat: Create a histogram from the output of the `diff` command. More information: <https://manned.org/diffstat>.
diffoscope: Compare files, archives, and directories. More information: <https://manned.org/diffoscope>.
diffimg: Calculate intersection between two images. Note: The supported extensions are `.png`, `.gif`, `.jpg`, `.ps`. More information: <https://manned.org/diffimg>.
diff: Compare files and directories. See also: `delta`, `difft`. More information: <https://manned.org/diff>.
diff-so-fancy: Colorize `diff` output in a more human readable way. More information: <https://github.com/so-fancy/diff-so-fancy#-usage>.
dict: Dictionary that uses the DICT protocol. More information: <https://manned.org/dict>.
dhcpwn: Test DHCP IP exhaustion attacks and sniff local DHCP traffic. More information: <https://github.com/mschwager/dhcpwn>.
dhcpig: Initiate an advanced DHCP exhaustion attack and stress test. More information: <https://github.com/kamorin/DHCPig#usage>.
dfc: Get an overview of the filesystem disk space usage with colors and graphs. More information: <https://manned.org/dfc>.
df: Display an overview of the filesystem disk space usage. See also: `ncdu`, `duf`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/df-invocation.html>.
dexter: Authenticate the `kubectl` users with OpenId Connect. More information: <https://github.com/gini/dexter#run-dexter>.
dexdump: Display information about Android DEX files. More information: <https://manned.org/man/debian-stretch/dexdump>.
devspace: Develop, deploy, and debug applications inside Kubernetes. More information: <https://www.devspace.sh/docs/cli>.
devpod: Launch reproducible development environments using Docker, Kubernetes, or SSH. More information: <https://devpod.sh/docs/quickstart/devpod-cli/>.
devenv: Fast, declarative, reproducible, and composable developer environments using Nix. More information: <https://devenv.sh/getting-started/#commands>.
devcontainer: Use a Docker container as a development environment. More information: <https://containers.dev/implementors/reference/>.
detox: Rename files to make them easier to work with. It removes spaces and other such annoyances like duplicate underline characters. More information: <https://manned.org/detox>.
depotdownloader: Content/depot downloader for Steam. More information: <https://github.com/SteamRE/DepotDownloader>.
deployment: Automatically pull Git repositories and run their `deploy` scripts. Reads deployments as `path,repository_url` rows from a CSV file. More information: <https://github.com/chrissxMedia/deployment>.
dep: Deploy PHP applications. Note: The Go command `dep` with the same name is deprecated and archived. More information: <https://deployer.org/docs/8.x/cli>.
deno: A secure runtime for JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly. Includes dependency management using `npm` or `jsr`, and tooling like bench, bundle, doc, and coverage. More information: <https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/>.
deluged: A daemon process for the Deluge BitTorrent client. More information: <https://manned.org/deluged>.
deluge-console: An interactive interface for the Deluge BitTorrent client. More information: <https://deluge-torrent.org/userguide/thinclient/>.
delta: A viewer for Git and diff output. See also: `diff`, `difft`. More information: <https://dandavison.github.io/delta/full---help-output.html>.
deepseek: An AI coding assistant using DeepSeek Coder models. More information: <https://github.com/holasoymalva/deepseek-cli#cli-commands>.
deemix: A barebone deezer downloader library built from the ashes of Deezloader Remix. It can be used as a standalone CLI app or implemented in a UI using the API. More information: <https://gitlab.com/RemixDev/deemix-py>.
declare: Declare variables and give them attributes. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-declare>.
decaffeinate: Move your CoffeeScript source to modern JavaScript. More information: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/decaffeinate#common-options>.
deallocvt: Deallocate unused virtual consoles. More information: <https://manned.org/deallocvt>.
ddgr: Search DuckDuckGo (HTML version) from the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/jarun/ddgr#usage>.
ddev: Container based local development tool for PHP environments. More information: <https://docs.ddev.com/en/stable/users/usage/cli/>.
dd: Convert and copy a file. See also: `caligula`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/dd-invocation.html>.
dcode: Recursively detect and decode strings, supporting hex, decimal, binary, base64, URL, FromChar encodings, Caesar ciphers, and MD5, SHA1, and SHA2 hashes. Warning: uses 3rd-party web services for MD5, SHA1, and SHA2 hash lookups. For sensitive data, use `-s` to avoid these services. More information: <https://github.com/s0md3v/Decodify>.
dcgmi: Manage and monitor NVIDIA Data Center GPUs. More information: <https://developer.nvidia.com/dcgm>.
dcfldd: Enhanced version of dd for forensics and security. More information: <https://manned.org/dcfldd>.
dc: An arbitrary precision calculator. Uses reverse polish notation (RPN). See also: `bc`, `qalc`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bc/manual/dc-1.05/html_mono/dc.html>.
dbx: Interact with the Databricks platform. Note: This tool has been retired and it is recommended to use Databricks Asset Bundles instead. More information: <https://dbx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/cli/#dbx>.
dbt: A tool to model transformations in data warehouses. More information: <https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core>.
dbeaver: A GUI SQL client supporting many databases. More information: <https://dbeaver.com/docs/dbeaver/Command-Line/>.
date: Set or display the system date. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/date-invocation.html>.
datashader_cli: Quick visualization of large datasets using CLI based on datashader. More information: <https://github.com/wybert/datashader-cli>.
dash: Debian Almquist Shell, a modern, POSIX-compliant implementation of `sh` (not Bash-compatible). More information: <https://manned.org/dash>.
daps: An open source program for transforming DocBook XML into output formats such as HTML or PDF. More information: <https://opensuse.github.io/daps/doc/index.html>.
dalfox: A powerful open-source XSS scanner focused on automation. More information: <https://dalfox.hahwul.com/reference/cli/>.
dagger: Programmable CI/CD engine that runs pipelines in containers locally, in CI, or in the cloud. More information: <https://docs.dagger.io/reference/cli>.
d8: Developer shell for the V8 JavaScript engine. More information: <https://v8.dev/docs/d8>.
d2: A modern diagram scripting language that turns text to diagrams. Note: The output file supports SVG and PNG file formats. More information: <https://d2lang.com/tour/man/>.
czkawka_cli: Find duplicates, empty folders, similar images, and much more. More information: <https://github.com/qarmin/czkawka/blob/master/czkawka_cli/README.md>.
cython: A compiler that converts `.pyx` files into C or C++ source files. More information: <https://docs.cython.org/en/latest/>.
cypher-shell: Open an interactive session and run Cypher queries against a Neo4j instance. See also: `neo4j-admin`, `mysql`. More information: <https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/cypher-shell/>.
cwebp: Compress an image file to a WebP file. More information: <https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/cwebp>.
cvs: Concurrent Versions System, a revision control system. More information: <https://manned.org/cvs>.
cut: Cut out fields from `stdin` or files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/cut-invocation.html>.
curl: Transfer data from or to a server. Supports most protocols, including HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SCP, etc. See also: `wcurl`, `wget`. More information: <https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html>.
cupstestppd: Test conformance of PPD files to the version 4.3 of the specification. Error codes (1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively): bad CLI arguments, unable to open file, unskippable format errors, and non-conformance with PPD specification. Note: This command is deprecated. See also: `lpadmin`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-cupstestppd.html>.
cupsreject: Reject jobs sent to printers. Note: Destination is referred as a printer or a class of printers. See also: `cupsaccept`, `cupsenable`, `cupsdisable`, `lpstat`. More information: <https://www.cups.org/doc/man-cupsaccept.html>.
cupsenable: Start printers and classes. Note: Destination is referred as a printer or a class of printers. See also: `cupsdisable`, `cupsaccept`, `cupsreject`, `lpstat`. More information: <https://www.cups.org/doc/man-cupsenable.html>.
cupsdisable: Stop printers and classes. Note: Destination is referred as a printer or a class of printers. See also: `cupsenable`, `cupsaccept`, `cupsreject`, `lpstat`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-cupsenable.html>.
cupsd: Server daemon for the CUPS print server. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-cupsd.html>.
cupsctl: Update or query a server's `cupsd.conf`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-cupsctl.html>.
cupsaccept: Accept jobs sent to destinations. Note: Destination is referred as a printer or a class of printers. See also: `cupsreject`, `cupsenable`, `cupsdisable`, `lpstat`. More information: <https://www.cups.org/doc/man-cupsaccept.html>.
cups: Open source printing system. Note: CUPS isn't a command, but a set of commands. More information: <https://www.cups.org/index.html>.
cups-config: Show technical information about your CUPS print server installation. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-cups-config.html>.
ctest: CMake test driver program. More information: <https://manned.org/ctest>.
ctags: Generate an index (or tag) file of language objects found in source files for many popular programming languages. More information: <https://docs.ctags.io/en/latest/man/ctags.1.html>.
csvtool: Utility to filter and extract data from CSV formatted sources. More information: <https://github.com/maroofi/csvtool>.
csvstat: Print descriptive statistics for all columns in a CSV file. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvstat.html>.
csvsql: Generate SQL statements for a CSV file or execute those statements directly on a database. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvsql.html>.
csvsort: Sort CSV files. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvsort.html>.
csvpy: Load a CSV file into a Python shell. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvpy.html>.
csvlook: Render a CSV file in the console as a fixed-width table. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvlook.html>.
csvgrep: Filter CSV rows with string and pattern matching. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvgrep.html>.
csvformat: Convert a CSV file to a custom output format. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvformat.html>.
csvcut: Filter and truncate CSV files. Like Unix's `cut` command, but for tabular data. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvcut.html>.
csvclean: Find and clean common syntax errors in CSV files. Included in csvkit. More information: <https://csvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/scripts/csvclean.html>.
csv2tsv: Convert CSV (comma-separated) text to TSV (tab-separated) format. More information: <https://github.com/eBay/tsv-utils/blob/master/README.md#csv2tsv>.
csv-diff: View differences between two CSV, TSV, or JSON files. More information: <https://github.com/simonw/csv-diff>.
csh: The shell (command interpreter) with C-like syntax. See also: `tcsh`. More information: <https://www.mkssoftware.com/docs/man1/csh.1.asp>.
csc: The Microsoft C# Compiler. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/command-line-building-with-csc-exe>.
cs: Application and artifact manager for the Scala language. Installs Scala applications and sets up a Scala development environment. Some subcommands such as `install`, `launch`, `java`, `fetch`, `resolve`, `complete-dep`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/overview>.
cs-resolve: Resolve lists the transitive dependencies of other dependencies. More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/cli-resolve>.
cs-launch: Launch an application from the name directly from Maven dependencies without the need of installing it. More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/cli-launch>.
cs-java: The `java` and `java-home` commands fetch and install JVMs. The `java` command runs them too. More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/cli-java>.
cs-install: Install an application in the installation directory configured when installing `cs` (to enable the binary to be loaded add to your `.bash_profile` the `$ eval "$(cs install --env)"` command). More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/cli-install>.
cs-fetch: Fetch fetches the JARs of dependencies. More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/cli-fetch>.
cs-complete-dep: Search for libraries without doing it directly on the web. More information: <https://get-coursier.io/docs/cli-complete>.
crystal: Manage Crystal source code. More information: <https://crystal-lang.org/reference/using_the_compiler>.
cryfs: A cryptographic filesystem for the cloud. More information: <https://manned.org/cryfs>.
crush: AI-powered terminal assistant for software development tasks. Provides interactive chat interface with AI capabilities, code analysis, and LSP integration. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush>.
crontab: Schedule cron jobs to run on a time interval for the current user. More information: <https://manned.org/crontab>.
cronic: Bash script for wrapping cron jobs to prevent excess email sending. More information: <https://manned.org/cronic>.
cron: A system scheduler for running jobs or tasks unattended. The command to submit, edit, or delete entries to `cron` is called `crontab`. More information: <https://manned.org/cron>.
croc: Send and receive files easily and securely over any network. More information: <https://github.com/schollz/croc>.
critique: Review Git changes with syntax highlighting and word-level diffs. More information: <https://github.com/remorses/critique#usage>.
crictl: Manage CRI-compatible container runtimes. More information: <https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/blob/master/docs/crictl.md>.
createuser: Create a PostgreSQL user (role). More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-createuser.html>.
createdb: Create a PostgreSQL database. More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-createdb.html>.
crane: Container images managing tool. Some subcommands such as `pull`, `push`, `copy`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane.md/>.
crane-version: Print the version of a binary. The version string is completely dependent on how the binary was built, so you should not depend on the version format. It may change without notice. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_version.md>.
crane-validate: Validate that an image is well-formed. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_validate.md>.
crane-tag: Efficiently tag a remote image without downloading it, which differs from the `copy` command. It skips the layer existence checks because we know the manifest already exists making it slightly faster. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_tag.md>.
crane-registry: This command serves a registry implementation on an automatically chosen port (`:0`), `$PORT`, or `--address`. The command blocks while the server accepts pushes and pulls and contents are can be stored in memory, and disk. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_registry_serve.md>.
crane-rebase: Rebase an image onto a new base image. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_rebase.md>.
crane-push: Push local image contents to a remote registry. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_push.md>.
crane-pull: Pull remote images by reference and store their contents locally. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_pull.md>.
crane-mutate: Modify image labels and annotations. The container must be pushed to a registry, and the manifest is updated there. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_mutate.md>.
crane-manifest: Get the manifest of an image. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_manifest.md>.
crane-ls: List the tags in a repository. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_ls.md>.
crane-index: Modify an image index. Some subcommands such as `append` and `filter` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_index.md>.
crane-index-filter: Modify a remote index by filtering based on platform. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_index_filter.md>.
crane-index-append: Append manifest to a remote index. This sub-command pushes an index based on an (optional) base index, with appended manifests. The platform for appended manifests is inferred from the configuration file or omitted if that is infeasible. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_index_append.md>.
crane-flatten: Flatten an image's layers into a single layer. Pushes digest to original image repository if no tags are specified. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_flatten.md>.
crane-export: Export filesystem of a container image as a tarball. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_export.md>.
crane-digest: Get the digest of an image. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_digest.md>.
crane-delete: Delete an image reference from its registry. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_delete.md>.
crane-cp: This command is an alias of `crane copy`.
crane-copy: Efficiently copy a remote image from source to target while retaining the digest value. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_copy.md>.
crane-config: Get the configuration of an image. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_config.md>.
crane-catalog: List the repositories in a registry. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_catalog.md>.
crane-blob: Read a blob from a registry. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_blob.md>.
crane-auth: Log in or access credentials. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_auth.md>.
crane-append: Push an image based on an (optional) base image. Appends layers containing the contents of the provided tarballs. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/doc/crane_append.md>.
cradle: The Cradle PHP framework. Some subcommands such as `install`, `package`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://cradlephp.github.io/docs/3.B.-Reference-Command-Line-Tools.html>.
cradle-sql: Manage Cradle SQL databases. More information: <https://cradlephp.github.io/docs/3.B.-Reference-Command-Line-Tools.html#sql>.
cradle-package: Manage packages for a Cradle instance. More information: <https://cradlephp.github.io/docs/3.B.-Reference-Command-Line-Tools.html#package>.
cradle-install: Install the Cradle PHP framework components. More information: <https://cradlephp.github.io/docs/3.B.-Reference-Command-Line-Tools.html#install>.
cradle-elastic: Manage the Elasticsearch instances for a Cradle instance. More information: <https://cradlephp.github.io/docs/3.B.-Reference-Command-Line-Tools.html#elastic>.
crackle: Crack and decrypt Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) encryption. More information: <https://github.com/mikeryan/crackle>.
cpuctl: Control and inspect system CPUs from command line. Note: At least one CPU in the system must always remain online. More information: <https://man.netbsd.org/cpuctl.8>.
cppclean: Find unused code in C++ projects. More information: <https://github.com/myint/cppclean>.
cppcheck: A static analysis tool for C/C++ code. Instead of syntax errors, it focuses on the types of bugs that compilers normally do not detect. More information: <https://manned.org/cppcheck>.
cpio: Copy files in and out of archives. Supports the following archive formats: cpio's custom binary, old ASCII, new ASCII, crc, HPUX binary, HPUX old ASCII, old tar, and POSIX.1 tar. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/cpio/manual/cpio.html#Invoking-cpio>.
cpan: Query, download, and build perl modules from CPAN sites. More information: <https://manned.org/cpan>.
cp: Copy files and directories. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/cp-invocation.html>.
cowsay: Print ASCII art (by default a cow) saying or thinking something. More information: <https://manned.org/cowsay>.
couchdb: Command-line interface for Apache CouchDB database server. More information: <https://manned.org/couchdb>.
cotton: Markdown test specification runner. More information: <https://github.com/chonla/cotton>.
cosign: Container Signing, Verification, and Storage in an OCI registry. More information: <https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/doc/cosign.md>.
coreutils: Cross-platform reimplementation of the GNU coreutils in Rust Language. Includes a multi-call binary from which the utils can be invoked. This reduces the binary size and can be useful for portability. See also: `toybox`, `busybox`. More information: <https://uutils.github.io/coreutils/docs/multicall.html>.
corepack: Zero-runtime-dependency package acting as bridge between Node projects and their package managers. More information: <https://github.com/nodejs/corepack>.
core-validate-commit: Validate commit messages for Node.js core. More information: <https://github.com/nodejs/core-validate-commit>.
cordova: Mobile apps with HTML, CSS & JS. More information: <https://cordova.apache.org/docs/en/latest/guide/cli/>.
copyq: Clipboard manager with advanced features. More information: <https://copyq.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command-line.html>.
coproc: Bash builtin for creating interactive asynchronous subshells. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Coprocesses>.
copr: This command is an alias of `copr-cli`.
copr-cli: Interface with Fedora-Projects copr instance for building RPMs and publishing them. More information: <https://manned.org/copr-cli>.
copilot: Interact with GitHub Copilot. More information: <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-copilot-cli>.
convmv: Convert filenames (NOT file content) from one encoding to another. More information: <https://www.j3e.de/linux/convmv/man/>.
convert: This command is an alias of `magick convert`. Note: This alias is deprecated since ImageMagick 7. It has been replaced by `magick`. Use `magick convert` if you need to use the old tool in versions 7+.
continue: Skip to the next iteration of a `for`, `while`, `until`, or `select` loop. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-continue>.
consul: Distributed key-value store with health checking and service discovery. Some subcommands such as `kv` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/commands>.
consul-kv: Distributed key-value store with health checking and service discovery. More information: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/automate/kv/store>.
confettysh: Display animated confetti and fireworks over SSH. See also: `ssh`. More information: <https://github.com/charmbracelet/confettysh>.
conda: Package, dependency, and environment management for any programming language. Some subcommands such as `create` have their own usage documentation. See also: `mamba`. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/index.html>.
conda-update: Update packages within a conda environment, including conda itself. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/update.html>.
conda-search: Search for packages and show their details. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/search.html>.
conda-run: Run an executable command in a conda environment. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/run.html>.
conda-repoquery: Advanced search for packages in a conda repository. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/repoquery/index.html>.
conda-rename: Rename an existing conda environment. The base environment and the currently-active environment cannot be renamed. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/rename.html>.
conda-remove: Remove packages from a conda environment. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/remove.html>.
conda-package: Create low-level conda packages. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/commands/package.html>.
conda-notices: Retrieve latest channel notifications. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/notices.html>.
conda-list: List installed packages in a conda environment. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/commands/list.html>.
conda-install: Install packages into an existing conda environment. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/install.html>.
conda-init: Initialize conda for shell interaction. Most shells need to be closed and restarted for changes to take effect. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/init.html>.
conda-info: Display details about the conda installation. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/info.html>.
conda-doctor: Display a health report for your environment. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/doctor.html>.
conda-deactivate: Deactivate a conda environment. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/deactivate.html>.
conda-create: Create new conda environments. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/create.html>.
conda-config: Modify configuration values in `.condarc`. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/commands/config.html>.
conda-compare: Compare packages between conda environments. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/commands/compare.html>.
conda-clean: Delete temporary or unused files: index cache, lock files, unused cache packages, tarballs, and log files. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/commands/clean.html>.
conda-activate: Activate a conda environment. See also: `conda deactivate`. More information: <https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/dev-guide/deep-dives/activation.html>.
conan: The open source, decentralized, and cross-platform package manager to create and share all your native binaries. More information: <https://docs.conan.io/2/reference/commands.html>.
composer: A package-based dependency manager for PHP projects. More information: <https://getcomposer.org/doc/03-cli.md>.
composer-require-checker: Analyze Composer dependencies for soft dependencies. More information: <https://github.com/maglnet/ComposerRequireChecker>.
composer-audit: Analyze a PHP project's dependencies to detect known security vulnerabilities and list affected packages. More information: <https://getcomposer.org/doc/03-cli.md#audit>.
compopt: Print or change the completion options for a command. `-o` means enabled and `+o` means disabled. See also: `compgen`, `complete`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-compopt>.
complete: Get and set argument autocompletion rules of shell commands in Bash. The specified completions will be invoked when `<Tab>` is pressed in Bash. See also: `compgen`, `compopt`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-complete>.
compgen: Bash built-in command for generating possible completion matches in Bash. Usually used within custom completion functions. See also: `complete`, `compopt`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-compgen>.
compare: This command is an alias of `magick compare`.
command: Force the shell to execute the program and ignore any functions, builtins, and aliases with the same name. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-command>.
comma: This command is an alias of `,`.
comm: Select or reject lines common to two files. Both files must be sorted. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/comm-invocation.html>.
comby: Tool for structural code search and replace that supports many languages. More information: <https://github.com/comby-tools/comby>.
combine: Perform set operations on lines of two files. The order of the output lines is determined by the order of the lines in the first file. See also: `diff`. More information: <https://manned.org/combine>.
colorpicker: A minimalist X11 colorpicker. Any mouse gesture except `<LeftClick>` will exit the program. More information: <https://github.com/ym1234/colorpicker>.
colorls: Beautify `ls` command output, with color and font-awesome icons. Available as a Ruby gem. More information: <https://github.com/athityakumar/colorls#flags>.
colordiff: A wrapper around `diff` that produces the same output but with pretty syntax highlighting. Color schemes can be customized. More information: <https://manned.org/colordiff>.
colon: Return a successful exit status code of 0. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-_003a>.
colima: Container runtimes for macOS and Linux with minimal setup. More information: <https://github.com/abiosoft/colima>.
colcrt: Filter nroff output for CRT previewing. More information: <https://manned.org/colcrt>.
colab: Command-line interface for Google Colab. Some subcommands such as `run` and `exec` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/googlecolab/google-colab-cli#command-index>.
colab-run: Run a Python script on a fresh Google Colab VM and automatically release it upon completion. More information: <https://github.com/googlecolab/google-colab-cli#execution>.
colab-exec: Execute code in an active Google Colab session. More information: <https://github.com/googlecolab/google-colab-cli#execution>.
cola: This command is an alias of `git-cola`.
coffee: Execute CoffeeScript scripts or compiles them into JavaScript. More information: <https://coffeescript.org#cli>.
codium: This command is an alias of `code`.
codex: Natural language code assistant for the terminal, powered by OpenAI. Reads and edits files in your current directory to fulfill requests. More information: <https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference>.
codespell: Spellchecker for source code. More information: <https://manned.org/codespell>.
codecrafters: Practice writing complex software. More information: <https://docs.codecrafters.io/cli/usage>.
code2prompt: Generate AI-ready prompts from a codebase (extract, filter, and format code for LLMs). More information: <https://code2prompt.dev/docs/how_to/filter_files/>.
code: Cross platform and extensible code editor. More information: <https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/command-line>.
co: Check out RCS revisions (retrieve working files from the Revision Control System). See also: `ci`, `rcs`, `rcsdiff`, `rlog`. More information: <https://manned.org/co>.
cmuwmtopbm: Convert a CMU window manager bitmap to a PBM image. See also: `pbmtocmuwm`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/cmuwmtopbm.html>.
cmusfm: Scrobble tracks from the `cmus` music player to Last.fm. More information: <https://github.com/Arkq/cmusfm#configuration>.
cmus: Command-line music player. Use `<ArrowKeys>` to navigate, `<Enter>` to select, and numbers `<1>`-`<8>` switch between different views. See also: `ncmpcpp`, `clementine`, `qmmp`. More information: <https://manned.org/cmus>.
cmp: Compare two files byte by byte. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/diffutils/manual/diffutils.html#Invoking-cmp>.
cmd-wrapped: View shell history statistics. More information: <https://crates.io/crates/cmd-wrapped>.
cmctl: Manage cert-manager resources inside your cluster. Check cert signing status, approve/deny requests, and issue new certificate requests. More information: <https://cert-manager.io/docs/reference/cmctl/>.
cmatrix: Show a scrolling Matrix like screen in the terminal. See also: `neo`, `cbonsai`, `asciiquarium`, `pipes.sh`. More information: <https://manned.org/cmatrix>.
cmark: Convert CommonMark Markdown formatted text to other formats. More information: <https://manned.org/cmark>.
cmake: Cross-platform build automation system, that generates recipes for native build systems. More information: <https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake.1.html>.
clusterdb: Cluster (reorganize) a PostgreSQL database. More information: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-clusterdb.html>.
cluster: Find clusters in a graph and augment the graph with this information. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/cluster.1.pdf>.
cloudflared: Create a persistent connection to the Cloudflare network. More information: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/>.
clojure: This command is an alias of `clj`.
clockwork-cli: Interface for the Clockwork PHP debugging framework. More information: <https://github.com/ptrofimov/clockwork-cli>.
cloc: Count lines of code. More information: <https://github.com/AlDanial/cloc#options->.
clj: Clojure tool to start a REPL or invoke a function with data. All options can be defined in a `deps.edn` file. More information: <https://clojure.org/guides/deps_and_cli>.
clip-view: Command Line Interface Pages (CLIP) render. Render for a TlDr-like project with much a more extensive syntax and several render modes. More information: <https://github.com/command-line-interface-pages/v2-tooling/tree/main/clip-view>.
clinfo: Show OpenCL platforms and devices. More information: <https://manned.org/clinfo>.
clifm: The command-line file manager. See also: `vifm`, `ranger`, `mc`, `nautilus`. More information: <https://github.com/leo-arch/clifm>.
clido: Save-state TODO app for the terminal. More information: <https://gitlab.com/Oglo12/clido-legacy#how-to-use>.
cli53: Tool for Amazon Route 53. More information: <https://github.com/barnybug/cli53>.
cli4: Python command-line interface for Cloudflare API. More information: <https://github.com/cloudflare/python-cloudflare>.
clementine: A modern music player and library organizer. See also: `audacious`, `qmmp`, `cmus`, `mpv`. More information: <https://manned.org/clementine>.
clear: Clear the screen of the terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/clear>.
claude: An agent-based coding tool that understands your code base and helps you code faster through natural language commands. More information: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference>.
clangd: Language server that provides IDE-like features to editors. It should be used via an editor plugin rather than invoked directly. More information: <https://manned.org/clangd-22>.
clang: Compile C, C++, and Objective-C source files. Can be used as a drop-in replacement for GCC. Part of LLVM. More information: <https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangCommandLineReference.html>.
clang-tidy: An LLVM-based C/C++ linter to find style violations, bugs, and security flaws through static analysis. More information: <https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/>.
clang-cpp: This command is an alias of `clang++`.
clang-check: Check basic errors and work with Clang's Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). Part of Clang's LibTooling and is useful for debugging and analyzing C/C++ code. More information: <https://manned.org/clang-check>.
clang++: Compile C++ source files. Part of LLVM. More information: <https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html#command-line-options>.
clamdscan: Scan for viruses using the ClamAV Daemon. More information: <https://docs.clamav.net/manual/Usage/Scanning.html#clamdscan>.
clamav: Open-source anti-virus program. ClamAV isn't a command, but a set of commands. More information: <https://www.clamav.net/>.
cksum: Calculate CRC checksums and byte counts of a file. Note: On old UNIX systems the CRC implementation may differ. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/cksum-invocation.html>.
cjxl: Convert and compress images to JPEG XL. Accepted input extensions are PNG, APNG, GIF, JPEG, EXR, PPM, PFM, PAM, PGX, and JXL. More information: <https://github.com/libjxl/libjxl/blob/main/doc/man/cjxl.txt>.
cjpeg: Compress an image file to a JPEG file. More information: <https://manned.org/cjpeg>.
circup: The CircuitPython library updater. More information: <https://github.com/adafruit/circup#usage>.
circo: Render an image of a `circular` network graph from a `graphviz` file. Layouts: `dot`, `neato`, `twopi`, `circo`, `fdp`, `sfdp`, `osage` & `patchwork`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/doc/info/command.html>.
cidr: Simplify IPv4/IPv6 CIDR network prefix management with counting, overlap checking, explanation, and subdivision. More information: <https://github.com/bschaatsbergen/cidr>.
ci: Check in RCS revisions (store file changes in the Revision Control System). See also: `co`, `rcs`, `rcsdiff`, `rlog`. More information: <https://manned.org/ci>.
chroot: Run command or interactive shell with special root directory. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/chroot-invocation.html>.
chronyc: Query the Chrony NTP daemon. More information: <https://chrony-project.org/doc/latest/chronyc.html>.
chronic: Display `stdout` and `stderr` of a command if and only if it fails. More information: <https://manned.org/chronic>.
chromium: Open-source web browser principally developed and maintained by Google. Note: You may need to replace the `chromium` command with your desired web browser, such as `brave`, `google-chrome`, `opera`, or `vivaldi`. More information: <https://www.chromium.org/developers/how-tos/run-chromium-with-flags/>.
chroma: A general-purpose syntax highlighter. The `--lexer` option is usually unnecessary, as it will be automatically determined based on the file extension. More information: <https://manned.org/chroma>.
chown: Change user and group ownership of files and directories. See also: `chgrp`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/chown-invocation.html>.
choose: A human-friendly and fast alternative to `cut` and (sometimes) `awk`. More information: <https://github.com/theryangeary/choose#usage>.
chmod: Change the access permissions of a file or directory. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/chmod-invocation.html>.
chkrootkit: Scan system for rootkits. More information: <https://manned.org/chkrootkit>.
chkfont: Verify the format of a FIGlet font file (`.flf`). See also: `figlet`, `figlist`, `showfigfonts`. More information: <https://manned.org/chkfont>.
chisel: Create TCP/UDP tunnels, transported over HTTP, secured via SSH. Includes both client and server in the same `chisel` executable. More information: <https://github.com/jpillora/chisel#usage>.
chgrp: Change group ownership of files and directories. See also: `chown`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/chgrp-invocation.html>.
chezmoi: Manage dotfiles across multiple diverse machines. See also: `stow`, `tuckr`, `vcsh`, `homeshick`. More information: <https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/>.
checksec: Check security properties of executables. Note: For older versions, use flags (e.g., `--file` instead of `file`). More information: <https://github.com/slimm609/checksec>.
checkov: Static code analysis tool for Infrastructure as Code (IaC). It is also a software composition analysis (SCA) tool for images and open source packages. More information: <https://www.checkov.io/1.Welcome/Quick%20Start.html>.
cheatshh: CLI cheatsheet with customized descriptions, tldr, and groups, to look into for your reference. Press `<Enter>` to a command to copy it to your clipboard and exit. See also: `tldr`, `cheat`, `navi`. More information: <https://github.com/AnirudhG07/cheatshh/blob/main/docs/man/cheatshh.1>.
cheat: Create and view interactive cheat sheets. See also: `tldr`, `cheatshh`, `navi`. More information: <https://github.com/cheat/cheat/blob/master/doc/cheat.1.md>.
chdman: Manage and convert CHD (Compressed Hunks of Data) images. Commonly used with MAME and retro game images. More information: <https://docs.mamedev.org/tools/chdman.html>.
chdir: This command is an alias of `cd`.
chatgpt: Shell script to use OpenAI's ChatGPT and DALL·E from the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/0xacx/chatGPT-shell-cli>.
chars: Display names and codes for various ASCII and Unicode characters and code points. More information: <https://github.com/boinkor-net/chars#running>.
charm: Set of tools that makes adding a backend to your terminal-based applications, without worrying about user accounts, data storage, and encryption. More information: <https://manned.org/charm>.
chainctl: The official CLI for Chainguard. More information: <https://edu.chainguard.dev/chainguard/chainctl/chainctl-docs/chainctl/>.
chafa: Image printing in the terminal. See also: `catimg`, `pixterm`. More information: <https://hpjansson.org/chafa/man/>.
cfv: Command-line File Verify, a utility to test and create checksum files. More information: <https://manned.org/cfv>.
cfssl: Cloudflare's PKI and TLS toolkit. See also: `openssl`. More information: <https://github.com/cloudflare/cfssl>.
cf: Manage apps and services on Cloud Foundry. More information: <https://docs.cloudfoundry.org/cf-cli/getting-started.html>.
certutil: Manage keys and certificates in both NSS databases and other NSS tokens. More information: <https://manned.org/certutil>.
cdparanoia: Extract audio tracks from CDs. More information: <https://xiph.org/paranoia/manual.html>.
cdk: AWS Cloud Development Kit. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/latest/guide/cli.html>.
cdecl: Compose and decode C and C++ type declarations. More information: <https://manned.org/cdecl>.
cd: Change the current working directory. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-cd>.
ccomps: Decompose graphs into their connected components. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/ccomps.1.pdf>.
ccache: C/C++ compiler cache. Note: Packages usually provide symlinks for compilers in `/usr/lib/ccache/bin`. Prepend this directory to `$PATH` to automatically use `ccache` for them. More information: <https://ccache.dev/manual/latest.html>.
cbt: Utility for reading data from Google Cloud's Bigtable. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/cbt-reference>.
cbonsai: A beautifully random bonsai tree generator. See also: `cmatrix`, `asciiquarium`, `pipes.sh`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/jallbrit/cbonsai>.
cb: Cut, copy, and paste anything in the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/Slackadays/Clipboard#-7>.
cavif: Convert PNG/JPEG images to AVIF. Written in Rust. See also: `convert`. More information: <https://github.com/kornelski/cavif-rs>.
catimg: Image printing in the terminal. See also: `pixterm`, `chafa`. More information: <https://manned.org/catimg>.
cat: Print and concatenate files. See also: `bat`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/cat-invocation.html>.
case: Bash builtin construct for creating multi-choice conditional statements. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-case>.
carp: REPL and build tool for Carp. More information: <https://carp-lang.github.io/carp-docs/Manual.html>.
cariddi: Crawl URLs and scan for endpoints, secrets, api keys, file extensions, tokens, and more from a list of domains. More information: <https://github.com/edoardottt/cariddi/wiki>.
cargo: Manage Rust projects and their module dependencies (crates). Some subcommands such as `build` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/cargo/>.
cargo-yank: Remove a pushed crate from the index. This should only be used when you accidentally release a significantly broken crate. Note: This does not remove any data. The crate is still present after a yank - this just prevents new projects from using it. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-yank.html>.
cargo-verify-project: Check the correctness of the `Cargo.toml` manifest and print the result as a JSON object. Note: This command is deprecated. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/deprecated-and-removed.html>.
cargo-vendor: Vendor all dependencies of a project into the specified directory (default: `vendor`). More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-vendor.html>.
cargo-update: Update dependencies as recorded in `Cargo.lock`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-update.html>.
cargo-uninstall: Remove a Rust binary installed globally using `cargo install`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-uninstall.html>.
cargo-tree: Display a tree visualization of a dependency graph. Note: In the tree, dependencies of packages marked with `(*)` have already been shown elsewhere in the graph, and so are not repeated. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-tree.html>.
cargo-test: Execute the unit and integration tests of a Rust package. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-test.html>.
cargo-search: Search for packages on <https://crates.io>. The crates are displayed along with descriptions in TOML format suitable for copying into `Cargo.toml`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-search.html>.
cargo-rustdoc: Build the documentation of Rust packages. Similar to `cargo doc`, but you can pass options to `rustdoc`. See `rustdoc --help` for all available options. See also: `rustdoc`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-rustdoc.html>.
cargo-rustc: Compile a Rust package. Similar to `cargo build`, but you can pass extra options to the compiler. See `rustc --help` for all available options. See also: `rustc`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-rustc.html>.
cargo-run: Run the current Cargo package. Note: The working directory of the executed binary will be set to the current working directory. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-run.html>.
cargo-report: Display various kinds of reports. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-report.html>.
