cargo-remove: Remove dependencies from a Rust project's `Cargo.toml` manifest. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-remove.html>.
cargo-publish: Upload a package to a registry. Note: You have to add an authentication token using `cargo login` before publishing a package. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-publish.html>.
cargo-pkgid: Print the fully qualified package ID specifier for a package or dependency in the current workspace. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-pkgid.html>.
cargo-package: Assemble a local package into a distributable tarball (a `.crate` file). Similar to `cargo publish --dry-run`, but has more options. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-package.html>.
cargo-owner: Manage the owners of a crate on the registry. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-owner.html>.
cargo-new: Create a new Cargo package. Equivalent of `cargo init`, but specifying a directory is required. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-new.html>.
cargo-msrv: Manage the Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) of a project. Note: This is not a built-in Cargo command, you need to install it first. More information: <https://gribnau.dev/cargo-msrv/>.
cargo-metadata: Output the workspace members and resolved dependencies of current package as JSON. Note: The output format is subject to change in future versions of Cargo. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-metadata.html>.
cargo-logout: Remove an API token from the registry locally. The token is used to authenticate to a package registry. You can add it back using `cargo login`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-logout.html>.
cargo-login: Save an API token from the registry locally. The token is used to authenticate to a package registry. You can remove it using `cargo logout`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-login.html>.
cargo-locate-project: Print the full path to the `Cargo.toml` manifest of a project. If the project is part of a workspace, the manifest of the project is shown, rather than that of the workspace. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-locate-project.html>.
cargo-install: Build and install a Rust binary. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-install.html>.
cargo-init: Create a new Cargo package. Equivalent of `cargo new`, but specifying a directory is optional. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-init.html>.
cargo-info: Display information about a Rust package. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-info.html>.
cargo-help: Display help on `cargo` and its subcommands. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-help.html>.
cargo-generate-lockfile: Generate the `Cargo.lock` file for the current package. Similar to `cargo update`, but has less options. If the lockfile already exists it will be rebuilt with latest version of every package. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/cargo/commands/cargo-generate-lockfile.html>.
cargo-fmt: Run `rustfmt` on all source files in a Rust project. See also: `rustfmt`. More information: <https://github.com/rust-lang/rustfmt>.
cargo-fix: Automatically fix lint warnings reported by `rustc`. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-fix.html>.
cargo-fetch: Fetch dependencies of a package from the network. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-fetch.html>.
cargo-doc: Build the documentation of Rust packages. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-doc.html>.
cargo-deb: Create Debian packages from Cargo projects. Note: This is not a built-in Cargo command, you need to install it first. More information: <https://github.com/kornelski/cargo-deb>.
cargo-clippy: A collection of lints to catch common mistakes and improve your Rust code. More information: <https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy>.
cargo-clean: Remove generated artifacts in the `target` directory. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-clean.html>.
cargo-check: Check a local package and all of its dependencies for errors. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-check.html>.
cargo-build: Compile a local package and all of its dependencies. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-build.html>.
cargo-binstall: Install Rust binaries from CI artifacts. Falls back to `cargo install` (from source code) if there are no binaries available. Note: This is not a built-in Cargo command, you need to install it first. More information: <https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall>.
cargo-bench: Compile and execute benchmarks. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-bench.html>.
cargo-add: Add dependencies to a Rust project's `Cargo.toml` manifest. More information: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-add.html>.
carbonyl: View webpages on the terminal using a Chromium backend. See also: `browsh`. More information: <https://github.com/fathyb/carbonyl>.
carbon-now: Create beautiful images of code. More information: <https://github.com/mixn/carbon-now-cli>.
cancel: Cancel print jobs. See also: `lp`, `lpmove`, `lpstat`. More information: <https://openprinting.github.io/cups/doc/man-cancel.html>.
calligrawords: Calligra's word processor application. See also: `calligraflow`, `calligrastage`, `calligrasheets`. More information: <https://manned.org/calligrawords>.
calligrastage: Calligra's presentation application. See also: `calligraflow`, `calligrawords`, `calligrasheets`. More information: <https://manned.org/calligrastage>.
calligrasheets: Calligra's spreadsheet application. See also: `calligraflow`, `calligrastage`, `calligrawords`. More information: <https://manned.org/calligrasheets>.
calligraflow: Calligra's flowchart and diagram application. See also: `calligrastage`, `calligrawords`, `calligrasheets`. More information: <https://manned.org/calligraflow>.
calibredb: Manipulate an e-book database. Part of the Calibre e-book library. More information: <https://manual.calibre-ebook.com/generated/en/calibredb.html>.
calibre-server: A server application to distribute e-books over a network. Note: E-books must already be imported into the library using the GUI or the `calibredb` CLI. Part of the Calibre e-book library. More information: <https://manual.calibre-ebook.com/generated/en/calibre-server.html>.
calendar: Display upcoming events from a calendar file. More information: <https://manned.org/calendar>.
calc: An interactive arbitrary-precision calculator in the terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/calc>.
cal: Display a calendar with the current day highlighted. More information: <https://manned.org/cal>.
cake: The processor for the CakePHP framework. More information: <https://book.cakephp.org/5/en/console-commands.html#cakephp-provided-commands>.
caddy: An enterprise-ready open source web server with automatic HTTPS, written in Go. More information: <https://caddyserver.com/docs/command-line>.
cadaver: WebDAV client for Unix. More information: <https://manned.org/cadaver>.
cabal: Interface to the Haskell package infrastructure (Cabal). Manage Haskell projects and Cabal packages from the Hackage package repository. More information: <https://cabal.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting-started.html>.
c99: Compile C programs according to the ISO C standard. More information: <https://manned.org/c99>.
c++: This command is an alias of `g++`.
bzip3: An efficient statistical file compressor. More information: <https://manned.org/bzip3>.
bzip2recover: Attempt to recover data from a damaged `.bz2` file. See also: `bzip2`. More information: <https://manned.org/bzip2recover>.
bzip2: A block-sorting file compressor. See also: `bzcat`, `bunzip2`, `bzip2recover`. More information: <https://manned.org/bzip2>.
bzgrep: Find patterns in `bzip2` compressed files using `grep`. More information: <https://manned.org/bzgrep>.
bzfgrep: This command is an alias of `bzgrep --fixed-strings`.
bzegrep: This command is an alias of `bzgrep --extended-regexp`.
bzcat: This command is an alias of `bzip2 --decompress --stdout`.
byobu: Window manager and terminal multiplexer. See also: `tmux`, `screen`. More information: <https://manned.org/byobu>.
bye: This command is an alias of `exit`.
bw: Access and manage a Bitwarden vault. More information: <https://bitwarden.com/help/cli/>.
bvnc: A GUI tool for browsing for SSH/VNC servers on the local network. See also: `bssh`, `bshell`. More information: <https://manned.org/bvnc>.
buzzphrase: Output a random buzzphrase. Written in Node.js. More information: <https://github.com/atomantic/buzzphrase#usage>.
busybox: A collection of small system utilities in a single executable. Executing `busybox` via a symlink is equivalent to running `busybox symlink_name`. Linux distributions that use BusyBox will usually provide symlinks for all programs. See also: `toybox`, `coreutils`. More information: <https://www.busybox.net/downloads/BusyBox>.
bup: Back up system based on the Git packfile format, providing incremental saves and global deduplication. More information: <https://manned.org/bup>.
bunzip2: This command is an alias of `bzip2 --decompress`.
bunx: Execute a package binary (installed locally or fetched remotely). Note: `bun x` can be used as an alias for `bunx`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/bunx>.
bundletool: Manipulate Android Application Bundles. Some subcommands such as `validate` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://developer.android.com/tools/bundletool>.
bundletool-validate: Manipulate Android Application Bundles. More information: <https://developer.android.com/tools/bundletool>.
bundletool-dump: Manipulate Android Application Bundles. More information: <https://developer.android.com/tools/bundletool>.
bundler: This command is an alias of `bundle`.
bundle: Dependency manager for the Ruby programming language. More information: <https://bundler.io/man/bundle.1.html>.
bun: JavaScript runtime and toolkit. Includes a bundler, a test runner, and a package manager. More information: <https://bun.com/docs>.
bun-x: This command is an alias of `bunx`.
bun-why: Explain why a package is installed by showing its dependency chain. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/why>.
bun-upgrade: Upgrade Bun to the latest version. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/installation#upgrading>.
bun-update: Update dependencies in a Bun project. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/update>.
bun-unlink: Unregister the current directory as a linkable package. See also: `bun link`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/link#unlinking>.
bun-test: Run tests using Bun's built-in test runner. It is a fast, Jest-compatible test runner that looks for `*.test.ts` (and similar) files. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/test>.
bun-run: Execute a JavaScript/TypeScript file, or a script from `package.json`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/runtime>.
bun-rm: This command is an alias of `bun remove`.
bun-remove: Remove a dependency from `package.json`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/remove>.
bun-publish: Publish a package to the npm registry. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/publish>.
bun-pm: A set of utilities for working with Bun's package manager. Some subcommands such as `pack`, `pkg`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm>.
bun-pm-version: Manage the `version` field in `package.json`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#version>.
bun-pm-trust: Mark dependencies as trusted. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#trust>.
bun-pm-scan: Scan packages for security vulnerabilities using Bun's integrated security scanner. This scan also runs automatically during `bun install` after configuring the scanner in `bunfig.toml` and installing `@bun-security-scanner/osv` from npm. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/security-scanner-api>.
bun-pm-pkg: Manage `package.json` data with `get`, `set`, `delete`, and `fix` operations. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#pkg>.
bun-pm-pack: Create a `.tgz` archive containing the files that would be published to npm (same behavior as `npm pack`). More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#pack>.
bun-pm-migrate: Convert another package manager's lockfile to a Bun-compatible lockfile without installing anything. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#migrate>.
bun-pm-ls: List installed dependencies and their versions. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#ls>.
bun-pm-hash: Generate and inspect the hash of the current lockfile. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#hash>.
bun-pm-bin: Display the path to `bin` directories. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/pm#bin>.
bun-patch: Prepare a package for patching or generate a patch file. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/patch>.
bun-outdated: List dependencies that have newer versions available. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/outdated>.
bun-list: This command is an alias of `bun pm ls`.
bun-link: Register a local package as linkable or link a registered package into a project. See also: `bun unlink`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/link>.
bun-install: Install JavaScript dependencies for a project from `package.json`. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install>.
bun-init: Scaffold an empty Bun project. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/runtime/templating/init>.
bun-info: Display package metadata from the npm registry. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/info>.
bun-i: This command is an alias of `bun install`.
bun-feedback: Send feedback to Bun. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/feedback#use-bun-feedback>.
bun-exec: Execute shell commands or script files using Bun's runtime. Note: When running from a shell, remember to escape quotes. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/runtime/shell>.
bun-create: Create a new project from a template. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/runtime/templating/create>.
bun-c: This command is an alias of `bun create`.
bun-build: Bundle JavaScript and TypeScript files with Bun's fast native bundler. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/bundler>.
bun-audit: Check installed packages for known security vulnerabilities. More information: <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/audit>.
bun-add: Add and install new dependencies to the current project. More information: <https://bun.com/docs>.
btop: A resource monitor that shows information about the CPU, memory, disks, network, and processes. A C++ version of `bpytop`. See also: `btm`, `glances`, `atop`, `htop`, `top`, `sensors`. More information: <https://github.com/aristocratos/btop#command-line-options>.
btm: Display system information about the CPU, memory, disks, network, and processes. An enhanced alternative to `top`. See also: `btop`, `glances`, `atop`, `htop`, `top`, `sensors`. More information: <https://clementtsang.github.io/bottom/nightly/#usage-and-configuration>.
bssh: A GUI tool for browsing for SSH/VNC servers on the local network. See also: `bvnc`, `bshell`. More information: <https://manned.org/bssh>.
bshell: A GUI for browsing for SSH/VNC servers on the local network. See also: `bssh`, `bvnc`. More information: <https://manned.org/bshell>.
brushtopbm: Convert a Xerox doodle brush file into a PBM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/brushtopbm.html>.
bru: CLI for Bruno, an Opensource IDE for exploring and testing APIs. More information: <https://docs.usebruno.com/bru-cli/overview>.
browsh: View webpages on the terminal using a Firefox backend. See also: `carbonyl`. More information: <https://www.brow.sh/docs/keybindings/>.
browser-sync: A local web server that updates browser on file changes. More information: <https://browsersync.io/docs/command-line>.
brotli: Compress/uncompress files with Brotli compression. More information: <https://manned.org/brotli>.
brittany: Pretty-print Haskell source files. More information: <https://github.com/lspitzner/brittany#readme>.
brew: Homebrew - a package manager for macOS and Linux. Some subcommands such as `install` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage>.
brew-upgrade: Upgrade outdated formulae and casks. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#upgrade-options-installed_formulainstalled_cask->.
brew-update: Fetch the newest version of Homebrew and all formulae from GitHub using `git` and perform any necessary migrations. To upgrade all installed formulae, use `brew upgrade`. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#update-up-options>.
brew-uninstall: Uninstall a Homebrew formula/cask. Use `brew autoremove` to remove unused dependencies afterwards. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#uninstall-remove-rm-options-installed_formulainstalled_cask->.
brew-tap: Tap a Homebrew formula repository. If no arguments are provided, list all installed Homebrew taps. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#tap-options-userrepo-url>.
brew-services: Manage background services with `launchctl` on macOS or `systemctl` on Linux. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#services-subcommand>.
brew-search: Search for casks and formulae. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#search--s-options-textregex->.
brew-rm: This command is an alias of `brew uninstall`.
brew-remove: This command is an alias of `brew uninstall`.
brew-reinstall: Uninstall and then reinstall a formula or cask using the same options it was originally installed with. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#reinstall-options-formulacask->.
brew-outdated: List outdated casks and formulae. To upgrade everything, use `brew upgrade`. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#outdated-options-formulacask->.
brew-list: List installed formulae/casks or their files. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#list-ls-options-installed_formulainstalled_cask->.
brew-leaves: List installed formulas that are not dependencies of another installed formula or cask. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#leaves---installed-on-request---installed-as-dependency>.
brew-install: Install a Homebrew formula or cask. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#install-options-formulacask->.
brew-info: Display information for Homebrew installation and formulae. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#info-abv-options-formulacask->.
brew-cleanup: Remove stale lock files and outdated downloads for all formulas and casks. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#cleanup-options-formulacask->.
brew-bundle: Bundler for Homebrew, Homebrew Cask, and the Mac App Store. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#bundle-subcommand>.
brew-autoremove: Remove unused formulae previously installed as dependencies. More information: <https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage#autoremove---dry-run>.
brew-abv: This command is an alias of `brew info`.
break: Break out of a `for`, `while`, `until`, or `select` loop. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-break>.
brave: This command is an alias of `chromium`. More information: <https://support.brave.app/hc/articles/360044860011-How-Do-I-Use-Command-Line-Flags-in-Brave>.
bq: A Python-based tool for BigQuery, Google Cloud's fully managed and completely serverless enterprise data warehouse. More information: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/bq-cli-reference>.
bpytop: A resource monitor that shows information about the CPU, memory, disks, network, and processes. A Python version of `bashtop`. More information: <https://github.com/aristocratos/bpytop#command-line-options>.
bpython: A fancy interface to the Python interpreter. Provides syntax highlighting and many other nice-to-haves in REPL mode. More information: <https://manned.org/bpython>.
bpkg: A package manager for Bash scripts. More information: <https://github.com/bpkg/bpkg>.
boxxy: Redirect file locations for programs that don't respect the XDG standards. More information: <https://github.com/queer/boxxy>.
boxes: Draw, remove, and repair ASCII art boxes. More information: <https://boxes.thomasjensen.com/boxes-man-1.html>.
box: A PHP application for building and managing Phars. More information: <https://github.com/box-project/box>.
bower: A package manager optimized for front-end web development. A package can be a GitHub user/repo shorthand, a Git endpoint, a URL, or a registered package. More information: <https://bower.io/#getting-started>.
botan: Provide cryptographic operations including hashing, encryption, and key generation. More information: <https://botan.randombit.net/handbook/cli.html>.
bosh: Deploy and manage the BOSH director. More information: <https://bosh.io/docs/cli-v2/>.
borg: Deduplicating backup tool. Create local or remote backups that are mountable as filesystems. More information: <https://borgbackup.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage/general.html>.
boot: Build tooling for the Clojure programming language. More information: <https://github.com/boot-clj/boot>.
bob: Manage and switch between Neovim versions. More information: <https://github.com/MordechaiHadad/bob#-usage>.
bmptoppm: This command has been superseded by `bmptopnm`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/bmptoppm.html>.
bmptopnm: Convert a BMP file into a PBM, PGM, or PNM image. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/bmptopnm.html>.
bmaptool: Create or copy block maps intelligently (designed to be faster than `cp` or `dd`). More information: <https://manned.org/bmaptool>.
bloodhound-python: A Python ingestor for BloodHound, used to enumerate Active Directory relationships. More information: <https://github.com/dirkjanm/BloodHound.py#usage>.
blockout2: Tetris like game in 3D. More information: <https://www.blockout.net/blockout2/>.
blender: Command-line interface to the Blender 3D computer graphics application. Arguments are executed in the order they are given. More information: <https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/advanced/command_line/arguments.html>.
blahaj: A lolcat-like output colorizer that also prints flags and colorful sharks. More information: <https://codeberg.org/GeopJr/BLAHAJ>.
blackfire: Monitor, profile, and test a PHP application. More information: <https://www.blackfire.io/>.
black: Format Python code automatically. See also: `ruff`. More information: <https://black.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage_and_configuration/the_basics.html>.
bk: Manage Buildkite builds, pipelines, and agents. More information: <https://github.com/buildkite/cli#usage>.
bitcoind: Bitcoin Core daemon. Uses the configuration defined in `bitcoin.conf`. More information: <https://manned.org/bitcoind>.
bitcoin-cli: Client to interact with the Bitcoin Core daemon via RPC calls. Uses the configuration defined in `bitcoin.conf`. More information: <https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Running_Bitcoin#Command-line_arguments>.
birdc: BIRD remote control. Retrieve information like routes from bird and perform configurations during runtime. More information: <https://bird.network.cz/?get_doc&v=30&f=bird-4.html>.
bird: BIRD Internet Routing Daemon. Routing daemon with support for BGP, OSPF, Babel, and others. More information: <https://bird.network.cz/?get_doc&v=30&f=bird-1.html#ss1.3>.
bioradtopgm: Convert a Biorad confocal file into a PGM file. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/bioradtopgm.html>.
biome: A toolchain for formatting, linting, and checking code quality for web projects. More information: <https://biomejs.dev/reference/cli/>.
bing-rewards: Automate daily Bing Rewards points. More information: <https://github.com/jack-mil/bing-rewards>.
bindkey: Add hotkeys to Z shell. See also: `zle`. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Zsh-Line-Editor.html#Zle-Builtins>.
bind: Bash builtin to manage bash hotkeys and variables. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-bind>.
biff: A simple utility for doing datetime arithmetic, parsing, and formatting. More information: <https://github.com/burntsushi/biff>.
biber: A backend bibliography processor for the `biblatex` package. See also: `latexmk`. More information: <https://texdoc.org/serve/biber.pdf/0#section.3>.
bgpgrep: Filter and print BGP data within MRT dumps. Can read files compressed with `gzip`, `bzip2`, and `xz`. More information: <https://codeberg.org/1414codeforge/ubgpsuite>.
bg: Resume suspended jobs (e.g. using `<Ctrl z>`), and keep them running in the background. See also: `jobs`, `fg`, `disown`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#index-bg>.
bfs: Breadth-first search for your files. More information: <https://manned.org/bfs>.
bfg: Remove large files or passwords from Git history like `git filter-branch`. Note: If your repository is connected to a remote, you will need to force push to it. More information: <https://rtyley.github.io/bfg-repo-cleaner/>.
betty: Use natural language to execute commands. More information: <https://github.com/pickhardt/betty>.
berks: Chef cookbook dependency manager. More information: <https://docs.chef.io/workstation/latest/tools/berkshelf/#berkshelf-cli>.
behat: A PHP framework for behavior-driven development. More information: <https://docs.behat.org/en/latest/user_guide/command_line_tool.html>.
bedtools: A swiss-army knife of tools for genomic-analysis tasks. Used to intersect, group, convert, and count data in BAM, BED, GFF/GTF, VCF format. More information: <https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/overview.html#summary-of-available-tools>.
bear: A tool to generate compilation databases for `clang` tooling. More information: <https://github.com/rizsotto/Bear>.
beanstalkd: A simple and generic work-queue server. More information: <https://manned.org/beanstalkd>.
bdfr: Bulk downloader for Reddit. More information: <https://github.com/Serene-Arc/bulk-downloader-for-reddit>.
bd: A lightweight memory system and git-backed issue tracker for AI coding agents. More information: <https://github.com/steveyegge/beads#usage>.
bcomps: Decompose graphs into their biconnected components. Graphviz filters: `acyclic`, `bcomps`, `comps`, `edgepaint`, `gvcolor`, `gvpack`, `mingle`, `nop`, `sccmap`, `tred`, and `unflatten`. More information: <https://graphviz.org/pdf/bcomps.1.pdf>.
bcftools: Tools for manipulating VCF and BCF files. More information: <https://samtools.github.io/bcftools/bcftools.html>.
bc: An arbitrary precision calculator language. See also: `dc`, `qalc`. More information: <https://manned.org/bc>.
bb: Native Clojure interpreter for scripting. More information: <https://book.babashka.org/#usage>.
bazel: Open-source build and test tool similar to Make, Maven, and Gradle. More information: <https://bazel.build/reference/command-line-reference>.
bats: Bash Automated Testing System: a TAP (<https://testanything.org/>) compliant testing framework for Bash. More information: <https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage.html>.
batch: Execute commands at a later time when the system load levels permit. Results will be sent to the user's mail. See also: `at`, `atq`, `atrm`, `mail`. More information: <https://manned.org/batch>.
bat: Print and concatenate files. A `cat` clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration. See also: `cat`. More information: <https://manned.org/bat>.
bastet: Clone of the game Tetris in the terminal. More information: <https://fph.altervista.org/prog/bastet.html>.
bashmarks: Save and jump to commonly used directories using 1 character commands. See also: `autojump`. More information: <https://github.com/huyng/bashmarks#shell-commands>.
bash: Bourne-Again SHell, an `sh`-compatible command-line interpreter. See also: `zsh`, `!`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Invoking-Bash>.
bash-it: A collection of community contributed Bash commands and scripts for Bash 3.2+. More information: <https://bash-it.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>.
basenc: Encode or decode file or `stdin` using a specified encoding, to `stdout`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/basenc-invocation.html>.
basename: Remove leading directory portions from a path. See also: `dirname`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/basename-invocation.html>.
base64: Encode or decode file or `stdin` to/from Base64, to `stdout`. More information: <https://manned.org/base64>.
base32: Encode or decode file or `stdin` to/from Base32, to `stdout`. More information: <https://manned.org/base32>.
basalt: Terminal user interface (TUI) application to manage Obsidian vaults and notes. More information: <https://basalt.page>.
banner: Print the argument as a large ASCII art. More information: <https://manned.org/banner>.
bandwhich: Display the current network utilization by process, connection, or remote IP/hostname. More information: <https://github.com/imsnif/bandwhich#usage>.
balena: Interact with the balenaCloud, openBalena, and the balena API. More information: <https://docs.balena.io/reference/balena-cli/latest/>.
badblocks: Search a device for bad blocks. Some usages of badblocks can cause destructive actions, such as erasing all data on a disk, including the partition table. More information: <https://manned.org/badblocks>.
bacon: A background code checker for Rust. More information: <https://github.com/Canop/bacon>.
babeld: Routing daemon for Babel which uses firewall-style filters. More information: <https://www.irif.fr/~jch/software/babel/babeld.html>.
babel: A transpiler which converts code from JavaScript ES6/ES7 syntax to ES5 syntax. More information: <https://babeljs.io/docs/babel-cli>.
b3sum: Calculate BLAKE3 cryptographic checksums. More information: <https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/tree/master/b3sum>.
b2sum: Calculate BLAKE2 cryptographic checksums. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/b2sum-invocation.html>.
b2: Access all features of Backblaze B2 Cloud Storage easily. More information: <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-command-line-tools>.
azurite: Azure Storage API compatible server (emulator) in local environment. More information: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/azurite>.

azcopy: Copy data to and from Azure Storage. See also: `az storage`. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-v10#list-of-commands>.

az-storage-table: Manage NoSQL key-value storage in Azure. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/table>.

az-storage-account: Manage storage accounts in Azure. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/account>.
az-sshkey: Manage SSH public keys with virtual machines. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/sshkey>.

az-repos: Manage Azure DevOps repos. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/repos>.
az-redis: Manage Redis caches. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/redis>.
az-quantum: Manage Azure Quantum workspaces and submit quantum jobs to providers (preview, requires quantum extension). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/quantum>.
az-provider: Manage resource providers. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/provider>.
az-pipelines: Manage Azure Pipelines resources. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/pipelines>.
az-network: Manage Azure Network resources. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/network>.
az-logout: Log out from an Azure subscription. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/reference-index#az-logout>.
az-login: Log in to Azure. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/reference-index#az-login>.
az-logicapp: Manage Logic Apps in Azure Cloud Services. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/logicapp>.
az-lock: Manage Azure locks. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/lock>.

az-group: Manage resource groups and template deployments. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/group>.

az-disk: Manage Azure Managed Disks. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/disk>.
az-devops: Manage Azure DevOps organizations. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/devops>.
az-container: Manage Azure Container Instances. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/container>.

az-bicep: Bicep CLI command group. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/bicep>.
az-appconfig: Manage App configurations on Azure. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/appconfig>.
az-apim: Manage Azure API Management services. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/apim>.
az-aks: Manage Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/aks>.
az-advisor: Manage Azure subscription information. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/advisor>.
az-acr: Manage private registries with Azure Container Registries. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/acr>.
az-account: Manage Azure subscription information. Part of `azure-cli` (also known as `az`). More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/account>.
axel: Download accelerator. Supports HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and FTPs. See also: `aria2c`. More information: <https://manned.org/axel>.
awslogs: Query groups, streams, and events from Amazon CloudWatch logs. More information: <https://github.com/jorgebastida/awslogs#options>.
aws: The official CLI tool for Amazon Web Services. Some subcommands such as `s3` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/>.
aws-vault: A vault for securely storing and accessing AWS credentials in development environments. More information: <https://github.com/99designs/aws-vault>.
aws-sts: Security Token Service (STS) allows IAM users or federated users to request temporary credentials. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/sts/>.
aws-sso: Manage access to AWS resources using Single Sign-On (SSO) credentials. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/sso/>.

aws-sns: Create topics and subscriptions, send and receive messages, and monitor events and logs for the Amazon Simple Notification Service. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/sns/>.
aws-ses: CLI for AWS Simple Email Service. High-scale inbound and outbound cloud email service. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ses/>.
aws-secretsmanager: Store, manage, and retrieve secrets. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/secretsmanager/>.
aws-s3api: Create and delete Amazon S3 buckets and edit bucket properties. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/>.
aws-s3: CLI for AWS S3 - provides storage through web services interfaces. Some subcommands such as `cp` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/>.
aws-s3-website: Set the website configuration for a bucket. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/website.html>.
aws-s3-sync: Recursively sync files and directories between your local system and an S3 bucket, or between S3 buckets. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/sync.html>.
aws-s3-rb: Delete an empty S3 bucket. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/rb.html>.
aws-s3-presign: Generate pre-signed URLs for Amazon S3 objects. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/presign.html>.
aws-s3-mv: Move local files or S3 objects to another location locally or in S3. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/mv.html>.
aws-s3-ls: List AWS S3 buckets, folders (prefixes), and files (objects). More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/ls.html>.
aws-s3-cp: Copy local files or S3 objects to another location locally or in S3. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/cp.html>.
aws-route53: CLI for AWS Route53 - Route 53 is a highly available and scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/route53/>.
aws-rds: Use AWS Relational Database Service, a web service for setting up, operating, and scaling relational databases. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/rds/>.
aws-quicksight: Create, delete, list, search, and update AWS QuickSight entities. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/quicksight/>.
aws-pricing: Query services, products, and pricing information from Amazon Web Services. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/pricing/>.
aws-mq: Define and operate message brokers in AWS. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/mq/>.
aws-logs: Interact with log files from various AWS services. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/logs/>.
aws-lightsail: Manage Amazon Lightsail resources. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/lightsail/>.
aws-lambda: Use AWS Lambda, a compute service for running code without provisioning or managing servers. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/lambda/>.
aws-kinesis: Interact with the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, a service that scales elastically for real-time processing of streaming big data. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/kinesis/index.html#cli-aws-kinesis>.
aws-kendra: CLI for AWS Kendra. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/kendra/>.
aws-kafka: Manage an Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) cluster. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/kafka/>.
aws-iam: Interact with Identity and Access Management (IAM), a web service for securely controlling access to AWS services. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/iam/>.
aws-history: Print AWS CLI command history (command history must be enabled). More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/history/>.
aws-help: Display help information about the AWS CLI. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-usage-help.html>.
aws-google-auth: Acquire AWS temporary (STS) credentials using Google Apps as a federated (Single Sign-On) provider. More information: <https://github.com/cevoaustralia/aws-google-auth>.
aws-glue: CLI for AWS Glue. Define the public endpoint for the AWS Glue service. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/glue/>.
aws-eks: Manage Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) addons, clusters, and node groups. Amazon EKS is a service for easily running Kubernetes on AWS. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/eks/>.
aws-ecs: Manage Elastic Container Service (ECS) clusters. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ecs/>.
aws-ecr: Push, pull, and manage container images. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ecr/>.
aws-ec2: Manage AWS EC2 instances and volumes. Provides secure and resizable computing capacity in the AWS cloud for faster development and deployment of applications. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ec2/>.
aws-dynamodb: Manipulate an AWS DynamoDB database, a fast NoSQL database with predictable performance and seamless scalability. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/dynamodb/>.
aws-cur: Create, query, and delete AWS usage report definitions. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cur/>.
aws-configure: Manage configuration for the AWS CLI. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/configure/>.
aws-cognito-idp: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool and its users and groups and authenticate them. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cognito-idp/>.
aws-codecommit: A managed source control service that hosts private Git repositories. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/codecommit/>.
aws-codeartifact: Manage CodeArtifact repositories, domains, packages, package versions, and assets. CodeArtifact is an artifact repository compatible with popular package managers and build tools like Maven, Gradle, npm, Yarn, Twine, pip, NuGet, and SwiftPM. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/codeartifact/>.
aws-cloudwatch: Monitor AWS resources to gain system-wide visibility into resource utilization, application performance, and operational health. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudwatch/>.
aws-cloudformation: Model, provision, and manage AWS and third-party resources by treating infrastructure as code. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudformation/>.
aws-cloud9: Manage Cloud9 - a collection of tools to code, build, run, test, debug, and release software in the cloud. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloud9/>.
aws-ce: Run cost management operations through the AWS Cost Explorer service. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ce/>.
aws-batch: Run batch computing workloads through the AWS Batch service. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/batch/>.
aws-backup: Unified backup service designed to protect Amazon Web Services and their associated data. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/backup/>.
aws-amplify: Development platform for building secure, scalable mobile and web applications. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/amplify/>.
aws-acm-pca: AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/acm-pca/>.
aws-accessanalyzer: Analyze and review resource policies to identify potential security risks. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/accessanalyzer/>.
awk: A versatile programming language for working on files. Note: Different implementations of AWK often make this a symlink of their binary. See also: `gawk`. More information: <https://github.com/onetrueawk/awk>.
avrdude: Driver program for Atmel AVR microcontrollers programming. More information: <https://www.nongnu.org/avrdude/user-manual/avrdude_3.html#Option-Descriptions>.
avo: The official interface for Avo. More information: <https://www.avo.app/docs/implementation/cli>.
avifenc: AV1 Image File Format (AVIF) encoder. More information: <https://aomediacodec.github.io/av1-avif/>.
avifdec: AV1 Image File Format (AVIF) decoder. More information: <https://aomediacodec.github.io/av1-avif/>.

autopep8: Format Python code according to the PEP 8 style guide. More information: <https://github.com/hhatto/autopep8>.
automake: Automated Makefile generation for software projects using GNU standards. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/automake.html#automake-Invocation>.
autoload: Mark functions for lazy loading in Zsh. Functions are not loaded into memory until first called, improving shell startup time. More information: <https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Shell-Builtin-Commands.html>.
autojump: Quickly jump among the directories you visit the most. Aliases like `j` or `jc` are provided for even less typing. See also: `bashmarks`. More information: <https://github.com/wting/autojump#name>.
autoflake: Remove unused imports and variables from Python code. More information: <https://github.com/PyCQA/autoflake#advanced-usage>.
autoconf: Generate configuration scripts to automatically configure software source code packages. More information: <https://manned.org/autoconf>.
audtool: Control Audacious using commands. See also: `audacious`. More information: <https://manned.org/audtool>.
auditd: This responds to requests from the audit utility and notifications from the kernel. Note: It should not be invoked manually. More information: <https://manned.org/auditd>.
audacious: An open-source audio player. Indirectly based on XMMS. See also: `audtool`, `clementine`, `mpc`, `ncmpcpp`. More information: <https://manned.org/audacious>.
atuin: Store your shell history in a searchable database. Optionally sync your encrypted history between machines. More information: <https://docs.atuin.sh/>.
attr: Manipulate extended attributes on filesystem objects. More information: <https://manned.org/attr>.
atrm: Remove jobs scheduled by `at` or `batch` commands. Note: To find job numbers use `atq`. More information: <https://manned.org/atrm>.
atq: Show jobs scheduled by `at` or `batch` commands. More information: <https://manned.org/atq>.
atoum: A simple, modern, and intuitive unit testing framework for PHP. More information: <https://atoum.readthedocs.io/en/latest/option_cli.html>.

atktopbm: Convert an Andrew Toolkit raster object to a PBM image. See also: `pbmtoatk`. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/atktopbm.html>.
at: Execute commands once at a later time. Results will be sent to the users mail. More information: <https://manned.org/at>.

astroterm: A terminal-based star map. More information: <https://github.com/da-luce/astroterm#usage>.
astronomer: Detect illegitimate stars from bot accounts on GitHub projects. More information: <https://github.com/Ullaakut/astronomer#arguments-and-options>.
ast-grep: Search, lint, and rewrite code using AST patterns. More information: <https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/cli.html>.

asdf: Manage versions of different packages. More information: <https://asdf-vm.com/manage/commands.html>.
asciitopgm: Convert ASCII graphics into a PGM file. More information: <https://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/asciitopgm.html>.
asciiquarium: Display an animated aquarium in ASCII art inside the terminal. See also: `cmatrix`, `cbonsai`, `pipes.sh`. More information: <https://robobunny.com/projects/asciiquarium/html/?page=2>.

ascii-image-converter: Convert an image into ASCII. More information: <https://github.com/TheZoraiz/ascii-image-converter#cli-usage>.
asar: A file archiver for the Electron platform. More information: <https://github.com/electron/asar#usage>.
arthas: Java diagnostic tool. See also: `arthas-watch`, `arthas-trace`. More information: <https://arthas.aliyun.com/en/>.

wlcrosshairctl: Overlay an uninteractable image on top of the screen. Requires the `~/.config/wlcrosshair/config.toml` to be configured before use. More information: <https://github.com/marzeq/wlcrosshair>.
wl-paste: Paste content in Wayland clipboard. See also: `wl-copy`, `xclip`. More information: <https://github.com/bugaevc/wl-clipboard>.
wl-copy: Clear and copy to Wayland clipboard. See also: `wl-paste`, `xclip`. More information: <https://github.com/bugaevc/wl-clipboard>.
wireplumber: A modular session/policy manager for PipeWire and a GObject-based high-level library that wraps PipeWire's API. See also: `wpctl`, `pipewire`. More information: <https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/>.
wipefs: Wipe filesystem, raid, or partition-table signatures from a device. More information: <https://manned.org/wipefs>.
winetricks: Manage Wine virtual Windows environments. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Winetricks>.
wineserver: Manage the Wine server, the daemon that backs each Wine prefix. More information: <https://manned.org/wineserver>.
winepath: Convert file paths between Windows and Unix formats for a Wine prefix. More information: <https://manned.org/winepath>.
winemaker: Generate build files to port Windows source code to a Winelib application. More information: <https://manned.org/winemaker>.
winedump: Dump the contents of Windows binaries (PE, NE, etc.), demangle C++ symbols, and generate Wine `.spec` files. More information: <https://manned.org/winedump>.
winedbg: The Wine debugger, for debugging Windows and Winelib applications. More information: <https://manned.org/winedbg>.
winecfg: Configure a Wine prefix (drives, libraries, graphics, and the emulated Windows version). More information: <https://manned.org/winecfg>.
wineboot: Simulate a Windows reboot, or initialize, update, or shut down a Wine prefix. More information: <https://manned.org/wineboot>.
wine: Run Windows executables on Unix-based systems. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wine-uninstaller: List and remove Windows applications installed in a Wine prefix. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wine-start: Launch a program or open a document in a Wine prefix. A reimplementation of the Windows `start` command. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wine-sc: Create, query, and control Windows services in a Wine prefix. A reimplementation of the Windows `sc` service control command. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wine-reg: Manage keys and their values in the Wine registry. Some subcommands such as `add`, `delete`, `query`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wine-reg-query: Display keys, values, and data in the Wine registry. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wine-reg-import: Import keys, values, and data into the Wine registry from a `.reg` file. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-import>.
wine-reg-export: Export keys, values, and data from the Wine registry to a `.reg` file. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-export>.
wine-reg-delete: Delete keys and values from the Wine registry. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-delete>.
wine-reg-copy: Copy a registry key to a new location within the Wine registry. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-copy>.
wine-reg-add: Add new keys and values to the Wine registry. More information: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-add>.
wine-net: Start, stop, and list Windows services in a Wine prefix. A reimplementation of a subset of the Windows `net` command. More information: <https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine/-/wikis/Commands>.
wifi-menu: Interactively connect to a wireless network. More information: <https://manned.org/wifi-menu>.
whiptail: Display text-based dialog boxes from shell scripts. See also: `dialog`, `gum`. More information: <https://manned.org/whiptail>.
whereis: Locate the binary, source, and manual page files for a command. See also: `which`, `whatis`, `type`. More information: <https://manned.org/whereis>.
whatis: Display one-line descriptions from manual pages. See also: `man`, `whereis`. More information: <https://manned.org/whatis>.
wf-recorder: Screencast for Wayland optionally with audio. By default you need to end the process with `<Ctrl c>`. More information: <https://github.com/ammen99/wf-recorder>.
wev: Print contents of Wayland events. More information: <https://manned.org/wev>.
wdctl: Show the hardware watchdog status. More information: <https://manned.org/wdctl>.
waypipe: Remotely run graphical applications under a Wayland compositor. More information: <https://manned.org/waypipe>.
waydroid: A container-based approach to boot a full Android system on a regular Linux system like Ubuntu. More information: <https://docs.waydro.id/usage/waydroid-command-line-options>.
warpd: A modal keyboard driven pointer manipulation program. More information: <https://github.com/rvaiya/warpd/blob/master/warpd.1.md>.
wami: An open-source and easy-to-use tool that recommends suitable programs for tasks. More information: <https://github.com/evait-security/wami>.
wall: Write a message on the terminals of users currently logged in. More information: <https://manned.org/wall>.
walker: A Wayland-native application launcher and runner with pluggable providers. See also: `fuzzel`, `wofi`, `rofi`. More information: <https://github.com/abenz1267/walker>.
wal-telegram: Generate themes for Telegram based the colors generated by pywal/wal. More information: <https://github.com/guillaumeboehm/wal-telegram>.
wajig: Simplified all-in-one-place system support tool for Debian-based systems. More information: <https://togaware.com/linux/survivor/wajig.html>.
waitpid: Wait for the termination of arbitrary processes. See also: `wait`. More information: <https://manned.org/waitpid>.
vzdump: Backup Utility for virtual machines and containers. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/vzdump.1.html>.
vso: Package manager, system updater, and a task automator for Vanilla OS. More information: <https://github.com/Vanilla-OS/vanilla-system-operator>.
vrms: Report non-free packages installed on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://salsa.debian.org/debian/check-dfsg-status>.
vpnc: A VPN client for the Cisco 3000 VPN Concentrator. More information: <https://manned.org/vpnc>.
vnstati: PNG image output support for vnStat. More information: <https://manned.org/vnstati>.
vnstat: A console-based network traffic monitor. More information: <https://manned.org/vnstat>.
vncviewer: Launch a VNC (Virtual Network Computing) client. More information: <https://manned.org/vncviewer>.
vncserver: Launch a VNC (Virtual Network Computing) desktop. More information: <https://manned.org/vncserver.1x>.
vmware-checkvm: Check if the current host is a VMware VM or not. More information: <https://manned.org/vmware-checkvm>.
vmstat: Report information about processes, memory, paging, block IO, traps, disks, and CPU activity. More information: <https://manned.org/vmstat>.
vkpurge: List or remove old kernel versions left behind by `xbps`. The `version` arguments support shell `glob`s. More information: <https://man.voidlinux.org/vkpurge.8>.
vivaldi-stable: This command is an alias of `chromium`. More information: <https://vivaldi.com/>.
virt-xml: Edit libvirt Domain XML files with explicit command-line options. Note: `domain` refers to the name, UUID, or ID for the existing VMs. See also: `virsh`. More information: <https://github.com/virt-manager/virt-manager/blob/main/man/virt-xml.rst>.
virt-xml-validate: Validate `libvirt` XML files against a schema. If a schema is not specified, the schema is determined by the root element in the XML file. More information: <https://libvirt.org/manpages/virt-xml-validate.html>.
virt-what: Shell script that detects if you are running in a virtual machine. Outputs a specific code for a virtual machine if detected. More information: <https://manned.org/virt-what>.
virt-sysprep: Reset, unconfigure, or customize a virtual machine image. This command can be used on a virtual machine or directly on a virtual machine disk image. Note: You may need to pass `--connect URI` to the commands or set up the URI in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/libvirt/libvirt.conf`. More information: <https://libguestfs.org/virt-sysprep.1.html>.
virt-sparsify: Make virtual machine drive images thin-provisioned. Note: Use only for offline machines to avoid data corruption. More information: <https://manned.org/virt-sparsify>.
virt-qemu-run: Experimental tool to run a QEMU Guest VM independent of `libvirtd`. More information: <https://libvirt.org/manpages/virt-qemu-run.html>.
virt-manager: A desktop user interface for managing KVM and Xen virtual machines and LXC containers. More information: <https://manned.org/virt-manager>.
virt-install: Create virtual machines with libvirt and begin OS installation. Note: You may need to pass `--connect URI` to the commands or set up the URI in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/libvirt/libvirt.conf`. More information: <https://manned.org/virt-install>.
virt-clone: Clone a libvirt virtual machine. More information: <https://manned.org/virt-clone>.
vipw: Edit the password file. More information: <https://manned.org/vipw>.
vigr: Edit the group file. More information: <https://manned.org/vigr>.
viewnior: Simple and elegant image viewer. More information: <https://manned.org/viewnior>.
vgscan: Scan for volume groups on all supported Logical Volume Manager (LVM) block devices. See also: `lvm`, `vgchange`. More information: <https://manned.org/vgscan>.
vgs: Display information about volume groups. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/vgs>.
vgremove: Remove volume group(s) in LVM. More information: <https://manned.org/vgremove>.
vgextend: Add one or more physical volumes to an existing volume group. More information: <https://manned.org/vgextend>.
vgdisplay: Display information about Logical Volume Manager (LVM) volume groups. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/vgdisplay>.
vgcreate: Create volume groups combining multiple mass-storage devices. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/vgcreate>.
vgchange: Change the attributes of a Logical Volume Manager (LVM) volume group. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/vgchange>.
vgcfgrestore: Restore volume group configuration (not user data) from a text back up file produced by `vgcfgbackup`. More information: <https://manned.org/vgcfgrestore>.
vgcfgbackup: Back up volume group configuration metadata to files (not user data). More information: <https://manned.org/vgcfgbackup>.
veracrypt: Free and open source disk encryption software. More information: <https://arcanecode.com/2021/06/21/veracrypt-on-the-command-line-for-ubuntu-linux/>.
ventoy: A tool to create bootable USB drives using ISO files. More information: <https://www.ventoy.net/en/doc_start.html#doc_linux_cli>.
vcgencmd: Print system information for a Raspberry Pi. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/os.html#vcgencmd>.
valheim: Create and start a headless Valheim server. Note: Configure the server by editing a copy of the `start_server.sh` script. More information: <https://www.valheimgame.com/support/a-guide-to-dedicated-servers/>.
v4l2loopback-ctl: Control Video4Linux2 loopback devices. More information: <https://manned.org/v4l2loopback-ctl>.
v4l2-ctl: Control video devices. See also: `cam`. More information: <https://manned.org/v4l2-ctl>.
uvcdynctrl: Manage dynamic controls in uvcvideo. More information: <https://manned.org/uvcdynctrl>.
uuidparse: Parse universally unique identifiers. See also: `uuidgen`. More information: <https://manned.org/uuidparse>.
uuidgen: Generate unique identifiers (UUIDs). See also: `uuid`. More information: <https://manned.org/uuidgen>.
uuidd: Daemon for generating UUIDs. More information: <https://manned.org/uuidd>.
uuid: Generate and decode Universally Unique Identifiers (UUID). See also: `uuidgen`. More information: <https://manned.org/uuid>.
utmpdump: Dump and load btmp, utmp, and wtmp accounting files. More information: <https://manned.org/utmpdump>.
usermod: Modify a user account. See also: `users`, `useradd`, `userdel`. More information: <https://manned.org/usermod>.
userdel: Remove a user account or remove a user from a group. See also: `users`, `useradd`, `usermod`. More information: <https://manned.org/userdel>.
userdbctl: Inspect users, groups, and group memberships on the system. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/userdbctl.html>.
useradd: Create a new user. See also: `users`, `userdel`, `usermod`. More information: <https://manned.org/useradd>.
usbip: Use USB devices remotely. More information: <https://manned.org/usbip>.
urxvt: Rxvt-unicode. A customizable terminal emulator. More information: <https://manned.org/urxvt>.
urpmq: Query information about packages and media in Mageia. See also: `urpmi`, `urpmi.update`, `urpmi.addmedia`, `urpmi.removemedia`, `urpmf`, `urpme`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpmq.8.html>.
urpmi.update: Update the list of packages from a package repository in Mageia. Note: Mageia documentation uses medium and repository as synonymous. See also: `urpmi`, `urpme`, `urpmi.addmedia`, `urpmi.removemedia`, `urpmf`, `urpmq`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpmi.update.8.html>.
urpmi.removemedia: Remove media in Mageia. Note: Mageia documentation uses medium and repository as synonymous. See also: `urpmi`, `urpme`, `urpmi.addmedia`, `urpmi.update`, `urpmf`, `urpmq`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpmi.removemedia.8.html>.
urpmi: Install packages in Mageia. See also: `urpmi.update`, `urpme`, `urpmi.addmedia`, `urpmi.removemedia`, `urpmf`, `urpmq`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpmi.8.html>.
urpmi.addmedia: Add media in Mageia. Note: Mageia documentation uses medium and repository as synonymous. See also: `urpmi`, `urpmi.update`, `urpme`, `urpmi.removemedia`, `urpmf`, `urpmq`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpmi.addmedia.8.html>.
urpmf: Find files in packages and query information about them in Mageia. See also: `urpmi`, `urpme`, `urpmi.addmedia`, `urpmi.removemedia`, `urpmi.update`, `urpmq`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpmf.8.html>.
urpme: Uninstall packages in Mageia. See also: `urpmi`, `urpmi.update`, `urpmi.addmedia`, `urpmi.removemedia`, `urpmf`, `urpmq`. More information: <https://man.linuxreviews.org/man8/urpme.8.html>.
uprecords: Display a summary of historical uptime records. More information: <https://manned.org/uprecords>.
upower: System utility to provide power and battery information and statistics. More information: <https://upower.freedesktop.org/docs/upower.1.html>.
upnpc: Configure port forwarding rules on your router via the UPnP protocol. More information: <https://manned.org/upnpc>.
upgradepkg: Upgrade Slackware packages by replacing existing packages with new versions. See also: `installpkg`, `removepkg`, `makepkg`, `pkgtool`. More information: <https://slackware.nl/slackware/slackware64-current/source/a/pkgtools/manpages/upgradepkg.8>.
updpkgsums: Update the checksums of the sources in a `PKGBUILD`. Unless a preexisting hashing algorithm is used, SHA256 will be used. More information: <https://manned.org/updpkgsums>.
updatedb: Create or update the database used by `locate`. It is usually run daily by cron. More information: <https://manned.org/updatedb>.
update-rc.d: Install and remove services which are System-V style init script links. Init scripts are in the `/etc/init.d/`. More information: <https://manned.org/update-rc.d>.
update-grub: This command is an alias of `grub-mkconfig --output /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
update-desktop-database: Build the cache database of MIME types handled by desktop files. More information: <https://manned.org/update-desktop-database>.
update-ca-certificates: Update the CA certificates bundle and regenerate `/etc/ssl/certs`. More information: <https://manned.org/update-ca-certificates>.
update-alternatives: Conveniently maintain symbolic links to determine default commands. More information: <https://manned.org/update-alternatives>.
unzipsfx: Create a self-extracting compressed binary file by prepending self-extracting stubs on a Zip file. More information: <https://manned.org/unzipsfx>.
unsquashfs: Uncompress, extract, and list files in squashfs filesystems. More information: <https://manned.org/unsquashfs>.
unshare: Execute a command in new user-defined namespaces. More information: <https://manned.org/unshare>.
unshadow: Utility provided by the John the Ripper project to obtain the traditional Unix password file if the system uses shadow passwords. More information: <https://www.openwall.com/john/doc/>.
unrtf: Convert RTF files to other file formats. More information: <https://manned.org/unrtf>.
unopkg: LibreOffice extensions manager. Download extensions from <https://extensions.libreoffice.org>. See also: `libreoffice`. More information: <https://manned.org/unopkg>.
unix2mac: Change Unix-style line endings to macOS-style. Replaces LF with CR. See also: `unix2dos`, `dos2unix`, `mac2unix`. More information: <https://manned.org/unix2mac>.
unix2dos: Change Unix-style line endings to DOS-style. Replaces LF with CRLF. See also: `unix2mac`, `dos2unix`, `mac2unix`. More information: <https://manned.org/unix2dos>.
uncompress: Uncompress files compressed using the Unix `compress` command. More information: <https://manned.org/uncompress>.
uname26: This command is an alias of `setarch uname26`.
ul: Underline a text. Each character in a string must be underlined separately. More information: <https://manned.org/ul>.
ukify: Build and sign Unified Kernel Images (UKIs). More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/ukify.html>.
uinput: Intercept and write input events to a virtual keyboard device using `/dev/uinput`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/interception/linux/tools/-/tree/master#uinput>.
ufw: Uncomplicated Firewall. Frontend for `iptables` aiming to make configuration of a firewall easier. Some subcommands such as `allow`, `enable`, `delete`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-version: Show the firewall version. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-status: Show the status of Uncomplicated Firewall and its rules. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-reset: Reset the firewall to its default state and disable it. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-reject: Reject traffic through the firewall. Similar to `ufw deny`, but sends a rejection response instead of silently dropping packets. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-limit: Rate limit connections to deny an IP initiating 6 or more attempts within 30 seconds. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-enable: Reload and enable the firewall on boot. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-disable: Unload and disable the firewall on boot. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-deny: Block traffic through the firewall. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-default: Change the default policy for traffic based on direction. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
ufw-app: Manage `ufw` application profiles and their associated firewall rules. Application profiles are defined in `/etc/ufw/applications.d/`. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw#head8>.
ufw-allow: Allow traffic through the firewall. More information: <https://manned.org/ufw>.
udisksctl: Interact with `udisksd` to query and manipulate storage devices. See also: `mount`. More information: <https://storaged.org/doc/udisks2-api/latest/udisksctl.1.html>.
udiskie: A user-level automounter for removable media using udisks2. See also: `udiskie-mount`, `udiskie-umount`. More information: <https://github.com/coldfix/udiskie/wiki/Usage>.
udiskie-umount: Manually unmount devices using udiskie. See also: `udiskie`, `udiskie-mount`. More information: <https://github.com/coldfix/udiskie/wiki/Usage>.
udiskie-mount: Manually mount devices using udiskie. See also: `udiskie`, `udiskie-umount`. More information: <https://github.com/coldfix/udiskie/wiki/Usage>.
udiskie-dmenu: A dmenu/rofi-based frontend for udiskie to mount and unmount devices interactively. Requires udiskie and either dmenu or rofi. More information: <https://github.com/fogine/udiskie-dmenu>.
udevmon: Intercept and monitor input devices for launching tasks. Filters or modifies events according to configuration file(s) (default: `/etc/interception/udevmon.d/*.yaml`). More information: <https://gitlab.com/interception/linux/tools/-/tree/master#udevmon>.
uci: Manage OpenWrt configuration files. More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/techref/uci>.
ubus: Interact with an OpenWrt ubusd server. More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/techref/ubus>.
ubuntu-security-status: Display information about security support for installed Ubuntu packages. More information: <https://git.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/update-manager/tree/ubuntu-security-status>.
ubuntu-drivers: Install drivers on Ubuntu. More information: <https://ubuntu.com/server/docs/how-to/graphics/install-nvidia-drivers/>.
ubuntu-bug: This command is an alias of `apport-bug`.
tzselect: Interactively select timezone. Note: This program doesn't actually set the timezone. More information: <https://manned.org/tzselect>.
tuxi: Scrape Google search results and SERPs and provide instant and concise answers. More information: <https://github.com/Bugswriter/tuxi#usage>.
turbostat: Report processor topology, frequency, temperature, power, and idle statistics. More information: <https://manned.org/turbostat>.
tunelp: Set various parameters for parallel port devices for troubleshooting or for better performance. Part of `util-linux`. More information: <https://manned.org/tunelp>.
tuned: Dynamic adaptive system tuning daemon. See also: `tuned-adm`. More information: <https://manned.org/tuned>.
tuned-adm: Manage and optimize system performance tuning profiles on Linux. More information: <https://manned.org/tuned-adm>.
tune2fs: Adjust parameters of an ext2, ext3, or ext4 filesystem. May be used on mounted filesystems. More information: <https://manned.org/tune2fs>.
tune.exfat: Adjust tunable filesystem parameters on an exFAT filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/tune.exfat>.
ttyplot: A realtime plotting utility for the command-line with data input from `stdin`. More information: <https://github.com/tenox7/ttyplot>.
tshark: Packet analysis tool, CLI version of Wireshark. More information: <https://tshark.dev/#sitemap-in-tshark---help>.
trust: Operate on the trust policy store. More information: <https://manned.org/trust>.
trizen: Arch Linux utility for building packages from the Arch User Repository (AUR). More information: <https://github.com/trizen/trizen/blob/master/TRIZEN.md>.
treetime: Provide routines for ancestral sequence reconstruction and inference of molecular-clock phylogenies. More information: <https://treetime.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials.html>.
trayer: A lightweight GTK-2 based systray. More information: <https://github.com/sargon/trayer-srg>.
trashy: An alternative to `rm` and `trash-cli` written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/oberblastmeister/trashy#usage>.
trash: Manage the trashcan/recycling bin. More information: <https://github.com/andreafrancia/trash-cli>.
trash-rm: The examples for this command have been moved together with `trash`.
trash-restore: The examples for this command have been moved together with `trash`.
trash-put: This command is an alias of `trash`.
trash-list: The examples for this command have been moved together with `trash`.
trash-empty: The examples for this command have been moved together with `trash`.
tracepath: Trace the path to a network host discovering MTU along this path. More information: <https://manned.org/tracepath>.
trace-cmd: Utility to interact with the Ftrace Linux kernel internal tracer. Some subcommands such as `list`, `record`, `report` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/trace-cmd>.
trace-cmd-report: Display recorded trace events. See also: `trace-cmd list`, `trace-cmd record`. More information: <https://manned.org/trace-cmd-report>.
trace-cmd-record: Capture kernel trace events. See also: `trace-cmd list`, `trace-cmd report`. More information: <https://manned.org/trace-cmd-record>.
trace-cmd-list: Show available tracers, events, or options for tracing. See also: `trace-cmd record`, `trace-cmd report`. More information: <https://manned.org/trace-cmd-list>.
toybox: Multipurpose tool that provides many standard Unix utilities. Commonly used in Android and embedded Linux systems. See also: `busybox`, `coreutils`. More information: <https://landley.net/toybox/>.
torsocks: Route the traffic of any application through the Tor network. Note: `torsocks` will assume that it should connect to the Tor SOCKS proxy running at 127.0.0.1:9050 being the defaults of the Tor daemon. More information: <https://manned.org/torsocks>.
torify: Route network traffic through the Tor network. Note: This command is deprecated, use `torsocks` instead. `torify` is now a backwards-compatible wrapper of `torsocks`. More information: <https://manned.org/torify>.
tor: Enable anonymous communication through the Tor network. More information: <https://manned.org/tor>.
top: Display dynamic real-time information about running processes. See also: `htop`, `atop`, `glances`, `btop`, `btm`. More information: <https://manned.org/top>.
toolbox: Manage containerized command-line environments on Linux. Some subcommands such as `create` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox>.
toolbox-run: Run a command in an existing Toolbx container. See also: `toolbox enter`. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-run>.
toolbox-rmi: Remove Toolbx images. See also: `toolbox rm`. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-rmi>.
toolbox-rm: Remove one or more Toolbx containers. See also: `toolbox rmi`. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-rm>.
toolbox-list: List existing Toolbx containers and images. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-list>.
toolbox-init-container: Initialize a running Toolbx container. This command should not be executed by the user, and cannot be run on the host. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-init-container>.
toolbox-help: Display help information about Toolbx. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-help>.
toolbox-enter: Enter a Toolbx container for interactive use. See also: `toolbox run`. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-enter>.
toolbox-create: Create a new Toolbx container. More information: <https://manned.org/toolbox-create>.
tomb: Manage encrypted storage directories that can be safely transported and hidden in a filesystem. More information: <https://dyne.org/docs/tomb/manpage/>.
togglesebool: Flip the current (non-persistent) values of SELinux booleans. Note: This command is deprecated, use `setsebool` instead. More information: <https://manned.org/togglesebool>.
tod: A tiny Todoist client in Rust. It takes simple input and dumps it in your inbox or another project. Taking advantage of natural language processing to assign due dates, tags, etc. More information: <https://github.com/tod-org/tod/blob/main/docs/usage.md#usage>.
tmt: Test Management Tool for creating, running, and debugging tests. Some subcommands such as `run`, `try`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://tmt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples.html>.
tmt-try: Quickly experiment with tests and environments. More information: <https://tmt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/stories/cli.html#try>.
tmt-run: Execute `tmt` test steps. By default, all steps are run. More information: <https://tmt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/stories/cli.html#run>.
tlp: Advanced power management for Linux. See also: `tlp-stat`. More information: <https://linrunner.de/tlp/usage/tlp.html>.
tlp-stat: Generate TLP status reports. See also: `tlp`. More information: <https://linrunner.de/tlp/usage/tlp-stat>.
tload: Show system load average using ASCII art. See also: `uptime`, `w`, `top`, `ps`. More information: <https://manned.org/tload>.
timekpra: Command-line administration client for Timekpr-nExT, a tool to manage and limit computer usage time per user account. More information: <https://mjasnik.gitlab.io/timekpr-next/>.
timedatectl: Control the system time and date. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/timedatectl.html>.
tic: Compile terminfo and install for ncurses. More information: <https://manned.org/tic>.
thunar: Graphical file manager for XFCE desktop environments. See also: `caja`, `dolphin`, `nautilus`, `mc`. More information: <https://docs.xfce.org/xfce/thunar/start>.
tftp: Trivial File Transfer Protocol client. More information: <https://manned.org/tftp>.
terraria: Create and start a headless Terraria server. More information: <https://terraria.wiki.gg/wiki/Server>.
termusic: A terminal music player written in Rust that uses vim-like key bindings. See also: `cmus`, `ncmpcpp`, `audacious`. More information: <https://github.com/tramhao/termusic>.
termshark: Terminal UI for `tshark`, but looks more like `wireshark`. More information: <https://github.com/gcla/termshark/blob/master/docs/UserGuide.md>.
terminator: Arrange multiple GNOME terminals in one window. More information: <https://gnome-terminator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/advancedusage.html>.
telinit: Change SysV runlevel. Since the concept SysV runlevels is obsolete the runlevel requests will be transparently translated into systemd unit activation requests. More information: <https://manned.org/telinit>.
tegrastats: Monitor memory usage and processor usage for NVIDIA Jetson-based devices. Note: Omitting `sudo` will leave out certain output. More information: <https://developer.nvidia.com/docs/drive/drive-os/7.0.3/public/drive-os-linux-sdk/development-workflow/NVIDIA_DRIVE_Utilities/tegrastats_Utility/tegrastatsOptions32.html>.
tcptraceroute: A traceroute implementation using TCP packets. More information: <https://manned.org/tcptraceroute>.
tcpkill: Kill specified in-progress TCP connections. More information: <https://manned.org/tcpkill>.
tcpick: Packet sniffing and network traffic analysis tool. It can capture and display TCP connections and data. It can also monitor network traffic on an interface, host, or port. More information: <https://manned.org/tcpick>.
tcpflow: Capture TCP traffic for debugging and analysis. More information: <https://manned.org/tcpflow>.
tc: Show/manipulate traffic control settings. More information: <https://manned.org/tc>.
taskset: Get or set a process' CPU affinity or start a new process with a defined CPU affinity. More information: <https://manned.org/taskset>.
talk: A visual communication program which copies lines from your terminal to that of another user. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/inetutils/manual/inetutils.html#talk-invocation>.
tailf: This command has been superseded by `tail -f`. More information: <https://manned.org/tailf>.
systool: View system device information by bus, and classes. This command is part of the `sysfs` package. More information: <https://manned.org/systool>.
