systemsettings: KDE central settings program. More information: <https://manned.org/systemsettings>.
systemd-umount: This command is an alias of `systemd-mount --umount`.
systemd-tty-ask-password-agent: List or process pending systemd password requests. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-tty-ask-password-agent.html>.
systemd-tmpfiles: Create, delete, and clean up volatile and temporary files and directories. This command is automatically invoked on boot by systemd services and running it manually is usually not needed. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-tmpfiles.html>.
systemd-sysusers: Create system users and groups. If the config file is not specified, files in the `sysusers.d` directories are used. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-sysusers.html>.
systemd-sysext: Activate or deactivate system extension images. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-sysext.html>.
systemd-stdio-bridge: Implement a proxy between `stdin`/`stdout` and a D-Bus. Note: It expects to receive an open connection via `stdin`/`stdout` when started, and will create a new connection to the specified bus. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-stdio-bridge.html>.
systemd-socket-activate: Socket activation for systemd services. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-socket-activate.html>.
systemd-run: Run programs in transient scope units, service units, or path-, socket-, or timer-triggered service units. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-run.html>.
systemd-resolve: Resolve domain names, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, DNS resource records, and services. Note: This tool has been renamed to `resolvectl` in new versions of `systemd`. More information: <https://manned.org/systemd-resolve>.
systemd-repart: Automatically grow and add partitions. Grows and adds partitions based on the configuration files described in repart.d. Does not automatically resize filesystem on partition. See systemd-growfs to extend filesystem. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-repart.html>.
systemd-path: List and query system and user paths. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-path.html>.
systemd-nspawn: Spawn a command or OS in a lightweight container. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-nspawn.html>.
systemd-notify: Notify the service manager about start-up completion and other daemon status changes. This command is useless outside systemd service scripts. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-notify.html>.
systemd-mount: Establish and destroy transient mount or auto-mount points. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-mount.html>.
systemd-machine-id-setup: Initialize the machine ID stored in `/etc/machine-id` at install time with a provisioned or randomly generated ID. Note: Always use `sudo` to execute these commands as they require elevated privileges. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-machine-id-setup.html>.
systemd-inhibit: Prohibit the system from entering certain power states. Inhibitor locks may be used to block or delay system sleep and shutdown requests as well as automatic idle handling. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-inhibit.html>.
systemd-id128: Generate and print sd-128 identifiers. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-id128.html>.
systemd-hwdb: Hardware database management tool. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-hwdb.html>.
systemd-firstboot: Initialize basic system settings on or before the first boot-up of a system. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-firstboot.html>.
systemd-escape: Escape strings for usage in systemd unit names. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-escape.html>.
systemd-dissect: Introspect and interact with filesystem OS disk images, specifically Discoverable Disk Images (DDIs). More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-dissect.html>.
systemd-detect-virt: Detect execution in a virtualized environment. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-detect-virt.html>.
systemd-delta: Find overridden systemd-related configuration files. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-delta.html>.
systemd-cryptsetup: Create or remove decrypted mappings of encrypted volumes. Equivalent of `cryptsetup open` and `cryptsetup close`. Arguments to this command are written exactly like a line in `/etc/crypttab`. It's used by systemd to unlock devices on boot. See also: `cryptsetup`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-cryptsetup.html>.
systemd-cryptenroll: Interactively enroll or remove methods used to unlock LUKS2-encrypted devices. Uses a password to unlock the device unless otherwise specified. In order to allow a partition to be unlocked during system boot, update the `/etc/crypttab` file or the initramfs. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-cryptenroll.html>.
systemd-creds: List, show, encrypt, and decrypt service credentials. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-creds.html>.
systemd-confext: This command is an alias of `systemd-sysext`. It follows the same principle as `systemd-sysext`, but instead of working on `/usr` and `/opt`, `confext` will extend only `/etc`.
systemd-cgtop: Show the top control groups of the local Linux control group hierarchy, ordered by their CPU, memory, or disk I/O load. See also: `top`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-cgtop.html>.
systemd-cgls: Show the contents of the selected Linux control group hierarchy in a tree. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-cgls.html>.
systemd-cat: Connect a pipeline or program's output streams with the systemd journal. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-cat.html>.
systemd-ask-password: Query the user for a system password. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-ask-password.html>.
systemd-analyze: Analyze and debug system manager. Show timing details about the boot process of units (services, mount points, devices, sockets). More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-analyze.html>.
systemd-ac-power: Report whether the computer is connected to an external power source. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-ac-power.html>.
systemctl: Control the systemd system and service manager. Some subcommands such as `disable`, `status`, `reboot`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html>.
systemctl-whoami: Show units that processes belong to. If no PID is specified, shows the unit the `systemctl` command itself is invoked in. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#whoami%20%5BPID%E2%80%A6%5D>.
systemctl-unset-environment: Unset one or more service manager environment variables. This undoes the effect of `systemctl set-environment`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#unset-environment%20VARIABLE%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-unmask: Unmask units to make them startable again. This undoes the effect of `systemctl mask`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#unmask%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-try-restart: Restart one or more units only if they are currently running. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#try-restart%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-try-reload-or-restart: Reload one or more units if they support it; otherwise restart them. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#try-reload-or-restart%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-thaw: Thaw (resume) one or more frozen units. Units can be frozen with `systemctl freeze`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#thaw%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-switch-root: Switch to a new root filesystem and execute a new system manager. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#switch-root%20ROOT%20INIT>.
systemctl-suspend-then-hibernate: Suspend the system, then automatically hibernate after a period of inactivity. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#suspend-then-hibernate>.
systemctl-status: Display the status of systemd units. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#status%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6%7CPID%E2%80%A6%5D>.
systemctl-soft-reboot: Shut down and reboot userspace, leaving the kernel running. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#soft-reboot>.
systemctl-show: Show properties of units or systemd itself. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#show%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6%7CJOB%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-show-environment: Display systemd environment blocks. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#show-environment>.
systemctl-set-property: Set the specified unit properties at runtime. See also: `systemctl revert`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#set-property%20UNIT%20PROPERTY=VALUE%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-set-environment: Set one or more service manager environment variables. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#set-environment%20VARIABLE=VALUE%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-set-default: Symlink the `default.target` alias to the given target unit. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#set-default%20TARGET>.
systemctl-service-watchdogs: Get or set the global state of service runtime watchdogs. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#service-watchdogs%20%5Byes%7Cno%5D>.
systemctl-service-log-target: Get or set the log target for a service. Only works for D-Bus integrated services. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#service-log-target%20SERVICE%20%5BTARGET%5D>.
systemctl-service-log-level: Get or set the runtime log level of a service via D-Bus. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#service-log-level%20SERVICE%20%5BLEVEL%5D>.
systemctl-revert: Revert unit files to their vendor versions. Undoes the effects of `edit`, `enable`, `disable`, `set-property`, and `mask`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#revert%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-restart: Stop and then start one or more systemd units. Can be used in place of `systemctl start` on a stopped unit, but `start` is safer so that a running unit isn't accidentally restarted. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#restart%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-reset-failed: Reset the "failed" state of one or more units. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#reset-failed%20%5BPATTERN%E2%80%A6%5D>.
systemctl-rescue: Enter rescue mode. See also: `systemctl emergency`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#rescue>.
systemctl-reload: Reload a service's configuration without restarting it. This reloads the service itself (like Apache or `nginx` configs), not the systemd unit file. To reload unit files, use `systemctl daemon-reload`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#reload%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-reload-or-try-restart: This command is an alias of `systemctl try-reload-or-restart`.
systemctl-reload-or-restart: Reload `systemd` unit(s) otherwise restart them. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#reload-or-restart%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-reenable: Re-enable one or more units. Used when targets of a service change. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#reenable%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-preset: Reset the enablement state of unit files to the defaults specified in preset policy files. See also: `systemctl preset-all`, `systemctl list-unit-files`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#preset%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-preset-all: Reset the enablement state of all installed units to the defaults specified in preset policy files. See also: `systemctl preset`, `systemctl list-unit-files`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#preset-all>.
systemctl-poweroff: Power off the system. See also: `poweroff`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#poweroff>.
systemctl-mount-image: Mount an image file into a unit's mount namespace. Only supported for the units that run within a mountspace i.e. with `RootImage=`, `PrivateMounts=`, etc. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#mount-image%20UNIT%20IMAGE%20%5BPATH%20%5BPARTITION_NAME:MOUNT_OPTIONS%5D%5D>.
systemctl-mask: Link units to `/dev/null` so that they cannot be started. See also: `systemctl revert`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#mask%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-log-target: Get or set the log target for the systemd manager. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#log-target%20%5BTARGET%5D>.
systemctl-log-level: Get or set the log level of the systemd manager. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#log-level%20%5BLEVEL%5D>.
systemctl-list-units: List units that systemd currently has in memory. See also: `systemctl list-unit-files`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-units%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-unit-files: List installed unit files and their enablement states. See also: `systemctl list-units`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-unit-files%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-timers: List all active systemd timers. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-timers%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-sockets: List active socket units currently in memory, ordered by listening address. See also: `systemctl list-units`, `systemctl list-unit-files`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-sockets%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-paths: List path units currently in memory, ordered by path. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-paths%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-machines: List the host and all running local virtual machines or containers with their state. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-machines%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-jobs: List of active systemd jobs that are currently queued or running on the system. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-jobs%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-dependencies: Show a unit's dependency tree in systemd. See also: `systemctl list-units`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-dependencies%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-list-automounts: List automount units currently in memory, showing mount paths and unit names. See also: `systemctl list-units`, `systemctl list-unit-files`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#list-automounts%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-link: Link a unit file located outside the unit file search path into the search path. See also: `systemctl disable`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#link%20PATH%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-kill: Send a signal to one or more processes of a unit. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#kill%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-kexec: Reboot the system via kexec. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#kexec>.
systemctl-isolate: Start the specified unit with its dependencies and stop all others. Ignores the units which have `IgnoreOnIsolate=yes`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#isolate%20UNIT>.
systemctl-is-system-running: Check the current state of the system. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#is-system-running>.
systemctl-is-failed: Check if one or more systemd units have failed. See also: `systemctl is-active`, `systemctl status`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#is-failed%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-is-enabled: Check whether unit files are enabled. See also: `systemctl enable`, `systemctl disable`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#is-enabled%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-is-active: Check if one or more systemd units are active. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#is-active%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-import-environment: Import environment variables from the shell into systemd's environment. See also: `systemctl show-environment`, `systemctl unset-environment`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#import-environment%20VARIABLE%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-hybrid-sleep: Put the system into hybrid sleep, which combines suspend-to-RAM and hibernate. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#hybrid-sleep>.
systemctl-hibernate: Hibernate the system by saving the current state to disk and powering off. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#hibernate>.
systemctl-help: Show the manual pages for one or more units, or for the unit a process belongs to (by PID). More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#help%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6%7CPID%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-halt: Shut down and halt the system (stop the OS kernel but keep hardware powered on). See also: `halt`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#halt>.
systemctl-get-default: Display the default target (runlevel) that the system will boot into. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#get-default>.
systemctl-freeze: Freeze one or more units. Frozen units can be resumed with `systemctl thaw`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#freeze%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-force-reload: This command is an alias of `systemctl try-reload-or-restart`.
systemctl-exit: Ask the service manager to quit. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#exit%20EXIT_CODE>.
systemctl-enable: Enable systemd services. See also: `systemctl revert`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#enable%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-edit: Edit systemd unit files. See also: `systemctl revert`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#edit%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-disable: Disable systemd services. See also: `systemctl revert`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#disable%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-default: Enter system default mode. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#default>.
systemctl-daemon-reload: Reload systemd manager configuration. Use this after creating, modifying, or deleting unit files. See also: `systemctl reload`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#daemon-reload>.
systemctl-daemon-reexec: Reexecute systemd while preserving current unit states. See also: `systemctl daemon-reload`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#daemon-reexec>.
systemctl-condstop: This command is an alias of `systemctl stop`.
systemctl-condrestart: This command is an alias of `systemctl try-restart`.
systemctl-condreload: This command is an alias of `systemctl try-reload-or-restart`.
systemctl-cat: Show the full contents of unit files as systemd sees them. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#cat%20PATTERN%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-cancel: Cancel one or more pending jobs in the system manager or user manager. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#cancel%20JOB%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-bind: Ephemerally bind-mount a file or directory from the host into a unit's mount namespace. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#bind%20UNIT%20PATH%20%5BPATH%5D>.
systemctl-add-wants: Add `Wants` dependencies to a target for one or more units. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#add-wants%20TARGET%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
systemctl-add-requires: Add `Requires` dependencies to a target for one or more units. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html#add-wants%20TARGET%20UNIT%E2%80%A6>.
sysdig: System troubleshooting, analysis, and exploration. Capture, filter, and store systemcalls. More information: <https://github.com/draios/sysdig/wiki>.
sysctl: List and change kernel runtime variables. More information: <https://manned.org/sysctl.8>.
synoupgrade: Upgrade Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) - the Synology NAS operating system. More information: <https://www.synology.com/dsm>.
synopkg: Package management utility for Synology DiskStation Manager. More information: <https://www.synology.com/dsm>.
sync: Flush all pending write operations to the appropriate disks. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/sync-invocation.html>.
sxiv: Simple X Image Viewer. More information: <https://manned.org/sxiv>.
swww: This command has been renamed to `awww`.
swupd: Package management utility for Clear Linux. More information: <https://github.com/clearlinux/clear-linux-documentation/blob/master/source/guides/clear/swupd.rst>.
switcherooctl: Launch a command on a specific GPU. More information: <https://manned.org/switcherooctl>.
switch_root: Use a different filesystem as the root of the mount tree. Note: `switch_root` will fail to function if the new root is not the root of a mount. Use bind-mounting as a workaround. See also: `chroot`, `mount`. More information: <https://manned.org/switch_root>.
swapon: Enable devices and files for swapping. Note: `path/to/file` can either point to a regular file or a swap partition. More information: <https://manned.org/swapon.8>.
swapoff: Disable devices and files for swapping. Note: `path/to/file` can either point to a regular file or a swap partition. More information: <https://manned.org/swapoff.8>.
swaplabel: Print or change the label or UUID of a swap area. Note: `path/to/file` can either point to a regular file or a swap partition. More information: <https://manned.org/swaplabel>.
swaks: Swiss Army Knife SMTP, the all-purpose SMTP transaction tester. More information: <https://github.com/jetmore/swaks/blob/develop/doc/base.pod>.
sview: Start a GUI to view and modify the state of Slurm. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sview.html>.
sulogin: Log in as root during single-user mode. More information: <https://manned.org/sulogin>.
su: Switch shell to another user. More information: <https://manned.org/su>.
strip: Discard symbols from executables or object files. More information: <https://manned.org/strip>.
strigger: View or modify Slurm trigger information. Triggers are actions that are automatically run when an event occurs on a Slurm cluster. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/strigger.html>.
stress: Stress test CPU, memory, and IO on a Linux system. More information: <https://manned.org/stress>.
stratis: Manage local storage pools and volumes using the Stratis storage manager. Stratis volumes use the XFS filesystem and require the `stratisd` service. More information: <https://stratis-storage.github.io/howto/>.
strace: Troubleshooting tool for tracing system calls. See also: `fatrace`. More information: <https://manned.org/strace>.
storagectl: Enumerate and mount storage volumes. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/storagectl.html>.
stegsnow: Steganography tool for concealing and extracting messages in text files encoded as tabs and spaces. More information: <https://darkside.com.au/snow/manual.html>.
steghide: Steganography tool for JPEG, BMP, WAV, and AU file formats. More information: <https://manned.org/steghide>.
steamosctl: Control the SteamOS system. More information: <https://gitlab.com/evlaV/steamos-manager>.
steamos-update: Update SteamOS. Note: This command is deprecated, use `atomupd-manager` instead. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-session-select: Manipulate which session is currently in use. Note: This command is deprecated, use `steamosctl` instead. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-select-branch: Select a SteamOS system release branch. Note: This command is deprecated, use `atomupd-manager` instead. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-readonly: Set the readonly status of the filesystem. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-finalize-install: Complete a SteamOS installation by setting up bootloaders and applying system updates. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-factory-reset: Reset SteamOS to factory settings. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-factory-reset-config: Generate configuration files required by `steamos-factory-reset`. This command is typically called internally and not meant to be run manually. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-dump-info: View SteamOS system information. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-devmode: Enable SteamOS developer mode. Note: Developer mode disables read-only protections and initializes the package manager. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-chroot: Switch root directory in a SteamOS environment. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-bootdebug: Manage the SteamOS boot process. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
steamos-boot-install: This command is an alias of `steamos-finalize-install`.
steamos-add-to-steam: Add a program to Steam library. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
startx: A front-end to `xinit` that provides a nice user interface for running a single session of the X Window System. More information: <https://www.x.org/releases/X11R7.6/doc/man/man1/startx.1.xhtml>.
st.term: A simple terminal emulator for the X Window System. More information: <https://manned.org/st>.
sstat: View information about running jobs. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sstat.html>.
sslstrip: Perform Moxie Marlinspike's Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) stripping attacks. Perform an ARP spoofing attack in conjunction. More information: <https://www.kali.org/tools/sslstrip/>.
sshare: List the shares of associations to a cluster. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sshare.html>.
ss: Utility to investigate sockets. More information: <https://manned.org/ss>.
sreport: Generate reports on jobs, users, and clusters from accounting data. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sreport.html>.
squeue: View the jobs queued in the SLURM scheduler. More information: <https://manned.org/squeue>.
sqfstar: Create a squashfs filesystem from a `.tar` archive. More information: <https://manned.org/sqfstar>.
sqfscat: Concatenate files from a squashfs filesystem and print them to `stdout`. More information: <https://manned.org/sqfscat>.
sprof: Read and display shared object profiling data. Note: Requires profile data generated via the `$LD_PROFILE` environment variable. More information: <https://manned.org/sprof>.
sprio: View the factors determining a job's scheduling priority. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sprio.html>.
sport: Search and install SlackBuilds. More information: <http://slackermedia.info/handbook/doku.php?id=slackbuilds>.
spi: A meta package manager that handles both packages and slackbuilds. More information: <https://github.com/gapan/spi/blob/master/man/spi.t2t>.
speedread: A Spritz-alike speed reader. Show text using per-word Rapid Serial Visual Presentation (RSVP). More information: <https://github.com/pasky/speedread>.
speedometer: Python script that shows a network traffic graph in the terminal. More information: <https://excess.org/speedometer/>.
spectre-meltdown-checker: Spectre and Meltdown mitigation detection tool. More information: <https://manned.org/spectre-meltdown-checker>.
speaker-test: Speaker test tone generator for ALSA. See also: `aplay`, `arecord`, `amixer`. More information: <https://manned.org/speaker-test>.
spa-resample: Resample an audio file using the PipeWire resampler. Note: This utility is primarily intended for testing and debugging the resampler. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_spa-resample_1.html>.
spa-monitor: Load a SPA plugin and instantiate a device from it. Note: This utility is primarily intended for debugging device plugins. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_spa-monitor_1.html>.
spa-json-dump: Convert a SPA JSON file to standard JSON. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_spa-json-dump_1.html>.
spa-inspect: Display SPA plugin information, list and try to instantiate available factories. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_spa-inspect_1.html>.
spa-acp-tool: Debug ALSA card profile probing without running PipeWire. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_spa-acp-tool_1.html>.
sos: A unified tool for collecting system logs and other debug information. Used by system administrators and support representatives to assist in troubleshooting. More information: <https://github.com/sosreport/sos>.
sockstat: List open Internet or UNIX domain sockets. See also: `netstat`. More information: <https://manned.org/sockstat>.
snapper: Filesystem snapshot management tool. More information: <http://snapper.io/manpages/snapper.html>.
snap.pkg: Manage the "snap" self-contained software packages. Similar to what `apt` is for `.deb`. More information: <https://manned.org/snap>.
snap: `snap` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
snap.esa: Sentinel Application Platform (SNAP) for processing satellite data from the European Space Agency (ESA). More information: <https://step.esa.int/main/download/snap-download/>.
snake4scores: Show the high scores from the snake4 game. More information: <https://manned.org/snake4>.
snake4: Snake game in the terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/snake4>.
smem: Print memory usage for programs. More information: <https://manned.org/smem>.
smbpasswd: Add/remove a Samba user or change its password. Samba users must have an existing local Unix account. More information: <https://manned.org/smbpasswd.8>.
smbnetfs: Mount SMB shares interactively. More information: <https://sourceforge.net/projects/smbnetfs/>.
smbget: `wget`-like utility for downloading files from SMB servers. More information: <https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbget.1.html>.
smbcacls: View and manipulate Windows ACLs on SMB shares. Part of the Samba suite. More information: <https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbcacls.1.html>.
sm: Display a short message fullscreen. More information: <https://github.com/nomeata/screen-message>.
slurp: Select a region in a Wayland compositor. More information: <https://github.com/emersion/slurp/blob/master/slurp.1.scd>.
slurmstepd: Slurm daemon for managing and monitoring individual job steps within a multi-step job. Note: It should not be invoked manually. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/slurmstepd.html>.
slurmrestd: Interface to Slurm via REST API. Note: Can be used in two modes: Inetd Mode and Listen Mode. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/slurmrestd.html>.
slurmdbd: A secure enterprise-wide interface to a database for Slurm. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/slurmdbd.html>.
slurmd: Monitor all tasks running on the compute node, accept tasks, launch tasks, and kill running tasks upon request. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/slurmd.html>.
slurmctld: Monitor all other Slurm daemons and resources, accept work (jobs), and allocate resources to those jobs. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/slurmctld.html>.
slop: Get a selection of the screen. More information: <https://manned.org/slop>.
slapt-src: A utility to automate building of slackbuilds. SlackBuild sources need to be configured in the slapt-srcrc file. More information: <https://github.com/jaos/slapt-src>.
slapt-get: An `apt` like system for Slackware package management. Package sources need to be configured in the slapt-getrc file. More information: <https://software.jaos.org/git/slapt-get/plain/README>.
slabtop: Display kernel slab cache information in real time. See also: `top`, `htop`, `atop`. More information: <https://manned.org/slabtop>.
size: Display the sizes of sections inside binary files. More information: <https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/binutils/size.html>.
sio: A comprehensive Linux hardware information and real-time sensor monitoring tool. More information: <https://github.com/level1techs/siomon>.
sinfo: View information about Slurm nodes and partitions. See also: `squeue`, `sbatch`. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sinfo.html>.
silentcast: Silent screencast creator. Saves in `.mkv` and animated GIF formats. More information: <https://github.com/colinkeenan/silentcast>.
sic: Simple IRC client. Part of the suckless tools. More information: <https://manned.org/sic>.
shutdown: Shut down and reboot the system. See also: `poweroff`. More information: <https://manned.org/shutdown.8>.
showkey: Display the keycode of pressed keys on the keyboard, helpful for debugging keyboard-related issues and key remapping. More information: <https://manned.org/showkey>.
shntool-split: This command is an alias of `shnsplit`.
shnsplit: Split audio files according to a `.cue` file. More information: <http://shnutils.freeshell.org/shntool/>.
shiny-mirrors: Generate a `pacman` mirror list for Manjaro Linux. Every run of shiny-mirrors requires you to synchronize your database and update your system using `sudo pacman -Syyu`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/Arisa_Snowbell/shiny-mirrors/-/blob/domina/shiny-mirrors/man/shiny-mirrors.md>.
shelly: A modern, unified package manager for Arch Linux. See also: `pacman`, `paru`, `yay`. More information: <https://www.seafoam-labs.org/shelly-alpm/docs/cli-reference/>.
sh5util: Merge HDF5 files produced by the `sacct_gather_profile` plugin. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sh5util.html>.
sfill: Securely overwrite the free space and inodes of the partition where the specified directory resides. More information: <https://manned.org/sfill>.
sfdisk: Display or manipulate a disk partition table. More information: <https://manned.org/sfdisk>.
setxkbmap: Set the keyboard using the X Keyboard Extension. More information: <https://manned.org/setxkbmap>.
setterm: Set terminal attributes such as colors, cursor visibility, and screen blanking. Note: Some options only work in virtual consoles (TTY). More information: <https://manned.org/setterm>.
setsid: Run a program in a new session if the calling process is not a process group leader. The created session is by default not controlled by the current terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/setsid>.
setserial: Read and modify serial port information. More information: <https://manned.org/setserial>.
setsebool: Set SELinux boolean value. See also: `semanage boolean`, `getsebool`. More information: <https://manned.org/setsebool>.
setleds: Set lock key and LED states. More information: <https://manned.org/setleds>.
setfont: Set the terminal font for TTYs. More information: <https://manned.org/setfont>.
setfiles: Set SELinux file security contexts based on policy rules. Similar to `restorecon` but reads contexts from a file_contexts file. See also: `restorecon`, `semanage fcontext`, `fixfiles`. More information: <https://manned.org/setfiles>.
setfattr: Set extended file attributes. See also: `getfattr`. More information: <https://manned.org/setfattr>.
setfacl: Set file access control lists (ACL). More information: <https://manned.org/setfacl>.
setenforce: Toggle SELinux between enforcing and permissive modes. To enable or disable SELinux, edit `/etc/selinux/config` instead. See also: `getenforce`, `semanage permissive`. More information: <https://manned.org/setenforce>.
setcap: Set capabilities of specified file. See also: `getcap`. More information: <https://manned.org/setcap>.
setarch: Change the reported architecture for a program's execution, primarily used to modify how programs behave based on system architecture. Useful for compatibility testing or running legacy applications. More information: <https://manned.org/setarch>.
sestatus: Print the current SELinux status. More information: <https://manned.org/sestatus>.
sesearch: Search SELinux policy rules. Part of the `setools` package. See also: `semodule`. More information: <https://manned.org/sesearch>.
service: Manage services by running init scripts. The full script path should be omitted (`/etc/init.d/` is assumed). More information: <https://manned.org/service>.
sensors: Report sensors information. See also: `btm`, `btop`. More information: <https://manned.org/sensors>.
sensible-editor: Open the default editor. More information: <https://manned.org/sensible-editor>.
sensible-browser: Open the default browser. More information: <https://manned.org/sensible-browser>.
semodule: Manage SELinux policy modules. See also: `audit2allow`, `semanage`. More information: <https://manned.org/semodule>.
semanage: SELinux persistent policy management tool. Some subcommands such as `boolean`, `fcontext`, `port`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage>.
semanage-user: Manage SELinux user mappings. See also: `semanage login`. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-user>.
semanage-port: Manage persistent SELinux port definitions. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-port>.
semanage-permissive: Manage persistent SELinux permissive domains. Note that this effectively makes the process unconfined. For long-term use, it is recommended to configure SELinux properly. See also: `getenforce`, `setenforce`. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-permissive>.
semanage-login: Manage SELinux login mappings between Linux users and SELinux users. See also: `semanage user`. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-login>.
semanage-interface: Manage SELinux network interface type definitions. See also: `semanage port`. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-interface>.
semanage-fcontext: Manage persistent SELinux security context rules on files/directories. See also: `matchpathcon`, `secon`, `chcon`, `restorecon`. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-fcontext>.
semanage-boolean: Manage persistent SELinux boolean settings. See also: `getsebool`, `setsebool`. More information: <https://manned.org/semanage-boolean>.
selinuxenabled: Check whether SELinux is enabled. Returns exit code 0 if SELinux is enabled, and 1 if it is not. See also: `getenforce`, `setenforce`, `sestatus`. More information: <https://manned.org/selinuxenabled>.
see: This command is an alias of `run-mailcap --action=view`.
secret-tool: Store and retrieve passwords, part of the `libsecret` package. Communicates with Freedesktop secret service implementations such as `gnome-keyring`. More information: <https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libsecret/>.
secon: Get the SELinux security context of a file, pid, current execution context, or a context specification. See also: `semanage`, `runcon`, `chcon`. More information: <https://manned.org/secon>.
sealert: Analyze and explain SELinux AVC denial messages. Part of the `setroubleshoot-server` package. See also: `audit2why`, `ausearch`, `audit2allow`. More information: <https://manned.org/sealert>.
sdiag: Show information about the execution of `slurmctld`. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sdiag.html>.
scrun: An OCI runtime proxy for Slurm that runs containers as jobs. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/scrun.html>.
scrub: Securely overwrite files, block devices, or free disk space. More information: <https://manned.org/scrub>.
scrontab: Manage Slurm crontab files. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/scrontab.html>.
scriptreplay: Replay a typescript created by the `script` command to `stdout`. More information: <https://manned.org/scriptreplay>.
scriptlive: Execute a typescript created by the `script` command in real-time. See also: `script`. More information: <https://manned.org/scriptlive>.
script: Record all terminal output to a typescript file. More information: <https://manned.org/script>.
screenkey: A screencast tool to display keys pressed. More information: <https://www.thregr.org/wavexx/software/screenkey/>.
scontrol: View information about and modify jobs. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/scontrol.html>.
schroot: Run a command or start an interactive shell with a different root directory. More customizable than `chroot`. More information: <https://wiki.debian.org/Schroot>.
scanimage: Scan images with the Scanner Access Now Easy API. More information: <http://sane-project.org/man/scanimage.1.html>.
scancel: Cancel a Slurm job. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/scancel.html>.
scalpel: Recover files from a disk image based on file headers and footers. File patterns must be enabled in the configuration file (all are commented out by default). More information: <https://manned.org/scalpel>.
sbpctl: Manage the systemd-boot-password boot manager, a systemd-boot fork with a password-protected editor. See also: `bootctl`. More information: <https://github.com/kitsunyan/systemd-boot-password#boot-manager-installing-and-configuration>.
sbctl: A user-friendly secure boot key manager. Note: Not enrolling Microsoft's certificates can brick your system. See <https://github.com/Foxboron/sbctl/wiki/FAQ#option-rom>. More information: <https://github.com/Foxboron/sbctl#usage>.
sbcast: Send a file to a job's allocated nodes. This command should only be used from within a Slurm batch job. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbcast.html>.
sbatch: Submit a batch job to the SLURM scheduler. More information: <https://manned.org/sbatch>.
sattach: Attach to a Slurm job step. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sattach.html>.
sar: Monitor performance of various Linux subsystems. More information: <https://manned.org/sar>.
sam: AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) CLI. More information: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-corecommands.html>.
salloc: Start an interactive shell session or execute a command by allocating one or more nodes in a cluster. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/salloc.html>.
sacctmgr: View, set up, and manage Slurm accounts. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacctmgr.html>.
sacct: Display accounting data from the Slurm service. More information: <https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacct.html>.
sa: Summarize accounting information about commands called by users, including basic information on CPU time spent processing and I/O rates. Part of the `acct` package. More information: <https://manned.org/sa.8>.
rusnapshot: BTRFS snapshotting utility written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/Edu4rdSHL/rusnapshot>.
runuser: Run commands as a user and group without asking for password. More information: <https://manned.org/runuser>.
runlim: Sample and limit time and memory usage of a program and its child processes using the proc filesystem on Linux. More information: <https://fmv.jku.at/runlim/>.
runlevel: SysV runlevel utility. See also: `init`. More information: <https://manned.org/runlevel>.
runcon: Run a program in a different SELinux security context. See also: `secon`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/runcon-invocation.html>.
run_init: Run init scripts in the proper SELinux context. Typically used to run system service scripts with correct SELinux domains. See also: `runcon`, `semanage`. More information: <https://manned.org/run_init>.
run0: Elevate privileges interactively. Similar to `sudo`, but it's not a SUID binary, authentication takes place via polkit, and commands are invoked from a `systemd` service. See also: `sudo`, `pkexec`, `doas`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/run0.html>.
run-mailcap: Execute programs via entries in the mailcap file. More information: <https://manned.org/run-mailcap>.
ruget: Alternative to `wget` written in Rust. More information: <https://github.com/ksk001100/ruget>.
rtmon: Save network state changes to a file. More information: <https://manned.org/rtmon>.
rtcwake: Enter a system sleep state until specified wakeup time relative to your BIOS clock. More information: <https://manned.org/rtcwake>.
rsh: Execute commands on a remote host. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/inetutils/manual/inetutils.html#rsh-invocation>.
rpmspec: Query an RPM spec file. More information: <https://manned.org/rpmspec>.
rpmkeys: Tool to import and remove RPM keys for RPM repositories. When adding an RPM repository, you must also import the corresponding RPM key. More information: <https://rpm-software-management.github.io/rpm/man/rpmkeys.8>.
rpmconf: Handle `.rpmnew`, `.rpmsave`, and `.rpmorig` files left over by package upgrades. See also: `rpm`. More information: <https://manned.org/rpmconf.8>.
rpmbuild: RPM Package Build tool. More information: <https://manned.org/rpmbuild>.
rpm2cpio: Convert an RPM package to a `cpio` archive. More information: <http://ftp.rpm.org/max-rpm/s1-rpm-miscellania-rpm2cpio.html>.
rpm: RPM Package Manager. For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. More information: <https://rpm-software-management.github.io/rpm/man/rpm.8>.
rpm-ostree: A hybrid image/package system. Manage ostree deployments, package layers, filesystem overlays, and boot configuration. More information: <https://coreos.github.io/rpm-ostree/administrator-handbook/>.
rpicam-vid: Capture a video using a Raspberry Pi camera. See also: `vlc`. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/camera_software.html#rpicam-vid>.
rpicam-still: Capture and store a photo using a Raspberry Pi camera with legacy features missing from `rpicam-jpeg`. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/camera_software.html#rpicam-still>.
rpicam-raw: Capture a raw video on a Raspberry Pi camera. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/camera_software.html#rpicam-raw>.
rpicam-jpeg: Capture and store a JPEG image using a Raspberry Pi camera. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/camera_software.html#rpicam-jpeg>.
rpicam-hello: View a live camera stream using a Raspberry Pi camera. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/camera_software.html#rpicam-hello>.
rpi-otp-private-key: Display the One-Time Programmable (OTP) private key of a Raspberry Pi. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/raspberry-pi.html#program-a-key-into-otp-with-rpi-otp-private-key>.
rpi-eeprom-update: Update EEPROM and view other EEPROM information. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/raspberry-pi.html#rpi-eeprom-update>.
rpcinfo: Make an RPC call to an RPC server and reports what it finds. More information: <https://manned.org/rpcinfo>.
rpcclient: MS-RPC client tool (part of the samba suite). More information: <https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/rpcclient.1.html>.
routel: List IP routing in a human readable format. See also: `ip route`, `route`. More information: <https://manned.org/routel>.
rofi: An application launcher and window switcher. More information: <https://github.com/davatorium/rofi#manpage>.
rmpc: A terminal music player client for the Music Player Daemon, with album art support. See also: `mpd`, `mpc`, `ncmpcpp`. More information: <https://rmpc.mierak.dev/reference/cli-command-mode/>.
rmmod: Remove modules from the Linux kernel. See also: `kmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/rmmod>.
rlogin: Log in to a remote host. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/inetutils/manual/inetutils.html#rlogin-invocation>.
rkhunter: Search for rootkits and malware. More information: <https://manned.org/rkhunter>.
ripmime: Extract attachments out of a MIME encoded email package. More information: <https://pldaniels.com/ripmime/>.
rig: Utility to piece together a random first name, last name, street number, and address, along with a geographically consistent (i.e. they all match the same area) city, state, ZIP code, and area code. More information: <https://manned.org/rig>.
rfkill: Enable and disable wireless devices. More information: <https://manned.org/rfkill>.
rexec: Execute a command on a remote host. Note: Use `rexec` with caution, as it transmits data in plain text. Consider secure alternatives like SSH for encrypted communication. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/inetutils/manual/inetutils.html#rexec-invocation>.
rev: Reverse a line of text or a file. More information: <https://manned.org/rev>.
retroarch: A frontend for emulators, game engines, and media players. The reference implementation of the libretro API. More information: <https://manned.org/retroarch>.
restorecond: Daemon that monitors file creation and automatically restores SELinux contexts. Useful for directories where files are frequently created with incorrect contexts. See also: `restorecon`, `semanage fcontext`. More information: <https://manned.org/restorecond>.
restorecon: Restore SELinux security context on files/directories according to persistent rules. See also: `semanage fcontext`. More information: <https://manned.org/restorecon>.
resolveip: Resolve hostnames to their IP addresses and vice versa. More information: <https://mariadb.com/docs/server/clients-and-utilities/networking-tools/resolveip>.
resolvectl: Resolve domain names, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, DNS resource records, and services. Note: `systemd-resolved.service` must be running. See also: `dig`, `nslookup`, `host`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/resolvectl.html>.
resize2fs: Resize an ext2, ext3, or ext4 filesystem. Does not resize the underlying partition. The filesystem may have to be unmounted first, read the man page for more details. More information: <https://manned.org/resize2fs>.
resize: Resize terminal size to the window size. More information: <https://manned.org/resize>.
reset: Reinitialize the current terminal. Clears the entire terminal screen. More information: <https://manned.org/reset>.
reptyr: Move a running process to a new terminal. Best used when you forget to start a long running task in `screen`. More information: <https://github.com/nelhage/reptyr#usage>.
repquota: Display a summary of existing file quotas for a filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/repquota>.
reportbug: Bug report tool of Debian distribution. More information: <https://manned.org/reportbug>.
repo-remove: Package database maintenance utility which removes packages from a local repository. See also: `repo-add`. More information: <https://manned.org/repo-remove>.
repo-add: Package database maintenance utility which enables installation of said package via Pacman. See also: `repo-remove`. More information: <https://manned.org/repo-add>.
rename.util: Rename multiple files. WARNING: This command will overwrite files without prompting unless the `--no-act` option is used. Note: This page refers to the command from the `util-linux` package. More information: <https://manned.org/rename>.
rename.ul: This command is an alias of `rename.util`.
removepkg: Remove a specified Slackware package. More information: <https://www.slackbook.org/html/book.html#PACKAGE-MANAGEMENT-PACKAGE-UTILITIES-REMOVEPKG>.
register_new_matrix_user: Register new users in a home server when registration has been disabled. More information: <https://manned.org/register_new_matrix_user>.
reflector: Arch script to fetch and sort mirrorlists. More information: <https://manned.org/reflector>.
readpe: Display information about PE files. More information: <https://manned.org/readpe>.
readelf: Display information about ELF files. More information: <https://manned.org/readelf>.
readcd: Read or write Compact Disc media data. More information: <https://manned.org/readcd>.
rdesktop: Remote Desktop Protocol client. It can be used to connect the remote computer using the RDP protocol. More information: <https://manned.org/rdesktop>.
rcp: Copy files between local and remote systems. It mimics the behavior of the `cp` command but operates across different machines. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/inetutils/manual/inetutils.html#rcp-invocation>.
rc-update: Add and remove OpenRC services to and from runlevels. See also: `openrc`. More information: <https://manned.org/rc-update>.
rc-status: Show status info about runlevels. See also: `openrc`. More information: <https://manned.org/rc-status>.
rc-service: Locate and run OpenRC services with arguments. See also: `openrc`. More information: <https://manned.org/rc-service>.
raw: Bind a Unix raw character device. More information: <https://manned.org/raw.8>.
rauc: Lightweight update client for Embedded Linux devices to create, inspect, and install update bundles. More information: <https://manned.org/rauc>.
raspinfo: Display Raspberry Pi system information. More information: <https://github.com/raspberrypi/utils/tree/master/raspinfo>.
raspi-config: An `ncurses` terminal GUI to config a Raspberry Pi. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/configuration.html>.
rankmirrors: Rank a list of Pacman mirrors by connection and opening speed. Writes the new mirrorlist to `stdout`. More information: <https://manned.org/rankmirrors>.
radeontop: Show utilization of AMD GPUs. May require root privileges depending on your system. See also: `nvtop`, `amdgpu_top`. More information: <https://github.com/clbr/radeontop/blob/master/radeontop.asc>.
qwen-vl: The examples for this command have been moved together with `inference-snap`. More information: <https://github.com/canonical/qwen-vl-snap>.
quotacheck: Scan a filesystem for disk usage; create, check, and repair quota files. It is best to run quota check with quotas turned off to prevent damage or loss to quota files. More information: <https://manned.org/quotacheck>.
quickget: Download and prepare materials for building a Quickemu virtual machine. Note: The parameter "edition" is sometimes optional. See also: `quickemu`. More information: <https://github.com/quickemu-project/quickemu>.
quickemu: Build and manage highly optimized desktop virtual machines quickly. Note: Virtual machine must be in stopped state when working with snapshots. See also: `quickget`. More information: <https://github.com/quickemu-project/quickemu>.
qtile: A full-featured, hackable tiling window manager written and configured in Python. More information: <https://docs.qtile.org/en/latest/manual/commands/shell/index.html>.
qtgrace: Display, plot, analyze 2D data. A Qt reimplementation of Grace (<https://plasma-gate.weizmann.ac.il/Grace/>), sharing its command-line interface. More information: <https://sourceforge.net/projects/qtgrace/>.
qtchooser: A wrapper used to select between Qt development binary versions. More information: <https://manned.org/qtchooser>.
qsub: Submit a script to the queue management system TORQUE. More information: <https://manned.org/qsub.1>.
qrcp: A file transfer tool. More information: <https://github.com/claudiodangelis/qrcp#usage>.
qm: QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. Some subcommands such as `list`, `start`, `stop`, `clone`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html>.
qm-wait: Wait until the virtual machine is stopped. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_wait>.
qm-vncproxy: Proxy Virtual Machine VNC (Virtual network computing) traffic to `stdin` or `stdout`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_vncproxy>.
qm-unlock: Unlock a virtual machine in QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_unlock>.
qm-unlink: This command is an alias of `qm disk unlink`.
qm-terminal: Attach to the serial console of a VM. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_terminal>.
qm-template: Create a Proxmox VM template. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_template>.
qm-suspend: Suspend a virtual machine (VM) in the Proxmox Virtual Environment (PVE). Use `--skiplock` and `--skiplockstorage` flags with caution, as they may lead to data corruption in certain situations. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_suspend>.
qm-stop: Stop a virtual machine. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_stop>.
qm-status: Show virtual machine status. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_status>.
qm-start: Start a virtual machine on QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_start>.
qm-snapshot: Create virtual machine snapshots. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_snapshot>.
qm-shutdown: Shut down a virtual machine on QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_shutdown>.
qm-showcmd: Show command-line which is used to start the VM (debug info). More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_showcmd>.
qm-set: Set virtual machine options. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_set>.
qm-sendkey: Send QEMU monitor encoding key event to a virtual machine. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_sendkey>.
qm-rollback: Roll back the VM state to a specified snapshot. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_rollback>.
qm-resume: Resume a virtual machine. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_resume>.
qm-resize: This command is an alias of `qm disk resize`.
qm-reset: Reset a virtual machine on QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_reset>.
qm-rescan: This command is an alias of `qm disk rescan`.
qm-remote-migrate: Migrate a virtual machine to a remote Proxmox host or cluster. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_remote-migrate>.
qm-reboot: Reboot a virtual machine by shutting it down, and starting it again after applying pending changes. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_reboot>.
qm-pending: Get the virtual machine configuration with both current and pending values. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_pending>.
qm-nbdstop: Stop embedded nbd server. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_nbdstop>.
qm-mtunnel: Used by `qmigrate`. Note: It should not be invoked manually. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_mtunnel>.
qm-move_disk: This command is an alias of `qm disk move`.
qm-move-disk: This command is an alias of `qm disk move`.
qm-monitor: Enter the QEMU Monitor interface. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_monitor>.
qm-migrate: Migrate a virtual machine. Used to create a new migration task. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_migrate>.
qm-listsnapshot: List snapshots of virtual machines. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_listsnapshot>.
qm-list: List all virtual machines. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_list>.
qm-importovf: Import a virtual machine from an Open Virtualization Format manifest. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_importovf>.
qm-importdisk: This command is an alias of `qm disk import`.
qm-import: Import supported images from VMware, VirtualBox, etc. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_import>.
qm-help: Display help for a command. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_help>.
qm-guest: Manage a VM guest agent. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_guest_cmd>.
qm-guest-exec: Execute a specific command via a guest agent. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_guest_exec>.
qm-destroy: Destroy a virtual machine in QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_destroy>.
qm-delsnapshot: Delete virtual machine snapshots. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_delsnapshot>.
qm-create: Create or restore a virtual machine on QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_create>.
qm-config: Display the virtual machine configuration with pending configuration changes applied. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_config>.
qm-clone: Create a copy of virtual machine on QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_clone>.
qm-cleanup: Clean up resources on QEMU/KVM Virtual Machine Manager like tap devices, VGPUs, etc. Called after a VM shuts down, crashes, etc. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/qm.1.html#cli_qm_cleanup>.
qm-agent: This command is an alias of `qm guest cmd`.
qjoypad: Translate input from gamepads or joysticks into keyboard strokes or mouse actions. More information: <https://qjoypad.sourceforge.net/doc/doc_index.html>.
pyrit: WPA/WPA2 cracking tool using computational power. More information: <https://manned.org/pyrit>.
pwn: Exploit Development Library designed for rapid prototyping. More information: <https://docs.pwntools.com/en/stable/commandline.html>.
pwdx: Print working directory of a process. More information: <https://manned.org/pwdx>.
pw-v4l2: Use v4l2 programs within PipeWire. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-v4l2_1.html>.
pw-top: View the PipeWire nodes and devices statistics in real-time. See also: `pipewire`, `pw-dump`, `pw-cli`, `pw-profiler`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-top_1.html>.
pw-reserve: Reserve a device for PipeWire. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-reserve_1.html>.
pw-record: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --record`.
pw-profiler: Profile a local or remote instance. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-profiler_1.html>.
pw-play: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --playback`.
pw-mon: Monitor objects on the PipeWire instance. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-mon_1.html>.
pw-midirecord: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --record --midi`.
pw-midiplay: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --playback --midi`.
pw-mididump: Dump MIDI messages to `stdout`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-mididump_1.html>.
pw-midi2record: Record MIDI 2.0 clips through PipeWire. Note: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --record --midi-clip`. See also: `pw-cat`, `pw-midi2play`, `pw-midirecord`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-cat_1.html>.
pw-midi2play: Play MIDI 2.0 clips through PipeWire. Note: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --playback --midi-clip`. See also: `pw-cat`, `pw-midi2record`, `pw-midiplay`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-cat_1.html>.
pw-metadata: Monitor, set, and delete metadata on PipeWire objects. See also: `pipewire`, `pw-mon`, `pw-cli`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-metadata_1.html>.
pw-loopback: Create loopback devices in PipeWire. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-loopback_1.html>.
pw-link: Manage links between ports in PipeWire. More information: <https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/Virtual-Devices>.
pw-jack: Run a JACK application with PipeWire. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-jack_1.html>.
pw-encplay: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --playback --encoded`.
pw-dump: Dump PipeWire's current state as JSON, including the information on nodes, devices, modules, ports, and other objects. See also: `pw-mon`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-dump_1.html>.
pw-dsdplay: This command is an alias of `pw-cat --playback --dsd`.
pw-dot: Create `.dot` files of the PipeWire graph. See also: `dot`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-dot_1.html>.
pw-container: Run a program in a new security context. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-container_1.html>.
pw-config: List configuration paths and sections that will be used by the PipeWire server and clients. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-config_1.html>.
pw-cli: Manage a PipeWire instance's modules, objects, nodes, devices, links, and much more. See also: `wpctl`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-cli_1.html>.
pw-cat: Play and record audio files through PipeWire. See also: `wpctl`, `pw-cli`. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pw-cat_1.html>.
pvscan: List all physical volumes and manage their online status. More information: <https://manned.org/pvscan>.
pvs: Display information about physical volumes. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/pvs>.
pvremove: Remove LVM labels from physical volume(s). More information: <https://manned.org/pvremove>.
pveversion: Proxmox VE version info. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Command_Line_Tools#Software_version_check>.
pvesubscription: Manage Proxmox subscription keys. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pvesubscription.1.html>.
pvesh: Interface with the Proxmox VE API. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pvesh.1.html>.
pveperf: A benchmarking tool in Proxmox Server. Gather CPU and hard disk performance data for the hard disk. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pveperf.1.html>.
pvenode-config: Get and set node configuration. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pvenode.1.html#cli_pvenode_config_get>.
pvecm: Proxmox VE Cluster Manager. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pvecm.1.html>.
pveam: Manage LXC container templates. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pveam.1.html>.
pve-firewall: Manage Proxmox VE Firewall. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Firewall>.
pvdisplay: Display information about Logical Volume Manager (LVM) physical volumes. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/pvdisplay>.
pvcreate: Initialize a disk or partition for use as a physical volume. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/pvcreate>.
pvck: Check and repair LVM metadata on physical volumes. More information: <https://manned.org/pvck>.
pvchange: Change attributes of physical volume(s). More information: <https://manned.org/pvchange>.
pulseaudio: The PulseAudio sound system daemon and manager. More information: <https://manned.org/pulseaudio>.
ptyxis: A container-oriented terminal for GNOME. More information: <https://gitlab.gnome.org/chergert/ptyxis#basic-usage--command-line-options>.
ptx: Generate a permuted index of words from text files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/ptx-invocation.html>.
pstree: A convenient tool to show running processes as a tree. More information: <https://manned.org/pstree>.
pstoedit: Convert PDF files into various image formats. More information: <http://www.calvina.de/pstoedit/pstoedit.htm>.
psd: Sync browser profiles between `tmpfs` and disk. More information: <https://manned.org/psd>.
prt-get: The CRUX package manager. More information: <https://crux.nu/doc/prt-get%20-%20User%20Manual.html>.
protonvpn: Official Proton VPN client. Some subcommands such as `connect` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://protonvpn.com/support/linux-cli#how-to-use-the-cli-for-linux>.
protonvpn-connect: Connect to Proton VPN. More information: <https://protonvpn.com/support/linux-cli#how-to-use-the-cli-for-linux>.
protontricks: A simple wrapper that runs Winetricks commands for Proton enabled games. More information: <https://github.com/Matoking/protontricks#usage>.
project-zomboid: Start a headless Project Zomboid server. More information: <https://pzwiki.net/wiki/Dedicated_server>.
proctl: Manage projects licenses and languages, switch between templated licenses. More information: <https://github.com/CreativeCodeCat/proctl>.
pro: Manage Ubuntu Pro services. More information: <https://manned.org/ubuntu-advantage>.
prlimit: Get or set process resource soft and hard limits. Given a process ID and one or more resources, prlimit tries to retrieve and/or modify the limits. More information: <https://manned.org/prlimit>.
prime-run: Run a program using an alternative Nvidia graphics card. More information: <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/PRIME#PRIME_render_offload>.
pridecat: Like cat but more colorful. More information: <https://github.com/lunasorcery/pridecat#flags>.
ppa-purge: Disable a PPA and revert its packages to the official versions. More information: <https://manned.org/ppa-purge>.
powertop2tuned: Create TuneD profiles from PowerTOP recommendations. Part of `tuned-utils`. See also: `powertop`, `tuned-adm`. More information: <https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/quick-docs/automatic-power-management-power2top/>.
powertop: Optimize battery power usage. More information: <https://github.com/fenrus75/powertop>.
powerstat: Measure the power consumption of a computer that has a battery power source or supports the RAPL interface. More information: <https://manned.org/powerstat>.
powerprofilesctl: Make power profiles handling available over D-Bus. More information: <https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/upower/power-profiles-daemon#how-to-use>.
poweroff: Power off the system. See also: `shutdown`. More information: <https://manned.org/poweroff>.
postfix: Postfix mail transfer agent (MTA) control program. More information: <https://www.postfix.org/postfix.1.html>.
postconf: Postfix configuration utility. This command displays the values of the `main.cf` configuration parameters by default and warns about possible mistyped parameter names. It can also change the `main.cf` configuration parameter values. More information: <https://manned.org/postconf>.
ports: Update/list the ports tree on a CRUX system. More information: <https://manned.org/ports>.
portageq: Query for information about Portage, the Gentoo Linux package manager. Queryable Portage-specific environment variables are listed in `/var/db/repos/gentoo/profiles/info_vars`. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Portageq>.
portablectl: A systemd utility for managing and deploying portable service images on Linux systems. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/portablectl.html>.
pokego: Display Pokémon sprites in color directly in your terminal. Inspired by Phoney badger's `pokemon-colorscripts` but offers enhanced speed and efficiency. More information: <https://github.com/rubiin/pokego#usage>.
podlet: Generate Podman Quadlet files from a Podman command, compose file, or existing object. See also: `podman`. More information: <https://github.com/containers/podlet>.
po4a: Update both PO files and translated documents. More information: <https://www.po4a.org/man/man1/po4a.1.php>.
po4a-updatepo: Update the translation (in PO format) of a documentation. More information: <https://www.po4a.org/man/man1/po4a-updatepo.1.php>.
po4a-translate: Convert a PO file back to documentation format. The provided PO file should be the translation of the POT file which was produced by `po4a-gettextize`. More information: <https://www.po4a.org/man/man1/po4a-translate.1.php>.
po4a-gettextize: Convert a file to a PO file. More information: <https://www.po4a.org/man/man1/po4a-gettextize.1.php>.
pmount: Mount arbitrary hotpluggable devices as a normal user. More information: <https://manned.org/pmount>.
pmap: Report memory map of a process or processes. More information: <https://manned.org/pmap>.
pluma: Edit files in MATE desktop environment. More information: <https://manned.org/pluma>.
playerctl: Control media players via MPRIS. More information: <https://github.com/altdesktop/playerctl#using-the-cli>.
plasmashell: Start and restart Plasma Desktop. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/plasma-desktop>.
plasma-apply-lookandfeel: Switch Plasma global themes. More information: <https://userbase.kde.org/System_Settings/Look_And_Feel>.
plasma-apply-desktoptheme: Switch Plasma desktop theme. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/plasma-workspace>.
plasma-apply-cursortheme: Switch Plasma cursor theme. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/plasma-workspace>.
plasma-apply-colorscheme: Switch Plasma color scheme. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/plasma-workspace>.
pkgtool: Interactive menu-driven tool for managing Slackware packages. See also: `installpkg`, `removepkg`, `upgradepkg`, `makepkg`. More information: <https://www.slackbook.org/html/book.html#PACKAGE-MANAGEMENT-PACKAGE-UTILITIES-PKGTOOL>.
pkgstats: Submit and view Arch Linux package popularity statistics. More information: <https://github.com/archlinux-de/pkgstats-cli#usage>.
pkgrm: Remove a package from a CRUX system. More information: <https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E88353_01/html/E72487/pkgrm-8.html>.
pkgmk: Make a binary package for use with pkgadd on CRUX. More information: <https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E88353_01/html/E37839/pkgmk-1.html>.
pkginfo: Query the package database on a CRUX system. More information: <https://crux.nu/Main/Handbook3-6#ntoc19>.
pkgfile: Search files from packages in the official repositories on Arch-based systems. See also: `pacman files`. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgfile>.
pkgdiff: Compare the file contents of two Slackware packages. More information: <https://slackware.nl/slackware/slackware64-current/source/a/pkgtools/manpages/pkgdiff.8>.
pkgctl: Unified frontend for Arch Linux devtools. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl>.
pkgctl-repo: Manage Git packaging repositories and their configuration for Arch Linux. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl-repo>.
pkgctl-release: Release step to commit, tag, and upload build artifacts. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl-release>.
pkgctl-diff: Compare package files using different modes. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl-diff>.
pkgctl-db-update: Update the `pacman` database as final release step for packages that have been transferred and staged on <https://repos.archlinux.org>. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl-db-update>.
pkgctl-build: Build packages inside a clean `chroot`. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl-build>.
pkgctl-auth: Authenticate `pkgctl` with services like GitLab. More information: <https://manned.org/pkgctl-auth>.
pkgadd: Add a package to a CRUX system. More information: <https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E88353_01/html/E72487/pkgadd-8.html>.
pkexec: Execute commands as another user. Asks for password in a GUI if available. See also: `sudo`, `run0`, `doas`. More information: <https://polkit.pages.freedesktop.org/polkit/pkexec.1.html>.
pkcon: PackageKit client used by Discover and Gnome software and alternative to `apt`. More information: <https://manned.org/pkcon>.
pivpn: Easy security-hardened OpenVPN setup and manager. Originally designed for the Raspberry Pi, but works on other Linux devices too. More information: <https://docs.pivpn.io/openvpn/>.
pivot_root: Change the root filesystem to a new directory and move the current root to a subdirectory of the new root. Commonly used during system initialization (e.g., in `initramfs`) to switch from a temporary root to the real root filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/pivot_root.8>.
pirut: Graphical frontend for `yum`. See also: `yum`. More information: <https://manned.org/pirut>.
pipewire: Start the PipeWire daemon. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pipewire_1.html>.
pipewire-pulse: Start a PulseAudio-compatible daemon for PipeWire. More information: <https://docs.pipewire.org/page_man_pipewire-pulse_1.html>.
pipewire-avb: This command is an alias of `pipewire`. Note: It starts the PipeWire daemon using the Audio Video Bridging (AVB) profile.
pipewire-aes67: This command is an alias of `pipewire`. Note: It starts the PipeWire daemon using the AES67 network audio profile.
pipetron: Electron node manager for PipeWire. More information: <https://codeberg.org/ponleou/pipetron#usage>.
pinout: View the current Raspberry Pi's GPIO pin-out information on the terminal with an ASCII diagram. More information: <https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/raspberry-pi.html#view-a-gpio-pinout-for-your-raspberry-pi>.
