pikman: PikaOS package manager utility. More information: <https://wiki.pika-os.com/en/custom-utils-wiki/pikman-manager-cli>.
pihole: Manage the Pi-hole ad-blocking DNS server. More information: <https://docs.pi-hole.net/main/pihole-command/>.
pidstat: Show system resource usage, including CPU, memory, IO etc. More information: <https://manned.org/pidstat>.
pidof: Get the ID of a process using its name. See also: `pgrep`. More information: <https://manned.org/pidof>.
pi: Compute decimal Archimedes' constant Pi. More information: <https://manned.org/pi>.
physlock: Lock all consoles and virtual terminals. More information: <https://github.com/xyb3rt/physlock#usage>.
phpquery: PHP extension manager for Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://code.google.com/archive/p/phpquery/wikis/CommandLineInterface.wiki>.
phpenmod: Enable PHP extensions on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://salsa.debian.org/php-team/php-defaults>.
phpdismod: Disable PHP extensions on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://salsa.debian.org/php-team/php-defaults>.
photorec: Deleted file recovery tool. It is recommended to write recovered files to a disk separate to the one being recovered from. More information: <https://www.cgsecurity.org/wiki/PhotoRec_Step_By_Step>.
phar: Create, update, or extract PHP archives (PHAR). More information: <https://manned.org/phar>.
pg: View files one page at a time. More information: <https://manned.org/pg>.
perf: Framework for Linux performance counter measurements. More information: <https://perfwiki.github.io/main/>.
pdfxup: N-up PDF pages. N-upping means putting multiple pages onto one page by scaling and rotating them into a grid. More information: <https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfxup>.
pdftoppm: Convert PDF document pages to portable Pixmap (image formats). More information: <https://manned.org/pdftoppm>.
pdftohtml: Convert PDF files into HTML, XML, and PNG images. More information: <https://manned.org/pdftohtml>.
pdfdetach: List or extract attachments (embedded files) from a PDF file. See also: `pdfattach`, `pdfimages`, `pdfinfo`. More information: <https://manned.org/pdfdetach>.
pdfcrop: Detect and remove margins in each page in a PDF file. More information: <https://github.com/ho-tex/pdfcrop>.
pdfbook2: Create a double sided printable PDF booklet from a PDF. Note: The booklet needs to be printed double-sided in landscape mode, flipped on the long edge. More information: <https://github.com/jenom/pdfbook2#examples>.
pdfattach: Add a new attachment (embedded file) to an existing PDF file. See also: `pdfdetach`, `pdfimages`, `pdfinfo`. More information: <https://manned.org/pdfattach>.
pdbedit: Edit the Samba user database. For simple user add/remove/password, you can also use `smbpasswd`. More information: <https://manned.org/pdbedit>.
pct: Manage LXC containers in Proxmox. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html>.
pct-unmount: Unmount a container's filesystem from the host. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_unmount>.
pct-template: Convert a container into a template. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_template>.
pct-stop: Abruptly stop a container without waiting for processes to exit. See also: `pct shutdown`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_stop>.
pct-status: Display the status of a container. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_status>.
pct-shutdown: Cleanly shutdown a container. See also: `pct stop`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_shutdown>.
pct-rollback: Restore a specific snapshot. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_rollback>.
pct-push: Copy a local file to a container. See also: `pct pull`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_push>.
pct-pull: Copy a file from a container to the local system. See also: `pct push`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_pull>.
pct-move_volume: This command is an alias of `pct move-volume`.
pct-move-volume: Move a volume to a different storage or to a different container. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_move-volume>.
pct-mount: Mount a container's filesystem on the host. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_mount>.
pct-listsnapshot: List snapshots of a container. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_listsnapshot>.
pct-list: List containers and their states. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_list>.
pct-fsck: Run a filesystem check on a container volume. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_fsck>.
pct-exec: Launch a command inside a specified container. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_exec>.
pct-enter: Launch a shell for a container. See also: `pct console`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_enter>.
pct-delsnapshot: Delete a container snapshot. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_delsnapshot>.
pct-create: Create LXC containers in Proxmox. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_create>.
pct-cpusets: Display the list of assigned CPU sets. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_cpusets>.
pct-console: Attach to a container TTY. See also: `pct enter`. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_console>.
pct-config: Print the configuration of a container. More information: <https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/pct.1.html#cli_pct_config>.
paxs: Manage packages across Yay, Flatpak, and Snap. Supports searching, installing, removing, and upgrading packages. More information: <https://github.com/zamhedonia/paxs#usage>.
patool: Archive file manager. Various archive formats can be created, extracted, tested, listed, searched, repacked, and compared. More information: <https://github.com/wummel/patool/blob/master/doc/patool.txt>.
pasuspender: Temporarily suspends `pulseaudio` while another command is running to allow access to alsa. More information: <https://manned.org/pasuspender>.
paru: An AUR helper and pacman wrapper. See also: `pacman`, `yay`. More information: <https://github.com/Morganamilo/paru#examples>.
partx: Parse a partition table and tell the kernel about it. More information: <https://manned.org/partx>.
partprobe: Notify the operating system kernel of partition table changes. More information: <https://manned.org/partprobe>.
parted: A partition manipulation program. See also: `parted.interactive`, `cfdisk`, `partprobe`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/parted/manual/parted.html#Invoking-Parted>.
parted.interactive: A partition manipulation program. See also: `partprobe`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/parted/parted.html>.
partclone: Copy and restore partitions to and from an image while disregarding empty blocks. More information: <https://manned.org/partclone>.
pamac: Utility for the GUI package manager pamac. If you can't see the AUR packages, enable it in `/etc/pamac.conf` or in the GUI. More information: <https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php/Pamac>.
palworld: Create and start a headless Palworld server. More information: <https://docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/arguments/>.
pactree: Package dependency tree viewer for pacman. More information: <https://manned.org/pactree>.
pactrans: Install, remove, and upgrade ALPM packages. See also: `pacinstall`, `pacremove`. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pactrans.pod>.
pacstrap: Install Arch Linux packages in the specified new root directory. More information: <https://manned.org/pacstrap>.
pacstall: An AUR package manager for Ubuntu. More information: <https://github.com/pacstall/pacstall>.
pacsift: Query and filter packages. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacsift.pod>.
pacreport: Generate a report of installed packages. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacreport.pod>.
pacrepairfile: Reset properties on files managed by alpm. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacrepairfile.pod>.
pacrepairdb: Fix corrupted database entries in libalpm database. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacrepairdb.pod>.
pacremove: This command is an alias of `pactrans --remove`.
pacman4console: A text-based console game inspired by the original Pacman. More information: <https://github.com/YoctoForBeaglebone/pacman4console>.
pacman: Arch Linux package manager utility. For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. See also: `pacman-sync`, `pacman-remove`, `pacman-query`, `pacman-upgrade`, `pacman-files`, `pacman-database`, `pacman-deptest`, `pacman-key`, `pacman-mirrors`. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-upgrade: Install packages manually from archive files. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-u: This command is an alias of `pacman --upgrade`.
pacman-t: This command is an alias of `pacman --deptest`.
pacman-sync: Synchronize packages from remote repositories. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-s: This command is an alias of `pacman --sync`.
pacman-remove: Remove packages from the system. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-r: This command is an alias of `pacman --remove`.
pacman-query: Query the local package database. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-q: This command is an alias of `pacman --query`.
pacman-mirrors: Generate a `pacman` mirrorlist for Manjaro Linux. Every run of `pacman-mirrors` requires you to synchronize your database and update your system using `sudo pacman -Syyu`. See also: `pacman`. More information: <https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=Pacman-mirrors>.
pacman-key: Wrapper script for GnuPG used to manage pacman's keyring. See also: `pacman`. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman-key>.
pacman-files: Query the local files database. See also: `pkgfile`. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-f: This command is an alias of `pacman --files`.
pacman-deptest: Check each dependency specified and return a list of dependencies that are not currently satisfied on the system. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-database: Operate on the Arch Linux package database. Modify certain attributes of the installed packages. More information: <https://manned.org/pacman.8>.
pacman-d: This command is an alias of `pacman --database`.
paclog: Filter pacman log entries. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/paclog.pod>.
paclock: Lock/unlock the libalpm database (used by `pacman`) to prevent or allow simultaneous package management operations. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/paclock.pod>.
pacinstall: This command is an alias of `pactrans --install`.
pacini: Query pacman-style configuration files. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacini.pod>.
pacinfo: Display information about installed packages. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacinfo.pod>.
pacgraph: Draw a graph of installed packages to PNG/SVG/GUI/console. More information: <https://manned.org/pacgraph>.
pacfile: Display information about package files, including repository data, filesystem checks, and database comparisons. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacfile.pod>.
pacdiff: Maintenance utility for `.pacorig`, `.pacnew`, and `.pacsave` files created by `pacman`. More information: <https://manned.org/pacdiff>.
pacconf: Query and display pacman's configuration options, showing either the full configuration or specific directive values as parsed by pacman. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/pacconf.pod>.
paccheck: Check installed packages on an Arch-based system to verify dependencies, integrity, and consistency. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/paccheck.pod>.
paccapability: Query and display the capabilities supported by libalpm. More information: <https://github.com/andrewgregory/pacutils/blob/master/doc/paccapability.pod>.
paccache: A `pacman` cache cleaning utility. More information: <https://manned.org/paccache>.
pacaur: A utility for Arch Linux to build and install packages from the Arch User Repository. More information: <https://github.com/rmarquis/pacaur#name>.
owut: OpenWrt Upgrade Tool for automating builds and installs via Attended SysUpgrade (ASU). More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/guide-user/installation/sysupgrade.owut>.
ostree: Version control for binary files similar to `git` but optimized for operating system root filesystems. Foundation for immutable image-based operating systems such as Fedora Silverblue, Fedora IoT, or Fedora CoreOS. More information: <https://ostreedev.github.io/ostree/>.
optimus-manager: GPU switching utility for Nvidia Optimus laptops. More information: <https://github.com/Askannz/optimus-manager>.
opkg: A lightweight package manager used to install OpenWrt packages. More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/guide-user/additional-software/opkg>.
opi: Search and install packages from openSUSE, community, and proprietary repositories. More information: <https://manpages.opensuse.org/Tumbleweed/opi/opi.8.en.html>.
opera-stable: This command is an alias of `chromium`. More information: <https://www.opera.com/>.
openrc: The OpenRC service manager. See also: `rc-status`, `rc-update`, `rc-service`. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/OpenRC>.
openfortivpn: A VPN client, for Fortinet's proprietary PPP+SSL VPN solution. More information: <https://manned.org/openfortivpn>.
oomctl: Analyze the state stored in `systemd-oomd`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/oomctl.html>.
oniux: Isolate an arbitrary application and route traffic over the Tor network. Note: This is experimental software. More information: <https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/oniux>.
oma: A package management frontend for dpkg-based Linux distributions. More information: <https://github.com/AOSC-Dev/oma#usage>.
objcopy: Copy the contents of an object file to another file. More information: <https://manned.org/objcopy>.
nvtop: Interactive ncurses-based GPU process and status viewer for AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs. See also: `amdgpu_top`, `radeontop`. More information: <https://manned.org/nvtop>.
numlockx: Control the number lock key status in X11 sessions. More information: <https://manned.org/numlockx>.
numactl: Control NUMA policy for processes or shared memory. More information: <https://manned.org/numactl>.
ntpq: Query the Network Time Protocol (NTP) daemon. More information: <https://manned.org/ntpq>.
ntpdate: Synchronize and set the date and time via NTP. More information: <https://manned.org/ntpdate>.
ntpd: The official NTP (Network Time Protocol) daemon to synchronize the system clock to remote time servers or local reference clocks. More information: <https://manned.org/ntpd>.
ntfsfix: Fix common problems on an NTFS partition. More information: <https://manned.org/ntfsfix>.
nsxiv: Neo Simple X Image Viewer. More information: <https://nsxiv.codeberg.page/man/>.
nsnake: Snake game in the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/alexdantas/nsnake/#controls>.
nsenter: Run a new command in a running process' namespace. Particularly useful for Docker images or chroot jails. More information: <https://manned.org/nsenter>.
nova: The OpenStack project that provides a way to provision compute instances. More information: <https://docs.openstack.org/nova/latest/>.
nordvpn: Command-line interface for NordVPN. More information: <https://support.nordvpn.com/hc/articles/20196094470929-Installing-NordVPN-on-Linux-distributions>.
nologin: Alternative shell that prevents a user from logging in. More information: <https://manned.org/nologin.8>.
nmtui: Text user interface for controlling NetworkManager. Use `<ArrowKeys>` to navigate, `<Enter>` to select an option. See also: `nmcli`. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmtui.html>.
nmtui-hostname: This command is an alias of `nmtui hostname`.
nmtui-edit: This command is an alias of `nmtui edit`.
nmtui-connect: This command is an alias of `nmtui connect`.
nmon: A system administrator, tuner, and benchmark tool. More information: <https://manned.org/nmon>.
nmcli: Manage the network configuration using NetworkManager. See also: `nmtui`, `iw`, `iwctl`. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html>.
nmcli-radio: Show the status of radio switches or enable/disable them using NetworkManager. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#radio>.
nmcli-networking: Manage the networking status of NetworkManager. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#networking>.
nmcli-monitor: Monitor changes to the NetworkManager connection status. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#monitor>.
nmcli-general: Manage general settings of NetworkManager. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#general>.
nmcli-device: Manage network interfaces and establish new Wi-Fi connections using NetworkManager. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#device>.
nmcli-connection: Manage connections with NetworkManager. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#connection>.
nmcli-agent: Run `nmcli` as a NetworkManager secret agent or polkit agent. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nmcli.html#agent>.
nm-online: Ask NetworkManager whether the network is connected. More information: <https://networkmanager.pages.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/nm-online.html>.
nixos-rebuild: Reconfigure a NixOS machine. More information: <https://nixos.org/nixos/manual/#sec-changing-config>.
nixos-option: Inspect a NixOS configuration. More information: <https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/index.html#sec-modularity>.
nixos-container: Start NixOS containers using Linux containers. More information: <https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/#ch-containers>.
nitrogen: Desktop background browser and setter for X Window. More information: <https://manned.org/nitrogen>.
nitch: A small and incredibly fast system fetch written fully in Nim. More information: <https://github.com/ssleert/nitch#usage->.
niri: A scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor. More information: <https://github.com/YaLTeR/niri>.
nft: Allow configuration of tables, chains, and rules provided by the Linux kernel firewall. Nftables replaces iptables. More information: <https://wiki.nftables.org/wiki-nftables/index.php/Main_Page>.
nft-monitor: Show real-time changes happening inside the Linux firewall `nftables`. More information: <https://manned.org/nft#head21>.
newrole: Run a new shell with a different SELinux role. Allows users to switch to a different SELinux security context. See also: `runcon`, `semanage user`. More information: <https://manned.org/newrole>.
newgrp: Switch primary group membership. More information: <https://manned.org/newgrp>.
networkctl: Query the status of network links. Manage the network configuration using `systemd-networkd`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/networkctl.html>.
netselect: Speed test for choosing a fast network server. More information: <https://manned.org/netselect>.
netselect-apt: Create a `sources.list` file for a Debian mirror with the lowest latency. More information: <https://manned.org/netselect-apt>.
netplan: Network configuration utility using YAML. More information: <https://netplan.readthedocs.io/en/stable/cli/>.
nethogs: Monitor bandwidth usage per process. More information: <https://manned.org/nethogs>.
nerdctl: Docker-compatible CLI for containerd. More information: <https://github.com/containerd/nerdctl/blob/main/docs/command-reference.md>.
neo: Simulate the digital rain from "The Matrix". See also: `cmatrix`. More information: <https://manned.org/neo>.
nemotron3-nano: The examples for this command have been moved together with `inference-snap`. More information: <https://github.com/canonical/nemotron-3-nano-snap>.
nemo: Manage files and directories in Cinnamon desktop environment. More information: <https://manned.org/nemo>.
needrestart: Check which daemons need to be restarted after library upgrades. More information: <https://manned.org/needrestart>.
ndctl: Utility for managing Non-Volatile DIMMs. More information: <https://manned.org/ndctl>.
ncat: Read, write, redirect, and encrypt data across a network. An alternative implementation of a similar utility called `netcat`/`nc`. More information: <https://nmap.org/ncat/guide/index.html>.
ncal: This command is an alias of `cal`.
navi: An interactive cheatsheet tool for the command-line and application launchers. See also: `tldr`, `cheatshh`, `cheat`. More information: <https://github.com/denisidoro/navi>.
nautilus: Default file explorer for GNOME desktop environment. Also known as GNOME Files. See also: `dolphin`, `caja`, `thunar`, `vifm`. More information: <https://manned.org/nautilus>.
natural-selection-2: Start a headless Natural Selection 2 server. More information: <https://naturalselection.fandom.com/wiki/Dedicated_Server>.
namei: Follow a pathname (which can be a symbolic link) until a terminal point is found (a file/directory/char device etc.). This program is useful for finding "too many levels of symbolic links" problems. More information: <https://manned.org/namei>.
named: Execute the DNS (Dynamic Name Service) server daemon that converts host names to IP addresses and vice versa. More information: <https://manned.org/named>.
namcap: Check binary packages and source `PKGBUILD`s for common packaging mistakes. More information: <https://manned.org/namcap>.
nala: Package management utility with better formatting. Front-end for the `python-apt` API. More information: <https://gitlab.com/volian/nala>.
mux: Intercept and multiplex streams of input events. More information: <https://gitlab.com/interception/linux/tools/-/tree/master#mux>.
mt: Control magnetic tape drive operation (commonly LTO tape). More information: <https://manned.org/mt>.
mssh: GTK+ based SSH client for interacting with multiple SSH servers at once. More information: <https://manned.org/mssh>.
mpg123: Console MPEG audio player. More information: <https://manned.org/mpg123>.
mountpoint: Test if a directory is a filesystem mountpoint. More information: <https://manned.org/mountpoint>.
mount.steamos: Mount or unmount SteamOS filesystem partitions. More information: <https://gitlab.com/users/evlaV/projects>.
mount.smb3: This command is an alias of `mount.cifs`. Note: For SMB versions before 3 you have to use `mount.cifs` instead.
mount: Get access to an entire filesystem in one directory. See also: `udisksctl`. More information: <https://manned.org/mount.8>.
mount.ddi: Mount Discoverable Disk Images. See also: `systemd-dissect`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-dissect.html>.
mount.cifs: Mount SMB (Server Message Block) or CIFS (Common Internet File System) shares. Note: You can also do the same thing by passing the `-t cifs` option to `mount`. More information: <https://manned.org/mount.cifs>.
mopac: MOPAC (Molecular Orbital PACkage) is a semiempirical quantum chemistry program based on Dewar and Thiel's NDDO approximation. More information: <https://github.com/openmopac/mopac>.
mons: Quickly manage two displays. More information: <https://github.com/Ventto/mons#usage>.
mono: Runtime for the .NET Framework. More information: <https://www.mono-project.com/docs/>.
mokutil: Configure Secure Boot Machine Owner Keys (MOK). Some operations, such as enabling and disabling Secure Boot or enrolling keys require a reboot. More information: <https://manned.org/mokutil>.
module: Modify a users' environment. More information: <https://lmod.readthedocs.io/en/latest/010_user.html>.
modprobe: Add or remove modules from the Linux kernel. See also: `lsmod`, `kmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/modprobe>.
modinfo: Extract information about a Linux kernel module. See also: `kmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/modinfo>.
modetest: Diagnose Direct Rendering Manager and Kernel Mode Setting. More information: <https://xilinx-wiki.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/A/pages/18841850/Video_Mixer#modetest>.
mocp: Music on Console (MOC) audio player. More information: <https://manned.org/mocp>.
mmdebstrap: Create a Debian chroot. Alternative to `debootstrap`. More information: <https://gitlab.mister-muffin.de/josch/mmdebstrap/>.
mmcli: Control and monitor the ModemManager. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/ModemManager/man/latest/mmcli.1.html>.
mlabel: Set an MS-DOS volume label for FAT and VFAT filesystems. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/mtools/manual/mtools.html#mlabel>.
mkvpropedit: Modify properties of existing Matroska files without a complete remux. More information: <https://mkvtoolnix.download/doc/mkvpropedit.html>.
mkswap: Set up a Linux swap area on a device or in a file. Note: `path/to/file` can either point to a regular file or a swap partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkswap>.
mksquashfs: Create or append files and directories to squashfs filesystems. More information: <https://manned.org/mksquashfs>.
mkosi: Build modern, legacy-free Linux images. Part of `systemd`. More information: <https://manned.org/mkosi>.
mknod: Create block or character device special files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/mknod-invocation.html>.
mklost+found: Create a lost+found directory. More information: <https://manned.org/mklost%2Bfound>.
mkisofs: Create ISO files from directories. Also aliased as `genisoimage`. More information: <https://manned.org/mkisofs>.
mkinitfs: Generate an initramfs on Alpine Linux. More information: <https://manned.org/mkinitfs>.
mkinitcpio: Generate initial ramdisk environments for booting the Linux kernel based on the specified preset(s). More information: <https://manned.org/mkinitcpio>.
mkid: Build an ID database for use with `lid` and other idutils tools. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/idutils/manual/idutils.html#mkid-invocation>.
mkhomedir_helper: Create the user's home directory after creating the user. More information: <https://manned.org/mkhomedir_helper>.
mkfs.xfs: Create an XFS filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.xfs>.
mkfs.vfat: This command is an alias of `mkfs.fat`.
mkfs.ntfs: Create an NTFS filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.ntfs>.
mkfs.minix: Create a Minix filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.minix>.
mkfs: Build a Linux filesystem on a hard disk partition. Note: This command is deprecated, use filesystem specific commands like `mkfs.ext4` instead. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs>.
mkfs.fat: Create an MS-DOS filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.fat>.
mkfs.f2fs: Create an F2FS filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.f2fs>.
mkfs.ext4: Create an ext4 filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.ext4>.
mkfs.exfat: Create an exfat filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.exfat>.
mkfs.erofs: Create an EROFS filesystem in an image. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.erofs>.
mkfs.cramfs: Create a ROM filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mkfs.cramfs>.
mkfs.btrfs: Create a BTRFS filesystem. Defaults to `raid1`, which specifies 2 copies of a data block spread across 2 different devices. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mkfs.btrfs.html>.
mkfs.bcachefs: Create a `bcachefs` filesystem inside a partition. See also: `bcachefs`. More information: <https://bcachefs-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mgmt-formatting.html>.
mke2fs: Create a Linux filesystem inside a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/mke2fs>.
mkarchiso: Build Arch Linux ISO images from an archiso profile. More information: <https://manned.org/mkarchiso>.
mirrorselect: Select the fastest Gentoo mirrors and update `GENTOO_MIRRORS` in `/etc/portage/make.conf`. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Mirrorselect>.
minicom: Communicate with the serial interface of a device. See also: `picocom`, `cu`, `tio`. More information: <https://manned.org/minicom>.
mimetype: Automatically determine the MIME type of a file. More information: <https://manned.org/mimetype>.
microcom: A minimalistic terminal program, used to access remote devices via a serial, CAN, or telnet connection from the console. More information: <https://manned.org/microcom>.
mhwd: Manjaro Hardware Detection utility. More information: <https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php/Manjaro_Hardware_Detection_Overview>.
mhwd-kernel: Manage and install Linux kernels in Manjaro. More information: <https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php/Manjaro_Kernels>.
mhwd-gpu: Configure graphics cards in Manjaro. More information: <https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php/Configure_NVIDIA_(non-free)_settings_and_load_them_on_Startup/en#Configure_The_Resolution.2FRefresh_Rate>.
megatools-dl: Download files from `mega.nz`. Part of the `megatools` suite. More information: <https://xff.cz/megatools/man/megatools-dl.html>.
megadl: This command is an alias of `megatools-dl`.
mediamtx: Real-time media server and proxy. More information: <https://github.com/bluenviron/mediamtx>.
mdbook: Create online books by writing Markdown files. More information: <https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/cli/index.html>.
mcookie: Generate random 128-bit hexadecimal numbers. More information: <https://manned.org/mcookie>.
mate-search-tool: Search files in MATE desktop environment. More information: <https://manned.org/mate-search-tool>.
mate-screenshot: Make screenshots in MATE desktop environment. More information: <https://manned.org/mate-screenshot>.
mate-calc: Calculate mathematic expressions in MATE desktop environment. More information: <https://manned.org/mate-calc>.
mate-calc-cmd: Calculate mathematic expressions in MATE desktop environment in terminal. More information: <https://manned.org/mate-calc-cmd>.
mate-about: Show information about MATE desktop environment. More information: <https://manned.org/mate-about>.
matchpathcon: Look up the persistent SELinux security context setting of a path. See also: `semanage fcontext`, `secon`, `chcon`, `restorecon`. More information: <https://manned.org/matchpathcon.8>.
mashtree: Make a fast tree from genomes. Does not make a phylogeny. More information: <https://github.com/lskatz/mashtree#usage>.
marzban-cli: Manage administrators, users, and subscriptions. More information: <https://github.com/Gozargah/Marzban/blob/master/cli/README.md>.
manpath: Determine the search path for manual pages. More information: <https://manned.org/manpath>.
mangohud: Display a monitoring HUD on top of a Vulkan or OpenGL graphical application. More information: <https://github.com/flightlessmango/MangoHud#normal-usage>.
mandb: Manage the pre-formatted manual page database. More information: <https://manned.org/mandb>.
makoctl: Control the `mako` notification daemon. Some subcommands such as `dismiss`, `invoke`, and `mode` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/makoctl>.
makoctl-mode: Manage notification modes in `mako`. Modes can be used to change notification behavior (e.g., do-not-disturb). More information: <https://manned.org/makoctl>.
makoctl-invoke: Invoke actions on notifications in `mako`. More information: <https://manned.org/makoctl>.
mako: Notification daemon for Wayland compositors. Can be controlled with `makoctl`. More information: <https://manned.org/mako>.
makepkg: Create a package which can be used with `pacman`. Uses the `PKGBUILD` file in the current working directory by default. More information: <https://manned.org/makepkg>.
machinectl: Control the systemd machine manager. Execute operations on virtual machines, containers, and images. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/machinectl.html>.
macchanger: Manipulate network interface MAC addresses. More information: <https://manned.org/macchanger>.
mac2unix: Change macOS-style line endings to Unix-style. Replaces CR with LF. See also: `unix2dos`, `unix2mac`, `dos2unix`. More information: <https://manned.org/mac2unix>.
lz: List all files inside a `.tar.gz` compressed archive. More information: <https://manned.org/lz>.
lynis: System and security auditing tool. More information: <https://cisofy.com/documentation/lynis/>.
lxterminal: Terminal emulator for LXDE. More information: <https://manned.org/lxterminal>.
lxi: Control LXI compatible instruments such as oscilloscopes. More information: <https://github.com/lxi-tools/lxi-tools#32-lxi>.
lxc: Manage Linux containers using the lxd REST API. Any container names or patterns can be prefixed with the name of a remote server. More information: <https://manned.org/lxc>.
lxc-top: Display resource usage of LXC containers. More information: <https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/manpages/man1/lxc-top.1.html>.
lxc-profile: Manage profiles for LXD containers. More information: <https://canonical.com/lxd/docs/latest/reference/manpages/lxc/profile/>.
lxc-network: Manage networks for LXD containers. More information: <https://canonical.com/lxd/docs/latest/reference/manpages/lxc/network/>.
lxc-info: Get info on a container. More information: <https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/getting-started/>.
lxc-console: Attach to a container. More information: <https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/manpages//man1/lxc-console.1.html>.
lxc-checkconfig: Check a kernel for LXC support. More information: <https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/getting-started/>.
lxc-attach: Attach to a container. More information: <https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/getting-started/>.
lvscan: Scan (list) all logical volumes in the system. Part of the LVM (Logical Volume Manager) suite. More information: <https://manned.org/lvscan>.
lvs: Display information about logical volumes. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvs>.
lvresize: Change the size of a logical volume. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvresize>.
lvrename: Rename a logical volume. More information: <https://manned.org/lvrename>.
lvremove: Remove logical volumes. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvremove>.
lvreduce: Reduce the size of a logical volume. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvreduce>.
lvmsar: LVM system activity reporter. Not supported under LVM2; prefer `dmstats`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmsar>.
lvmsadc: LVM system activity data collector (not supported under LVM2; prefer `dmstats`). More information: <https://manned.org/lvmsadc>.
lvmpolld: LVM poll daemon that supervises long-running LVM operations. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmpolld>.
lvmpersist: Manage persistent reservations (PR) on block devices or all PVs in a volume group. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmpersist>.
lvmdump: Collect diagnostic information about LVM2 (Logical Volume Manager). By default, outputs a compressed `.tar` archive with system and configuration data in the home directory. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmdump>.
lvmdiskscan: Scan for devices that may be used as physical volumes by LVM. Note: This command is deprecated, use `pvs` instead. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmdiskscan>.
lvmdevices: Manage the LVM devices file that lists block devices allowed for physical volumes. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmdevices>.
lvmconfig: Display and manipulate LVM configuration information. More information: <https://manned.org/lvmconfig>.
lvm_import_vdo: Import a VDO volume created by the VDO manager into an LVM-managed logical volume (irreversible). More information: <https://manned.org/lvm_import_vdo>.
lvm: Manage physical volumes, volume groups, and logical volumes using the Logical Volume Manager (LVM) interactive shell. More information: <https://manned.org/lvm>.
lvextend: Increase the size of a logical volume. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvextend>.
lvdisplay: Display information about Logical Volume Manager (LVM) logical volumes. See also: `lvm`, `lvs`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvdisplay>.
lvcreate: Create a logical volume in an existing volume group. A volume group is a collection of logical and physical volumes. See also: `lvm`. More information: <https://manned.org/lvcreate>.
lvconvert: Convert or modify the type, redundancy, or state of logical volumes. More information: <https://manned.org/lvconvert>.
lvchange: Change attributes or the activation state of logical volumes. More information: <https://manned.org/lvchange>.
lure: A distro-agnostic build system and user repository for Linux. More information: <https://github.com/lure-sh/lure/blob/master/docs/usage.md>.
ltrace: Display dynamic library calls of a process. More information: <https://manned.org/ltrace>.
lsusb: Display information about USB buses and devices connected to them. More information: <https://manned.org/lsusb>.
lstopo-no-graphics: Manage and query hardware topology information. More information: <https://manned.org/lstopo-no-graphics>.
lsscsi: List SCSI devices (or hosts) and their attributes. More information: <https://manned.org/lsscsi>.
lspci: List all PCI devices. More information: <https://manned.org/lspci>.
lsns: List information about all namespaces or about the specified namespace. More information: <https://manned.org/lsns>.
lsmod: Show the status of Linux kernel modules. See also: `modprobe`, `kmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/lsmod>.
lsmem: List the characteristics of the system's memory, including size and type of memory modules. More information: <https://manned.org/lsmem>.
lslogins: Show information about users on a Linux system. More information: <https://manned.org/lslogins>.
lslocks: List local system locks. More information: <https://manned.org/lslocks>.
lsipc: Show information on System V IPC facilities currently employed in the system. See also: `ipcs`. More information: <https://manned.org/lsipc>.
lsinitrd: Show the contents of an initramfs image. See also: `dracut`. More information: <https://github.com/dracutdevs/dracut/blob/master/man/lsinitrd.1.asc>.
lsinitcpio: View the contents of an initramfs image. See also: `mkinitcpio`. More information: <https://manned.org/lsinitcpio>.
lshw: List detailed information about hardware configurations as root user. See also: `inxi`, `hwinfo`, `dmidecode`. More information: <https://ezix.org/project/wiki/HardwareLiSter>.
lsfd: List open files and the corresponding processes in Linux. More information: <https://manned.org/lsfd>.
lsdev: Display installed hardware detected in the `/proc` director. More information: <https://manned.org/lsdev>.
lscpu: Display information about the CPU architecture. More information: <https://manned.org/lscpu>.
lsblk: List information about devices. More information: <https://manned.org/lsblk>.
lsb_release: Get LSB (Linux Standard Base) and distribution-specific information. More information: <https://manned.org/lsb_release>.
lsattr: List file attributes on a Linux filesystem. See also: `chattr`. More information: <https://manned.org/lsattr>.
lrzuntar: This command is an alias of `lrztar --decompress`.
lrztar: A wrapper for `lrzip` to simplify compression of directories. See also: `tar`, `lrzuntar`, `lrunzip`. More information: <https://manned.org/lrztar>.
lrzip: A large file compression program. See also: `lrunzip`, `lrztar`, `lrzuntar`. More information: <https://manned.org/lrzip>.
lrunzip: This command is an alias of `lrzip --decompress`.
losetup: Set up and control loop devices. More information: <https://manned.org/losetup>.
lookandfeeltool: This command is an alias of `plasma-apply-lookandfeel`.
logwatch: Summarize many different logs for common services (e.g. apache, pam_unix, sshd, etc.) in a single report. More information: <https://manned.org/logwatch>.
logsave: Save the output of a command in a logfile. More information: <https://manned.org/logsave>.
logrotate: Rotate, compress, and mail system logs. More information: <https://manned.org/logrotate>.
logread: Read the `logd` ring buffer log. More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/guide-user/base-system/log.essentials>.
loginctl: Manage the systemd login manager. See also: `lslogins`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/loginctl.html>.
login: Initiate a session for a user. More information: <https://manned.org/login>.
localedef: Manage locale definition files. More information: <https://manned.org/localedef>.
localectl: Control the system locale and keyboard layout settings. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/localectl.html>.
locale-gen: Generate locales defined in `/etc/locale.gen`. More information: <https://manned.org/locale-gen>.
loadkeys: Load the kernel keymap for the console. See also: `localectl`. More information: <https://manned.org/loadkeys>.
lndir: Create a shadow directory of symbolic links to another directory tree. More information: <https://manned.org/lndir>.
lnav: Advanced log file viewer to analyze logs with little to no setup. More information: <https://docs.lnav.org/en/latest/cli.html>.
lldpctl: Print link layer discovery protocol information. More information: <https://manned.org/lldpctl>.
llama-cli: Command-line interface for LLM inference. More information: <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp#llama-cli>.
linux64: This command is an alias of `setarch linux64`.
linux32: This command is an alias of `setarch linux32`.
linux-boot-prober: Probe a partition for bootable operating systems. More information: <https://github.com/MaddieM4/os-prober>.
links2: Command-line web browser with optional graphics support. See also: `links`. More information: <https://links.twibright.com/user_en.html#subch-browser_calibration>.
links: Command-line text-only web browser. See also: `links2`. More information: <https://links.twibright.com/user_en.html#subch-browser_calibration>.
line: Read a single line of input. More information: <https://manned.org/line.1>.
limine: An advanced, portable, multiprotocol bootloader. See also: `limine-enroll-config`, `limine-entry-tool`, `limine-snapper-sync`. More information: <https://codeberg.org/Limine/Limine>.
limine-snapper-sync: Synchronize Limine boot menu entries with Btrfs snapshots managed by Snapper. More information: <https://gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-snapper-sync>.
limine-scan: This command is an alias of `limine-entry-tool --scan`.
limine-entry-tool: A helper script to manage Limine bootloader entries on UEFI systems. More information: <https://gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-entry-tool>.
limine-enroll-config: Embed or reset the BLAKE2B hash of `limine.conf` in the Limine EFI executable. Used to ensure the configuration file has not been tampered with when Secure Boot is enabled. More information: <https://codeberg.org/Limine/Limine/src/branch/trunk/USAGE.md#secure-boot>.
light: Control the backlight of your screen. More information: <https://manned.org/light>.
lid: `lid` can refer to multiple commands with the same name.
lid.libuser: Display a user's groups or a group's users. More information: <https://manned.org/lid>.
lid.idutils: Query an ID database for tokens matching a pattern. Note: An ID database must first be built using `mkid`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/idutils/manual/idutils.html#lid-invocation>.
libuser-lid: This command is an alias of `lid`.
libtoolize: An `autotools` tool to prepare a package for using `libtool`. It performs various tasks, including generating necessary files and directories to integrate `libtool` seamlessly into a project. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/libtool/manual/libtool.html#Invoking-libtoolize>.
libtool: A generic library support script that hides the complexity of using shared libraries behind a consistent, portable interface. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/libtool/manual/libtool.html#Invoking-libtool>.
lftp: Sophisticated file transfer program. More information: <https://lftp.yar.ru/lftp-man.html>.
legit: Complementary command-line interface for Git. More information: <https://frostming.github.io/legit/>.
ledctl: Intel(R) Enclosure LED Control Application. More information: <https://manned.org/ledctl>.
lddd: Find broken library links on the system. This tool is only available on Arch Linux. More information: <https://manned.org/lddd>.
ldd: Display shared library dependencies of a binary. Do not use on an untrusted binary, use objdump for that instead. More information: <https://manned.org/ldd>.
ldconfig: Configure symlinks and cache for shared library dependencies. More information: <https://manned.org/ldconfig>.
ldapdomaindump: Dump users, computers, groups, OS, and membership information via LDAP to HTML, JSON, and greppable output. See also: `ldapsearch`. More information: <https://github.com/dirkjanm/ldapdomaindump#usage>.
lci: LOLCODE interpreter written in C. More information: <https://github.com/justinmeza/lci>.
lchage: Display or change user password policy. More information: <https://manned.org/lchage>.
lbu: Manage `apk` overlay files on a diskless Alpine Linux system. Note: Subcommands like `include` write to `/etc`, which is stored in RAM. You need to run `lbu commit` to save the changes. More information: <https://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/Alpine_local_backup>.
latte-dock: Replacement dock for Plasma desktop. More information: <https://github.com/KDE/latte-dock>.
lastlog: Show the most recent login of all users or of a user. More information: <https://manned.org/lastlog>.
lastb: List last logged in users. More information: <https://manned.org/lastb>.
last: View the last logged in users. More information: <https://manned.org/last>.
larasail: Manage Laravel on Digital Ocean servers. More information: <https://github.com/thedevdojo/larasail#setup-your-server>.
laptop-detect: Attempt to determine if the script is running on a laptop or desktop. More information: <https://gitlab.com/debiants/laptop-detect>.
kwriteconfig5: Write KConfig entries for KDE Plasma. More information: <https://userbase.kde.org/KDE_System_Administration/Configuration_Files>.
kwrite: Text editor of the KDE Desktop project. See also: `kate`. More information: <https://docs.kde.org/stable_kf6/en/kate/kwrite/command-line-options.html>.
kwallet-query: Read and write to a KDE Wallet. More information: <https://manned.org/kwallet-query>.
ksvgtopng5: Convert SVG files to PNG format. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kde-cli-tools/-/blob/master/ksvgtopng/ksvgtopng.cpp>.
kscreenctl: Manage display outputs on KDE Plasma. See also: `kscreen-doctor`, `kscreen-console`. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kscreen>.
kscreen-doctor: Change and manipulate the screen setup. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/libkscreen>.
krfb-virtualmonitor: Create a virtual monitor and allow that monitor to be used with VNC. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/network/krfb>.
kreadconfig5: Read KConfig entries for KDE Plasma. More information: <https://userbase.kde.org/KDE_System_Administration/Configuration_Files>.
krdpserver: Start an RDP server. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/krdp#running-the-example-server>.
krdc: Connect to a remote desktop server. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/network/krdc#usage>.
kpartx: Create device maps from partition tables. More information: <https://manned.org/kpartx>.
kpackagetool6: KPackage Manager: install, list, remove Plasma packages. More information: <https://manned.org/kpackagetool6>.
kpackagetool5: KPackage Manager: install, list, remove Plasma packages. More information: <https://manned.org/kpackagetool5>.
konsave: Save and apply your Linux customizations with just one command. More information: <https://github.com/Prayag2/konsave>.
koji: Interact with kojihub. Some subcommands such as `build`, `tag-build`, `download-build`, `buildinfo`, `call`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-untag-build: Remove a tag from one or more builds. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-taginfo: Print basic information about a tag. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-tag-build: Apply a tag to one or more builds. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-resubmit: Retry a cancelled or failed task, using the same parameter as the original task. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-help: Display help information for Koji commands. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/HOWTO/#exploring-koji>.
koji-download-build: Download a built package. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-cancel: Cancel active tasks running on the Koji build system. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-call: Execute an arbitrary XML-RPC call. Example: a build function declaration is `build(src, target, opts=None, priority=None, channel=None)`. More information: <https://koji.fedoraproject.org/koji/api>.
koji-buildinfo: Print basic information about a build. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
koji-build: Build an RPM package. More information: <https://docs.pagure.org/koji/>.
knockd: Port knocking daemon to listen for port knocking and execute scripts. More information: <https://manned.org/knockd>.
knock: Port knocking client to open specific ports on firewall. More information: <https://manned.org/knock>.
kmscon: Use the framebuffer instead of text mode to draw a terminal in a TTY. More information: <https://manned.org/kmscon>.
kmod: Manage Linux kernel modules. This program is usually called via its symlinks: `lsmod`, `rmmod`, `insmod`, `modinfo`, `modprobe`, and `depmod`. See their respective pages for more information. More information: <https://manned.org/kmod>.
kjv: The word of God available right on your desktop. More information: <https://github.com/layeh/kjv#kjv>.
kinfocenter: KDE information center to show system information. More information: <https://manned.org/kinfocenter>.
keyctl: Manipulate the Linux kernel keyring. More information: <https://manned.org/keyctl>.
kexec: Directly reboot into a new kernel. More information: <https://manned.org/kexec>.
kernelstub: Automatically manage Linux kernel loading on (U)EFI. More information: <https://github.com/isantop/kernelstub#usage>.
kernel-install: Add and remove kernel and initrd images to and from `/boot`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/kernel-install.html>.
kdocker: Easily dock applications to the system tray. More information: <https://github.com/user-none/KDocker>.
kdialog: Show KDE dialog boxes from within shell scripts. More information: <https://develop.kde.org/docs/administration/kdialog/>.
kdesrc-build: Easily build KDE components from its source repositories. More information: <https://manned.org/kdesrc-build>.
kde-inhibit: Inhibit various desktop functions while a command runs. More information: <https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kde-cli-tools/-/blob/master/kdeinhibit/main.cpp>.
kde-builder: Easily build KDE components from its source repositories. Drop-in replacement for `kdesrc-build`. More information: <https://kde-builder.kde.org/en/cmdline/supported-cmdline-params.html>.
just.js: A V8 JavaScript runtime for Linux. More information: <https://github.com/just-js/just>.
jpegtran: Perform lossless transformation of JPEG files. More information: <https://manned.org/jpegtran>.
journalctl: Query the systemd journal. See also: `dmesg`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/journalctl.html>.
jhead: Image timestamp and EXIF data manipulation. More information: <https://www.sentex.net/~mwandel/jhead/usage.html>.
iwlist: Get detailed information from a wireless interface. More information: <https://manned.org/iwlist>.
iwinfo: Retrieve information about wireless interfaces on OpenWrt. More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/guide-developer/ubus/iwinfo>.
iwctl: Control the `iwd` network supplicant. See also: `nmcli`, `iw`. More information: <https://manned.org/iwctl>.
iwconfig: Configure and show the parameters of a wireless network interface. More information: <https://manned.org/iwconfig>.
iw: Show and manipulate wireless devices. See also: `nmcli`, `iwctl`. More information: <https://wireless.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/en/users/documentation/iw.html>.
iw-reg: Manage WLAN regulatory domains. More information: <https://wireless.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/en/users/documentation/iw.html>.
iw-event: Listen to wireless events. More information: <https://wireless.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/en/users/documentation/iw.html>.
iw-dev: Show and manipulate wireless devices. For a list of channels, frequencies, and reg information: <https://wireless.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/en/developers/documentation/channellist.html>. More information: <https://wireless.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/en/users/documentation/iw.html>.
isosize: Display the size of an ISO file. More information: <https://manned.org/isosize>.
isoinfo: Utility programs for dumping and verifying ISO disk images. More information: <https://manned.org/isoinfo>.
iscsiadm: Manage iSCSI sessions, nodes, and discovery. More information: <https://manned.org/iscsiadm>.
iptables: Configure tables, chains, and rules of the Linux kernel IPv4 firewall. Use `ip6tables` to set rules for IPv6 traffic. See also: `iptables-save`, `iptables-restore`. More information: <https://manned.org/iptables>.
iptables-save: Save the `iptables` IPv4 configuration. Use `ip6tables-save` to do the same for IPv6. More information: <https://manned.org/iptables-save>.
iptables-restore: Restore the `iptables` IPv4 configuration. Use `ip6tables-restore` to do the same for IPv6. More information: <https://manned.org/iptables-restore>.
ipset: Create IP sets for firewall rules. More information: <https://manned.org/ipset>.
ipcrm: Delete IPC (Inter-process Communication) resources. More information: <https://manned.org/ipcrm>.
ipcmk: Create IPC (Inter-process Communication) resources. More information: <https://manned.org/ipcmk>.
ip6tables: This command is an alias of `iptables` for the IPv6 firewall.
ip6tables-save: This command is an alias of `iptables-save` for the IPv6 firewall.
ip6tables-restore: This command is an alias of `iptables-restore` for the IPv6 firewall.
ip: Show/manipulate routing, devices, policy routing, and tunnels. Some subcommands such as `address` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/ip.8>.
ip-tuntap: Manage TUN/TAP virtual network interfaces. More information: <https://baturin.org/docs/iproute2/#ip-tuntap>.
ip-stats: Manage and show interface statistics. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-stats>.
ip-rule: IP routing policy database management. See also: `ip route`. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-rule>.
ip-route: IP Routing table management subcommand. See also: `routel`, `ip rule`. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-route>.
ip-route-show: This command is an alias of `ip route list`.
ip-route-list: Display subcommand for IP Routing table management. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-route>.
ip-route-get: Get a single route to a destination and print its contents exactly as the kernel sees it. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-route>.
ip-route-add: Add a new networking route. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-route>.
ip-neighbour: This command is an alias of `ip neighbor`.
ip-neighbor: Neighbor/ARP/NDP tables management IP subcommand. See also: `arp-scan`. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-neighbour>.
ip-monitor: Monitor network for state changes. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-monitor>.
ip-address: IP Address management subcommand. More information: <https://manned.org/ip-address>.
iostat: Report statistics for devices and partitions. More information: <https://manned.org/iostat>.
ionice: Get or set program I/O scheduling class and priority. Scheduling classes: 1 (realtime), 2 (best-effort), 3 (idle). Priority levels: 0 (the highest) - 7 (the lowest). More information: <https://manned.org/ionice>.
inxi: Print a summary of system information and resources for debugging purposes. See also: `lshw`, `hwinfo`, `dmidecode`. More information: <https://manned.org/inxi>.
intercept: Read raw input events from a specified input event device and redirect it to `stdout`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/interception/linux/tools/-/tree/master#intercept>.
instaloader: Download pictures, videos, captions, and other metadata from Instagram. Note: You will need to provide Instagram login information if you want high-quality media downloads. More information: <https://instaloader.github.io/cli-options.html>.
installpkg: Install a Slackware package. More information: <https://www.slackbook.org/html/book.html#PACKAGE-MANAGEMENT-PACKAGE-UTILITIES-INSTALLPKG>.
insmod: Dynamically load modules into the Linux Kernel. See also: `kmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/insmod>.
inputattach: Attach a device to the Linux input system. The input devices are presented as files in `/dev/input/`. More information: <https://manned.org/inputattach>.
inotifywait: Wait for changes to files. See also: `fatrace`. More information: <https://manned.org/inotifywait>.
init: Linux run level manager. Requires the SYSVINIT compile-time option to be enabled if using systemd. More information: <https://manned.org/init.8>.
informant: Read Arch Linux package news. More information: <https://github.com/bradford-smith94/informant>.
inference-snap: Chat with generative AI Language Models that runs locally without internet. Here inference-snap is one of the supported models: `deepseek-r1`, `gemma3`, `gemma4`, `nemotron3-nano`, `qwen-vl`. More information: <https://documentation.ubuntu.com/inference-snaps/>.
imv: CLI image viewer for wayland and X11 aimed at tiling window managers. Handles multiple formats including Photoshop (PSD). More information: <https://sr.ht/~exec64/imv/>.
importctl: Download, Import, or Export disk images. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/importctl.html>.
impala: Manage Wi-Fi networks through a TUI. More information: <https://github.com/pythops/impala#-usage>.
imp: A helper to use native systemd support under WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux). Note: To run these from Windows rather than an already-running distribution, precede them with `wsl`. More information: <https://github.com/arkane-systems/bottle-imp#usage>.
imhex: Hex editor for reverse engineers and programmers. More information: <https://docs.werwolv.net/imhex>.
imgp: Resize and rotate JPEG and PNG images. More information: <https://github.com/jarun/imgp#usage>.
img2webp: Convert an image to WebP. More information: <https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/img2webp>.
img2txt: Convert images to color ASCII characters and output them to text-based colored files. More information: <https://manned.org/img2txt>.
ikaros: Vanilla OS Tool for managing drivers for your device. More information: <https://github.com/Vanilla-OS/Ikaros>.
iftop: Show bandwidth usage on an interface by host. More information: <https://manned.org/iftop>.
ifstatus: Display OpenWRT interface status in JSON format. More information: <https://openwrt.org/docs/techref/netifd>.
ifstat: View network interface statistics. More information: <https://manned.org/ifstat>.
ifreload: Reload network interface configuration. More information: <https://manned.org/ifreload>.
ifmetric: An IPv4 route metrics manipulation tool. More information: <https://0pointer.de/lennart/projects/ifmetric/>.
id3v2: Manage id3v2 tags, convert and list id3v1 tags. More information: <https://manned.org/id3v2>.
ico: Display an animation of a polyhedron. More information: <https://manned.org/ico>.
i7z: An Intel CPU (only i3, i5, and i7) realtime reporting tool. More information: <https://manned.org/i7z>.
i3status: Status line for the i3 window manager. This command is usually called from the i3 configuration file. More information: <https://i3wm.org/i3status/manpage.html>.
i3exit: Exit the i3 window manager. More information: <https://gitlab.manjaro.org/packages/extra/i3exit/-/blob/master/i3exit>.
i386: This command is an alias of `setarch i386`.
i3-scrot: Wrapper script around the screenshot utility `scrot` for the i3 window manager. The default save location is `~/Pictures` and can be changed in `~/.config/i3-scrot.conf`. More information: <https://gitlab.manjaro.org/packages/extra/i3-scrot>.
i2cset: Set the value of a register of an I2C device. Note: All addresses should be specified in hexadecimal. See also: `i2cdetect`, `i2cdump`, `i2cget`. More information: <https://manned.org/i2cset>.
i2cget: Read from a register of an I2C device. Note: All addresses should be specified in hexadecimal. See also: `i2cdetect`, `i2cdump`, `i2cset`. More information: <https://manned.org/i2cget>.
i2cdump: Dump I2C device registers. Note: All addresses should be specified in hexadecimal. See also: `i2cdetect`, `i2cget`, `i2cset`. More information: <https://manned.org/i2cdump>.
i2cdetect: Scan I2C buses. See also: `i2cdump`, `i2cget`, `i2cset`. More information: <https://manned.org/i2cdetect>.
hyprsunset: A blue light filter for Hyprland. Optionally configured via `~/.config/hypr/hyprsunset.conf`. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Hypr-Ecosystem/hyprsunset/>.
hyprshot: Screenshot utility for the Hyprland Wayland compositor. More information: <https://github.com/Gustash/Hyprshot>.
hyprpm: Control plugins for the Hyprland Wayland compositor. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Plugins/Using-Plugins/#hyprpm>.
hyprpicker: Minimal Wayland color picker for wlroots compositors (e.g., Hyprland). Requires a Wayland session. For clipboard autocopy, `wl-copy` must be installed. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Hypr-Ecosystem/hyprpicker/>.
hyprpaper: Wallpaper utility for Hyprland with the ability to dynamically change wallpapers. Controlled by the config file `~/.config/hypr/hyprpaper.conf`. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Hypr-Ecosystem/hyprpaper/>.
hyprlock: GPU-accelerated screen locker for the Hyprland Wayland compositor. Configured via `~/.config/hypr/hyprlock.conf`. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Hypr-Ecosystem/hyprlock/>.
hypridle: Idle management daemon for the Hyprland Wayland compositor. Executes commands based on inactivity timeouts. Configured via `~/.config/hypr/hypridle.conf`. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Hypr-Ecosystem/hypridle/>.
hyprcursor-util: Utility to create and extract Hyprcursor cursor themes for Hyprland. More information: <https://github.com/hyprwm/hyprcursor/blob/main/hyprcursor-util/README.md>.
hyprctl: Control parts of the Hyprland Wayland compositor. More information: <https://wiki.hypr.land/Configuring/Advanced-and-Cool/Using-hyprctl/>.
hwloc-ls: This command is an alias of `lstopo-no-graphics`.
hwinfo: Probe for the hardware present in the system. See also: `inxi`, `lshw`, `dmidecode`. More information: <https://manpages.opensuse.org/hwinfo/hwinfo.8.en.html>.
hwclock: Read or change the hardware clock. More information: <https://manned.org/hwclock>.
hw-probe: Probe for hardware and upload the information to <https://linux-hardware.org>. More information: <https://manned.org/hw-probe>.
http_load: An HTTP benchmarking tool. Runs multiple HTTP fetches in parallel to test the throughput of a web server. More information: <https://www.acme.com/software/http_load/>.
http-prompt: An interactive HTTP client featuring autocomplete and syntax highlighting. More information: <https://github.com/httpie/http-prompt>.
htpdate: Synchronize local date and time via HTTP headers from web servers. More information: <https://www.vervest.org/htp/>.
hostnamectl: Get or set the hostname of the computer. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/hostnamectl.html>.
homeshick: Synchronize Git dotfiles. See also: `chezmoi`, `stow`, `tuckr`, `vcsh`. More information: <https://github.com/andsens/homeshick/wiki>.
homectl: Create, remove, change, or inspect home directories using the systemd-homed service. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/homectl.html>.
hollywood: Fill your console with Hollywood melodrama technobabble. More information: <https://manned.org/hollywood>.
hlint: Suggest improvements to Haskell code. More information: <https://hackage.haskell.org/package/hlint>.
hdparm: Get and set SATA and IDE hard drive parameters. More information: <https://manned.org/hdparm>.
hddtemp: Display temperature of HDD via S.M.A.R.T. More information: <https://manned.org/hddtemp>.
hd-idle: Spin down external disks after a period of idle time. More information: <https://manned.org/hd-idle>.
hcitool: Monitor, configure connections, and send special commands to Bluetooth devices. More information: <https://manned.org/hcitool>.
haveged: Hardware-based random number generator. More information: <https://manned.org/haveged>.
hardlink: Consolidate duplicate files by replacing them with hard links. Part of `util-linux`, useful for saving disk space when identical files exist across directories. More information: <https://manned.org/hardlink>.
hardinfo: Show hardware information in GUI window. More information: <https://manned.org/hardinfo>.
handlr: Manage your default applications. More information: <https://github.com/chmln/handlr#usage>.
gzexe: Compress executable files while keeping them executable. Back up the original file, appending `~` to its name, and create a shell script that uncompresses and executes the binary inside it. More information: <https://manned.org/gzexe>.
gummy: Screen brightness/temperature manager for Linux/X11. More information: <https://github.com/Gitoffthelawn/gummy>.
guix-package: Install, upgrade, and remove Guix packages or roll back to previous configurations. More information: <https://guix.gnu.org/manual/en/guix.html#Invoking-guix-package>.
guake: A drop-down terminal for GNOME. See also: `yakuake`. More information: <https://manned.org/guake>.
gtk-launch: Launch applications from `.desktop` files that reside in standard locations. More information: <https://manned.org/gtk-launch>.
gst-launch-1.0-v4l2src: Read frames from a Video4Linux2 device. More information: <https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/documentation/video4linux2/v4l2src.html>.
gst-launch-1.0-pipewiresrc: Read data from a PipeWire node. More information: <https://github.com/PipeWire/pipewire/tree/master/src/gst>.
gst-launch-1.0-pipewiresink: Create a PipeWire node to output data from. More information: <https://github.com/PipeWire/pipewire/tree/master/src/gst>.
gsettings: Query and modify dconf settings with schema validation. More information: <https://manned.org/gsettings>.
gs: GhostScript, a PDF and PostScript interpreter. More information: <https://manned.org/gs>.
grubby: Tool for configuring `grub` and `zipl` bootloaders. More information: <https://manned.org/grubby.8>.
grub2-mkpasswd-pbkdf2: Generate a hashed password for GRUB. More information: <https://manned.org/grub2-mkpasswd-pbkdf2>.
grub-set-default: Set the default boot entry for GRUB. More information: <https://manned.org/grub-set-default>.
grub-script-check: The program `grub-script-check` takes a GRUB script file and checks it for syntax errors. It may take a path as a non-option argument. If none is supplied, it will read from `stdin`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html#Invoking-grub_002dscript_002dcheck>.
grub-reboot: Set the default boot entry for GRUB, for the next boot only. More information: <https://manned.org/grub-reboot>.
grub-probe: Probe device information for a particular path or device. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/html_node/Invoking-grub_002dprobe.html>.
grub-mount: Mount a filesystem or filesystem image read-only using GRUB's filesystem drivers. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html#Invoking-grub_002dmount>.
grub-mkrescue: Make a GRUB CD/USB/floppy bootable image. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html#Invoking-grub_002dmkrescue>.
grub-mkrelpath: Convert a system path to a path relative to its filesystem root for GRUB. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/html_node/Invoking-grub_002dmkrelpath.html>.
grub-mkfont: Convert common font file formats into the PF2 format used by GRUB. More information: <https://manned.org/grub-mkfont>.
grub-mkconfig: Generate a GRUB configuration file. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html#Invoking-grub_002dmkconfig>.
grub-install: Install GRUB to a device. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html#Installing-GRUB-using-grub_002dinstall>.
grub-file: Check if a file is of a bootable image type. More information: <https://manned.org/grub-file>.
grub-editenv: Edit GRUB environment variables. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html>.
grub-bios-setup: Set up a device to use GRUB with a BIOS configuration. You should use `grub-install` instead of `grub-bios-setup` in most cases. More information: <https://manned.org/grub-bios-setup>.
growpart: Extend a partition in a disk or disk image to fill available space. More information: <https://github.com/canonical/cloud-utils>.
groupmod: Modify existing user groups in the system. See also: `groups`, `groupadd`, `groupdel`. More information: <https://manned.org/groupmod>.
groupdel: Delete existing user groups from the system. See also: `groups`, `groupadd`, `groupmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/groupdel>.
groupadd: Add user groups to the system. See also: `groups`, `groupdel`, `groupmod`. More information: <https://manned.org/groupadd>.
grim: Grab images (screenshots) from a Wayland compositor. By default, files are saved to `$GRIM_DEFAULT_DIR` or `$XDG_PICTURES_DIR` if the first variable is unset. If none of the environment variables are set, files are saved to the current working directory. More information: <https://manned.org/grim>.
grdctl: Manage GNOME Remote Desktop service. More information: <https://github.com/GNOME/gnome-remote-desktop/blob/main/man/grdctl.txt>.
grabc: A tool to identify a pixel color of an X Window. More information: <https://manned.org/grabc>.
gpu-screen-recorder: Record the screen and encode the video with a GPU. More information: <https://git.dec05eba.com/gpu-screen-recorder/about/>.
gpm: Enable mouse support for the Linux virtual console. More information: <https://manned.org/gpm>.
gphoto2: Control digital cameras from the command line. More information: <http://www.gphoto.org/doc/manual/ref-gphoto2-cli.html>.
gpclient: Connect to a GlobalProtect VPN on Linux via OpenConnect. More information: <https://github.com/yuezk/GlobalProtect-openconnect>.
google-chrome-stable: This command is an alias of `chromium`. More information: <https://www.google.com/chrome/>.
goobook: Access Google contacts from `mutt` or the command-line. More information: <https://manned.org/goobook>.
goldeneye.py: An HTTP DoS test tool. More information: <https://github.com/jseidl/GoldenEye#usage>.
goaccess: An open source real-time web log analyzer. More information: <https://goaccess.io/man>.
