gnuls: This command is an alias of GNU `ls`.
gnulogname: This command is an alias of GNU `logname`.
gnuln: This command is an alias of GNU `ln`.
gnulink: This command is an alias of GNU `link`.
gnujoin: This command is an alias of GNU `join`.
gnuinstall: This command is an alias of GNU `install`.
gnuid: This command is an alias of GNU `id`.
gnuhostid: This command is an alias of GNU `hostid`.
gnuhead: This command is an alias of GNU `head`.
gnugroups: This command is an alias of GNU `groups`.
gnufold: This command is an alias of GNU `fold`.
gnufmt: This command is an alias of GNU `fmt`.
gnufalse: This command is an alias of GNU `false`.
gnufactor: This command is an alias of GNU `factor`.
gnuexpr: This command is an alias of GNU `expr`.
gnuexpand: This command is an alias of GNU `expand`.
gnuenv: This command is an alias of GNU `env`.
gnuecho: This command is an alias of GNU `echo`.
gnudu: This command is an alias of GNU `du`.
gnudirname: This command is an alias of GNU `dirname`.
gnudircolors: This command is an alias of GNU `dircolors`.
gnudir: This command is an alias of GNU `dir`.
gnudf: This command is an alias of GNU `df`.
gnudd: This command is an alias of GNU `dd`.
gnudate: This command is an alias of GNU `date`.
gnucut: This command is an alias of GNU `cut`.
gnucsplit: This command is an alias of GNU `csplit`.
gnucp: This command is an alias of GNU `cp`.
gnucomm: This command is an alias of GNU `comm`.
gnucksum: This command is an alias of GNU `cksum`.
gnuchown: This command is an alias of GNU `chown`.
gnuchmod: This command is an alias of GNU `chmod`.
gnuchgrp: This command is an alias of GNU `chgrp`.
gnuchcon: This command is an alias of GNU `chcon`.
gnucat: This command is an alias of GNU `cat`.
gnubasenc: This command is an alias of GNU `basenc`.
gnubasename: This command is an alias of GNU `basename`.
gnubase64: This command is an alias of GNU `base64`.
gnubase32: This command is an alias of GNU `base32`.
gnub2sum: This command is an alias of GNU `b2sum`.
gnuarch: This command is an alias of GNU `arch`.
gnu[: This command is an alias of GNU `[`.
gnome-terminal: The GNOME Terminal emulator. More information: <https://help.gnome.org/users/gnome-terminal/stable/>.
gnome-software: Add and remove applications and update your system. More information: <https://manned.org/gnome-software>.
gnome-screenshot: Capture the screen, a window, or a user-defined area and save the image to a file. More information: <https://manned.org/gnome-screenshot>.
gnome-extensions: Manage gnome extensions from the terminal. More information: <https://wiki.gnome.org/Projects/GnomeShell/Extensions>.
gnome-calculator: The official calculator for the GNOME desktop environment. More information: <https://wiki.gnome.org/Apps/Calculator>.
gksudo: Frontend for `sudo`. Run graphical commands which need root access without having to run an X terminal emulator. Note: This command is deprecated and no longer maintained, use `pkexec` instead. See also: `gksu`. More information: <https://manned.org/gksudo>.
gksu: Frontend for `su`. Run graphical commands which need root access without having to run an X terminal emulator. Note: This command is deprecated and no longer maintained, use `pkexec` instead. See also: `gksudo`. More information: <https://manned.org/gksu>.
gio: Handle local and virtual files (GVfs). Part of GLib used in GNOME-based systems. More information: <https://manned.org/gio>.
gio-trash: Move files to the trash bin. Used by GNOME to handle trash. More information: <https://manned.org/gio>.
gif2webp: Convert a GIF image to WebP. More information: <https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/gif2webp>.
getsebool: Get SELinux boolean value. See also: `semanage boolean`, `setsebool`. More information: <https://manned.org/getsebool>.
getfattr: Display file names and extended attributes. See also: `setfattr`. More information: <https://manned.org/getfattr>.
getfacl: Get file access control lists (ACL). More information: <https://manned.org/getfacl>.
getent: Get entries from Name Service Switch libraries. More information: <https://manned.org/getent>.
getenforce: Get the current mode of SELinux (i.e. enforcing, permissive, or disabled). See also: `setenforce`, `semanage permissive`. More information: <https://manned.org/getenforce>.
getconf: Get configuration values from your Linux system. More information: <https://manned.org/getconf.1>.
getcap: Display the name and capabilities of each specified file. More information: <https://manned.org/getcap>.
get-edid: Retrieve monitor specifications using the VESA VBE DDC protocol. See also: `edid-decode`. More information: <https://manned.org/get-edid>.
genkernel: Gentoo Linux utility to compile and install kernels. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Genkernel>.
genisoimage: This command is an alias of `mkisofs`.
genie: Set up and use a "bottle" namespace to run systemd under WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux). To run these from Windows rather than an already-running distribution, precede them with `wsl`. More information: <https://github.com/arkane-systems/genie>.
genfstab: Generate output suitable for addition to the `/etc/fstab` file. More information: <https://manned.org/genfstab>.
gemma4: The examples for this command have been moved together with `inference-snap`. More information: <https://github.com/canonical/gemma4-snap>.
gemma3: The examples for this command have been moved together with `inference-snap`. More information: <https://github.com/canonical/gemma3-snap>.
gedit: Text editor of the GNOME Desktop project. More information: <https://manned.org/gedit>.
gdisk: GPT (GUID Partition Table) disk partitioning tool. See also: `cfdisk`, `fdisk`, `parted`. More information: <https://manned.org/gdisk>.
gdbus: Interact with D-Bus objects. Part of GLib. More information: <https://manned.org/gdbus>.
gcrane-completion: Generate the autocompletion script for gcrane for the specified shell. The available shells are Bash, fish, PowerShell, and Zsh. More information: <https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/gcrane/README.md>.
gcov: Code coverage analysis and profiling tool that discovers untested parts of a program. Also displays a copy of source code annotated with execution frequencies of code segments. More information: <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Invoking-Gcov.html>.
gbp: A system to integrate the Debian package build system with Git. More information: <https://honk.sigxcpu.org/projects/git-buildpackage/manual-html/gbp.html>.
gamescope: A micro-compositor used as a game layer. See also: `cage`. More information: <https://github.com/ValveSoftware/gamescope#keyboard-shortcuts>.
gamemoderun: Invoke a set of optimizations to improve game performance. More information: <https://github.com/FeralInteractive/gamemode#requesting-gamemode>.
fwupdtool: Update device firmware manually or manipulate firmware files. See also: `fwupdmgr`. More information: <https://github.com/fwupd/fwupd/blob/main/src/fwupdtool.md>.
fwupdmgr: Update device firmware, including UEFI, using `fwupd`. See also: `fwupdtool`. More information: <https://github.com/fwupd/fwupd/blob/main/src/fwupdmgr.md>.
fwconsole: Manage and configure your FreePBX system (PBX server). More information: <https://sangomakb.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PG/pages/41779247/fwconsole+commands+13>.
fuzzel: A Wayland-native application launcher and fuzzy finder, inspired by `rofi` and `dmenu`. More information: <https://codeberg.org/dnkl/fuzzel>.
fuser: Display process IDs currently using files or sockets. More information: <https://manned.org/fuser>.
fuseiso: FUSE module to mount ISO, BIN, NRG, MDF and IMG filesystem images. More information: <https://manned.org/fuseiso>.
fstrim: Discard unused blocks on a mounted filesystem. Only supported by flash memory devices such as SSDs and microSD cards. More information: <https://manned.org/fstrim>.
fscrypt: Go tool for managing Linux filesystem encryption. More information: <https://github.com/google/fscrypt#example-usage>.
fsck: Check the integrity of a filesystem or repair it. The filesystem should be unmounted at the time the command is run. More information: <https://manned.org/fsck>.
fsadm: Check or resize a filesystem on a device. More information: <https://manned.org/fsadm>.
fs_cli: Connect to and control a running FreeSWITCH server using the FreeSWITCH Command Line Interface (ESL client). More information: <https://developer.signalwire.com/freeswitch/FreeSWITCH-Explained/Client-and-Developer-Interfaces/1048948/>.
free: Display amount of free and used memory in the system. More information: <https://manned.org/free>.
fprintd: Fingerprint management daemon. `fprintd` isn't a command, but a set of commands. More information: <https://fprint.freedesktop.org/>.
fprintd-verify: Verify fingerprints against the database. More information: <https://manned.org/fprintd-verify>.
fprintd-enroll: Enroll fingerprints into the database. More information: <https://manned.org/fprintd-enroll>.
fprintd-delete: Remove fingerprints from the database. More information: <https://manned.org/fprintd-delete>.
foremost: Recover files using their headers, footers, and data structures. More information: <https://manned.org/foremost>.
fonttools: Manipulate fonts in Python. More information: <https://fonttools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>.
fonttools-subset: Generate subsets of fonts or optimize file sizes. More information: <https://fonttools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subset/index.html>.
fluidsynth: Synthesize audio from MIDI files. More information: <https://github.com/FluidSynth/fluidsynth/wiki/UserManual>.
flock: Manage file locks from shell scripts. It can be used to ensure that only one instance of a command is running. More information: <https://manned.org/flock>.
flex: Lexical analyzer generator. Given the specification for a lexical analyzer, generates C code implementing it. More information: <https://manned.org/flex>.
flatpak: Build, install, and run flatpak applications and runtimes. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak>.
flatpak-update: Update flatpak applications and runtimes. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-update>.
flatpak-uninstall: Uninstall flatpak applications and runtimes. See also: `flatpak install`, `flatpak update`. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-uninstall>.
flatpak-run: Run flatpak applications and runtimes. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-run>.
flatpak-remote-info: Show information about an application or runtime in a remote. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-remote-info>.
flatpak-mask: Mask out updates and automatic installation. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-mask>.
flatpak-install: Install flatpak applications and runtimes. See also: `flatpak`, `flatpak update`, `flatpak run`. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-install>.
flatpak-history: Show historical changes to Flatpak installations on the system. See also: `journalctl`. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-history>.
flatpak-config: Manage configuration for Flatpak. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-command-reference.html#flatpak-config>.
flatpak-builder: Help build application dependencies. More information: <https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/flatpak-builder-command-reference.html>.
flashrom: Read, write, verify, and erase flash chips. More information: <https://manned.org/flashrom>.
flash: Flash cards in the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/tallguyjenks/fla.sh>.
flameshot: Screenshot utility with a GUI. Supports basic image editing, such as text, shapes, colors, and imgur. More information: <https://flameshot.org/docs/advanced/commandline-options/>.
fixfiles: Fix file SELinux security contexts. More information: <https://manned.org/fixfiles>.
firewall-cmd: The firewalld client. View and adapt the runtime or permanent firewall configuration state. More information: <https://firewalld.org/documentation/man-pages/firewall-cmd>.
firejail: Securely sandboxes processes to containers using built-in Linux capabilities. More information: <https://manned.org/firejail>.
findfs: Find a filesystem by label or UUID. More information: <https://manned.org/findfs>.
fincore: Display how much cache memory a file is taking. See also: `fadvise`. More information: <https://manned.org/fincore>.
finch: Console-based modular messaging client. More information: <https://developer.pidgin.im/wiki/Using%20Finch>.
filefrag: Report how badly fragmented a particular file might be. More information: <https://manned.org/filefrag>.
fgconsole: Print the number of the foreground virtual terminal. See also: `chvt`. More information: <https://manned.org/fgconsole>.
fftest: Test force-feedback devices (e.g., controllers with rumble functionality). More information: <https://manned.org/fftest>.
feedreader: A GUI desktop RSS client. Note: FeedReader is no longer being maintained. More information: <https://manned.org/feedreader>.
fdisk: Manage partition tables and partitions on a storage drive. See also: `partprobe`, `parted`, `cfdisk`. More information: <https://manned.org/fdisk>.
fbset: Show and modify frame buffer device settings. More information: <https://manned.org/fbset.1>.
fbi: Display images in a terminal framebuffer. More information: <https://manned.org/fbi>.
fbgrab: Generate screenshots directly from the framebuffer. More information: <https://github.com/GunnarMonell/fbgrab#fbgrab>.
fatrace: Report file access events. See also: `inotifywait`. More information: <https://manned.org/fatrace>.
fatlabel: Get or set the label of a FAT32 partition. More information: <https://manned.org/fatlabel>.
farge: Display the color of a specific pixel on the screen in either hexadecimal or RGB formats. More information: <https://github.com/sdushantha/farge#usage>.
fancontrol: Automated fan speed management. Uses a configuration file to control a wide range of variables. More information: <https://manned.org/fancontrol>.
fallocate: Reserve or deallocate disk space to files. The utility allocates space without zeroing. More information: <https://manned.org/fallocate>.
faketime: Fake the system time for a command. More information: <https://manned.org/faketime>.
fakeroot: Run a command in an environment faking root privileges for file manipulation. More information: <https://manned.org/fakeroot>.
faillock: Display and modify authentication failure record files. More information: <https://manned.org/faillock>.
fail2ban-client: Configure and control the fail2ban server. More information: <https://manned.org/fail2ban-client>.
fadvise: Control Linux file caching behavior. See also: `fincore`. More information: <https://manned.org/fadvise>.
factorio: Create and start a headless Factorio server. More information: <https://wiki.factorio.com/Multiplayer>.
f5fpc: A proprietary commercial SSL VPN client by BIG-IP Edge. More information: <https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K47922841>.
eyed3: Read and manipulate metadata of MP3 files. More information: <https://manned.org/eyeD3>.
extundelete: Recover deleted files from ext3 or ext4 partitions by parsing the journal. See also: `date`, `umount`. More information: <https://extundelete.sourceforge.net/options.html>.
extrepo: Manage external Debian repositories. It is used to manage external repositories in Debian. More information: <https://manned.org/extrepo.1p>.
explodepkg: Extract the contents of a Slackware package to the current directory. See also: `installpkg`, `removepkg`, `upgradepkg`, `makepkg`, `pkgtool`. More information: <https://www.slackbook.org/html/book.html#PACKAGE-MANAGEMENT-EXPLODEPKG>.
expect: Script executor that interacts with other programs that require user input. More information: <https://manned.org/expect>.
expac: A data extraction tool for alpm databases, offering printf-like flexibility for pacman-based utilities. See also: `pacman`. More information: <https://github.com/falconindy/expac#name>.
exiqgrep: Perl script offering possibilities to `grep` in the Exim queue output. More information: <https://www.exim.org/exim-html-current/doc/html/spec_html/ch-exim_utilities.html>.
exif: Show and change EXIF information in JPEG files. More information: <https://manned.org/exif>.
exch: Swap the filepaths and filenames of two files. More information: <https://manned.org/exch>.
eww: Implement your own custom widgets in any window manager. More information: <https://elkowar.github.io/eww/>.
evtest: Display information from input device drivers. More information: <https://manned.org/evtest>.
euse: Enable, disable, and obtain information about Gentoo USE flags. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Euse>.
eu-readelf: Display information about ELF files. More information: <https://manned.org/eu-readelf>.
ethtool: Display and modify Network Interface Controller (NIC) parameters. More information: <https://manned.org/ethtool>.
etckeeper: Track system configuration files in Git. More information: <https://manned.org/etckeeper>.
eselect: Gentoo's multi-purpose configuration and management tool. It consists of various modules that take care of individual administrative tasks. Some subcommands such as `kernel`, `locale`, `profile`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eselect>.
eselect-repository: An `eselect` module for configuring ebuild repositories for Portage. After enabling a repository, you have to run `emerge --sync repo_name` to download ebuilds. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eselect/Repository>.
eselect-profile: An `eselect` module for managing the `/etc/portage/make.profile` symlink, which sets the system profile. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eselect#Profile>.
eselect-news: An `eselect` module for reading Gentoo news items. Note: Portage will print a notice when a repository is synchronized and there are unread news items. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eselect#News>.
eselect-locale: An `eselect` module for managing the `$LANG` environment variable, which sets the system language. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eselect#Locale>.
eselect-kernel: An `eselect` module for managing the `/usr/src/linux` symlink. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eselect#Kernel>.
esearch: Perform a new Entrez search using terms in indexed fields. It is part of the `edirect` package. More information: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK179288/>.
equery: View information about Portage packages. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Equery>.
eopkg: Package manager for Solus. More information: <https://help.getsol.us/docs/user/package-management/basics/>.
eog: View and manage images. More information: <https://manned.org/eog>.
envycontrol: GPU switching utility for Nvidia Optimus laptops. More information: <https://github.com/bayasdev/envycontrol#%EF%B8%8F-usage>.
enum4linux: Enumerate Windows and Samba information from remote systems. More information: <https://labs.portcullis.co.uk/tools/enum4linux/>.
engrampa: Package files into `zip`/`.tar` file in MATE desktop environment. See also: `zip`, `tar`. More information: <https://github.com/mate-desktop/engrampa>.
emerge: Gentoo Linux package manager utility. For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Portage#emerge>.
emaint: Perform Portage maintenance tasks. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Portage#emaint>.
elink: Look up precomputed neighbors within a database, or find associated records in other databases. It is part of the `edirect` package. More information: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK179288/>.
elfedit: Update the ELF header and program properties of ELF files. See also: `readelf`, `objcopy`. More information: <https://manned.org/elfedit>.
eject: Eject CDs, floppy disks, tape drives, and USB sticks. More information: <https://manned.org/eject>.
eix: Utilities for searching local Gentoo packages. Update local package cache using `eix-update`. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eix>.
einfo: Provide the number of records indexed in each database field, the last update date of the database, and the available links from the database to other Entrez databases. More information: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK179288/>.
ego: Funtoo's official system personality management tool. More information: <https://funtoo-ego.readthedocs.io/en/develop/>.
eglinfo: Display platform EGL information. More information: <https://github.com/dv1/eglinfo>.
efibootmgr: Manipulate the UEFI Boot Manager. More information: <https://manned.org/efibootmgr>.
efibootdump: Dump boot entries from a variable or a file. More information: <https://manned.org/efibootdump>.
edquota: Edit quotas for a user or group. By default it operates on all filesystems with quotas. Quota information is stored permanently in the `quota.user` and `quota.group` files in the root of the filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/edquota>.
edid-decode: Parse EDID information of a display. See also: `get-edid`. More information: <https://manned.org/edid-decode>.
eclean: Clean repository source files and binary packages. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Eclean>.
eclean-kernel: Remove old kernels in Gentoo. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Kernel/Removal#Using_eclean-kernel>.
ebuild: A low level interface to the Gentoo Portage system. More information: <https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Ebuild>.
e4defrag: Defragment an ext4 filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/e4defrag>.
e2undo: Replay undo logs for an ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystem. This can be used to undo a failed operation by an e2fsprogs program. More information: <https://manned.org/e2undo>.
e2label: Change the label on an ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/e2label>.
e2image: Save critical ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystem metadata to a file. More information: <https://manned.org/e2image>.
e2fsck: Check a Linux ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystem. The partition should be unmounted. More information: <https://manned.org/e2fsck>.
e2freefrag: Print the free space fragmentation information for ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystems. More information: <https://manned.org/e2freefrag>.
dysk: Display filesystem information in a table. More information: <https://manned.org/dysk>.
dutree: Analyze filesystem usage with colorful text-based trees. More information: <https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree#usage>.
duperemove: Find duplicate filesystem extents and optionally schedule them for deduplication. An extent is small part of a file inside the filesystem. On some filesystems one extent can be referenced multiple times, when parts of the content of the files are identical. More information: <https://markfasheh.github.io/duperemove/>.
dumpe2fs: Print the super block and blocks group information for ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystems. Unmount the partition before running this command using `umount device`. More information: <https://manned.org/dumpe2fs>.
dump.exfat: Show on-disk information of an exFAT filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/dump.exfat>.
dstat: Versatile tool for generating system resource statistics. Note: This command is deprecated and no longer maintained. More information: <https://github.com/dstat-real/dstat>.
dropbearkey: Generate SSH keys in Dropbear format. More information: <https://manned.org/dropbearkey>.
dropbearconvert: Convert between Dropbear and OpenSSH private key formats. More information: <https://manned.org/dropbearconvert>.
drm_info: Dump information about Direct Rendering Manager devices. More information: <https://manned.org/drm_info>.
drawing: Free basic raster image editor in GNOME desktop environment. More information: <https://maoschanz.github.io/drawing/>.
dracut: Generate initramfs images to boot the Linux kernel. Dracut uses options from configuration files in `/etc/dracut.conf`, `/etc/dracut.conf.d/*.conf`, and `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/*.conf` by default. More information: <https://github.com/dracut-ng/dracut-ng/blob/main/man/dracut.8.adoc>.
dpkg: Debian package manager. For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. Some subcommands such as `deb` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/dpkg>.
dpkg-reconfigure: Reconfigure an already installed package. More information: <https://manned.org/dpkg-reconfigure>.
dpkg-query: Display information about installed packages. More information: <https://manned.org/dpkg-query>.
dpkg-deb: Pack, unpack, and provide information about Debian archives. More information: <https://manned.org/dpkg-deb>.
dpkg-buildpackage: Compile binary and/or source Debian packages from source code. Normally executed inside a source tree that contains a `debian/` directory. Also handles build dependencies, creates files like `.buildinfo` and `.changes`, and signs the result if applicable. More information: <https://manned.org/dpkg-buildpackage>.
dpigs: Show which installed packages occupy the most space on `apt` based systems. More information: <https://manned.org/dpigs>.
dphys-swapfile: Manage the swap file on Debian-based Linux systems. More information: <https://manned.org/dphys-swapfile>.
dos2unix: Change DOS-style line endings to Unix-style. Replaces CRLF with LF. See also: `unix2dos`, `unix2mac`, `mac2unix`. More information: <https://manned.org/dos2unix>.
dolphin: KDE's file manager to manage files and directories. See also: `nautilus`, `caja`, `thunar`, `ranger`. More information: <https://apps.kde.org/dolphin/>.
dockerd: A persistent process to start and manage Docker containers. More information: <https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/dockerd/>.
do-release-upgrade: The Ubuntu release upgrader. More information: <https://manned.org/do-release-upgrade>.
dnstracer: Determine where a DNS gets its information from. More information: <https://manned.org/dnstracer>.
dnsmap: Scan a domain for common subdomains e.g. smtp.domain.org. More information: <https://github.com/resurrecting-open-source-projects/dnsmap>.
dnsdomainname: Show the system's DNS domain name. Note: The tool uses `gethostname` to get the hostname of the system and then `getaddrinfo` to resolve it into a canonical name. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/inetutils/manual/inetutils.html#dnsdomainname-invocation>.
dnf5: This command is an alias of `dnf`.
dnf5-group: This command is an alias of `dnf group`. Note: From Fedora 37 to 40 (inclusive), `dnf` runs DNF v4 while `dnf5` runs DNF v5.
dnf5-copr: Manage Copr repositories on Fedora-based systems. More information: <https://dnf5.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dnf5_plugins/copr.8.html>.
dnf4: Package manager for RHEL 8/9 and older Fedora versions (pre-41). For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. More information: <https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_ref.html>.
dnf: Package manager for Fedora 41+ and RHEL 10. For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. More information: <https://dnf5.readthedocs.io/en/latest/commands/index.html>.
dnf-versionlock: Protect packages from updates to newer versions. Not default to `dnf` but supported via `dnf-plugins-core`. More information: <https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/versionlock.html>.
dnf-system-upgrade: Upgrade Fedora to a new major release. More information: <https://dnf5.readthedocs.io/en/latest/commands/system-upgrade.8.html>.
dnf-reposync: Synchronize packages and metadata of a remote DNF repository to a local directory. Not default to `dnf` but supported via `dnf-plugins-core`. More information: <https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reposync.html>.
dnf-repoquery: Query packages for information. More information: <https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_ref.html#repoquery-command>.
dnf-install: Install packages on Red Hat-based distributions. More information: <https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_ref.html#install-examples>.
dnf-group: Manage virtual collections of packages on Fedora-based systems. More information: <https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_ref.html#group-command>.
dnf-download: Download RPM packages from the DNF repositories. Not default to `dnf` but supported via `dnf-plugins-core`. More information: <https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/download.html>.
dnf-deplist: This command is an alias of `dnf repoquery --deplist`.
dnf-config-manager: Manage DNF configuration options and repositories on Fedora-based systems. Not default to `dnf` but supported via `dnf-plugins-core`. More information: <https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config_manager.html>.
dnf-clean: Perform cleanup of temporary files kept for Red Hat-based repositories. More information: <https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_ref.html#clean-command>.
dnf-changelog: View the changelogs for a given package. Not default to `dnf` but supported via `dnf-plugins-core`. More information: <https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/changelog.html>.
dnf-builddep: Install dependencies to build a given package. Not default to `dnf` but supported via `dnf-plugins-core`. More information: <https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/builddep.html>.
dmidecode: Display the DMI (alternatively known as SMBIOS) table contents in a human-readable format. See also: `inxi`, `lshw`, `hwinfo`. More information: <https://manned.org/dmidecode>.
dmesg: Write the kernel messages to `stdout`. See also: `journalctl`. More information: <https://manned.org/dmesg>.
dmenu: Dynamic menu. Create a menu from a text input with each item on a new line. More information: <https://manned.org/dmenu>.
dm-tool: A tool to communicate with the display manager. More information: <https://manned.org/dm-tool>.
dkms: A framework that allows for dynamic building of kernel modules. More information: <https://manned.org/dkms>.
distrobox: Use any Linux distribution inside your terminal in a container. Install & use packages inside it while tightly integrating with the host OS, sharing storage (`home` directory) and hardware. Note: `distrobox` isn't a command, but a set of commands. More information: <https://github.com/89luca89/distrobox>.
distrobox-upgrade: Upgrade one or multiple Distrobox containers. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-upgrade/>.
distrobox-stop: Stop a Distrobox container. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-stop/>.
distrobox-rm: Remove a Distrobox container. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-rm/>.
distrobox-list: List all Distrobox containers. Distrobox containers are listed separately from the rest of normal Podman or Docker containers. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-list/>.
distrobox-host-exec: Execute a command on the host from inside a Distrobox container. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-host-exec/>.
distrobox-export: Export app/service/binary from container to host OS. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-export/>.
distrobox-enter: Enter a Distrobox container. Default command executed is your `$SHELL`, but you can specify different shells or entire commands to execute. If used inside a script, an application, or a service, you can use the `--headless` mode to disable the tty and interactivity. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-enter/>.
distrobox-create: Create a Distrobox container. The container created will be tightly integrated with the host, allowing sharing of the user's `$HOME` directory, external storage, external USB devices, graphical apps (X11/Wayland), and audio. See also: `distrobox`. More information: <https://distrobox.it/usage/distrobox-create/>.
dirbuster: Brute force directories and filenames on servers. More information: <https://www.kali.org/tools/dirbuster/>.
dirb: Scan HTTP-based webservers for directories and files. More information: <https://manned.org/dirb>.
dir: This command is an alias of `ls -C --escape`.
diff3: Compare three files line by line. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/diffutils/manual/diffutils.html#Invoking-diff3>.
dialog: Display dialog boxes on the terminal. See also: `gum`, `whiptail`. More information: <https://manned.org/dialog>.
dex: DesktopEntry Execution is a program to generate and execute DesktopEntry files of the Application type. More information: <https://github.com/jceb/dex#dex>.
depmod: Generate `modules.dep` and map files for Linux kernel modules. See also: `modprobe`. More information: <https://manned.org/depmod>.
deluser: Delete a user from the system. More information: <https://manned.org/deluser>.
delpart: Ask the Linux kernel to forget about a partition. More information: <https://manned.org/delpart>.
deepseek-r1: The examples for this command have been moved together with `inference-snap`. More information: <https://github.com/canonical/deepseek-r1-snap>.
debuild: Build a Debian package from source. More information: <https://manned.org/debuild>.
debugfs: An interactive ext2/ext3/ext4 filesystem debugger. More information: <https://manned.org/debugfs>.
debtap: Convert Debian packages into Arch Linux packages. See also: `pacman-upgrade`. More information: <https://github.com/helixarch/debtap#available-options>.
debsecan: Debian Security Analyzer, a tool to list vulnerabilities on a particular Debian installation. More information: <https://manned.org/debsecan>.
deborphan: Display orphan packages on operating systems using the APT package manager. More information: <https://manned.org/deborphan>.
debootstrap: Create a basic Debian system. More information: <https://wiki.debian.org/Debootstrap>.
debman: Read man pages from uninstalled packages. More information: <https://manned.org/debman>.
debchange: Maintain the debian/changelog file of a Debian source package. More information: <https://manned.org/debchange>.
deb-get: `apt-get` functionality for `.deb` packages published in third party repositories or via direct download. Works with Linux distributions which use `apt-get`. More information: <https://github.com/wimpysworld/deb-get>.
ddrescue: Data recovery tool that reads data from damaged block devices. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/ddrescue/manual/ddrescue_manual.html#Invoking-ddrescue>.
ddcutil: Control the settings of connected displays via DDC/CI. This command requires the kernel module `i2c-dev` to be loaded. See also: `modprobe`. More information: <https://www.ddcutil.com/commands/>.
dconf: Manage dconf databases. See also: `gsettings`. More information: <https://manned.org/dconf>.
dconf-write: Write key values in dconf databases. More information: <https://manned.org/dconf>.
dconf-reset: Reset key values in dconf databases. More information: <https://manned.org/dconf>.
dconf-read: Read key values from dconf databases. More information: <https://manned.org/dconf>.
dbus-daemon: The D-Bus message daemon, allowing multiple programs to exchange messages. More information: <https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-daemon.1.html>.
dbclient: Lightweight Dropbear Secure Shell client. More information: <https://manned.org/dbclient>.
datamash: Perform basic numeric, textual, and statistical operations on input textual data files. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/datamash/manual/datamash.html#Invoking-datamash>.
darling: Run macOS software on Linux. More information: <https://docs.darlinghq.org/darling-shell.html>.
daemonize: Run a command (that does not daemonize itself) as a Unix daemon. More information: <https://software.clapper.org/daemonize/>.
daemon: Turn other processes into daemons. More information: <https://manned.org/daemon.1>.
curlie: A frontend to `curl` that adds the ease of use of `httpie`. More information: <https://github.com/rs/curlie#usage>.
cu: Call Up another system and act as a dial-in/serial terminal or perform file transfers with no error checking. See also: `picocom`, `minicom`, `tio`. More information: <https://manned.org/cu>.
ctrlaltdel: Utility to control what happens when `<Ctrl Alt Del>` is pressed. More information: <https://manned.org/ctrlaltdel>.
ctr: Manage `containerd` containers and images. More information: <https://manned.org/ctr>.
ctop: Instantly visualize container performance and health with real-time metrics on CPU, memory, and block IO usage. More information: <https://github.com/bcicen/ctop#usage>.
csplit: Split a file into pieces. This generates files named `xx00`, `xx01`, and so on. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/csplit-invocation.html>.
cs2: This command is an alias of `counter strike 2`.
cryptsetup: Manage plain `dm-crypt` and LUKS (Linux Unified Key Setup) encrypted volumes. Some subcommands such as `luksFormat` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/cryptsetup>.
cryptsetup-open: Create a decrypted mapping of an encrypted volume. Note: Enabling TRIM may leak minimal information (freed blocks, possibly revealing the filesystem in use), but is still recommended since the data stays safe and SSDs without TRIM wear out faster. More information: <https://manned.org/cryptsetup-open>.
cryptsetup-luksformat: Initialize a LUKS partition and the initial key slot (0) with a passphrase or keyfile. Note: This operation overwrites all data on the partition. More information: <https://manned.org/cryptsetup-luksFormat>.
cryptcat: Netcat fork with encryption capabilities. More information: <https://manned.org/cryptcat>.
crond: Daemon to execute scheduled commands from crontab files. More information: <https://manned.org/crond>.
criu: Freeze a running application or a process tree and restore it later. More information: <https://manned.org/criu>.
createrepo: Initialize an RPM repository in a directory, including all XML and SQLite files. More information: <https://manned.org/createrepo>.
create_ap: Create an AP (Access Point) at any channel. More information: <https://github.com/oblique/create_ap>.
cpupower: Tools regarding CPU power and tuning options. More information: <https://manned.org/cpupower>.
cpulimit: A tool to throttle the CPU usage of other processes. More information: <https://manned.org/cpulimit>.
cpuid: Display detailed information about all CPUs. More information: <https://manned.org/cpuid.1>.
cpufreq-set: A tool to modify CPU frequency settings. The frequency value should range between the output of command `cpufreq-info -l`. More information: <https://manned.org/cpufreq-set>.
cpufreq-info: Show CPU frequency information. More information: <https://manned.org/cpufreq-info>.
cpufreq-aperf: Calculate the average CPU frequency over a time period. More information: <https://manned.org/cpufreq-aperf>.
counter-strike-2: Host a headless Counter Strike 2 server. More information: <https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Counter-Strike_2/Dedicated_Servers>.
coredumpctl: Retrieve and process saved core dumps and metadata. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/coredumpctl.html>.
conntrack: Interact with the Netfilter connection tracking system. Search, list, inspect, modify, and delete connection flows. More information: <https://manned.org/conntrack>.
conky: Light-weight system monitor for X. More information: <https://github.com/brndnmtthws/conky>.
con2fbmap: Show and manage terminal to framebuffer mapping. More information: <https://manned.org/con2fbmap>.
compsize: Calculate the compression ratio of a set of files on a btrfs filesystem. See also: `btrfs filesystem`. More information: <https://manned.org/compsize>.
compseq: Calculate the composition of unique words in sequences. More information: <https://www.bioinformatics.nl/cgi-bin/emboss/help/compseq/>.
compress: Compress files using the Unix `compress` command. More information: <https://manned.org/compress>.
compose: This command is an alias of `run-mailcap --action=compose`.
column: Format `stdin` or a file into multiple columns. Columns are filled before rows; the default separator is a whitespace. More information: <https://manned.org/column>.
collectd: System statistics collection daemon. More information: <https://manned.org/collectd>.
col: Filter reverse line feeds from input. More information: <https://manned.org/col>.
cointop: Track and monitor cryptocurrencies in the terminal. More information: <https://github.com/cointop-sh/cointop>.
cockpit-ws: Communicate between the browser application and various configuration tools and services like `cockpit-bridge`. More information: <https://cockpit-project.org/guide/latest/cockpit-ws.8.html>.
cockpit-tls: TLS terminating HTTP proxy to encrypt traffic between a client and `cockpit-ws`. More information: <https://cockpit-project.org/guide/latest/cockpit-tls.8.html>.
cockpit-desktop: Securely access Cockpit pages in a running session. It starts `cockpit-ws` and a web browser in an isolated network space and a `cockpit-bridge` in a running user session. More information: <https://cockpit-project.org/guide/latest/cockpit-desktop.1.html>.
cockpit-bridge: Relay messages and commands between the front end and server in the cockpit suite. More information: <https://cockpit-project.org/guide/latest/cockpit-bridge.1.html>.
cloud-init: Manage cloud instance initialization. More information: <https://cloudinit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/cli.html>.
cliphist: Manage clipboard history for Wayland compositors. Works with `wl-copy` and `wl-paste`. More information: <https://github.com/sentriz/cliphist#usage>.
chvt: Change foreground virtual terminal. See also: `fgconsole`. More information: <https://manned.org/chvt>.
chsh: Change user's login shell. Part of `util-linux`. More information: <https://manned.org/chsh>.
chrt: Manipulate the real-time attributes of a process. More information: <https://manned.org/chrt>.
chpasswd: Change the passwords for multiple users by using `stdin`. See also: `passwd`. More information: <https://manned.org/chpasswd>.
choom: Display and change the adjust out-of-memory killer score. More information: <https://manned.org/choom>.
chntpw: A utility that can edit windows registry, reset user password, promote users to administrator by modifying the Windows SAM. Boot target machine with live cd like Kali Linux and run with elevated privileges. More information: <https://pogostick.net/~pnh/ntpasswd/MANUAL.txt>.
chmem: Modify the state of memory blocks (online or offline) in a Linux system. Typically used in virtualized environments to manage memory hotplug. More information: <https://manned.org/chmem>.
chkconfig: Manage the runlevel of services on CentOS 6. More information: <https://manned.org/chkconfig>.
chfn: Update `finger` info for a user. More information: <https://manned.org/chfn>.
checkupdates: Check pending updates in Arch Linux. More information: <https://manned.org/checkupdates>.
checkupdates-aur: Check pending updates from the Arch User Repository (AUR). More information: <https://metacpan.org/dist/OS-CheckUpdates-AUR>.
checkinstall: Track the local installation of a software package, and produce a binary package which can be used with a system's native package manager. More information: <https://checkinstall.izto.org/docs.php>.
check-support-status: Identify installed Debian packages for which support has had to be limited or prematurely ended. More information: <https://manned.org/check-support-status>.
check-language-support: Display a list of missing language packages on Ubuntu. More information: <https://manned.org/check-language-support>.
check-dfsg-status: Report non-free packages installed on Debian-based OSes. This command was formerly known as `vrms`. More information: <https://salsa.debian.org/debian/check-dfsg-status>.
chcpu: Enable/disable a system's CPUs. More information: <https://manned.org/chcpu>.
chcon: Change SELinux security context of a file or files/directories. See also: `secon`, `restorecon`, `semanage fcontext`. More information: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/chcon-invocation.html>.
chcat: Change SELinux security category for files. Categories provide an additional level of access control based on MCS (Multi-Category Security). See also: `chcon`, `semanage`. More information: <https://manned.org/chcat>.
chattr: Change attributes of files or directories. See also: `lsattr`. More information: <https://manned.org/chattr>.
chat: Automate conversations with a modem or serial device. Commonly used to establish PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) connections. More information: <https://manned.org/chat>.
chage: Change user account and password expiry information. More information: <https://manned.org/chage>.
cgroups: Linux kernel feature for limiting, measuring, and controlling resource usage by processes. Cgroups (control groups) however is not a command, but rather a collection of commands, see the relevant pages below. More information: <https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/cgroup-v2.txt>.
cgexec: Limit, measure, and control resources used by processes. Multiple cgroup types (aka controllers) exist, such as `cpu`, `memory`, etc. More information: <https://manned.org/cgexec>.
cgcreate: Create cgroups, used to limit, measure, and control resources used by processes. `cgroups` types can be `memory`, `cpu`, `net_cls`, etc. More information: <https://manned.org/cgcreate>.
cgclassify: Move running tasks to `cgroups`. More information: <https://manned.org/cgclassify>.
cfdisk: Manage partition tables and partitions on a hard disk using a curses UI. See also: `parted`. More information: <https://manned.org/cfdisk>.
cewl: URL spidering tool for making a cracking wordlist from web content. More information: <https://digi.ninja/projects/cewl.php#usage>.
certtool: Generate and manage X.509 certificates, keys, and PKI structures using GnuTLS. More information: <https://gnutls.org/manual/gnutls.html#certtool-Invocation>.
certbot: The Let's Encrypt Agent for automatically obtaining and renewing TLS certificates. Successor to `letsencrypt`. More information: <https://eff-certbot.readthedocs.io/en/latest/using.html>.
cephadm: Deploy and manage a Ceph cluster using containers. Part of the Ceph orchestrator framework. More information: <https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/man/8/cephadm/>.
ceph: A unified storage system. More information: <https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/man/8/ceph/>.
cec-ctl: Control kernel CEC devices. See also: `cec-client`. More information: <https://manned.org/cec-ctl>.
cec-client: Manage serial bus CEC connections. See also: `cec-ctl`. More information: <https://manned.org/cec-client>.
cdrecord: Record data to CDs or DVDs. Some invocations of cdrecord can cause destructive actions, such as erasing all the data on a disc. More information: <https://manned.org/cdrecord>.
cdrdao: Read and write CDs in disc-at-once mode. More information: <https://manned.org/cdrdao>.
cdemu: Manage emulated CD devices. More information: <https://manned.org/cdemu>.
cc: This command is an alias of `gcc`.
cbatticon: A lightweight and fast battery icon that sits in your system tray. More information: <https://github.com/valr/cbatticon>.
cam: Frontend tool for `libcamera`. See also: `v4l2-ctl`. More information: <https://docs.libcamera.org/>.
caligula: A user-friendly, lightweight TUI for disk imaging. See also: `dd`. More information: <https://github.com/ifd3f/caligula>.
calcurse: A text-based calendar and scheduling application. More information: <https://github.com/lfos/calcurse/blob/pu/doc/calcurse.1.txt>.
caja: Manage files and directories in the MATE desktop environment. See also: `nautilus`, `dolphin`, `thunar`, `ranger`. More information: <https://manned.org/caja>.
cage: Open applications in a kiosk mode. See also: `gamescope`. More information: <https://github.com/cage-kiosk/cage/blob/master/cage.1.scd>.
caffeine: Prevent desktop idleness in full-screen mode. More information: <https://manned.org/caffeine>.
caffeine-indicator: Manually inhibit desktop idleness with a toggle. More information: <https://manned.org/caffeine-indicator>.
caffeinate: Prevent desktop from sleeping. More information: <https://manned.org/caffeinate>.
cacaview: Display an image in PMN format. More information: <https://manned.org/cacaview>.
cacafire: Display an animated ASCII fire. More information: <https://manned.org/cacafire>.
cacademo: Display a random ASCII art animation. More information: <https://manned.org/cacademo>.
cacaclock: Display the current time as ASCII art. More information: <https://packages.debian.org/sid/caca-utils>.
bwrap: Run programs in a lightweight sandbox. More information: <https://manned.org/bwrap>.
bwa: Burrows-Wheeler Alignment tool. Short, low-divergent DNA sequences mapper against a large reference genome, such as the human genome. More information: <https://manned.org/bwa>.
busctl: Introspect and monitor the D-Bus bus. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/busctl.html>.
burpsuite: A GUI based application mainly used in web application penetration testing. More information: <https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/troubleshooting/launch-from-command-line>.
bully: Brute-force the WPS pin of a wireless access point. Necessary information must be gathered with `airmon-ng` and `airodump-ng` before using `bully`. More information: <https://salsa.debian.org/pkg-security-team/bully>.
btrfs: A filesystem based on the copy-on-write (COW) principle for Linux. Some subcommands such as `device` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs.html>.
btrfs-subvolume: Manage btrfs subvolumes and snapshots. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-subvolume.html>.
btrfs-send: Transfer data (subvolume/snapshot) from one filesystem to another in a streamable format. Note: `send` requires the snapshot be read-only. See also: `btrfs-subvolume`, `btrfs-property`. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Send-receive.html>.
btrfs-scrub: Scrub btrfs filesystems to verify data integrity. It is recommended to run a scrub once a month. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-scrub.html>.
btrfs-restore: Try to salvage files from a damaged btrfs filesystem. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-restore.html>.
btrfs-rescue: Try to recover a damaged btrfs filesystem. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-rescue.html>.
btrfs-receive: The examples for this command have been moved together with `btrfs send`.
btrfs-property: Get, set, or list properties for a BTRFS filesystem object (files, directories, subvolumes, filesystems, or devices). More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-property.html>.
btrfs-inspect-internal: Query internal information of a btrfs filesystem. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-inspect-internal.html>.
btrfs-device: Manage devices in a btrfs filesystem. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-device.html>.
btrfs-check: Check or repair a btrfs filesystem. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-check.html>.
btrfs-balance: Balance block groups on a btrfs filesystem. More information: <https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-balance.html>.
btrbk: Create snapshots and remote backups of btrfs subvolumes. More information: <https://digint.ch/btrbk/doc/readme.html>.
bsub: Submit batch jobs to LSF (Load Sharing Facility) scheduler. More information: <https://www.ibm.com/docs/spectrum-lsf/latest?topic=reference-bsub>.
bspwm: A tiling window manager based on binary space partitioning. See also: `bspc`. More information: <https://github.com/baskerville/bspwm/blob/master/doc/bspwm.1.asciidoc>.
bspc: Configure and control `bspwm`, managing nodes, desktops, monitors, and more. See also: `bspwm`. More information: <https://github.com/baskerville/bspwm/blob/master/doc/bspwm.1.asciidoc>.
broot: Navigate directory trees interactively. More information: <https://github.com/Canop/broot>.
brightnessctl: Utility for reading and controlling device brightness for Linux operating systems. More information: <https://github.com/Hummer12007/brightnessctl#usage>.
bridge: Show and manipulate network bridge addresses and devices. More information: <https://manned.org/bridge>.
braa: Ultra-fast mass SNMP scanner allowing multiple hosts simultaneously. More information: <https://manned.org/braa>.
br: This command is an alias of `broot`.
bpftrace: High-level tracing language for Linux eBPF. More information: <https://github.com/bpftrace/bpftrace/blob/master/man/adoc/bpftrace.adoc>.
bpftool: Inspect and manipulate eBPF programs and maps in a simple way. More information: <https://manned.org/bpftool>.
bore: Start a local proxy to a remote server using Bore. Some subcommands such as `local` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://github.com/ekzhang/bore#detailed-usage>.
bore-local: Start a local proxy to a remote server using Bore. More information: <https://github.com/ekzhang/bore#detailed-usage>.
bootctl: Control EFI firmware boot settings and manage boot loader. See also: `kernel-install`. More information: <https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/bootctl.html>.
bootc: Boot and upgrade via container images. Manage transactional, in-place operating system updates using OCI/Docker container images. More information: <https://manned.org/bootc>.
bootc-switch: Target a new container image reference to boot. More information: <https://manned.org/bootc-switch>.
bmon: Monitor bandwidth and capture network related statistics. More information: <https://manned.org/bmon>.
blurlock: A simple wrapper around the i3 screen locker `i3lock`, which blurs the screen. See also: `i3lock`. More information: <https://gitlab.manjaro.org/packages/extra/i3exit/-/blob/master/blurlock>.
bluetui: Manage Bluetooth devices with a terminal UI. See also: `bluetoothctl`. More information: <https://github.com/pythops/bluetui#-usage>.
bluetoothd: Daemon to manage bluetooth devices. More information: <https://manned.org/bluetoothd>.
bluetoothctl: Manage Bluetooth devices. See also: `bluetui`. More information: <https://manned.org/bluetoothctl>.
bluebuild: Build Containerfiles and custom images based on your `recipe.yml`. More information: <https://github.com/blue-build/cli#how-to-use>.
blockdev: Manage, query, and manipulate block devices. More information: <https://manned.org/blockdev>.
blkpr: Register, reserve, release, preempt, and clear persistent reservations on a block device that supports Persistent Reservations. More information: <https://manned.org/blkpr>.
blkid: List all recognized partitions and their Universally Unique Identifier (UUID). More information: <https://manned.org/blkid>.
blkdiscard: Discard device sectors on storage devices. Useful for SSDs. More information: <https://manned.org/blkdiscard>.
blight: Utility for changing the display brightness. More information: <https://github.com/gutjuri/blight#usage>.
bleachbit: Clean junk files on the filesystem. More information: <https://docs.bleachbit.org/doc/command-line-interface.html>.
bitwise: Multi base interactive calculator supporting dynamic base conversion and bit manipulation. More information: <https://github.com/mellowcandle/bitwise>.
bindfs: Mount a directory elsewhere with different permissions. More information: <https://bindfs.org/docs/bindfs.1.html>.
betterlockscreen: Simple, minimal lock screen. More information: <https://github.com/betterlockscreen/betterlockscreen#usage>.
betterdiscordctl: Manage BetterDiscord on Linux. More information: <https://github.com/bb010g/betterdiscordctl#manual>.
beet: Manage the beets media library. More information: <https://beets.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/cli.html>.
beep: A utility to beep the PC speaker. More information: <https://manned.org/beep>.
bchunk: Convert CD images to a set of `.iso` and `.cdr` tracks. More information: <https://manned.org/bchunk>.
bcachefs: Manage `bcachefs` filesystems/devices. Some subcommands such as `device` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://bcachefs-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html>.
bcachefs-device: Manage devices within a running `bcachefs` filesystem. More information: <https://bcachefs-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mgmt-devicemanagement.html>.
battop: An interactive viewer for the batteries installed in your notebook. More information: <https://github.com/svartalf/rust-battop>.
batcat: This command is an alias of `bat`.
barotrauma: Start a headless Barotrauma server. Note: The server is configured by editing the `serversettings.xml` file in the game directory. More information: <https://barotraumagame.com/wiki/Hosting_a_Dedicated_Server>.
balooctl: File indexing and searching framework for KDE Plasma. More information: <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Baloo>.
backlight_control: Control a linux machine's backlight using percentage values. More information: <https://github.com/Hendrikto/backlight_control#usage>.
b4: A tool for working with patches and pull requests in a public-inbox archive. Some subcommands such as `am`, `shazam`, `prep`, and `send` have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://manned.org/b4>.
b4-shazam: Retrieve and apply patches from a public-inbox archive directly to the current Git tree. More information: <https://b4.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/maintainer/am-shazam.html>.
b4-send: Send a patch series prepared with `b4 prep` to a mailing list. More information: <https://b4.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/contributor/send.html>.
b4-prep: Prepare a new patch series for submission to a mailing list. More information: <https://b4.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/contributor/prep.html>.
b4-am: Retrieve and prepare patches from a public-inbox archive for applying with `git am`. More information: <https://b4.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/maintainer/am-shazam.html>.
awww: Efficient animated wallpaper daemon for Wayland. More information: <https://codeberg.org/LGFae/awww>.
away: Lock terminal with an away message. More information: <https://manned.org/away>.
avahi-resolve: Translate between host names and IP Addresses. More information: <https://manned.org/avahi-resolve>.
avahi-resolve-host-name: This command is an alias of `avahi-resolve --name`.
avahi-resolve-address: This command is an alias of `avahi-resolve --address`.
avahi-browse: Display services and hosts exposed on the local network via mDNS/DNS-SD. Avahi is compatible with Bonjour (Zeroconf) found in Apple devices. More information: <https://manned.org/avahi-browse>.
autorecon: A multi-threaded network reconnaissance tool which performs automated enumeration of services. More information: <https://github.com/AutoRecon/AutoRecon>.
autorandr: Automatically change screen layout. More information: <https://manned.org/autorandr>.
autopkgtest: Run tests on Debian packages. More information: <https://manned.org/autopkgtest>.
autoexpect: Generate a script from watching a session. More information: <https://manned.org/autoexpect>.
auto-cpufreq: Automatic CPU speed & power optimizer. More information: <https://github.com/AdnanHodzic/auto-cpufreq#auto-cpufreq-modes-and-options>.
authconfig: Configure system authentication resources. More information: <https://manned.org/authconfig>.
ausyscall: Map syscall names and numbers. More information: <https://manned.org/ausyscall>.
ausearch: Query the Linux audit log for events. Part of the `audit` package. See also: `audit2why`, `audit2allow`, `aureport`. More information: <https://manned.org/ausearch>.
aurvote: Vote for packages in the Arch User Repository. To be able to vote, the file `~/.config/aurvote` must exist and contain your AUR credentials. More information: <https://github.com/archlinuxfr/aurvote#name>.
aurpublish: Publish Arch User Repository packages. More information: <https://github.com/eli-schwartz/aurpublish/blob/master/doc/aurpublish.1.asciidoc>.
aurman: An Arch Linux utility to build and install packages from the Arch User Repository. See also: `pacman`. More information: <https://github.com/polygamma/aurman#syntax>.
aureport: Generate summary reports of auditd logs. More information: <https://manned.org/aureport>.
auracle: Interact with Arch Linux's User Repository, commonly referred to as the AUR. More information: <https://github.com/falconindy/auracle/blob/master/man/auracle.1.pod>.
aura: The Aura Package Manager: a secure, multilingual package manager for Arch Linux and the AUR. More information: <https://github.com/fosskers/aura>.
aur: Build packages from the AUR and manage local repositories. Note: A local repository needs to be defined in `/etc/pacman.conf` and `vifm` needs to be installed for this to fully function. More information: <https://github.com/aurutils/aurutils>.
aur-sync: Download and build AUR packages automatically. Note: A local repository needs to be defined in `/etc/pacman.conf` and `vifm` needs to be installed for this to fully function. More information: <https://github.com/aurutils/aurutils>.
auditctl: Utility to control the behavior, get status, and manage rules of the Linux Auditing System. More information: <https://manned.org/auditctl>.
audit2why: Explain SELinux denials from audit logs. Part of the `policycoreutils-python-utils` package. See also: `audit2allow`, `ausearch`, `sealert`. More information: <https://manned.org/audit2why>.
audit2allow: Generate SELinux policy allow rules from audit logs. Part of the `policycoreutils-python-utils` package. See also: `audit2why`, `ausearch`, `semodule`. More information: <https://manned.org/audit2allow>.
atop: Linux system and process monitor. See also: `htop`, `top`, `btop`, `btm`, `glances`. More information: <https://manned.org/atop>.
asusctl: Control various features of ASUS laptops on Linux. More information: <https://github.com/OpenGamingCollective/asusctl>.
asterisk: Run and manage telephone and exchange (phone) server instances. More information: <https://docs.asterisk.org/Operation/>.
asciiart: Convert images to ASCII. More information: <https://github.com/nodanaonlyzuul/asciiart#in-the-command-line>.
ascii: Show ASCII character aliases. More information: <http://www.catb.org/~esr/ascii/ascii.html>.
ascii-xfr: Transfer files using the ASCII protocol. Part of `minicom`. More information: <https://manned.org/ascii-xfr>.
as: Portable GNU assembler. Primarily intended to assemble output from `gcc` to be used by `ld`. More information: <https://manned.org/as>.
arptables: Manage ARP filtering rules using the `nftables` backend. Part of the `xtables-nft` suite for ARP packet filtering. More information: <https://manned.org/arptables>.
arpspoof: Forge ARP replies to intercept packets. More information: <https://manned.org/arpspoof>.
arpaname: Get the corresponding ARPA name for an IP address. More information: <https://manned.org/arpaname>.
ark-survival-evolved: Create and start a headless ARK: Survival Evolved server. More information: <https://ark.wiki.gg/wiki/Server_configuration>.
ark-survival-ascended: Create and start a headless ARK: Survival Ascended server. More information: <https://ark.wiki.gg/wiki/Server_configuration>.
arithmetic: Quiz on simple arithmetic problems. More information: <https://manned.org/arithmetic>.
arecord: Sound recorder for ALSA soundcard driver. More information: <https://manned.org/arecord>.
archlinux-java: Switch between installed Java environments. More information: <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Java#Switching_between_JVM>.
archivemount: Mount an archive for access as a filesystem. More information: <https://manned.org/archivemount>.
archinstall: Guided Arch Linux installer. More information: <https://archinstall.archlinux.page/installing/guided.html>.
archey: Simple tool for stylishly displaying system information. More information: <https://lclarkmichalek.github.io/archey3/>.
arch-update: Interactively check for, notify, and apply updates on Arch Linux. More information: <https://github.com/Antiz96/arch-update>.
arch-chroot: Enhanced `chroot` command to help in the Arch Linux installation process. More information: <https://manned.org/arch-chroot>.
apx: Package management utility with support for multiple sources, allowing you to install packages in subsystems. More information: <https://docs.vanillaos.org/docs/en/apx-manpage>.
apx-subsystems: Manage subsystems in `apx`. Subsystems are containers that can be created based on pre-existing stacks. More information: <https://docs.vanillaos.org/docs/en/apx-manpage#subsystems>.
apx-stacks: Manage stacks in `apx`. Note: User-created stack configurations are stored in `~/.local/share/apx/stacks`. More information: <https://docs.vanillaos.org/docs/en/apx-manpage#stacks>.
apx-pkgmanagers: Manage package managers in `apx`. Note: User-created package manager configurations are stored in `~/.local/share/apx/pkgmanagers`. More information: <https://docs.vanillaos.org/docs/en/apx-manpage#pkgmanagers>.
aptitude: Debian and Ubuntu package management utility. More information: <https://manned.org/aptitude>.
apt: Package manager for Debian-based distributions. Intended as a user-friendly alternative to `apt-get` for interactive use. For equivalent commands in other package managers, see <https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pacman/Rosetta>. More information: <https://manned.org/apt.8>.
apt-mark: Utility to change the status of installed packages. More information: <https://manned.org/apt-mark>.
apt-list: List packages. Note: Recommended to run `apt update` first to refresh local package index files. More information: <https://manned.org/apt.8>.
apt-key: Key management utility for the APT Package Manager on Debian and Ubuntu. Note: This command is deprecated (except for the use of `apt-key del` in maintainer scripts). More information: <https://manned.org/apt-key>.
apt-install: Install packages for Debian-based distributions. More information: <https://manned.org/apt.8>.
apt-get: Debian and Ubuntu package management utility. Search for packages using `apt-cache`. It is recommended to use `apt` when used interactively in Ubuntu versions 16.04 and later. More information: <https://manned.org/apt-get.8>.
apt-file: Search for files in `apt` packages, including ones not yet installed. More information: <https://manned.org/apt-file>.
apt-clone: Clone/back up/restore the package state of a Debian-based system. More information: <https://github.com/mvo5/apt-clone>.
apt-cache: Debian and Ubuntu package query tool. More information: <https://manned.org/apt-cache>.
apt-add-repository: This command is an alias of `add-apt-repository`.
apptainer: Manage containers for HPC and scientific computing. Some subcommands such as `build`, `pull`, `push`, etc. have their own usage documentation. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli.html>.
apptainer-verify: Verify digital signatures of SIF container images. See also: `apptainer-sign`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_verify.html>.
apptainer-test: Run the testscript defined in an Apptainer container image. The testscript is defined in the `%test` section of the container's definition file. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_test.html>.
apptainer-sign: Add digital signatures to a SIF container image. See also: `apptainer-verify`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_sign.html>.
apptainer-shell: Start an interactive shell within an Apptainer container. See also: `apptainer exec`, `apptainer run`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_shell.html>.
apptainer-search: Search a Container Library for container images. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_search.html>.
apptainer-run: Run the default runscript of an Apptainer container. The runscript is defined in the `%runscript` section of the container's definition file. See also: `apptainer exec`, `apptainer shell`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_run.html>.
apptainer-run-help: Display user-defined help for an Apptainer container image. Help text is defined in the `%help` section of the container's definition file. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_run-help.html>.
apptainer-registry: Manage authentication to OCI/Docker registries. See also: `apptainer pull`, `apptainer push`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_registry.html>.
apptainer-push: Push container images to remote registries. See also: `apptainer-pull`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_push.html>.
apptainer-pull: Pull container images from remote sources. See also: `apptainer-push`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_pull.html>.
apptainer-overlay: Manage EXT3 writable overlay images for Apptainer containers. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_overlay.html>.
apptainer-inspect: Display metadata of Apptainer container images. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_inspect.html>.
apptainer-exec: Execute a command within an Apptainer container. See also: `apptainer run`, `apptainer shell`. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_exec.html>.
apptainer-delete: Delete container images from a remote library. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_delete.html>.
apptainer-config: Manage various Apptainer configurations. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_config.html>.
apptainer-capability: Manage Linux capabilities for users and groups. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_capability.html>.
apptainer-cache: Manage the local Apptainer cache. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_cache.html>.
apptainer-build: Build Apptainer container images. More information: <https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_build.html>.
apport-bug: File a bug report on Ubuntu. More information: <https://ubuntu.com/project/docs/contributors/debugging/apport/>.
appman: Package manager for AppImages. More information: <https://github.com/ivan-hc/AppMan>.
apparmor_status: This command is an alias of `aa-status`.
apparmor_parser: Load, compile, and manage AppArmor security profiles. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_apparmor_parser.8>.
aplay: Sound player for ALSA soundcard driver. More information: <https://manned.org/aplay>.
apk: Alpine Linux package management tool. More information: <https://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/Alpine_Package_Keeper>.
apachectl: Control an Apache HTTP server. More information: <https://manned.org/apachectl>.
apache2ctl: Administrate the Apache HTTP web server. This command comes with Debian based OSes, for RHEL based ones see `httpd`. More information: <https://manned.org/apache2ctl>.
anbox: Run Android applications on any Linux operating system. More information: <https://manned.org/anbox>.
ananicy-cpp: Feature-rich C++ rewrite of the Ananicy auto-nice daemon for Linux. More information: <https://gitlab.com/ananicy-cpp/ananicy-cpp>.
amixer: Mixer for ALSA soundcard driver. More information: <https://manned.org/amixer>.
amdgpu_top: Tool to display AMD GPU utilization and hardware metrics using the AMDGPU driver. See also: `nvtop`, `radeontop`. More information: <https://github.com/Umio-Yasuno/amdgpu_top#usage>.
alternatives: This command is an alias of `update-alternatives`.
alsamixer: Graphical mixer for ALSA soundcard driver. More information: <https://manned.org/alsamixer>.
alpine: An email client and Usenet newsgroup program with a pico/nano-inspired interface. Supports most modern email services through IMAP. More information: <https://manned.org/alpine>.
alpaca: A graphical frontend to chat with Ollama models. See also: `ollama`. More information: <https://jeffser.com/alpaca/launch-options.html>.
alien: Convert different installation packages to other formats. See also: `debtap`. More information: <https://manned.org/alien>.
akmods: Automatic Kernel Module management system for Fedora/RHEL-based distributions. Rebuilds out-of-tree kernel modules (like NVIDIA drivers) dynamically when kernels update. More information: <https://manned.org/akmods>.
aide: Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment to validate file integrity. More information: <https://manned.org/aide>.
ahost: DNS lookup utility to display the A or AAAA record linked with a hostname or IP address. More information: <https://manned.org/ahost>.
agetty: Alternative `getty`: Open a `tty` port, prompt for a login name, and invoke the `/bin/login` command. It is normally invoked by `init`. Note: The baud rate is the speed of data transfer between a terminal and a device over a serial connection. More information: <https://manned.org/agetty>.
adig: Print information received from Domain Name System (DNS) servers. More information: <https://manned.org/adig>.
addr2line: Convert addresses of a binary into file names and line numbers. More information: <https://manned.org/addr2line>.
addpart: Tell the Linux kernel about the existence of the specified partition. A simple wrapper around the `add partition` ioctl. More information: <https://manned.org/addpart>.
acpi_listen: Listen to ACPI events. More information: <https://manned.org/acpi_listen>.
acpi: Show battery status or thermal information. More information: <https://manned.org/acpi>.
acountry: Print the country where an IPv4 address or hostname is located. More information: <https://manned.org/acountry>.
abrt: This command is an alias of `abrt-cli`.
abrt-cli: Automatic Bug Reporting Tool for Fedora-based systems. Used to detect, analyze, and report application crashes. More information: <https://abrt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage.html>.
abrt-action-analyze-c: Calculate UUID for a problem data directory with `coredump`. More information: <https://manned.org/abrt-action-analyze-c>.
abrt-action-analyze-backtrace: Analyze C/C++ backtrace. Generate duplication hash, backtrace rating, and identify crash function. Save the data as new elements `duphash`, `rating`, `crash_function` in the problem directory. More information: <https://manned.org/abrt-action-analyze-backtrace>.
abroot: Utility providing full immutability and atomicity by transacting between 2 root partition states (A<=>B). Updates are performed using OCI images, to ensure that the system is always in a consistent state. More information: <https://docs.vanillaos.org/docs/en/abroot-manpage>.
abbr: Manage abbreviations for the fish shell. User-defined words are replaced with longer phrases after they are entered. More information: <https://fishshell.com/docs/current/cmds/abbr.html>.
aa-update-browser: Update AppArmor browser profiles to use supported abstractions. Part of the AppArmor suite. More information: <https://manned.org/aa-update-browser>.
aa-unconfined: List processes with open TCP/UDP ports that do not have AppArmor profiles loaded. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-unconfined.8>.
aa-teardown: Tear down all AppArmor profiles and disable AppArmor enforcement. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-teardown.8>.
aa-status: List currently loaded AppArmor modules. See also: `aa-complain`, `aa-disable`, `aa-enforce`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-status.8>.
aa-remove-unknown: Remove AppArmor profiles that are no longer present in the configuration directory. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-remove-unknown.8>.
aa-mergeprof: Merge AppArmor security profile files into the profile directory. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-mergeprof.8>.
aa-logprof: Interactively update AppArmor security profiles based on logged violations. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-logprof.8>.
aa-genprof: Generate AppArmor security profiles by monitoring program behavior. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-genprof.8>.
aa-enforce: Set an AppArmor profile to enforce mode. See also: `aa-complain`, `aa-disable`, `aa-status`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-enforce.8>.
aa-disable: Disable AppArmor security policies. See also: `aa-complain`, `aa-enforce`, `aa-status`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-disable.8>.
aa-decode: Decode AppArmor audit logs into a human-readable format. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-decode.8>.
aa-complain: Set an AppArmor policy to complain mode. See also: `aa-disable`, `aa-enforce`, `aa-status`. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-complain.8>.
aa-cleanprof: Clean AppArmor security profiles by removing unused rules. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-cleanprof.8>.
aa-audit: Set AppArmor security profiles to audit mode. More information: <https://gitlab.com/apparmor/apparmor/-/wikis/manpage_aa-audit.8>.
a2query: Retrieve runtime configuration from Apache on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2query>.
a2ensite: Enable an Apache virtual host on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2ensite>.
a2enmod: Enable an Apache module on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2enmod>.
a2enconf: Enable an Apache configuration file on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2enconf>.
a2dissite: Disable an Apache virtual host on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2dissite>.
a2dismod: Disable an Apache module on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2dismod>.
a2disconf: Disable an Apache configuration file on Debian-based OSes. More information: <https://manned.org/a2disconf>.
